0022d5d2ee0fa87f.text: The remains of the Corongiu nuraghe lie in the municipality of Ollastra, in the Serra Laccus area. Unfortunately the monument has been almost completely dismantled. It must have been a tholos nuraghe, but its ground-plan module is not clear.

00255c319c8644c3.text: Natural cave used as a storage place for large containers for foodstuffs dating to the Middle Bronze Age, found intact on the spot,

0025e6faa271a4a4.text: Almost on the summit of a small hill stands the nuraghe of Monte Pedrosu. During the First or Second World War it was used as a pillbox, as shown by the concrete masonry added to the top of the archaeological monument.

002fe3f0054ac9c6.text: Remains of a Nuragic village composed of about fifty huts. Communication took place through underground passages, many of which are still unexplored today. One notes the presence of the "meeting hut", conspicuously restored.

0044e4789e967362.text: Single-tower nuraghe with a probable settlement.

005407399da1246a.text: Nuraghe Loschiri, in the territory of Semestene, a small village in the Meilogu (visible in the background to the right of the image). Partly ruined, it preserves the entrance and large parts of the interior intact.

0066d8f888a686a0.text: Nuragic doorway giving access to the rock above the cliff.

0090c9430f1eba3d.text: The settlement is characterised by the presence of a village, documented by pockets of deposits and hut foundations, attributable to the Nuragic age, more specifically to the Middle Bronze, Recent Bronze, Final Bronze and Early Iron Age phases. The Recent Bronze Age phases are attested, for the most part, by the numerous finds of grey-slate pottery made in the 1980s at the same time as the site was first reported.

0093f57fadd2b56a.text: In the countryside around Samatzai there are several scattered menhirs. Many of them, once standing, now lie overturned at the edges of paths and farmland; some have become and are used as boundary stones between one village and another, like the one still visible on top of the hill Bruncu sa Furca, where a prehistoric village may have stood. This standing stone is 1.30 m high, with a quadrangular section, rounded at the top, and without any particular signs of working.

009e2b84bf042855.text: The state of abandonment and decay before us is serious. Unfortunately, the indifference of the institutions, which still fail to act despite repeated calls to do so, provokes indignation. The structure is interesting and some parts can still be visited despite the collapses. The corridor remains clearly visible, opening through a dolmenic doorway onto the nearby cliff.

00c10e5347143ec5.text: It is the best-preserved nuraghe in the territory of Tratalias and stands in one of the many medaus, called precisely Is Cuccus. It is a single-tower nuraghe with a surviving height of about 5 m, built of megalithic andesite blocks. The circular inner chamber is about 5.50 m wide, has a tholos with its top missing, and is completely clear of collapse.

00d8ee3c51378cf2.text:
The monument, of the tholos type, cannot be entered because of collapse, but it has a circular plan about 9 metres in diameter and preserves, on the outside, a stretch of wall up to 2.20 metres high, formed by five courses of large trachyte boulders.

A short distance from the nuraghe are the remains of a wall, probably a surviving stretch of outer wall.

00e29de96df8ff60.text: The Ruiu in question is an abandoned single-tower nuraghe completely overgrown with vegetation, but we still managed to force our way through the scrub to get inside. The tholos is not intact and unfortunately the vegetation has taken over.

00f7a4e93e7076ae.text: As far as can be seen through the vegetation it is a single-tower nuraghe with a curtain wall; I believe it is well preserved despite the collapsed tholos, but it needs excavation and cleaning.

00f7d61f05100a58.text:
It was built in the Nuragic period for the water cult. Situated in the locality of Is Pirois, this Nuragic sacred well has the peculiarity of a single-tower nuraghe erected on its summit, built on the false dome that closes the well chamber.

The vestibule is defined by two wall faces composed of granite blocks. From the lintelled entrance one enters the stairway leading down into the well chamber, which is closed at the top by a false dome.

0112c126875b0b52.text: Visible from the road, these are domus de janas with a modified entrance, set below ground level and lying inside the sheepfold.

01429a0e0110d865.text: The Atzara nuraghe is a three-lobed complex nuraghe with a tall central tower distinguished by a broad base. The walls linking the three outer towers are still in good condition, while the reinforcement structures were built in Punic and Roman times. It has recently been cleared but awaits a more thorough excavation to understand its structure better.

0176ec711785071e.text:
The funerary site, datable to the 3rd millennium BC and used until the early centuries of the 2nd millennium BC, consists of thirteen domus de janas. The finds recovered are attributable to the Ozieri, Abealzu-Filigosa, Monte Claro, Beaker and Bonnanaro cultures and are now largely preserved in the Villa Sulcis Museum in Carbonia.

A single-tower nuraghe stands on the summit of the hill on which the necropolis is situated.

019265a5a00a2afe.text: A small isolated hill in the middle of ploughed fields. Many maintain that a nuraghe lies completely covered with earth inside it. The upper crowning of stone ashlars also suggests this.

01f195b88098662c.text: The monument stands in a commanding position; the extensive collapse of the outer wall face prevents an accurate reading, but it appears to be a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan and two storeys, with a spaced outer wall.

01f591470bd3e1ef.text: On a plateau used for crops and pasture, only the basal course has been identified, made of large, roughly dressed blocks, of what is thought to have been a nuraghe. Its sub-circular ground plan, which incorporates a large natural granite boulder, is still legible. Because of stone-clearing work and the reuse of the ashlars for dry-stone walls, not even traces of the collapse survive.

01fad16c4d292bf3.text: It comprises three hypogea, the first of which (with seven cells) should also be called "Sa Spelunca de Nonna".

0229d8b7ecbb1e15.text: The lower register of the stele, slightly trapezoidal (1.02 m – 1.05 m – height 0.98 m), has a frame running along the profile of three sides (0.16/0.18 m wide on the upper line; from 0.18 m to 0.13 m on the vertical sides), raised by 0.35/0.15 m. The thickness of the slab differs on the two sides: on the left, at the lower edge it measures 0.34 m; 0.40 m at the top and 0.56 m in the middle zone; on the right it decreases from the base (59 cm) to the top (32 cm).

02446a93da58467f.text:
We approach the south-east wall with the internal wall face of the nuraghe, past the "guard niche" on the right and the start of the helical staircase on the left.

These two chambers are inaccessible because the interior has completely collapsed and is full of ashlars. The clear trace of their course remains, however, with the upper part of the staircase re-emerging above the entrance passage after completing the circuit of the tower.

024b681ec33f1d06.text: Partially collapsed single-tower nuraghe covered by vegetation

025dbdae9b1668d7.text:
It is of mixed type, built of large granite blocks, with a central tower reaching 12 metres in height, with corridors and surrounded by three secondary towers. The lintelled entrance gives access to a corridor with a side chamber containing a well just under 2 metres deep. In the central chamber there is another corridor where the helical staircase leading to the upper floor is located.

The other three towers are partially collapsed and difficult to access;

0262bfc32dcd94ce.text: Nuraghe built of limestone ashlars. A shelter was later built on it, with new walls of small limestone ashlars. To the north, at the entrance, there is an ashlar with a worked hollow.

027859001ccc6685.text:
Administratively it belongs to the municipality of Thiesi, province of Sassari, from which it is about 10 kilometres away.

The necropolis consists of four domus de janas cut into a trachyte outcrop on the slopes of Monte Ittiresu. Among them, Tomb III stands out for its importance; also known as the "Painted Tomb", it is considered one of the most interesting testimonies of the Sardinian Neolithic. Because the site has been left abandoned, the frescoes are undergoing continuous and rapid deterioration.

02acf19a9755561e.text:
The nuraghe is a single-tower nuraghe with a sub-elliptical plan, built of roughly dressed trachyte blocks, collapsed on the south side and partly buried, and completely overgrown with vegetation.

Of the central chamber only traces of the staircase and a niche can just be made out.

On the side facing the valley one can see what must have been an opening in the outer wall.

02b1e8100436d410.text: A ruined nuraghe of which three courses remain. A probable nuraghe belonging to the "unfinished" category.

02e265fdcd43bb61.text: Single-tower nuraghe with a ruined and buried village

02e5ed197683aaf2.text: 那些那些那些那些那些

02eaad7d2b6d2982.text: A tancato-type nuraghe with a main tower and an added building unit (second tower and courtyard). The monument stands right next to the parish church.

02f94fb45e5d48ec.text: Single-tower nuraghe situated on the plain, enclosed by a wire fence. Four courses of the external wall face on the north-east side are currently visible, in medium-sized blocks. The presence of other archaeological remains around it cannot be ruled out.

02fb93c6a37331ca.text:
The tomb is part of the Campu Majore necropolis, composed of 24 domus de janas, which lie on private property and are not accessible without permission.

The entrance of this domus de janas faced the village of Busachi; during the Second World War it was altered with a reinforced concrete wall and adapted by the owners as a shelter against bombing.

It is now used as a water reservoir.

03095083a1d01ccd.text: The menhir complex originally consisted of 12 menhirs arranged in a circle. Only one now remains, about two metres high. The others have disappeared, perhaps removed during works.

03107a242d36fc82.text: Various domus de janas for which no description was found

0310c9ab029607ea.text:
The split rock, a narrow, low space, dark and dusty, that forces you to kneel as if to remind you that you are in a sacred place.

But it is when you turn on the light that everything lights up, the rock takes shape, and the ancient symbols seize you and carry you back in time.

031362500d6378cd.text: A well a short distance from the Unia nuraghe, along the bed of a stream, probably of Nuragic construction.

034b24ead383619f.text: "Nuraghe Ianna Bassa, below Monte Sedda Sos Campos, near good springs are the remains of the nuraghe, part of the base and above it a heap of stones. On land belonging to Antioco Sanna." Taramelli's description, seventy years on, still substantially matches the present state of the ruins.

034fe8ed0a35ac54.text: The nuragic complex consists of nine towers, three belonging to the central structures and six to the robust outer wall. Its absolute peculiarity is the direct superimposition on its structures of the ruins of a small country church, dedicated to the eponymous saint and dating to the early 17th century; eleven burials found in the area around the sacred building belong to its period of use. On the hill of San Sebastiano, traces of a Punic occupation are legible.

038ff9c22e11617d.text: Complex nuraghe, completely buried and destroyed; of the main monument three courses survive, 1.20 m high, and its diameter is about 9/10 metres.

039dbb95e4d64bf4.text: The monument comprises a main tower, against whose front side, from east to south-south-west, a bastion (8) has been built enclosing an open courtyard (11), and two corner towers (13-14). All around are visible the ruins of several structures, probably belonging to the associated settlement.

03a20587dc28c360.text: Now engulfed in dense scrub, it is in very poor condition with boulders scattered through it.

03a40af86b6e7b1c.text: It could refer to the construction of a giants' tomb or of some Nuragic hut linked to the eponymous nuraghe a short distance away.

03a494f8116c2021.text: An elliptical building, disturbed, on a slight artificial rise. Function to be verified.

03b3d8bce6a92bd5.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. It is almost completely covered by climbing vegetation, especially on the side facing N–NE. The western side is the most legible, with structural remains standing just over 4 m high, while the tower as a whole is about 7 m high.

03dc4f0b5a90f147.text: A single-tower nuraghe that has collapsed inwards, of which the doorway and about five courses of the tower survive.

03f2eed4bebea07a.text: Two giants' tombs probably belonging to the nearby nuraghe Prizzada

03fb528bb302c5f6.text:
Isolated domus with reuse.

Taken from the publication "Ricerche archeologiche nel Marghine-Planargia" by Moravetti

0405a09fbe71e3e5.text:
It can be counted among the most extensive of those known and is rich in particular architectural symbolism. Hewn from a rocky plateau of red trachyte, it consists of at least twenty hypogea.

The domus de janas very often reproduce the ground plans and certain details of the dwellings of the living.

In some of them anthropomorphic petroglyphs are carved, known as “capovolti” because they are thought to represent the souls of the dead returning to mother earth.

043a873fbccde45d.text: The necropolis of Iscala Mugheras consists of six domus de janas. Nos. IV, V and VI in particular have been used as livestock shelters by the owner of the land on which they are located.

044c7f731283edf2.text: It is a tomb with a rectangular burial chamber in a clear state of decay, almost completely covered by brambles and hard to identify; it is about 15 metres long.

04628ea2ecf62ce7.text: Single-tower nuraghe completely ruined. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

0468c206689a1116.text: Nearby there is a giants' tomb

0469dc0966e4ee91.text: Nuraghe in very poor condition, visible on the outside at only a few points; many boulders lie scattered on the adjacent ground, and almost the whole structure is covered by vegetation.

047d72b1943b2e07.text: It is reduced to ruins but very interesting for its star-shaped layout. A Megaron-type temple is present. For clarity I will use the number I to indicate the first of the three found in a very small area with the place-name Giaganu Dominigu. I do not have the systematic survey carried out by the Sassari Superintendency; on my part I propose an ideal reconstruction that comes as close as possible to the real one, considering that we are "on home ground".

0489a33d2629f084.text: Complex nuraghe, consisting of a central tower and four added towers. The building, datable to 1400–1000 BC, lies on the boundary between the municipalities of Oristano and Villaurbana. Surrounded by scrub and vegetation, it is not easily accessible or visitable.

048e09a1eb1c9626.text: Destroyed nuraghe, no longer visible today

04cdfb8b48db9796.text: Single-tower nuraghe in good condition, with entrance and tholos partly buried but relatively intact.

04de16dd429b4a4e.text: The site is interesting for a whole series of structural and typological considerations regarding the Domus de Janas. It is a true necropolis: the domus are both simple and complex. They range from one with an antechamber and a single cell to the most complex, with many well-made chambers. The vault of some has collapsed, but a careful visit is still possible.

0519b885f0326450.text: Complex nuraghe with village. It lies on the border with the municipality of Sinnai in the Campidano State Forest. A mountainside is completely covered with stones and it is very difficult to make out structures. In some places wall structures are visible.

05275dc39021e8b5.text: The nuraghe, of which no trace remains, stood on the headland now called Torre Canai – Turri. The map of Sant'Antioco drawn by the geographer Major Besson in 1744 suggests that the tower, built by order of the King of Sardinia, Charles Emmanuel III, in 1757 on the headland “su moru”, was constructed using the Nuragic structures.

05285af62c002dfe.text: Natural with adaptations, it is attributable to the Bonnanaro culture period. (2200–1800 BC) Used as a burial.

05299977d78d81d2.text: Discovered in 1881, it was then buried again and brought back to light in 1982 by the Superintendency.

056c8fec6e61bca2.text:
Dimensions: h. 1.50 m; length 10.50 m; width 1.40 m.

The tomb stands on a small rise whose gentle slopes are currently used for vine cultivation. The left wing of the exedra survives, formed by large blocks that decrease in size from the entrance towards the lateral ends. The entrance, lacking the stele, shows an interesting arrangement for its setting: a shaped granite block on which a stele presumably rested.

056d341b94307511.text:
The burial – of the coursed type with an arched stele – partly preserves the apsidal tomb body, oriented to the east and built of medium-sized polyhedral blocks of granite and porphyry. The short rectangular inner corridor has walls formed by basal orthostats supporting three courses of roughly dressed blocks; the floor consists of the outcropping rock.

The burial dates to around 1500 BC.

05714d6e265cfd66.text: A giants' tomb in a state of total abandonment, it lies a few dozen metres from the nuraghe.

057ca08ba01ab740.text: "Tancato" nuraghe Funtana Mela, Macomer. The plan is taken from Moravetti, Archaeological research in the Marghine-Planargia.

058ff5a3d50d8de5.text: The building, probably Nuragic, shows straight wall lines that enclose a rectangular shape oriented on a north–south longitudinal axis. It seems plausible that stones taken from the ancient building were used for the later enclosure and hut; at first glance its shape and evident features recall a megaron temple.

059a3724fb272071.text: At Scivu, by the beach of the same name, stands the nuraghe known as Nuraghe Narocci or Cancedda. The nuraghe sits on the hill of Punta su Nuraxi, 226 metres above sea level, overlooking the valley that slopes down to the coast. The structure consisted of at least four towers and covered a large area. Some of the scattered material has been found even at the foot of the hill.

05dd806986afd12c.text: Ruined single-tower nuraghe. Part of the tholos survives on the west side. In the past it was altered to house a sheepfold shelter.

05e4978406f67e83.text: Described by Lamarmora and Mackenzie, who saw it almost intact, at least in its ground plan, and defined by Pinza as “the elevation of the finest giants’ tomb known in Sardinia”, the giants’ tomb of Imbertighe is now reduced to the arched stele and the wings of the exedra, which consist of three courses of stones.

05e720eb7ce2d0e5.text: Stone circle. It may be an unfinished nuraghe.

05e83484ab0d6271.text: The nuraghe stands at the bottom of a valley on a small rocky spur.

05f1d89f910dcd91.text: What remains of a completely ruined dolmenic giants' tomb, of which mainly the vertical elements and the perimeter foundations survive

05f3934f8432297a.text: Complex nuraghe composed of two simple towers added laterally and joined tangentially, oriented SSE and NNW. The SSE tower has its interior choked with collapse; on the south side there is a break in the wall outline. The second tower, oriented NNW, does not preserve its full perimeter, which is interrupted in several stretches by collapse probably caused by the dense vegetation there. Other building masses are present but not clearly definable because of collapse and vegetation.

05feab4866339001.text: It is one of the many nuraghi in the Tertenia area and retains an intact tholos.

060d73ed56cd7276.text: A few metres from the two tombs of Sa Perda e s'Altare are the foundations of a circular hut (diam. 10.70 – wall th. 0.50) which, given its dimensions and type of construction, appears to be Nuragic; unfortunately only the basal course remains.

060e1dce1b912005.text: Shown on topographic maps but evidently destroyed in the past. The sheepfold visible in the photo is not the nuraghe.

062a90eefcb03308.text:
It is a burial with a rectangular corridor cut into the rock and provided with a limestone pavement.

The walls of the chamber are built of marl ashlars, originally bonded with mud mortar, laid in horizontal courses, which in the upper part of the wall face have an oblique exposed face. No trace remains, however, of the exedra's hemicycle.

062bfd198bf1fb0c.text: It dates to about 1500 BC; the collapse is dated to the 9th century BC, and it remained uninhabited until 100 BC when the Romans arrived. It consists of a central tower surrounded by five other towers and an outer wall (outer enclosure), with a further seven towers forming another defensive curtain wall enclosing several courtyards. A second outer curtain wall and a third with three more towers are also present. The total number of towers is twenty-one. The area exceeds 5000 m².

065b0bbd285842fe.text: It is in a state of complete abandonment, overgrown with vegetation, partly buried but mostly collapsed, also due to the action of tomb robbers. A nuraghe with at least two chambers or smaller towers leaning against the main tower and an entrance certainly oriented to the south-east. It is mentioned as a nuraghe with a smelting furnace. In visual contact with the nuraghi S'Omu 'e S'Orku, Monte Eghedda and Brandanu.

06614473dc3ab248.text:
The necropolis consists of 18 domus de janas, cut into three superimposed horizontal levels starting from the base line of the ridge, for a maximum height of 3 m above the ground.

The finds recovered during the excavations have allowed the burials to be dated to a period ranging from the Late Neolithic (San Michele culture, 3200–2800 BC) to the Early Bronze Age (Bonnanaro culture, 1800–1600 BC).

06a324c12a48b20f.text: During the Nuragic period the territory was densely inhabited because of its enviable strategic position: near the lake numerous nuraghi rise, among them the one called Sa Pigalva.

06cc102901d056ac.text: It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, diameter 11.20 m, with surviving walling 3.20 m high, four courses. Masonry of polyhedral blocks, barely dressed. Already in Taramelli's time the nuraghe was destroyed; only the base remains.

06d79757f5109603.text: Wild olive trees growing in the tomb corridor are demolishing what remains. Branches, foliage and wind-blown sediment have covered the cavities. On the front of this giants' tomb someone had built a kind of hut using some of the exedra ashlars. Today, however, because of the thorny shrubs the tomb is not even easily reachable.

06de47d91947acec.text: Nuraghe in good condition. The interior is almost intact. The tholos is open because the keystone is missing.

06e09c4c563c1afc.text: A large cave consisting of a single chamber used from the beginning of the Middle Bronze Age, where materials of the Bonnanaro culture were found.

06e9365b7ae94767.text: A few steps from the centre of Gonnesa, in a channel in the schist walls, we find the Domus de Janas. The tomb is very simple, with a round plan, and consists of a single burial chamber. The vegetation around the site is lush, so it is possible that the channel conceals other burials.

06f1c6adef737819.text: Domus de janas inside the settlement of Buddusò, cut with a cruciform plan into a granite outcrop

0711a552a181ceae.text: The nuraghe survives to about 3 metres on the north side and has a diameter of about 10 metres. Built of medium-sized trachyte rough blocks, it is partly covered by vegetation. A scatter of medium-sized Roman material lies on the north-east side of the site.

071618fcf9ed6c07.text: Nuraghe Piscu, situated inside the municipal archaeological park since 1982, runs alongside the SS 128 towards Mandas. Piscu is the monument most representative of the Nuragic civilisation of the Trexenta.

07466f961edf2433.text: At the foot of the nuraghe, beneath a rocky outcrop, there is a cave used as a water cistern. The cave entrance has been narrowed by the construction of masonry structures, built by superimposing trachyte boulders of various shapes and sizes, which thus increased the capacity of the water cistern. Its interior is full of stones and mud.

07475599e06b992e.text: Ruined and buried complex nuraghe whose structure cannot be defined

075b5f9436d8c5c4.text: Collapsed single-tower nuraghe. Some people mistakenly call the nearby Molafà nuraghe "Piandanna".

075bb741efa64013.text: The near-total absence of building stones has left just enough to understand the nuraghe's ground plan. There is practically an X-ray of the layout: it is as if someone had razed it to the ground, for a massive entrance with its lintel still in situ is detectable, and another, megalithic lintel lying on the ground. The basal circle is composed of ordered stones with a corridor and orthogonal cells. Formidable for specialist study.

0760512fd139a736.text: The megalithic wall is pre-Nuragic. It has a covered entrance with lintels on the south side. It ends at the bed of the stream to the west and, following an arcing course, at the eponymous proto-nuraghe on the north side.

0760f97bb47fdc52.text: Partly ruined nuraghe with intact tholos

076275318240b8c8.text: A collective burial of the Nuragic period. The monument lies next to a farm track that may have caused its damage; it is covered by vegetation, but its corridor and wall structure of courses of roughly squared granite stones can still be seen.

07b19a36cc3335ce.text: Submerged Nuragic village reported by Pierluigi Montalbano in public lectures

07c1d8569543696a.text: Domus de janas well-chamber at the entrance to the park on the south side

07e5f7bb74e92144.text:
The hypogeum lies about 750 metres south-west of the Nuraghe s'Infurcadu, while some fifty metres to the north-west there are two menhirs and traces of ancient occupation that have unfortunately been swept away by uncontrolled stone-clearing work.

The domus de janas, cut into a bank of basalt rock, consists of a short vestibule leading into a cell with a niche.

07ff3fc77d206c78.text:
Il Corvos, apparently a single-tower nuraghe, is in fact a complex nuraghe whose central two-coloured tower still survives in excellent condition, with the first level in limestone and the second in trachyte.

Once through the entrance threshold, the unusual anticlockwise staircase is immediately noticeable, starting on the left side of the corridor; the chamber, which has three niches and is largely buried, preserves its intact tholos, about 5 metres high. The upper floor, however, has collapsed.

0807994981b2dd9f.text: The necropolis consists of three domus de janas, among which Tomb I stands out for its size and decorations.

08115f711fb6013e.text: Megalithic circle on Monte Ladu. It lies near a small allée couverte.

08305cf0388399da.text: Single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, built of large worked limestone blocks preserved for six or seven courses (height 3.50 m). It has an entrance to the east and a long corridor opening on the left and right into two chambers in the wall.

08347f327fdd64c5.text: The site is hard to locate because of the Mediterranean scrub. On the slope along the road there is a substantial scatter of pottery, probably Roman. Traces of collapse are visible around the nuraghe.

086d37a1474bc614.text:
It is a proto-nuraghe in a dominant position on the edge of Pranu e Muru, the basalt lava flow in the territory of Nurri, east of the Flumendosa river. From the red crown one commands the Santa Vittoria mountains as far as the Gennargentu and, below, the canyon in which the roughly 17 kilometres of the Medio Flumendosa lake have been formed.

The corridor nuraghe joins its austere bareness to the majesty of the landscape that can be admired from there in a full 360 degrees.

08ad114f8392c67a.text: Single-tower nuraghe. The corridor leading to the circular chamber, which lacks a vault, has on the left a staircase about 1 metre wide.

08cf87675554882b.text: A natural cavity adapted as a domus de janas that hosted the games of several generations of children from the village of Uri, now left to itself as times have changed. It is entered from above by a fairly dangerous "manoeuvre", about 6/7 metres above the ground.

08da93a8deb20899.text: The name comes from the place name Monte Atarzu. In the Chiaramonti dialect of Sardinian we say de sa pedra atarzina, of which the mountain is very rich. The name could not be more appropriate, because several flint-working sites have been identified for making tools for everyday use or for hunting, such as knives and arrowheads. There are a few large megaliths hidden by a big thicket of mastic.

08e6f9420cec0bfa.text: On the slopes of Monte Santo three separate boulders hold ancient Neolithic tombs along an uphill path. Three erratic boulders in which the tombs were cut. In the first boulder encountered on the way to the summit, Su Crastu de Santu Eliseu, which gives the site its name, the domus de janas has been reused as a Christian place of worship. Next comes Su Crastu de Santu Elia and finally Su Crastu de Santu Enoch, which has a domus de janas with two fine bull's-head protomes.

0927a2fdfe6f1aca.text: Single-tower nuraghe in good condition, partly covered by vegetation. In the field, a scatter of Roman pottery.

094df33a93748ff2.text:
The domus de janas of Silattari (Bosa – OR) are cut into the limestone slope that faces south towards the Modolo valley.

They are two hypogea with closely spaced entrances: one consists of 12 chambers and the second of two cells. Probable location

0959ba4cbdb1e13c.text: Around the nuraghe lies an extensive Nuragic village; most of the huts are now reduced to heaps of rubble, but large enclosures remain with walls higher than usual that in places look like ramparts, so it was probably a fortified settlement.

0959efa3be73cdb1.text: Complex nuraghe, with a frontal addition, surrounded by a village

The nuraghe has yielded an extraordinary Nuragic altar. Three construction phases can be identified.

The first, perhaps of Middle Bronze Age I (16th–15th century BC), saw the laying out of a bastion and an outer wall with corridors and cells.

In the second, of Middle Bronze Age II (14th century BC), a sinusoidal trilobed bastion was superimposed, together with a new outer wall of four towers linked by irregularly straight curtain walls.

In the third phase the outer wall was provided with another tower and curtain walls.

0a6d014814e6e9f3.text: The nuraghe lies inside the Fertilia Military Airport, in an area skirted by one of the internal connecting roads. 128d68f21c7d270e.text: The Nuraghe Codas is a single-tower nuraghe built of basalt blocks, situated about 7 km south of Paulilatino. Together with the Nuraghi Forreddos, De Mesu and Su Guzzu it forms a quadrilateral between the territories of Zerfaliu and Paulilatino. Despite several collapses it has kept its majesty intact.

12a667dfd59cc79e.text: Domus de janas enriched with several bull's-head protomes carved in limestone

1301ff876f81b113.text: Collapsed nuraghe of which only a few courses remain

130817fa9e3cf015.text: Single-tower nuraghe in ruins with a collapsed tholos, accessible inside

131193dc597df707.text: Nuragic village with remains of Roman-period dwellings that were largely destroyed by the municipality during eucalyptus reforestation.

131dcbc721a74dc3.text:
A single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. Several courses are still visible in elevation, and the entrance, facing south, can be seen with its monolithic lintel still in situ.

The interior of the chamber is filled with collapse debris from the structure itself. Blocks from the collapse are found around the standing remains, mainly to the north, west and south.

13308d41469ec027.text: It is the only one in the whole territory that is inaccessible because of environmental incompatibility: the total disappearance of the monument is presumed. mu

1373d0b90cb65231.text:
The nuraghe is known by several names: Nido dei Passeri – l'Egua – Spiaggia Grande. It is a single-tower nuraghe in a mediocre state of preservation.

The nuraghe that stands on the cliff at the locality Nido dei Passeri is a single-tower nuraghe built of trachyte stone.

1387de6a3fbeb585.text:
This nuraghe has a trilobate plan, that is, it consists of three towers, a central one and two lateral ones that are half destroyed.

In the central tower we find the main chamber, a circular room in which the wall, narrowing as it rises, forms a true vault ending in an opening that was probably closed in the past by two smaller stones. Near the entrance, on the left-hand side, a spiral staircase with rough steps begins.

138bc494fb3d3809.text: A multi-lobed nuraghe of very complex structure. A central tower against which at least four towers lean, linked by a curtain wall that encloses a large courtyard.

13d54441cb7ea593.text: Situated on top of the hill called Montes. It commands a broad view of the landscape.

13da45e2688a857d.text: Single-tower nuraghe with a chamber flanked by at least one niche, built of trachyte.

13fbc668bd7a31e6.text:
It preserves an intact tholos.

Single-tower basalt nuraghe about 10.80 m high; from the entrance, 1.60 m high, you enter the corridor and immediately on the left the stair with 13 steps.

13fee44c222c3688.text: Pre-Nuragic and Nuragic village of which very few traces remain, already disappeared by the end of the Bronze Age

140884f3c8322e20.text: The archaeological site of Mont'e Prama, where the statues, baetyls and the linear necropolis of pit graves were found.

141b02027bc3ee70.text: Single-tower nuraghe. Destroyed by a bulldozer to build a restaurant in the 1980s–85. A pot and a bronze dagger were found during the excavation. Built in the Recent Bronze Age (1300–1150 BC).

1424e5e0cd1bda6f.text: It comprises the remains of a nuraghe and a village, the whole "correctly" transformed into dry-stone walls.

1438ab1cbf8ece0f.text:
The nuraghe is in very poor condition (no more than two surviving courses) and is completely covered by vegetation.

Around it there is a vast scatter of pottery, bricks and roof tiles.

144653848b72b120.text:
It lies within the municipal territory of Donori.

Archaeological features of protohistoric and historic date; the archaeological area is partly damaged, with overlapping cultural phases presumably attributable to the Nuragic, Punic and Roman periods. There is a large quantity of cyclopean boulders entirely of grey granite, indicating the presence of the village and the cemetery.

1449d252751882a2.text:
Archaic nuraghe, corridor type. The building stands on a solid rocky base controlling the southern bank of the Rio Cispiri. The nuraghe is built of polygonal blocks of local basalt which, in the basal courses, are of considerable size.

In visual contact with various nuraghi such as Zenna Uda, Muschiu, and Serra Crastula.

147654e5cbabbf9b.text: Complex nuraghe of the lateral-addition type. Built of local basalt. The vault is partly collapsed and was recently altered in connection with its last use as a livestock shelter.

14aa4ff88c34e7ee.text:
Traces of a nuraghe and a Nuragic village, with finds from the Roman period as well.

The monument stands on a granite crag overlooking a large wooded area, about 1220 metres north-east of the village of Lei. Around the Nuragic building, especially to the east, the remains of a village can be made out and the ground is scattered with pottery of various periods. A short distance away, traces of Roman buildings were found in 1867.

14c7ee5e56513192.text: A single-tower nuraghe with its top missing, built of limestone blocks, whose perimeter is broken on the south side by the collapse of the outer wall face. The interior of the chamber is not visible because it is hidden by vegetation and filled with earth and debris.

14ce2eef3059f187.text: Structures belonging to an archaic-type nuraghe, a corridor nuraghe. The building is made of large polygonal blocks of local basalt. The plan is vaguely quadrangular, although the monument cannot be read accurately because it is completely overgrown with vegetation.

14ebae0bd791f06f.text: A Nuragic temple in the territory of Nulvi, almost completely collapsed. At the apex a worked lintel remains that surmounted a doorway, reached by a spiral staircase inaccessible from the inside; the last steps and the covering slabs in a single block survive. From the remains the pediment appears to have been similar to that of giants' tombs. Around it are various remains of nuraghi, a village, and the enclosure wall that ran around the apex of the promontory.

14ec08367915c178.text: Connected with the Grotta di sa Ucca de su Tintirriolu. It opens through a tiny gap among stones and then earth (hard to find), followed by a deep, dangerous shaft 28 m deep. Exploration is NOT RECOMMENDED! even for experienced cavers, because the shaft does not open into solid rock.

152e98f59bdd1bc6.text: A bronze "antenna" sword found at Ploaghe near the nuraghe "Attentu" (in 1874 the nuraghe was studied by the archaeologist Giovanni Spano, a native of Ploaghe, who carried out the first stratigraphic excavation in Sardinia there)

155c28e6bdb1ba9e.text: A nuraghe that has almost completely disappeared, mentioned by Prof. S. Ghiani in “La Trexenta Antica”. At the foot of the hill there is a large rock with artificial cavities.

155fec9a146e403b.text:
The Piscina Caboni archaeological complex belongs to the Circles Culture of the Arzachena territory, which until a few years ago seemed to be confined to the Gallura region.

In the absence of excavation data, the site's occupation can be placed from the 3rd millennium BC.

15638b94ad0fd8fe.text: The monolith, of well-worked basalt, stands on flat ground less than 100 m from a domus de janas called "Su forru'e su Taleri".

1567acaee8476bb6.text: This is the second nuraghe named Peppe Gallu in the territory of Uri, after Peppe Gallu di Cuga. The associated village, which was very extensive, has been destroyed by agricultural mechanisation. It is a proto-nuraghe with a circular corridor. It has two raised entrances, above the level of the surrounding ground, which could be reached by wooden or rope ladders.

15796582236069c9.text:
Situated 500 m from the village along the road to Sarule, the circular-plan nuraghe was probably a single-tower type.

Today only the basal course of squared trachyte blocks is visible, and to the north a stretch of the second course.

1582054cbe6e5f37.text: Only a mound of earth remains of the tower, from which the courses of the nuraghe emerge; it was probably a complex nuraghe.

158d8620d8be85d7.text: A central tower surrounded by a wall emerges for up to four courses, to a height of over 2 metres. The whole is in turn linked to circular and straight walls that emerge from the ground but only for the upper base of the ashlars of the top course. Most of the nuragic complex is buried under earth. About 7–8 metres to the north-east of the tower there may be a sacred well.

15925617c6acf71d.text: Domus de janas with the peculiarity of a double doorway on two opposite sides, broken through the vault.

15963b1acd066da4.text: Less than 100 metres south of the nuraghe lies a small giants' tomb, of which the burial chamber in large granite orthostatic blocks survives, together with traces of the outer wall face and the peristalith.

159b50c8e110c642.text: "Nuraghe Su Nuragheddu, or de Sa Taula, or de Su Coddu 'e Su Nuraghe. It stands near the Rio di Posada, in a narrow gorge between cliffs, guarding a pass; it is destroyed, but clear traces of the nuraghe remain. On land belonging to Deiana Serafino."

15b2193e3b8ee4ee.text: Situated near the municipal pinewood, four kilometres north of the village, the nuraghe Jana is in a poor state of preservation. Not only has the nuraghe collapsed internally, but it was also used in the past as a shepherds' shelter, so that many of its stones have been laid out radially as a boundary wall.

15d7eb3a586e447e.text: Domus de janas with a façade and additions on the stele

15dd7172bdd0222a.text: The main nucleus of the Pidighi archaeological complex lies inside the Municipal Park of the same name; it consists of two nuraghi (Pidighi and Muru Accas) with their respective settlements and their respective water sources...

15e0ace0e6025880.text: A burial of the Nuragic period. The monument, of small size, is identifiable only by the funerary corridor, while the other parts that composed it are not visible (still buried or destroyed).

1656c492a5a6f0a9.text:
Complex nuraghe built of the local volcanic rock. Largely covered by vegetation and hidden by collapse, stretches of walling from the towers that made up the building can be made out. One part has been disturbed by illicit excavations.

At the foot of the hill, to the north, a hypogeum, perhaps an air-raid shelter.

It is likely that on the summit of the hill, in the private land enclosed by fences and inaccessible, traces of the protohistoric cluster of huts may survive.

165ffcb67754b2f7.text: A fully exposed dolmenic giants' tomb, of which the trapezoidal stele and part of the original exedra remain.

166d4d3777dddd7b.text: Nuraghe from the final phase of the Nuragic period, built on the cliff overlooking the valley of the San Pietro Paradiso waterfall, or as the locals call it, "Cascata de s'ascedu".

168cb2285c1212d3.text: Giants' tomb of which the basal ashlars, one ashlar of the stele and one of the apse remain.

16a831d9b0dadcb7.text: The tomb is almost buried under a substantial mound of earth and stones. The basal orthostats follow almost the entire perimeter: a semi-circular exedra (arc 10.40 m – chord 3.80 m) flattened on the south-east side with arms surviving for 6.66 m on the right and 4.45 m on the left; a rectangular body 10.60 m long and 4.20 m wide where it meets the exedra wings; a burial corridor (length 7.20 m – width 1.10 m) bounded by upright slabs.

16ac0b0107236255.text: The tomb, still buried, clearly shows the violations it suffered at the hands of looters. The chamber is rectangular, built of boulders of various sizes, only roughly dressed, laid dry with packing wedges. The entrance, facing ESE, has its doorway completely buried, topped by a lintel shaped like a rectangular block whose sides appear perfectly smoothed. The tomb was preceded by an exedra, of which some boulders remain in situ to the north of the tomb body.

16db2a0af53a8dc3.text: Deruta giants' tomb. It lies in the immediate vicinity, 50 m, of another giants' tomb in better condition on which the Municipality has carried out minor cleaning and accessibility works.

16eea19268438a6c.text: Nuraghe with a buried entrance. Access to the interior is via a passage leading to the stairwell. The chamber has three niches with the tholos intact. Several baetyls and cinerary urns are also found in the area.

16fb7e2399a28261.text: Only a few traces remain of two towers added tangentially.

170717e38444da92.text: Composed of ten parallelepiped-shaped megaliths placed side by side (an eleventh is found in the centre), thus forming a semicircle about 10 metres across. Some pottery fragments found on the site are attributable to the Monte Claro Culture period, therefore the Eneolithic.

1727440595a86384.text:
The Sas Arzolas de Goi necropolis dates to the Ozieri Culture period (3200–2800 BC).

Five domus de janas have been identified so far; they lie on the slope of a trachyte hill that has been extensively affected by quarrying.

Tomb 1 is particularly interesting because it displays two complete bull's-head protomes, with ears and head, carved above the entrance hatch and on the pillar inside the burial chamber. The horns at the entrance are carved in convex relief.

173cd08f5426e4de.text:
There are two hypogea at the site: the first tomb is the more interesting because it shows a series of incisions above the entrance hatch; the second lies a little further on, near the edge of the road, and its interior is almost completely flooded.

Both burials are pit graves and would date to about 3000 BC.

1744f42a69491cea.text: The archaeological site stands a few dozen metres from the Christian-medieval one, set among centuries-old olive trees. It is divided into two areas: in the first you will find a sacred well temple, dating to the Final Bronze Age (12th century BC), embraced by a sacred enclosure (themenos) shaped like a keyhole. Built of finely worked basalt ashlars with precise techniques, the temple is a jewel of perfect geometric forms.

178d45ac31aaa436.text: A group of domus de janas immediately below the road embankment. It is thought that other domus de janas may lie either beneath it or were destroyed during the road construction.

179685665d4843c5.text: During construction a spring was found beneath the site, which keeps the domus full of water even in times of drought. For this reason it became a temple dedicated to fertility, so much so that the female reproductive organ was carved into the rock around the entrance of the domus and, above it, the male reproductive organ. These are joined by a small channel cut in the rock, signifying fertilisation.

17b4c09023bd3817.text: From the aerial photograph it looks like a complex nuraghe with a village.

181db1e077030ae0.text:
Also known as Su Lotto. In ruins, a few boulders of the primary circle remain that define the base.

Nuraghe della Sorgente della Pietra. The name probably derives from the fact that the site, used for centuries as a quarry, so that the nuraghe has now almost completely disappeared, is characterised by the presence of surface springs.

182050e17514ed77.text: The imposing single-tower nuraghe Sa Fraigada stands a few dozen metres from the summit of Monte Cresia and is the largest in the area. The ancient Nuragic building has suffered major collapses, making its ground plan hard to understand; the lintelled entrance, presumably on the east side, is not visible. The circular tower is about 8 metres in diameter and can still be seen to a surviving height of 3.70 metres on its south-western side.

18280f73747d52cf.text: The nuraghe lies within the territory of Villaputzu. It appears as a sub-circular building of which only a few structures are visible, owing to demolition carried out to obtain wall ashlars for the construction of the adjacent church. On the northern side a semicircular building is annexed.

1859d46b049d82fe.text: Probable location. Today only the basic megalithic structures of the nuraghe remain, and it is quite conceivable that most of the stones that once stood above them ended up, duly broken up, in the walls of the Villa La Favorita.

185db7d77cd3c013.text: Ruins on a rocky outcrop overlooking the valley below.

186e88c9cd794522.text: It lies within the municipality of Nuoro. It is not the only Nuragic site in the town, but it is the only one to have been systematically excavated. Around the nuraghe the remains of a village dating to about 1600 BC (the early Nuragic period) are visible; it originally consisted of more than 200 huts. Historical sources also report the presence of several domus de janas along the hill.

187f8e3d6991adaf.text: Megalithic astronomical clock, built in the early Nuragic period, before the 15th–18th century BC. It is circular and built of large boulders with open spaces to let sunlight pass onto a central boulder covered with white pebbles that favoured the reflection of the sun's rays at different times — equinoxes, solstices — and in the lunar phases it reflected moonlight in specific directions.

188b3c68aebe7d2b.text: Locally also known by the place name of the land "serra porcheddos". It would appear to be a single-tower nuraghe, even though the whole surrounding area shows a high probability of survey evidence. — Tripod Nuraghe. For other nuraghi whose names refer to objects of use or connected with worship, compare Nuraghe Trìbides, Cogàlzos, Manos d'òro.mu

1896c13293c257e9.text: Nuraghe Maistu Peldu (commonly called De Su Par e Pelda) still has two small towers standing, each 2 metres high. The collapsed vault reveals the interior of the tholos, about 1 m deep. The ashlars, which are fairly large, suggest that the site may be a watchtower nuraghe controlling the entrance to the Chia valley. In front of it stands a menhir, the "praying menhir", De Su Par 'e Pelda, visible from provincial road 72.

189877885177222d.text: A single-tower nuraghe built on a spur of granite rock, following its contours and in places incorporating it. The interior of the nuraghe is filled with backfill earth and large blocks that belonged to the masonry. The nuraghe stands in a commanding position on the coast with a broad view over Tavolara and Capo Ceraso. It is a watchtower of which five courses of stone survive on the outside and about two metres of masonry inside.

189af447aee1de03.text: Cave frequented from the earliest phases of the Nuragic civilisation, known for the discovery of three, older, "Mother Goddess" figurines in bone.

18a1514d22f4e619.text:
The nuraghe stands on the summit of a high watershed whose north and east slopes are very steep, while to the west, a few metres from the nuraghe, the hill ends in a high cliff.

It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, 10.30 m in diameter. Very little of the nuraghe survives because of the substantial collapses it has suffered over the centuries.

Further reading:

Bibliography: E.E.M. 1922, p. 104; MERELLA 1996-97, vol. V, pp. 770-773, fig. 37, pl. XXIII.

18ae647dad975c9f.text: It is buried on a hillock, in Sardinian cucuru. The upper part, certainly the top of the main tower, can be visited. We see concentric courses of large stones. At the top there are small openings which, if excavated, would lead inside the structure.

18c1ff4ccd6e451e.text: A typical domus de janas with a façade, with an arched stele carved on the limestone wall.

18c82d393866d2c9.text:
Remains of a nuraghe and traces of a Nuragic village.

Built on a granite rise, this nuraghe is not currently recognisable among the remains of an extensive village that lasted into the Roman and early medieval periods, as attested by fragments of pottery, roof tiles and jars.

18efb1b53c2c0729.text: On the remains of the nuraghe Crixionis a fortified concrete position protected against small-calibre fire, i.e. an observation post serving the coastal defence batteries of the sector, was built during the Second World War.

190942347351f410.text: A probable ruined nuraghe lies nearby, to the north-east, where a megalithic wall is present.

190ba7503fefe9bd.text: A massive single-tower nuraghe, of imposing diameter, built with large, roughly worked granite blocks. The entrance faces south and is three-quarters covered. The tholos is almost intact. Inside there are as many as three niches, cut into the wall thickness. Moreover, a spiral staircase starts from the wall to the left of the entrance corridor and certainly led to the upper floor, but is unfortunately blocked by collapse; opposite the stairwell there is a further niche.

19115f523fe78db8.text: On the north-western tip a few alignments of small blocks can be made out, suggesting the remains of a nuraghe tower; on the south-eastern tip a short stretch of curvilinear walling; in the hollow to the north a closing wall between the two tips.

193426b6f3fa9108.text: A sanctuary area consisting of several rooms surrounded by an irregularly elliptical enclosure. One of these buildings has a perfectly circular plan with a floor paved with limestone slabs fitted together with absolute precision. The accuracy of the construction and the existence of an original design plan are shown by the traces of the circular layout mark of the first course on the floor, drawn with a kind of compass.

194a3d243291fe0f.text: The Mereu nuraghe, also called 'Intro de Padente', built entirely of white limestone with well-squared medium-sized stones, stands on a rise overlooking the surrounding territory. It is a complex nuraghe, consisting of a central tower and two secondary towers further protected by straight bastions.

194d67ac48c98e6c.text: Partially ruined nuraghe with open tholos

1965b599887e4d98.text: A careful survey found no trace of the nuraghe Lavrone, although some old people said it must have been there. The site has certainly been modified by humans, as shown by the presence of some man-made objects. The curious anecdote is that Uncle Giacomino, who is no longer with us, built more than "one nuraghe", meaning the heaps of stones gathered when clearing the fields. "Nuraghe dell'alloro grande". mu

199cda66bfdefda6.text: Reported nuraghe whose type cannot be determined

19a3f0a5ed526e0f.text: Four domus de janas, side by side, cut into the sandstone. The first one consists of a single chamber, the others of several chambers. The first domu is not connected to the others; the others are interconnected.

19a5759802ccc927.text: Probable proto-nuraghe of which four very irregular courses survive

19c27b7195fce363.text: Small menhir placed along the road opposite the turn-off for Rocca Doria

19c4e66d692cc1c7.text:
The complex consists of a nuraghe with a settlement, a giants' tomb, and a spring.

The nuraghe, built on a rock outcrop, belongs to the complex type: it comprises a main tower to which three secondary towers have been added in a frontal-lateral arrangement.

19cdb225b68d6b37.text: Cave currently blocked by a collapse that prevents entry. Inside, some ceramic fragments attributable to the Bonu Ighinu culture have been found.

19dbfd8bf73de758.text: A single-tower nuraghe built of large blocks of white limestone, it occupies a space cut out within an olive grove, while to the north-west it looks out over a sheer drop to the Canale Orune. Three courses survive, with a maximum height of about 3 metres.

19e026c2fe8ef0fb.text: Single-tower nuraghe with its tholos intact

19ee5af3eb52b9c4.text: A single-tower tholos nuraghe, built of large polygonal blocks of local basalt. It survives to a height of 4–5 courses and the inner chamber has collapsed in on itself, leaving it filled with collapse debris. The diameter is about 12 m. The entrance faces south-east, although it is hidden by the structures of a later hut built against it.

19f0486bd21739e2.text:
The visitable part consists of numerous chambers adorned with concretions, stalactites and stalagmites (the tallest measures 11 metres), columns rising up to 15 m, aragonite crystals and underground lakes.

Inside, the remains of several oil votive lamps of Nuragic origin and artefacts of Phoenician and Roman date have in fact been found.

1a182ce9b31b0d48.text: The nuraghe Ola is a single-tower nuraghe about 12 m in external diameter and 10 m high, dating to the Recent Bronze Age. What is particularly striking is the use of different building materials: on the outside the base consists of 12 courses of granite blocks, while above them sit 13 courses of trachyte.

1a3d4c8101454dae.text: A collective burial of the Nuragic period. The monument has recently been brought to light after the vegetation covering it was cleared. Besides the coursed-stone corridor, the lower part of the large stele also survives.

1a5d5732c79156b6.text: According to the map in the publication "L'Altare preistorico di Monte d'Accoddi" by Ercole Contu, the correct name of the nuraghe should be "Camusina", which moreover appears on the IGM map as "Camuscina". It is in very poor condition and completely covered by dense vegetation.

1a7003dce6225389.text: A series of natural caves used in the Neolithic for collective burials. Finds of the Monte Claro Culture.

1a73323809d16c07.text: Completely dismantled. Probably partly still existing under the vegetation, which shows stones lying in no order.

1a7ce61396ce08f8.text: It is an artificial cave cut into the tufa and altered over the centuries, most likely from a domus de janas into a building for the grape harvest or a store for agricultural produce or a shelter for tools. There are many clues pointing to such a sequence.

1a9d186422cc9b31.text:
Even though it is reduced to a major ruin, the importance of this feature can be grasped; it belongs to the group of nuraghi with an underground chamber, still accessible.

Literally "nuraghe of the cows' urine". See Pìsciu 'àccas.

Cf. MAURO MAXIA, I nomi di luogo dell'Anglona e della Bassa valle del Coghinas, ed. Il Torchietto, Ozieri 1994, pp. 73-74 for the entry "Anglona".

1ab05918631277c8.text: Collapsed nuraghe in which it is possible to enter the fallen tholos

1abb2d8959283740.text: The interpretation of these buildings is that during festivals the Nuragic people (and not only them?) traded all kinds of goods, taking advantage of the large influx of people. Besides the "stands" there are two circular meeting huts and a livestock enclosure.

1adefc98184c9bfa.text: Six domus de janas at the locality Sas Concheddas de Pianu Edras, cut into a rocky outcrop, this time of trachyte tuff, are the six Domus de Janas of the Prehistoric Hypogean Necropolis of Pianu Edras, among which the Domus delle Cappelle is worth noting.

1af8fb46c3364bef.text: The nuraghe takes its name from the locality on the south-eastern slopes of the Giara di Gesturi. It is mentioned by Taramelli in his study of the prehistoric monuments of the Giara; however, the survey carried out in the 1980s no longer recorded any trace of it.

1b06e27d1ccc01bf.text: The complex system of structures comprising springs and water-collection structures, with ingenious channels and a rectangular building in isodomic masonry.

1b0871d1fe0bfca0.text: It is the largest and most important cave of Bonu Ighinu. It has recently been connected with the overlying Grotta del Pozzaccio. Morphologically the cavity can be divided into two main parts: the fossil branch, which is the initial one, and the active branch, crossed along its entire length by a stream; the large hall in the innermost part is also fossil. Overall the cave is 740 m long and its spatial development is 1500 m.

1b204e1b9b9e5b8b.text: Small rock-cut tombs with pre-Nuragic burials.

1b2b53f96f5f4554.text: Near the village of San Salvatore, on private property, the nuraghe is in very poor condition, but the remains of a substantial Nuragic settlement are clearly visible.

1b2f99fd4882b019.text: One of the nuraghi in the municipal territory of Villa Sant'Antonio is the nuraghe of 'Genna sa Pira', datable to the full Middle Bronze Age (1500–1200 BC), although its construction saw numerous later additions over the centuries.

1b611ff15d0b31fc.text:
Nuraghi that have disappeared completely or almost completely over time; this is one of them, and it lies near Morimenta, not far from the nuraghe Santu Sciori of Pabillonis.

Other archives mention the ruins of a little church, but there is very little of a church to be seen.

1b9ce89bd8ab176e.text: Multi-lobed nuraghe, consisting of a main tower plus three smaller towers. The diameter is about 11 metres. The central tower is built of large boulders, while the front addition uses smaller stones.

1bb1f6564fbf0f8b.text: Declared assets of cultural interest on 31/05/2018.

1bc2e0965747f77d.text:
On the hill of San Giovanni a Punic fortified complex has been identified on the remains of a pre-existing Nuragic village.

Opposite are the Domus de Janas of Burdaga.

In Giuseppa Tanda's recent publication it is stated that, among the various types of Domus de Janas, there is one characterised by the fact that the necropolis is carved into pre-existing rock shelters, perhaps enlarged by artificial excavation, almost as if the overhang could provide shelter for the sacred remains of the dead.

1be4ec75757a1d61.text: The nuraghe is completely hidden by earth and vegetation, which give it the appearance of a modest hillock (in Sardinian “cuccuru”) several metres high rising above the waters of the State saltworks; the material conceals the millennia-old structure.

1c366008c7eda9e9.text:
It is a medium-sized single-tower nuraghe. The building style is the one typical of the sites in the area.

It stands on a small rise a short distance from the Pardu river and commanded a good view over the lower part of the valley formed by the same river.

The site is not in very good condition. The entrance side is intact, but the interior has almost completely collapsed. Only the corridor and the internal staircase can be made out. The vegetation is dense, making the site difficult to visit.

It consists of small and medium-sized polygonal boulders. Vaguely ovoid in shape, its major radius is 33.00 metres. Sacred functions linked to initiation were performed here, and rites and events connected with the seasons and the years of men and women were propitiated.

1c5567e6a6969199.text: A ruined nuraghe on the so-called crown, of basalt, of the Giara di Gonnosnò/Genoni. Covered in vegetation, it is not easily accessible.

1c8cdb9c34843f68.text: It is an age-old wild olive tree, certainly the oldest in the territory of Chiaramonti. 1c8d9f7d14ddbb6a.text: It is a single cell cut inside a prominence of friable limestone. In the immediate vicinity considerable working is evident from the presence of other outcrops that were abandoned or on which the work was never finished.

1d0f0d9b5ff111fc.text: A ruined nuraghe of which only the two basal courses apparently survive. It is very likely that an entire village once stood around it, given its commanding position and the remains that can be glimpsed.

1d1de5fdc4749321.text: Along the road to Erula, the Nuraghe Majore rises on a height, protected by walls and on the north-east side by a sheer drop. A single-tower nuraghe, still in excellent condition, its tholos is almost intact.

1d410e98e6c95333.text: The simple nuraghe was transformed into the "a tancato" type. 1d61ea20a3e38d2b.text:
The fortress was built by the Carthaginians, making use of a pre-existing Nuragic building; behind the wall traces of buildings can be seen that were probably Nuragic at first and later occupied by the Carthaginians.

1d82de58f1344153.text:
The monument is now known as Nuraghe Urpes, but it is actually Nuraghe Bighinzone, while Nuraghe Urpes, which stood nearby, has been completely destroyed.

The nuraghe looks at first sight like a single-tower nuraghe, but a closer analysis of the structures shows it to be a four-lobed nuraghe with curtain walls of concave-convex profile, itself enclosed by an outer wall with towers of which a few significant traces still remain.

1d981ee59d8b7084.text: The nuraghe has been completely destroyed. The area is described as a Nuragic settlement covering a vast area.

1d9905f7e1211aba.text: A few hundred metres from the nuraghe Paddaggiu lies the nuraghe Li Colti. It may be a four-lobed nuraghe. The central tower survives to a height of 6 m, while the bastion appears as high mounds of rubble and only one tower is discernible.

1dad53168a5125f6.text: Single-tower nuraghe, of which only a few traces remain

1de10bc29f359baf.text: Complex nuraghe of which a circular chamber in a central position survives. It may be the central tower, of which the entire perimeter outline survives, though only for a single course. The inner wall face of the central tower is visible on the sides oriented from north to south-east. The tower abuts the edge of a rocky ridge, with a sheer drop to the north. A built structure is abutted against the original tower, of which the points of contact oriented to the west and north-west survive.

1de393d29aaaf10f.text: Single tower of irregular shape in basalt and porphyry

1e15f1b165ef7d99.text: The single-tower nuraghe, in a fair-to-poor state of preservation (six courses above ground), stands on top of a promontory overlooking a rocky ridge, built against the bedrock.

1e1cd1a5f0b1b0ea.text: The Luzzanas domus de janas lie near the river and can only be entered from above through a shaft entrance. Once you have gone down you find yourself in a chamber with two hatches leading to two tombs, one of which consists of an antechamber plus three cells, only two of which are accessible. In this domus there is a very unusual carving depicting a labyrinth, but it may have been made in the Roman period.

1e3bf415ff6dac70.text: Both burials have their entrances oriented to the south-west. Inside the first domus, about 5 x 3 m, the remains of two columns that once adorned the chamber are still visible in both the ceiling and the floor. The second tomb, similar to the first, has an antechamber with two raised steps on either side, and the rectangular burial chamber contains two raised lateral benches.

1e4356c5f606b318.text: The monument lies at 191 metres above sea level in the locality of Fidrigu. The nuraghe is completely destroyed; the few remaining boulders are scattered and it is impossible to reconstruct the original structure. The situation was made worse by the work carried out to install an Enel pylon. As stated above, the nuraghe was abandoned and consequently completely destroyed, and now not even all the boulders that made up the nuraghe remain. The site is on private property.

1e44b440363aeaeb.text: The little that remains of the nuraghe Li Espi near the Liscia dam

1e65d8ff68447121.text: Three courses of roughly dressed limestone blocks survive. The stair opening and perhaps the chamber roof are visible on the summit. The south-east side of the entrance has collapsed. Military structures lean against the north and north-east sides. Partly enveloped in Mediterranean scrub, the nuraghe is in a good state of preservation. It is a single-tower nuraghe, originally accompanied by a village. Structures currently reused are also reported in the immediate vicinity.

1e820bb5199f5dfb.text: Single-tower nuraghe, standing on a sheer ridge along which it has collapsed, inaccessible but with a base at least 12 m in diameter. Around it are the remains of a megalithic wall built to defend the site.

1e88aaf2d1c6d775.text: Ruins of the Su Oi nuraghe. Only the basal course remains.

1ea0cea26a23d315.text:
At the head of a dominant ridge overlooking the beds of two watercourses that fed the pond behind the harbour, before it was transformed by the present buildings.

Remains of Nuragic towers beside the abandoned house.

There were probably two towers, contiguous, one of them built on a granite outcrop, exactly like all the other Nuragic towers of Santa Teresa. The perimeter of the tholos is clear, collapsed inwards and filled with ashlars for at least three metres in height.

1eac49d33bfa50d5.text: Group of four single-chambered domus de janas with a façade

The inner chamber has collapsed in its upper part and the collapse debris fills the rest. The entrance cannot be identified.

1eb5e0dfb52228a0.text:
The stronghold was built in a strategic position: from the top of the hill on which it stands one can see the Campidano plain, the Linas mountain range and several nuraghi in the territory of Pabillonis. Of considerable size (it covers an area of almost 4,000 square metres), it consists of four towers linked by a rhomboidal curtain wall.

1ece534efe1d9389.text: Nuraghe with remains of a village and a Roman settlement.

1edc87fb1ddcf73d.text: Reduced to an extreme state of ruin. Since the 1970s a fire lookout post of the Sardinian Forestry Corps has stood on it. 1ede6161833ddc24.text: Complex nuraghe with remains of a village; in 2016 it was surrounded by dense vegetation, making it impossible to visit.

The domu is partially collapsed, but the incised and low-relief decorations (with the double-horn motif) that adorn the walls are still appreciable. Traces of red paint are also present.

A few metres to the right another partially buried domus, equally dilapidated.

1efe76a32b452d61.text:

A badly ruined nuraghe; only a few courses of limestone ashlars remain at the base.

An old cart track used to pass nearby, branching off the Florinas–S. Maria di Sea municipal road, but its course has been almost completely erased by pastures.

1f43b533d236e590.text: The complex four-lobed nuraghe is reduced to a heap of large stones covered by thick vegetation; even so, its great bulk can still be perceived.

22e92eb3b6b8973e.text: Single-tower nuraghe, in basalt, with its tholos collapsed.

Until the 1950s and 1960s they were inhabited by whole family groups who carried out agro-pastoral activities.
