It is known for giving its name to an important culture of the Sardinian Chalcolithic, the Filigosa culture, which is closely linked to the Abealzu culture, so much so that the term Abealzu-Filigosa culture is often used. The necropolis consists of four multi-chambered domus de janas, cut into a tuff hillock and characterised by the presence of long entrance dromoi.

It was used from the 3rd millennium BC until the early centuries of the 2nd millennium BC;

2487810d71df2a9c.text: Single-chambered domus de janas near the Riu fruscu

248d1f1eb313a900.text: The nuraghe and the adjacent village lie behind the hill that holds the Nuragic sanctuary of Santa Vittoria di Serri.

248dc61e2bd8c4c2.text: Situated at 140 m above sea level, a Nuragic complex partially damaged by the construction of the Ussana–Donori provincial road. Barrali. The ground plans of the structures belonging to the Nuragic complex were to be brought to light in order to define their structural characteristics and assign a precise chronological date; although the owners granted permission, the excavation campaign was not carried out.

248eac800a0add05.text: The ruins of the megalithic structure were pointed out, during a survey at the nearby nuraghe Perdu Lodde, by a local shepherd.

2494ee1ef8eced3b.text: Nuragic hut of which the ground-level circle remains. It stands on the edge of the plateau above the hill, Monte Crastu, and from there overlooked the area of the probable village of Badde Cannalza.

2499c3e9ae452ae3.text: Dolmen with a stone slab resting on megalithic walls

249c013a6dd47b8c.text: Two-tower nuraghe, collapsed and inaccessible, facing north and dominating the whole north coast from Stintino to Isola Rossa.

249fb1e41dc75f3d.text: It is one of the many nuraghi scattered across the territory of Torralba; this one lies near the railway that runs from Mores to Torralba station. It is a complex nuraghe, consisting of a central tower with a frontal addition of two secondary towers linked by a solid wall face. It is dated to the period between the Middle and Final Bronze Age (1600–1000 BC).

24a645214bde9b19.text:
The Murruzzone or Thiortorro Nuraghe. It was not easy to spot because it is surrounded by brambles, but it lies almost on the valley floor near some springs. A surviving wall about 4 m long remains, and inside it a circular niche whose entrance faces east, accessible from the inside and measuring about 2 m.

Most of it is probably still buried.

24cbd0cec5c9e77c.text: Built of limestone and marl blocks, the nuraghe has a four-lobed ground plan, with a central tower and four outer towers oriented to the cardinal points... surrounded by an outer wall, and the remains of four more towers. A sacred well lies inside the complex.

24d7c8fb523cf0b4.text:
It is in very poor condition.

Probable location.

24f120d6f0394afa.text: Single-tower nuraghe with an elliptical plan. Several courses are visible. In the area there are large lumps of clay and other wall structures that suggest the existence of a settlement of huts.

25150e9d3687abc8.text:
Important giants' tomb near Sant'Antonio di Santadi.

It appears to be in apparently good condition.

The name is unknown to me, but it is certainly of great historical importance. Found by cross-referencing data from several maps.

2517546202e187a1.text: Complex nuraghe with a central tower and two lateral towers joined by straight walls, with a courtyard between them as a linking space. In the immediate vicinity the remains of a Bronze Age stone quarry can be seen.

2517f09500153dfb.text: A ruined nuraghe wrapped in prickly pears and vegetation. It preserves the fine entrance portal with its split and dangerous lintel, the tholos, and the stair to the upper floor.

252aca0711584de7.text: The monument, located near the Borore cemetery and a short distance from the Nuraghe Pischedda, is reduced to a few courses of the elevation, which nevertheless allow it to be identified as a complex nuraghe of the “a tancato” type, consisting of the central tower to the north-west, joined to a smaller opposing tower to the south-east by two straight wall wings that enclose a trapezoidal space; the whole is bounded by an outer wall. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

252db24617366b24.text: A ruined single-tower nuraghe; in the surrounding area the traces of a quarry and a settlement can be seen.

253f7dda11006ad1.text:
It lies in the municipality of Marrubiu (OR).

More precisely it is an archaic nuraghe, or corridor nuraghe, with an elliptical plan, with a large village of circular huts.

2540396e6e335f3e.text: The cave is about 130 metres long and consists essentially of three chambers. Important archaeological finds have been made inside, in particular some human remains dated to about 20,000 years ago, which constitute the earliest evidence of Homo sapiens in Sardinia. The famous Sardinian bandit Giovanni Corbeddu took refuge in this cave, from which it takes its name.

25686d0ae3c755a6.text: Area around which, besides the dolmen Su Crastu Covaccadu, the giants' tomb Sa Pedra Coveccada is also found, of which only the arched stele remains, broken at the base.

2598f934b6145747.text: While still a student, Giovanni Lilliu reported the presence of twenty circular and elliptical huts, some of which were later excavated, yielding ceramic materials of various kinds such as large jars, bowls, copper beads, and a bronze figurine depicting two oxen found during agricultural work. Despite the destruction, the emerging remains of some walls, large fragments of furnishings, and large fragments of basalt querns are still on the ground.

259b00e8cb14e998.text: Of the Olai nuraghe, in this heap of stones, only the foundation is now visible.

259e1180def35830.text: Only a few stretches of the first basal course of the corridor nuraghe, perhaps sub-elliptical in plan, survive, built of granite masonry.

25a8ba726df17693.text: The Coroneddu necropolis (Bosa – OR) consists of three hypogea, two of them side by side and a third set further apart. It opens on a rocky spur on the southern slope of a limestone hill that extends into the Modolo valley. Probable location

25c83b32612c8a67.text: It is a very interesting Nuragic building where the corner junction between the perimeter walls can be seen. Experts define it as a Greek megaron type.

25f1bd3df7758cf8.text: The domus de janas was cut into a rock outcrop situated halfway up the hill known as Serra Nuarxis. The tomb has a Greek-cross plan and consists of a rectangular vestibule, a quadrangular doorway leading to the actual chamber, and the chamber itself. The chamber, semi-circular in plan, contains three niches, slightly raised above the floor level, oriented to the south-west, north-west and south-east. The niches have arched walls and rectangular bases.

25f786cd919c5da1.text: Complex nuraghe with a central tower and two lateral towers linked by bastions enclosing a courtyard.

25fc3ba5c1ff99c4.text:
The nuraghe Paddaggiu, "pagliaio", lies less than one kilometre from "dall'elefante".

It appears to be a single-tower nuraghe but is in fact a complex nuraghe, consisting of a central tower and a bastion with two lateral towers that are barely legible. The peculiarity of this nuraghe is the presence of a chamber set above the entrance corridor, originally reached by a staircase inside the right-hand niche of the main chamber. The tholos and the staircase leading to the upper floor survive intact.

260516b3e7e18d52.text: Heaps of ashlars typical of an ancient settlement abandoned and covered by woodland, and various stretches of wall, mostly circular: on the south side there is a wall about 5 metres long, almost straight, and a small circular wall further down, while on the west side of the settlement we find a circular wall of large blocks in 2–3 courses, suggesting a Nuragic date.

26387c63c18f3852.text:
It consists of 18 domus de janas arranged in three groups about 200 m apart. The first group has five hypogea aligned on an east–west axis; the second group, south of the first cluster, has three aligned on a north–south axis; the third group, 250 m to the east, comprises ten small rock-cut chambers that are difficult to reach and interpret.

The burials are of the horizontal-projection type with entrances between east and south. A system of channels cut into the rock protected the tomb interiors.

2659310d391d0370.text: Small nuraghe reduced to a heap of rubble.

26c6fa6ed7924510.text: Little now remains of the Nuragic huts; there are only circular and square heaps of stone, probably the result of stone-clearing work.

26eea7bcc5fa288b.text: It stands on the road from Alghero to Uri. The tomb is badly damaged but still preserves inside the typical elements of the false door and the probable bull's-head protomes above it.

27038db9f7a4b601.text: It is elliptical in shape, extends for a length of about 30 metres, has a diameter of about 22 metres and survives to a height of about 4 metres. In the north-west sector of the curtain wall an entrance can be seen leading to an internal corridor that served as a link between the two main towers and was originally roofed with massive slabs laid flat.

2763b907711be301.text:
It consists of an apsidal corridor set on an exedra with a narrow bench. In the centre is a small lintelled doorway with jambs and a threshold. The roof is a pointed vault.

Excavations have uncovered the remains of numerous human skeletons, deposited one on top of another, evidence of its use as a collective burial, whose size is also the origin of the name. Tradition holds that these burials must have belonged to gigantic beings.

278f11302b473912.text: Single-tower nuraghe, built of local basalt blocks. The outer wall face survives to a maximum height of about 4 m. The entrance is identifiable to the south-east, from the remains of the entrance passage, with the stairwell opening on the left and a niche on the right, leading to the inner chamber. The latter survives to about half its original height and has a large internal niche facing south.

27b9df3b3b3e6818.text: The Nuraghe di Ozzilo lies in the territory of Aidomaggiore. It is a corridor nuraghe, entered from above because the interior is choked with rubble from the collapse. The chamber inside is filled with collapse debris that has affected part of the "navetiform" vault. Two giants' tombs lie a short distance away; one of them has unfortunately been partly destroyed.

27f70c0c2ece79af.text:
An interesting monument in the territory of Villanova Monteleone, oriented south-west; part of the exedra is still visible, but unfortunately no trace of the stele remains. The well-preserved corridor, built of well-squared trachyte blocks, is 7.10 m long and 2.80 m wide; two slabs laid flat still survive of the roofing.

To the left of the monument a setting of stones covered by a slab can be seen, perhaps a dolmen.

280fae6b5ea13ec9.text: It is a Nuragic village on Monte Tiscali inside a doline, destroyed by the Romans and by tomb robbers; the bases of the huts can be seen, and of one a part of the walling still stands. It is very difficult to reach — 45 minutes' walk — because you have to climb a steep mule track strewn with stones and pass through a fissure in the rock if you come from Oliena; in compensation you will enjoy a view over the limestone mountains of the Supramonte.

281652cf92bcd8b8.text:
Partially incorporated into a dry-stone wall, it still preserves only three orthostats in situ (0.35 x 0.22 thick – h. 0.50; 0.80 x 0.30 thick – h. 0.50; 0.60 x 0.15 thick – h. 0.50) and the capstone (1.70 x 1.52 x 0.52/0.40 thick); another orthostat can be made out beneath the wall.

Numerous slabs scattered around the burial on Sunday indicate the existence of a peristalith of which no other trace now remains.

281715da0da7b322.text: The tower is almost completely destroyed; the interior, where there are three niches, is easily accessible. The best-preserved part of the tower stands about 4 metres high. It is easy to reach and lies about 300 metres from the road. Around the nuraghe there is a magnificent prickly-pear garden.

2821f0e96d34da7c.text: Very little information exists about the Serra Su Parone nuraghe because it has been almost completely dismantled. It is perhaps a single-tower nuraghe of which only a few traces remain; a stretch of the tower wall survives discontinuously, consisting of two courses of trachyte boulders. Its state of preservation is very poor.

2822972d1f0e9ddc.text: A semi-destroyed nuraghe, surmounted by a fire lookout post, with few visible remains. Excellent panorama ranging from the nuraghe Seruci to the large beach of Porto Paglia/Punta S'Arena/Plag'e Mesu/Fontanamare as far as Pan di Zucchero.

2837ef5d2855c263.text: Nuraghe no longer existing. The nuraghe is mentioned in Spanish documents of the Episcopal Curia (12 October 1720) as a landmark, under the name “Nuraxy de Condiazzus/Candiazus”. It also appears in Angius as “Nuargi de Candiazzus” (1840), on the IGM maps (1897), in Taramelli (1910?), and from my fellow citizen Pinuccio Orlando as Nuarxi de su candiacciu (Toponimi dell'Isola).

284075d8613e335e.text: The Nuragic well/spring was built at the edge of a rocky outcrop with trachyte ashlars. It is ovoid in shape and descends to an approximate depth of about 2.50 m. The wall on the north side continues from ground level for a rise of about 2 m and for an equal width. In recent times a watering trough for livestock was built nearby.

2861bfe9edfbe77f.text: The nuraghe lies in the territory of Riola Sardo, right on the edge of the marsh. It was not recorded in the census, and it does not appear on maps either.

28644f6a7c8fa6e8.text:
A burial of the Nuragic period.

The monument is in very poor condition and its construction type cannot be determined. On the ground an alignment of stones is visible (probably belonging to the exedra), while the final stretch of the corridor can be glimpsed buried under a bramble bush.

2895f228802d9dc2.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. Of considerable size, it survives to a maximum height of about 5.40 m. Built of polygonal blocks of local basalt, it is well preserved on its western side, while the eastern side is partly collapsed and covered with vegetation. The entrance can be identified on the east side, but it has collapsed and is reduced to a simple opening.

28bf27f57e2a5d62.text:
It is a coursed Nuragic construction that rests on the rugged profile of the hill, which dictates its irregular plan. At the top a small chamber filled with collapse is visible; no entrances or other structural elements can be seen.

It should be noted that building on this rocky spur, where movement is extremely difficult and dangerous, is hard to understand: it looks more like a lookout post than a defensive structure.

28c4595d6989e06f.text: Nuragic village where 32 settlement structures dug deep into the ground, a nuraghe, a silver quarry and pre-Nuragic finds have been found. The site was covered with concrete in the 1980s to create a large irrigation tank that never went into operation.

29461d807716c006.text: On Monte Zara there are nine domus de janas, including a pair known locally as Is ogus de monti, "the eyes of the mountain". A majestic staircase of about sixty steps cut entirely into the rock leads to the summit, from which there is a broad view of the Cagliari coast. Here lies a Nuragic sacred area dating to the 7th century BC, with an altar and several cisterns for collecting rainwater.

29462dc8d53b38bb.text: A rock shelter characterised by several areas, one of which was inhabited from the Early Neolithic with subsequent funerary use. The finds recovered can be attributed to the Cardial culture.

29688efbf6b92c37.text: It lies inside a military training area, which is closed to the public.

29870d4978ff4e56.text:
It is a circular single-tower nuraghe (diam. 13 x 13.50 m) with a corridor niche and a provisional chamber of two niches; the existence of a staircase is probable but not certain.

The tower survives to a maximum height of 5.54 m and is built of medium-sized blocks, roughly dressed and laid in horizontal courses that are not always regular.

A corridor 4.25 m long leads into the circular tholos chamber (diam. 4.20 x 4 m), now reduced to a maximum height of just 3.10 m with 7 courses.

2989d004b880a992.text: The walls are built of rubble of various and medium sizes, roughly dressed, with a cyclopean stone set upright in the ground closing one end. The coverings are megalithic; some are still in situ while others have been torn up by land-improvement works.

299998810d52fe0f.text: On a raised spot of ground above a natural drainage hollow, a circle of stones is visible that could be the base of a partially buried nuraghe.

29afe399cf8cba98.text: Nuraghe consisting of a primitive central tower and several towers. The interior of the central tower is filled with earth and fallen boulders. On the east side a lintelled corridor is visible, interrupted by collapse after a few metres. A short distance from the central tower there is a curvilinear wall that probably enclosed a peripheral tower. To the NNW, adjoining the nuraghe, an oval chamber is visible. Numerous pottery fragments of various periods lie on the surface in the area.

29ba1aa9c9fe745b.text: Complex nuraghe with a central tower and two lateral towers linked by bastions and a courtyard. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

29c19ade7c2a9223.text: The monument is located in the locality of Boe and is completely destroyed; a few courses of the base are visible.

29c1e6e5f280f7cc.text: Sacred well temple, one of the most refined in Nuragic Sardinia, follows the layout with a vestibule leading into a stairway that connects to the well chamber. The building is constructed of perfectly worked limestone ashlars laid in regular courses. The vestibule, rectangular (width 2.70 m; depth 1.88 m), with a perfectly paved floor, has two bench-seats along the walls, each formed from two worked blocks.

29ce18b1938e4e99.text: Or at least what is left of it. During the rebuilding of the Sibiri road it was gutted to allow an easier alignment. In effect the bends in the old alignment were removed and the tomb was destroyed. Today a stretch of about 2 metres remains. In short, a victim of "Progress".

29d55015ea86006a.text: The nuraghe, located in an area used for pasture, is completely covered by vegetation. Because of the condition the nuraghe is in, it was impossible for us to determine its type, or the possible presence of an entrance or a lintel.

2a003accff479ad0.text: The place takes its name from the fact that a nuraghe once stood here, of which no trace remains. It was demolished around 1960, when the present Castelsardo–Santa Teresa Gallura road (SP90) was built; the stone was used for that work.

2a69ef6b5cc3d80c.text: At the Sa Brèca site two buildings are currently clearly distinguishable: the Sacred Well Temple and a sub-circular hut with benches along the walls. The whole complex appears to be enclosed by a temenos that must have separated the Sacred Area from the nearby settlement (not yet investigated by excavation sondages).

2a8b94eff43b625e.text:
Proto-nuraghe of sub-circular shape (D. Carta 2010)

The single-tower nuraghe dates to the Middle Nuragic period. The building is unusual; its chamber is partly cut into the rock.

Investigations by G. Ugas led to the identification in 1981 of a Punic settlement at Is Argiddas, on the border with the municipality of Sanluri.

The Punic centre, of which stretches of walling in small stones bonded with mud have been identified, overlies a prehistoric and protohistoric settlement.

2a8e3f93acb1456c.text: A tomb body about 11 m long survives. The tomb has its top missing. The exedra and the apse are still visible.

2a91217903f49cd4.text: Single-tower nuraghe. The entrance is completely blocked by collapse debris; the inner chamber is visible from the top of its summit. It stands on a hill covered with wild olives near the springs of S'ena Ruia.

2ac062285fc4bce4.text:
Seen from a short distance it looks like a rubble hill that hardly suggests a prehistoric monument. We are facing a colossus that offers several readings and which I personally classify among the infrapiano type.

Nuraghe del (terreno) chiuso del re. The presence of the term re almost certainly indicates that in the giudicale period the site belonged to the personal or family estate of one of the judges or kings of Torres or of Logudoro. See Tanca de su re. mu

2b0c7e78aa481d32.text: Nuraghe built of basalt blocks. Unfortunately the surviving elevation has not been properly enhanced and the site is neither legible nor accessible, also because of the dense vegetation.

2b1adf0d9ae7b3c5.text: The main sacred building consists of two rooms: a sub-rectangular atrium (originally fitted with a bench) probably covered by a gabled roof, and a circular cell accessible from the atrium, originally with a tholos (false dome) roof. In the centre of the cell are the remains of a hearth showing several phases of use, and against the wall face a bench-like embankment.

2b20bb375f01e18b.text: A single-tower nuraghe surviving to half its height, completely buried.

2b2996673d2bd0b9.text:
Nuraghe immersed in vegetation. Nearby is the eponymous Nuragic burial.

On the west side of the monument a short stretch of wall tangent to the central tower is still partly visible, while the plan shows the course of the outer perimeter.

The entrance to the tower is lintelled, with a trapezoidal cross-section, and leads into a corridor with a flat ceiling.

2b4220bd1558a9b2.text: The entrance was later adapted by building a wall to create a kind of shelter for domestic animals.

2b53bcd8e165a5f6.text: From its position on the Badde ridge it commands the right-hand course of the Rio Giunturas and joins the cliff edge superbly, almost as if to declare its dominating position. The inner chamber with its characteristic orthogonal cells can be made out, and the chamber is covered on the sides by organic debris.

2b54572189410afd.text:
It lies to the north-east of the village, a short distance from the nuraghe Luas and the proto-nuraghe Friarosu, and is visible from the provincial road that leads to Ruinas after the turn-off for Villa Sant'Antonio.

The plan of the nuraghe is decidedly unusual in that it has two circular structures joined by a corridor.

What makes the site even more interesting is the presence of a large granite boulder, oriented to the east, placed there presumably in the pre-Nuragic period.

2b57b0677613c95e.text:
Structures belonging to a complex nuraghe of the three-lobed type, built of polygonal basalt blocks. The building has been heavily robbed; only two or three courses survive in elevation, depending on the stretch.

The bastion, three towers and part of the curtain wall can be made out, against which large heaps of rubble lean. In place of the central tower a large excavation dug by mechanical means is visible. The whole structure is covered by a considerable depth of soil.

2b6d534c554929e3.text: Uncertain structure; it appears to be a Nuragic foundation.

2b712f45f0c1688d.text:
From the IGM map. The aerial photograph shows the polygon occupied by a modern cottage.

The nuraghe is probably destroyed today, or at any rate not locatable.

2b7c190f04407a2e.text: Apart from a large worked slab, nothing of the probable tomb remains except a pile of stones.

2b83cae71ededa63.text: A complex tholos nuraghe with lateral additions, with a clearly legible main tower and two further towers added. One of these is legible, though covered by vegetation, the other only discernible beneath the dense scrub. The main tower survives in fair condition and has a lintelled entrance oriented to the south-east. On the IGM maps the nuraghe is marked as Serra Crastula.

2b89debe6b0aeb9f.text:
The monument stands on top of a steep hill, partly covered by dense woodland and used for grazing. The single-tower nuraghe has collapsed on the east side, so the entrance is not visible.

It survives to a maximum height of 5.50 m and a minimum of 1 metre, with wall faces built of granite blocks laid in irregular courses.

2b8a25eb84bc4fb0.text: A circle of cyclopean masonry with the typical form of Nuragic sacred wells.

2ba002d3d62a4560.text: A small domus de janas whose entrance was walled up in the past to serve as a lamb shelter.

2bde1637a93c6027.text: It retains an intact tholos except for a few top courses.

2befc409de2b8db0.text: They lie on a slight rise at 184 m. The four rock-cut chambers are hewn in sandstone and each consists of a single elliptical cell with a vaulted roof. The many artificial cuttings, clearly visible in the rock face that flanks the domus de janas on the right-hand side for a stretch of 12 m, are clear signs of ancient quarrying that has largely destroyed the original layout of the site.

2bf1706a89cef968.text: Destroyed nuraghe of which very little remains

2c3d0e089c61b4f8.text: The probable Nuragic village consists of several huts of which only shapeless remains survive. In some cases walls made of several courses (3–5) of boulders of various sizes remain. Most of the buildings are overgrown by vegetation whose growth has damaged their structure; where the structures lie in open ground the remains are indecipherable to the eye.

2c6aa8eb8c98c26f.text:
Su Nuraxi Serra Manalgiu, about one kilometre from the old "Ortuabis" railway station, in the territory of Meana Sardo.

Around the nuraghe there are many fallen stones and many holm oaks, which keep it good company.

Of interest one can observe a wall built with rows of stones of the same height and a chamber with a collapsed vault.

2c6add6a4030ee68.text:
A corridor nuraghe with an elliptical plan, built in polygonal technique with red trachyte boulders.

The short southern side survives to a height of about 3 m and contains the entrance, topped by a granite lintel, which gives access to a small sub-circular chamber that led to a second room through another entrance with a granite lintel.

2cc76b793ad093c3.text: The tomb, situated about 300 metres north of the nuraghe of the same name, is in a good state of preservation. The entrance, facing east, gives access to a rectangular tomb about 10 metres long and about 1.20 metres high, built of well-shaped ashlars laid in regular courses.

2ceb9eb2019afb3a.text:
The nuraghe, set in Mediterranean scrub, is a fine prehistoric single-tower building constructed of black basalt stones of fairly regular size.

The inner chamber, reached through a well-preserved corridor, has two side niches and a terrace, situated at a height of about eight metres, accessible via a flight of steps.

2cf20a6a5a9eec02.text: Single-chambered domus de janas cut into the granite

2d2eab78f5bed382.text: It lies within the municipal territory of Pozzomaggiore (SS). It is a large proto-nuraghe, almost completely destroyed. There is an entrance covered in scrub and a corridor about 10 metres long with a height of 2 metres. In the upper part an entrance is still visible. Numerous boulders lie all around.

2d400a2cb6dd090f.text: It lies within the municipal territory of Pozzomaggiore (SS). Partially destroyed, about 2 metres high, covered in scrub.

2d5bdaf1216a0b69.text: It is in poor condition. Position verified with GPS.

2d81cc7110c916d5.text: Nuraghe with a sub-rectangular plan (13.40 m long on the NS axis and 10.60 m wide on the EW axis), characterised by straight long sides and convex short sides. The nuraghe is completely destroyed and practically illegible. It lies in the territory of the municipality of Ittiri.

2d8646652f2d29d5.text: The building has collapsed on the south side and dense vegetation conceals its full extent. The central tower measures about 12 m in diameter and its present height is 7.30 m. At present a short stretch of the stairwell is visible on the north side, where the facing survives and may be the remains of the bastion of a complex building. The nuraghe stands on natural outcrops of trachyte. Around the nuraghe lies an extensive settlement that was also occupied in Roman times.

2d9aa91fb9cb45f3.text:
On the plain there are two massive rocky outcrops that emerge, more or less 200 metres long, 30 m wide, 6 m high.

I only saw Site I from a distance, but they are clearly visible and the landowner confirmed that there are several domus de janas.

Site II has about ten domus de janas all facing perfectly west, all very small except for two with several chambers. They are set at different heights in the rock, from 30 cm up to 4 metres above ground level.

2dec371728af03d9.text:
The area includes a dolmen, a domus de janas and remains of a megalithic circle.

A distinctive area marked by the megalithic enclosure within which the dolmen stands. About 20 m from the dolmen lies the single-chamber Domus de Janas with a dolmenic corridor, added at a later period to create another tomb. Datable between the 3rd and 2nd millennium BC from the municipal information board.

2e0849e9ae894069.text: Second domus de janas. It is in poor condition because of the brambles that overgrow it.

2e17ee27bc545c2c.text: Nuraghe about 9 m high, built of large basalt ashlars. Entrance corridor about 5 m long with a stair on the left and a niche on the right. Intact tholos, diameter 5.30 m.

2e1a73900b6f060d.text:
It consists of three small tombs. It lies in the territory of Montresta.

Probable location.

2e28b475883570fb.text: The nuraghe is a complex type, with a central tower at the centre of a four-lobed bastion with a straight-curved profile enclosing a vaguely rectangular open-air courtyard. The whole structure measures 22.00 x 20.00 m (W-E / N-S axis), while the maximum surviving height is 6.20 m to the south-west and the wall thicknesses are 6.40 m to the south-west and 2.80 m to the north. Of the towers, only the one to the east is detectable, accessible from the courtyard through a corridor with steps visible in the final stretch.

2e5f18f957451fe4.text: The monument has collapsed in several places and is not altogether easy to interpret: it appears to have been a single-tower nuraghe, yet curvilinear wall outlines are visible around the main building. These could be dwelling units (huts?) or additional structures attached to the main body, in which case it would be a complex nuraghe.

2e6377a134963077.text: The corridor nuraghe, rectangular in plan and built of large granite boulders, survives to a maximum height of 4 m; it has an entrance topped by a lintel leading to a flat-roofed corridor, off which open a semicircular niche and an elongated chamber.

2e830284bef5b032.text: Nuraghe completely overgrown and partly ruined because of the vegetation. The structure is not easily legible.

2e8d610ac03ec8e6.text: Multi-lobed, with a central tower of which only the basal course survives; this breaks off to the south and south-west for a length of 8 m, where the foundations of four peripheral towers appear, originally joined by straight curtain walls, forming a basal platform supporting the main tower, which has a diameter of 9.60 m. About 11 m from the central tower the basal walling of a circular hut 8.40 m in diameter is almost entirely visible. The structures of the complex are composed of sandstone blocks.

2e90859e2bce06d4.text:
The building is a single-tower nuraghe that retains its chamber, accessible via a corridor with a stair and a niche, and provided with three subsidiary chambers.

The tower is built in its lower courses with large blocks; above these are set smaller boulders, carefully dressed and laid in regular horizontal courses.

Several light openings, triangular or quadrangular, arranged almost in a spiral, are visible on the outer wall face.

A short distance from the nuraghe a domus de janas has been cut.

2eae93d2fb0e1c97.text: A few wall remains and many doubts: the historical memory of the elders and the presence of the few basal remains of the eponymous nuraghe are a frequent help. mu.

2eb432fa7664c163.text: The necropolis comprises 4 domus de janas.

2ec1bcee2317d756.text: On the limestone plateau of sas cudinas to the north-east stands the single-tower nuraghe of roughly squared stones, of which only a few basal circles survive. It overlooks the whole valley of the rio Iscanneddu, the plain of Mamucada, and the fertile Orria Pitzinna.

2ed8c1ffd6feea10.text: The exact name of the nuraghe (which has a mezzanine above the entrance corridor) should be S'Olteri.

2eea640cf5a14c63.text:
The monument stands in the marly basin of Coni at the foot of the Valenza hill, in the historic region of Part'e Alenza, between the Marmilla and the Sarcidano. The sacred well of Coni, built of basalt blocks in pseudo-isodomic masonry, although lacking a vestibule, follows the classic architectural scheme of Nuragic wells.

The monument consists of a descending staircase protected by a corridor (2.60 m long) and an underground chamber that encloses the spring vein.

2f2730a0871acc77.text:
It lies in the municipality of Orani (NU). It consists of 17 domus de janas and 2 rock shelters (probably used as burials). A text by Chiara Chisu states there are 15 domus, but I have recorded at least 17 (some may have been missed because of the dense vegetation).

They must not be confused with those at Oniferi which are called Sas Concas.

2f3bfc056f452299.text: Necropolis consisting of domus de janas reused in the Roman period.

2f457cdea927d1c8.text:
North-west of the Muntone nuraghe, from which they can be reached by a path, lie first a settlement and then the megalithic tomb of Tanca Noa.

The settlement, which appears to extend for about 400 sq m, consists of the remains of structures whose ground plans are not easily defined; the wall structures, of which only the basal course survives, are built in the double-skin technique, using trachyte and dry-stone construction.

2f6b60eebd54dc07.text: A collective burial of the Nuragic period. The monument stands next to the tomb of Battos I and repeats both its type and the fine workmanship of its well-squared and finished basalt ashlars, but it is not as well preserved. Among the fallen ashlars the corridor and the exedra can still be made out, while in the apsidal area there are two monolithic arches. The dentilled ashlar is visible on the ground.

2f6ee3dbfa7d2283.text:
Completely buried on the outside, it preserves a small tholos inside that continues into a blind corridor.

More precisely it is a proto-nuraghe or corridor nuraghe.

2f77325898f9dc0a.text: Giovanni Lilliu defines the Nuraghe Ruinas as the highest in Sardinia. At an altitude of 1205 metres, above the nuraghe there is a wonderful panoramic view over the surrounding territory and the ruins of the numerous circular huts that surround it (at least 200).

2f8c3039ce83990b.text: These are the remains of a nuraghe that is difficult to classify typologically; the collapses and the dense shrub vegetation growing on the exposed masonry do not allow a proper survey. However, the data gathered during repeated inspections of the site, which among other things made it possible to locate the entrance facing north-west, lead me to hypothesise that it may belong to the class of so-called corridor nuraghi with an associated settlement.

2f94c70b86d28c57.text: The cist is formed of medium-sized stones set on edge in the ground. A single stone closes the cist, while a baetyl is visible at the front.

2fbac5c8d12403fb.text:
Megalithic tomb consisting of a burial corridor bounded by two parallel rows of orthostats.

A single large, well-finished quadrangular slab of the roofing remains, resting on the side walls at the far end of the tomb.

For the enhancement and public use of the monument, the surrounding pertinent area has been fenced and linked to the municipal road network by a path bordered by dry-stone walls.

2fc51abef626148c.text: The perforated rock of Suttaterra stands on the limestone summit of Punta Su Nuraghe, where you can admire not only the natural arch but also a megalithic wall a short distance away, and get a sense of how far you are from the Codula di Ilune and the other beauties of the area.

2ff88629cf7002e7.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. The nuraghe has been almost completely dismantled and the remains consist of the first two basal courses, built of roughly dressed blocks of local basalt. The maximum surviving height is about 1 m, while the diameter of the nuraghe is about 12 m. The entrance must have been to the south-east, where a hut has been built.

3005d1570a09ff73.text: The complex nuraghe, of which ruins of the central tower and two curtain walls on two different levels survive. The original tower retains its outline almost intact. The two curtain walls are visible on the side facing north-east of the central tower; they follow a curvilinear course for several metres, interrupted from north-east to north-west by a substantial collapse that starts from the central tower.

30097d8a28f31060.text: They are six single-chambered domus de janas.

300bf2a5a0fc89e6.text: Complex nuraghe consisting of three towers standing in a line, perched on the rocky peak of Monte Sirimagus, one of which has a well cut into the rock. All around is a village with dozens of huts surrounded by as many as three enclosing walls. The site has been extensively disturbed by tomb robbers. At the foot of the mountain a perennial pond was used in the Nuragic period.

3011ec213a57fe6f.text: A single-tower nuraghe with ten courses of porous basalt still in place. It lies in the territory of Sorradile (OR); its present position is curious, for after the Omodeo artificial reservoir was built the monument stands on the lake shore, subject to the continual fluctuations of the water level.

303239c12eb265ab.text: It lies about 30 metres at right angles to the minor road off the SS 131, in a state of complete abandonment.

303c82f0dc5a0b1b.text: Undetermined nuraghe. An area with finds attributable to a settlement with a nuraghe; the nuraghe has been demolished. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

3065746ff76fba8c.text: The Santu Millanu nuraghe is a single-tower nuraghe surrounded by a four-lobed bastion that is barely discernible.

3070f2fa2f3ad42b.text: The most well-known nuraghe is undoubtedly the one discovered in the Santa Maria area during excavations carried out beneath the sacristy of the rural chapel; the foundations were uncovered in 1843, and some nuraghe stones are incorporated into the fence wall of the church courtyard. www.aserramanna.it/storia/ www.serramanna.altervista.org/storia.htm

30712b0761b34c11.text: It lies in the municipality of Buddusò (OT) at a lower elevation than the road that runs through the granite quarry.

3079ad8117f3c27c.text:
The dolmen has a burial chamber of a vaguely polygonal shape (1.51 x 1.20 x 0.71 m high) and still preserves six orthostats in their original position, on which the large polygonal covering slab, worked with some care, rests (2.20 x 1.90 x 0.50 m thick).

Around the monument, among numerous overturned stones, three orthostats still in situ can be seen maintaining an alignment parallel to the perimeter of the tomb and forming part of its peristalith.

30831f9bc26811aa.text: The Costa nuraghe, commonly called Sa Reggia, comprises a complex nuraghe, a surrounding village and a massive outer wall. The nuraghe consists of a central tower and a bastion of four secondary towers enclosing a courtyard. The central tower (14 metres in diameter) is built of polygonal basalt blocks in the lower part and well-worked blocks in the upper part.

308690c5e25226f9.text: Single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, of which only the base survives, controlling the valley of the Rio Gutturu Mannu to the east. Taken from the archaeological map of Sant'Andrea Frius drawn up by Roberta Relli and Antonio Forci.

308a2f3a9e1be906.text: Very ruined, but large blocks of roughly dressed hard limestone remain, showing the construction technique. The entrance is visible to the south-south-east, with the lintel on the ground near the two jambs. The typology of the nuraghe points to its sacredness, linked to the conjunction with the god, since the monument is the prolongation of the mountain shaped like a truncated cone. mu

308f718ea684ede2.text: The tomb has a rectangular chamber that is completely blocked by fallen boulders and covered in vegetation. In the area in front of the tomb there are boulders that certainly belong to the exedra wall, some still in their original position. Given its present condition it is difficult to determine its dimensions.

30b14ea8cef9275b.text:
The Perda Longa archaeological complex, situated in a hilly area a few kilometres from Tortolì, comprises fifteen menhirs, most of them fallen, two giants' tombs (these are not easy to locate) and three nuraghi on the surrounding hills.

Among the perdas fittas (the Sardinian name for menhirs), several blocks stand over 4 metres high. The archaeological site dates to the fourth millennium BC (pre-Nuragic), but continued to be frequented into the Roman period.

30e74538a18ee09f.text: It is a nuraghe of which few or no traces remain.

30eb33bb99935e9b.text: A farm track skirts the foot of the hill, which must in any case be climbed on foot (there are no paths or mule tracks).

3103656d09c41070.text:
Site where a proto-Sardinian healing god was worshipped.

Rectangular-plan temple built of large blocks, with a spring that collected in a round well. Taramelli judged that all the elements of a sanctuary with a healing character were present: a therapeutic spring and a temple to the healing deity, where the most remarkable find in Sardinian archaeology came to light. The bronze column base with inscriptions in Greek, Punic and Latin dedicated to the god Eshmun.

31163f7356630ac9.text: This is Domus I, the most important and easily visible of a prehistoric necropolis consisting of 7 hypogea. The other tombs lie on private land, about 600 metres away as the crow flies to the south-east. Two of the hypogea mentioned above are more properly burials in rock shelters. Prehistoric necropolis that gave its name to the first phase of the Early Bronze Age in Sardinia (1800–1600 BC), the so-called Bonnanaro Culture.

311d84200c0f45c7.text:
The nuraghe has a sub-elliptical plan, with its long sides aligned east–west. The masonry is roughly polygonal.

The entrance faces north and has a lintel resting on a few large blocks that form the jambs; it is surmounted by a smaller ashlar, which in turn is set within a semicircular ring of blocks that diverts the weight of the superstructure onto the jambs.

311ebdf056fb98c5.text: Ruined and demolished structures, destroyed by vegetation. Difficult to interpret.

3136580e158b1093.text: Reduced to the utmost state of ruin. A few variously rough-hewn boulders of the basal circle survive, all inside a large thicket of mastic.

313aeb43f6ad9fe9.text: Called Nuraghe de su casteddu de Monte Maria, a possible fortress nuraghe, set on a granitic base. Difficult to reach, it was visited and catalogued by Lamarmora as early as 1830; a lightning strike is said to have reduced it to its present state. The north and south turrets can be visited; it appears to be a corridor nuraghe that was adapted over time.

31581427f1a11ebe.text: Four-lobed nuraghe, with four towers at the corners of the quadrangular bastion and an internal courtyard in front of the entrance to the central tower.

3161fdbc287ab7a2.text: It is a simple tholos nuraghe whose outer plan is not visible because it is completely buried. The course of the corridor (max. length 3.40 m) and the sub-circular shape of the chamber with a niche on the left side can be made out. The building is constructed with courses of granite blocks that become progressively smaller towards the higher courses.

316d3eee248bce05.text: A short distance from the megalithic circle are the basal remains of a simple circular nuraghe of the advanced Nuragic period, and a little further downhill the Ochila domus de janas, some of them richly decorated with symbolic and architectural elements in relief. The megalithic enclosure consists of ten (plus an eleventh lying overturned in the centre of the area) irregularly parallelepiped megaliths set side by side, forming a semicircle 9–10 metres in diameter.

318ab94ad193c26f.text: Several remains of circular buildings, terraces and massive megalithic curtain walls are visible, while on the highest point stands a complex-plan structure of granite blocks, in which a quadrangular tower can be seen. The settlement is crossed by the seasonal stream Riu Bidd'e Mores, a tributary of the Riu Gutturu Mannu.

31a42914f2483654.text: Single-tower nuraghe heavily altered by mid-20th-century agricultural mechanisation

31d70928501aaeb0.text:
Built of granite blocks, it consists of a circular courtyard, a vestibule – a small space linking the courtyard and the well – and the well itself, reached from the vestibule by several steps; the spring lies 17 steps down.

Excavated completely in 1938, the sacred well of Sa Testa has an overall length of 17.50 metres. It was a place of worship for spring waters. Numerous finds came to light during the excavations, such as Punic-period incense burners.

31dc0f43b6392d53.text:
The underground tomb is cut into a schist boulder; on the side opposite the entrance, to the north, the start of the excavation of another tomb can clearly be seen. The domus de janas is entered through a small doorway with a drainage channel cut into its threshold:

the doorway has a frame topped by a lintel, carved into the rock to set off this architectural feature

31e247234d5a7ad2.text: Its entrance was narrowed and adapted in the Nuragic period so as to make it hard to find and extremely easy to defend in the event of an outside attack. The rather steep dromos, with a final drop of 8 metres, was altered by adding a retaining wall and creating an access via a narrow, steep staircase of 18 steps. Inside, traces of Nuragic-period use are clearly visible.

31ebd232396a7903.text: Known as a nuraghe, it is in fact a fine example of a giants' tomb with an attached ceremonial circle. Facing east is the dolmenic exedra that opens into the rectangular stone cist. From the sides of the exedra, large dressed stones radiate in a circle to form the circle for ceremonies. Mu

31eefa9b0d874fc9.text: This domus de janas is part of the larger Abealzu-Calancoi complex, which contains dozens of domus de janas. It lies on the mid-slope of a limestone hillside, facing south, and is difficult to reach on foot. Its state of decay is considerable, due to the crumbling of the limestone and later reuse.

31f28ea0bd272ee7.text: Single-tower nuraghe with a ruined and buried village whose structure cannot be defined

31fec4807eaacd9a.text:
The monument consists of an atrium and the spring itself from which the spring water flows.

The atrium is a rectangular space measuring 5.15 by 1.80 m, bounded on the sides by two benches of equal length built of basalt blocks and, on the left side, by a section of walling 2 by 3 m made of well-squared ashlars laid in regular courses. The floor is paved with blocks of the same kind.

320766da9ccee450.text: Single-tower nuraghe submerged beneath the waters of Lake Cuga. It was recorded by the archaeologist Ercole Contu in the period before the dam on the Cuga was built. It belongs to the complex of nuraghi in the Chessedu–Cuga valley.

321cefb7695150cc.text: It is a large area of archaeological interest and lies near the ruins of a country church that are visible in the territory of Sanluri, just beyond the border with our village. It saw a succession of prehistoric settlements, datable from the Middle Bronze Age (16th–14th century BC) to the Iron Age (9th–8th century BC).

325a5bf026d9f36f.text: A group of seven or more domus de janas on the pass, towards the Mariani farm, from which the Santa Lucia plain and the underlying Sant'Andrea Priu necropolis and the valley of the nuraghi of Torralba can be seen. Tomb seven, with the double spiral in red ochre, has recently been restored.

3299010eb6ab75ae.text:
The nuraghe stands on the northern edge of a modest trachyte plateau, from which it overlooks the whole valley below. Not far from it lie the Runara dolmen and the Pittigheddu nuraghe.

The nuraghe is in very poor condition, having been used as a stone quarry to build several enclosures that stand right up against the building, making it extremely difficult to follow the plan of the ancient structure.

32ca612e6014a921.text: The necropolis consists of 33 hypogea of the domus de janas type cut into the tuff and divided into two groups. The site, datable to the Neolithic, was used by the peoples of the Ozieri, Abealzu-Filigosa, Monte Claro, Beaker and Bonnanaro cultures, and also by the Nuragic people of Iloi in the Middle Bronze Age, with re-use in the medieval period.

32d3576b0851e5e1.text: The necropolis consists of five hypogea and numerous cavities that were probably domus de janas, but now appear destroyed or incomplete. One domus (the first) has an interesting column in the main cell.

32d8b37953b33ecb.text: .。那些. function那些那些. function。 function. function

32f02fa66b99660a.text: Completely buried .. and ignored. In the village they say it was originally the largest in the area and that part of the upper tower was taken away for building material.

32f62beb1095ea26.text: The nuraghe is buried on the hilltop. Single-tower with a staircase. Completely with its top missing.

32fff02ff6c99fa2.text: The giants' tomb lies about fifty metres south of the Nuraghe Figu. Part of the tomb body and a small portion of the exedra can be seen.

331e99c6b0bfb7c5.text: A very unusual menhir, pierced in several places, perhaps artificially.

3320fc699e192ee2.text: It consists of several single-room units, some with an antechamber and two or three small internal rooms. It is reasonable to think that others exist, not yet evident in the womb of Mother Earth. Almost all of them stand on the ridge of the mountain and on the gentle slope of sa pala de s'Ozastru. On the plateau are the remains of the eponymous nuraghe, with a clear link between the two sites of different periods and reasonably an example of cultural and religious syncretism. mu

3328571419e638b7.text: It is an isolated, tree-covered hillock shaped like a cone on a plateau, on which various boulders of different shapes, from conical-prismatic to parallelepiped, are set. The setting is evocative, and stories are told of events that take place during sacred or initiatory-propitiatory ceremonies.

332aa681d407c33b.text: It lies in the municipality of Florinas and consists of three hypogea.

332d19abb2ec57ff.text: The nuraghe Franzesu stands in a commanding position on the Spiritu Santu plateau, with a wide view ranging from the Gulf of Asinara to Corsica, controlling important access routes. The nuraghe consists of a central tower and a bilobed frontal bastion without a facing. The bastion is built of large trachyte blocks; it is thought that some of these may be reused menhirs, and at least one certainly was.

3349bf13298a31c7.text: The lower part of the nuraghe survives, also used as a sheepfold. Probably elliptical or in any case not circular. Diameter at the top of the surviving masonry about 10 m.

336694de11079cf5.text: In a precarious state of preservation, it is overgrown with bramble patches and shrubs that could undermine its stability.

336af29ca3582be2.text: A ruined and buried nuraghe whose structure is difficult to define

33882dd1dbc2becf.text: A large megalithic circle a few steps from the Mitza Salamu Sacred Well.

339b795a4e72da67.text: In a total state of ruin, a few boulders of the basal circle survive, identifying its type. The boulders are large and the chamber has collapsed together with a mass of debris that has accumulated over time. Prickly pear plants and thorny shrubs have colonised the site.

33b70cca9edb29b2.text: The complex consists of six hypogeal tombs cut into large isolated blocks of limestone, erratic boulders. Tombs I and IV stand out for their decorative ornaments, represented by spiral motifs carved in relief with the direct pecking technique, and architectural elements typical of contemporary dwellings, such as beams and joists (reproducing a double-pitched roof), frames, pilasters, plinths, steps and false doors, carved in bas-relief.

33bb6bd20ecc0ce1.text: Not easily reached because it stands on a high, particularly striking ridge, it comprises a complex nuraghe. The ruined structure is hard to read owing to the abundant collapse; courses of limestone blocks are visible.

33d3e2d7e470fb51.text: It consists of a pseudo-rectangular pit 1 m deep. Lined with three courses of blocks. Covered by a flat lintel of three schist slabs 25 cm thick. Single burial with Monte Claro pottery.

33e4721797cb5ad2.text: A village without a nuraghe. From the same area comes a Copper Age dagger with a leaf-shaped blade, and a pink trachyte basin with a rim diameter of 70 cm. The presence of a bronze hoard at Sant'Elia is noted; it has been lost and was reported by Giuseppe Atzori.

3400100038e5a5bc.text:
Of the practically destroyed monument only the burial corridor remains, consisting of a depression in the ground, and numerous shaped ashlars indicating that the tomb was of the coursed type in isodomic masonry.

Among the ashlars, which are very carefully worked, one can observe the so-called dentilled stele of considerable size, and a monolithic arch belonging to the apsidal area.

341f1e0b0ed05c85.text: Complex nuraghe consisting of a central tower and four towers. The outline of the walls of the original tower survives almost entirely; its interior is filled with earth, collapse debris and vegetation. Three towers added laterally stand to the south-east, north-west and north-east, all overgrown with vegetation that makes their structure hard to see. The fourth tower lies to the south-west, detached from the main body. Traces left by illegal excavators are clearly visible.

345fc7c154b7400b.text: Complex nuraghe. Traces of at least three towers, probably added concentrically, can be identified. The original tower retains its wall outline, broken to the south by a small opening. The interior is partly blocked by soil and collapse debris. To the south and south-south-east there are two triangular corridors whose outlines, interrupted by collapse, are visible for several metres; one suggests the presence of a stairwell. Clandestine excavations are visible.

347c6509c15da260.text:
A burial of the Nuragic period built in courses of polygonal limestone blocks.

Although partly covered by vegetation and fill, the ground plan with its apse and exedra, whose arms run in straight lines, is clearly legible. On the façade, in front of the entrance doorway, a rectangular slab lies on the ground and may be the lintel of the entrance.

347e39d08ef341ae.text: The building, a circular single-tower nuraghe about 10 metres in diameter, adapts to the plateau, incorporating rock outcrops into its basal structures. The external wall face, made of roughly dressed limestone blocks laid in regular courses, survives to a maximum height of 8.10 metres. On the west and south-east sides, at a height of 3 to 3.5 metres from the ground, a restoration carried out in antiquity is clearly visible, made necessary by the subsidence of the masonry.

34b75d2417ce8148.text: A particularly ruined corridor nuraghe. The corridor is lintelled with stone slabs. Niches are built transversely.

34bf7c128e23a3a0.text: Two nuraghi (no longer existing and/or buried) located in the territory of Ussana and reported by Taramelli (see "Ussana - Scoperte di tombe di età incerta in territorio del Comune, regione di Salomea", in Notizie degli Scavi, 1906, pp. 57-58). The first was probably situated in the centre of the village at Bruncu Sa Turri, more or less corresponding to the old municipal aqueduct (Via Aldo Frau).

34d4ffd77b9af2e1.text: The hypogeum lies at the southern edge of a small plateau, characterised by dense woodland. The burial is cut into a block of heavily fractured granite, so that part of the antechamber has completely broken away and now lies right next to the entrance. The entrance to the cell is about 0.70 m above ground level; it has jambs and a lintel carved in relief, with carefully finished surfaces.

34e812783c92679c.text: The probable Nuragic village consists of several huts of which linear wall remains survive, formed by several courses (in some cases up to five) of stones of various sizes. They were probably rectangular structures. Unfortunately, dense and tangled vegetation conceals most of the structures. To the north, about 100 metres away, lies the Noccus pond, a water reserve for the villages in the area.

34f31a32abbbe4dc.text: The monument, about 300 metres north-west of the Nuraghe Su Figu, is now almost completely buried under rubble from the clearance of the surrounding fields, a fact that makes the plan of the nuraghe extremely difficult to read. It appears to be a circular single-tower nuraghe, with a stair and a corridor niche, visible where the top is missing.

351c3c255bb7c2bf.text: These are Domos belonging to the complex-architecture type. The layout of the rooms cannot be understood because Mother Earth preserves the site almost entirely. Access is possible thanks to the collapse of the vault of one of the chambers. Inside, clear construction details, fittings and petroglyphs can be seen. Mu

352bc0de8dd017fa.text: This is a report by an enthusiast, verified by an archaeologist. It appears to be a giants' tomb or dolmenic corridor previously unknown.

3532d8801c1337ec.text:
More precisely, it is a proto-nuraghe.

Nearby there are also a particular giants' tomb and a domus de janas.

355a8dacd2db9384.text: Nuragic village of Su Putzu, composed of about a hundred huts surrounding a sacred well, precisely Su Putzu.

356b86aea2594cd0.text:
It lies on the boundary between the municipal territories of Bortigali (NU) and Dualchi (NU), but belongs to the municipality of Dualchi.

More precisely it is a proto-nuraghe. Several cinerary urns are found around it. It consists of two megalithic walls still partly intact.

3570f36c7102d51f.text: The nuraghe, the best-visible side of which is from the vineyard in front of the pigsty, appears in any case to have been a single-tower nuraghe, built with roughly dressed blocks of fairly regular parallelepiped shape and medium-to-large size.

357cdb00e939ef38.text: It lies in the territory of Pozzomaggiore (SS), near the nuraghe (proto-nuraghe) Sinadorzu or Scale e Ozzastru; there are several huts and enclosure walls, and nearby one can see probable remains of giants' tombs and perhaps a Nuragic sacred well, obviously all in deplorable condition.

357fbab393ded136.text: The nuraghe stands on the Gullei. It is a single enormous lava flow several kilometres long. The village is not easy to reach because it is wrapped in dense wild scrub. The nuraghe is a three-lobed one whose walls are visible. For at least one or two hectares around, the village spreads out, with a furnace, a well and more besides. From the top of the towers the whole territory and the coast are visible as far as the Mariolu cliffs to the south and Cala Ginepro to the north.

3582b38b98e67b15.text: The domus de janas, cut into the flank of the basalt hill, are five in number, all attributable to the Ozieri Culture and excavated between 3100 and 2900 BC. The pre-Nuragic village, also dating to the Ozieri Culture, lies at the foot of the hill.

359808c65aa7484e.text:
In some publications it is actually distinguished from the village and necropolis of Porcili Mannu, but the area is that of Sa Sucraxia and the local inhabitants refer to it by that name.

Almost hidden among the large trees, clearly visible remains of a large stone village can be seen, with several buildings, some dwellings, remains of tombs and other structures that cannot be more closely identified.

359ebb88b9f1dbda.text: Menhir / stele carved with concentric circles

35a024338b497214.text: It lies to the north-east along the provincial road near the boundary with the territory of Ruinas. It stands on a large limestone base and is filled with its own rubble, which makes access impossible. According to local belief it originally consisted of a succession of three superimposed chambers. The remains of a staircase are visible on a ridge.

35c2cb3f1abf45ac.text: Giants' tomb belonging to the nuraghe of the same name. Very poor state of preservation.

35cff6ce23ba502b.text: It consists of a nuraghe of an unusual type, built of roughly squared megalithic blocks laid in fairly regular courses. To the north-east an extensive village spreads out, mostly reduced to a scatter of stones; from the general collapse a few megalithic structures and some huts uncovered by unauthorised diggers emerge. The nuraghe, on the other hand, retains its original elevation to a certain height, but its ground plan is not immediately legible.

35e7c6b26ff19799.text: They are four small hypogean burials cut into an isolated rock outcrop.

35fb788aae59037d.text: Domus de janas cut into the granite, of particular charm for the double doorway separated by a pillar

3604611dfbe5ca93.text:
The Serra Paulis Nuragic complex now survives only as a ruin, with four wall structures already identified by Struglia around the 1980s.

Its dominant position over the whole territory allows a 360° view.

The site was probably reused in the Roman period as a foundry workshop, given the considerable remains of materials burnt and deformed by fire found in situ.

3606441ecee8545e.text: The Taulera domus de janas lies near the civil hospital of Alghero. In 1941–42 some soldiers encamped there found a skull showing a double trepanation. The individual to whom the skull belonged survived the first trepanation for at least a year, probably dying during the second.

3625651afb95cb26.text: Nuraghe of uncertain type built on a rocky spur, taking advantage of its elevations; characterised by a massive collapse, concentrated especially to the north-west. Situated at 418 m.

36365659deb4f519.text: Giants' tomb Sa Canna, in the Sàrrala area of Tertenia but administratively belonging to one of the many enclaves in the zone (39.61237 N 9.63864 E). This was my first encounter with a tomb built of schist, a stone used only sporadically for this type of monument. It is of the coursed type, considered more recent than the 'dolmenic' or 'arched stele' type, and has an elegant exedra — although it lacks the dentilled ashlar characteristic of the more refined examples — standing 2.55 m high at its apex. The tomb shows some gaps due to clandestine disturbance (the missing ashlar from the left arm of the exedra is clearly visible), which prevent the exact width of the semicircle from being determined, though it can be assessed as having a slight curvature. The chamber, not very large, is 6.75 metres long measured at the outer threshold and 6.40 metres at the inner threshold, and is distinguished by a perfect ogive with a descending height from 1.95 m at the entrance to 1.40 m (presumed, since the clandestine excavation has disturbed the basal paving) at the rear, where traces of ancient plastering seem to be detectable (unless this is due to a neoformation of clay caused by the loss of the corridor's waterproofing — which, on the other hand, remains intact for almost its entire length). The entrance doorway is trapezoidal (50 cm wide at the base and 60 cm at the top), 57 cm high, and easily passable. This is therefore one of the tombs in which it is clear that access from the top of the corridor was not possible, as most island archaeologists maintain (on the other side of the 'barricade' stood the great Ercole Contu, who in my opinion took a more scientific approach to the question), since there is no possibility of removing any ashlars from the corridor to allow such hypothetical access. The tomb almost certainly belongs to a settlement located about 500 metres away as the crow flies, on another saddle of the same ridge, of which only a few remains can be identified today: a non-canonical type of nuraghe and a few surrounding traces attributable to huts (the area is also known as Serra 'e Mari, and a boundary stone — the municipalities concerned are Lanusei and Arzana — was placed on the nuraghe in 1953).

3664093265f864c9.text: Wall alignments and structural remains, among which a hut with a sub-rectangular plan is recognisable, surviving to a maximum height of about 1 m, built of small basalt blocks laid dry, with a small lintelled window. Modern and contemporary enclosures stand in the area of the concentration. The area of what was presumably a settlement extends around the nuraghe Marzacche.

366d8486efdd2e7d.text:
At the foot of the hill on which the nuraghe Su Gattu stands, the remains of a burial in granite are visible.

Of the giants' tomb a stretch of the apse and part of the rectangular chamber bounded by large granite boulders survive, while outside the remains of the peristalith emerge.

36734870daa2d37c.text: The monument is in a pitiful state of disintegration. It stands on a secondary peak of Monte Nibbarone (237 m) at an altitude of 168 m a.s.l., from where it overlooks the whole valley below.

367b23e5d0718900.text: An interesting giants' tomb with a bilithic arched stele, of which the lower part with the doorway survives. The exedra and the burial chamber are also present.

367d02ee76ff5a86.text: An area with a small single-tower nuraghe around which there is a small necropolis of four domus de janas, in which there are decorations of carved bull's-head protomes.

36b51bf237f13772.text: Situated on the boundary with the territory of Guasila, at the foot of the basalt plateau of Lasìna, on the western side that slopes down towards the territory of Samatzai. The building consists of a single tower with an external diameter of 12 m and preserves the basal course intact around its entire circumference. The materials used are sandstone.

36c269c919b13893.text:
It lies in the municipality of Santu Lussurgiu (OR), a few kilometres from the hamlet of San Leonardo de Siete Fuentes.

It is a three-lobed nuraghe with a central tower and two minor towers, one to the south-west and the other to the north-east. Traces of a curtain wall a few metres from the entrance of the first tower, which enclosed the complex, also survive.

36c7ac0d4b1983d2.text:
On a rocky spur stands the corridor nuraghe, rectangular in plan, built of pink trachyte boulders. The interior of the monument is not accessible because of the many collapses.

The giants' tomb lies to the south, about 500 metres from the nuraghe; only part of the inner wall face of the chamber and traces of the peristalith are visible.

On an area of about 2000 sq m around the giants' tomb, numerous structures are visible, of which only the basal courses remain.

36db5ee2d0833f1a.text: The sacred area, dominated to the east by the striking granite crests of Monte Senes (about 862 m above sea level), was built in the Nuragic period at the Janna 'e Pruna pass, now crossed by the Irgoli–Norghio road and a crossing point (about 590 m above sea level) that has been used since very ancient times along a mountain route linking the Riu Siniscola valley with the Cedrino valley, important corridors from the coast into the interior of the island.

36e8677da1829e56.text:
The burial lies on the southern slope of a gentle incline. The burial chamber is partly visible, and about 3.50 m from it two partly buried blocks can be seen, probable elements of the exedra. The tomb has unfortunately been disturbed by illicit digging that has affected the rear part of the tomb.

As far as can be seen, the latter consists of medium-sized granite slabs, well dressed on the exposed face, and set as orthostats.

3700cdfde2e40a7e.text:
The four-lobed bastion has a rather disordered structure of large polyhedral blocks; all the chambers have collapsed vaults, while the courtyard is partly filled with rubble; the main entrance is visible on the eastern side.

A stretch of enclosure wall can be seen to the west of the bastion, but it is not clear whether it extends around the other sides as well. All the ground around the bastion has been completely cleared of stones and is cultivated, with abundant Roman pottery on the surface.

370d43a0d61267ac.text: Single-tower nuraghe and settlement, destroyed for the construction of the railway. The position is not exact. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

372f9efc2963203a.text: It lies in the municipality of San Vito (CA), inside the church of the same name.

3731d46ab3c2667b.text: The nuraghe is in a very advanced state of collapse. The full outline of the original tower survives for a maximum of two courses. Given the few remaining boulders on site, it may have been dismantled so its stones could be reused. A few metres away there are boulders that probably belonged to the nuraghe, used to build a yard for watering livestock. At present the nuraghe is completely overgrown with vegetation.

3747d1613ef62132.text:
Also known as "Sa Domu 'e s'Orku", it is built of local granite blocks laid in "cyclopean style". It has the unique feature of being oriented exactly to the north.

This giants' tomb is of the "coursed façade" type, typical of the giants' tombs of southern Sardinia; the façade and the exedra, 10 m wide, are built in megalithic masonry; on the right-hand side of the exedra there are three "ritual hearths", circular in shape.

3751186c7f0ac95d.text: Both the nuraghe and the giants' tomb are in very poor condition and covered by vegetation.

375b78263209220b.text: The boulder of “La Serra” takes its name from the nearby Nuraghe, a monument thousands of years old, shaped like a truncated cone and now reduced to a ruin. The massive multi-cupmarked find is assigned to the Late Neolithic, although there are no certain dates; what is certain is that the monolith belongs to a period much earlier than the Nuraghe. (Pieragica)

375d31b3a5309a4a.text: The Nuraghe Sa mandra e sa Giua no longer exists; it has been razed to the ground, and its ashlars were used to build dry-stone walls and the settlement of romana.

3778bade1efc9912.text: Complex nuraghe, covered by dense vegetation; near the nuraghe a menhir and several giants' tombs can be seen, hidden by the very thick vegetation.

3780bc59e218f5ff.text: A ruined nuraghe whose layout cannot be recognised

37b78bde83516541.text: The nuraghe has suffered major collapses and is covered in dense vegetation.

37d86c662b34635d.text: One can admire the sculptures of the bull's head representing the head of the male God, worshipped by the Neolithic peoples who buried their dead in these artificial caves.

37dd2f097faa47d5.text: It consists of two quadrangular chambers cut into solid granite.

37f62d4938388b0a.text: Overgrown with vegetation, only a few courses of this nuraghe survive. It has never been excavated or studied.

37fec134d49a55e9.text: The existence of this single-tower nuraghe is assumed, even though very few remains survive.

3807d7b442520666.text: It is built of cyclopean andesite blocks and consists of a large central tower joined to three towers. Of these, two show their entire interior structure: precisely the east and the west towers. It would be possible to enter the west one to explore the inside of the nuraghe, but I had neither the time nor the wish to risk it. Up to seven courses of the central tower are visible, reaching a height of almost three metres, while up to six courses of the west tower are visible, reaching a height of two and a half metres.

3815d30b9625705c.text: Ruins of a small granite nuraghe

3835535ba07fbfd7.text:
In the municipal territory of Gonnosnò stands the nuraghe Tramatza which, together with the nuraghe Emmauru, overlooked the valley of the rio Figu, a winding watercourse among the hills at the foot of the plateau.

Only a few traces of the nuraghe remain; the original structure was a single-tower nuraghe with a truncated-conical shape, built by superimposing stone blocks, and contained the main chamber inside, connected to the outside by a narrow corridor.

384427714a7b9c52.text: The ruins of the Lepuri nuraghe are not easy to locate. Of the nuraghe, perhaps placed to guard the stream that once flowed a short distance to the south, only a few non-contiguous wall segments survive, suggesting an elongated plan and construction with large, completely unworked or at most roughly dressed boulders.

387b809573e40b87.text: A single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal basalt blocks. Four to five courses of large blocks laid in a circle remain, forming a structure of fair size, very similar to other nuraghi in the area. The maximum surviving height is about 3 m. The inner chamber has collapsed and is filled with collapse debris. The entrance cannot be identified.

389114bec8664d7c.text: Single-cell domus de janas carved into limestone

38ad27a4279d8e94.text: Complex nuraghe belonging to a much larger settlement that has never been excavated.

38b8a3c397b7bf00.text: Complex nuraghe with lateral addition, with two secondary towers added to the main tower. Built of local basalt blocks laid in fairly regular courses. The entrance to the main tower is on the east side; it is trapezoidal with a lintel formed by three irregular blocks and surmounted by an irregular relieving window.

38cfe7e611241a37.text:
Single-tower nuraghe destroyed during the clearing of the field for cultivation, although traces of ceramic finds can still be detected during survey.

The site is hard to read because of the cultivation; it would therefore be desirable to recover the materials found on the site and document them in order to reconstruct the site, even if only partially.

38d06e44235a0a1f.text: Complex tancato nuraghe, with a central tower and a secondary tower joined by walls, and a courtyard between the two towers. Remains of walls, embankments and wells used for collecting water are also present.

38dbe0248f16e0eb.text: It is a fine example of a fortress with a wall of large polygonal boulders following a vaguely circular course in broken lines from north round through west to south. To the east it takes advantage of the steep, almost vertical, inaccessible ridge overlooking the Ozieri plain. To the north there is a fine large dolmenic trilithon with a lintel. The entrance to the south is smaller. mu

38ea08e0f8c8a8cb.text: The Tracucu Necropolis is a beautiful and extensive archaeological site about three kilometres from Lotzorai, along the road to Talana. It consists of thirteen domus de janas, marked by wooden signs, which can be admired by following a guided path through the granite rocks and dense vegetation.

3906ac882af98e04.text: The site, dating to the Late Bronze Age (1300–1000 BC), is a complex nuraghe consisting of a central tower to which eight further towers were subsequently added, forming a bastion. The bastion is surrounded by a megalithic wall equipped with five towers fitted with loopholes. The construction mainly used granite boulders, a material available on the spot.

390e91d803df8b32.text: Single-tower nuraghe, ruined and collapsed inwards

3911c2eae41fd967.text: In this locality the remains of an extensive settlement with an associated necropolis are clearly visible. From the material found in this citadel it emerges that it was inhabited from the earliest times of the Bonnanaro, Ozieri, Monte Claro and Bell Beaker cultures, and then by the Nuragic, Phoenician-Punic and Roman peoples. It seems the village was inhabited until 500 AD and was abandoned following a fire that caused its destruction.

39150a304d600790.text:
Along the road from Samatzai towards S. Pietro.

Collapsed complex nuraghe, situated on a gentle slope with a central tower and two smaller ones. It has an elongated plan with the three towers arranged on the same longitudinal axis oriented north to south. A short distance from the central tower the basal structures of three circular huts are recorded, certainly belonging to a small surrounding village. The structures are built of marly and basaltic materials.

391c243125b48615.text: The exedra of the giants' tomb has been smashed up and used to build the dry-stone wall.

3940d86080ca33d1.text: It is fairly well known to the local population because the lintel of the main entrance draws attention for being made of white limestone, probably from the Giombachis or Iscala Ilvena area. Here too one must speak of an advanced state of decay owing to the many collapses that the cyclopean monument has suffered. Some constructional and architectural details are nevertheless still evident.

39424b270b286720.text:
The tomb has three rectangular chambers cut into the rock and communicating with one another.

It dates to the Bonnanaro culture period (1500–1300 BC).

394baff5037e2d84.text: "Giants' tomb of Torrà, near the tributary Rio Torrà of Rio di Posada; few remains of a large cist or corridor can be seen, almost completely dismantled. On land belonging to Antonio Nanu, it was Giovanni." With this brief description and some geographical inaccuracies (the Riu Thorra is not a tributary of the Posada but of the Mannu, which is in turn a tributary of the Posada river), Taramelli reported the presence of the giants' tomb of Thorra, without however mentioning the nearby nuraghe.

39530e5cecd691d3.text: Probable corridor nuraghe and remains of a Nuragic settlement

398ef4e7f1958984.text: Collective burial of the Nuragic period. In very poor condition.

39a2e753d31c3e59.text: It is a tholos nuraghe with an outer wall, situated near the village and in a precarious state of preservation.

39ac00beb4bfda8c.text: Concentric-plan nuraghe ... (a short distance from the nuraghe there is another uncertain structure which, in my opinion, dates to the Nuragic period – see photo). At the top the view is breathtaking! A 360° panorama of forest! To the east, in the background, the whole of the Supramonte.

39d2ca0e9e4676c5.text: A few blocks of the basal perimeter in white limestone. The entrance is visible and little else, all within a dense thicket of fetid anagyris (sa giolva). The name should derive from the place-name of the land. Hill of the liburni, a shrubby legume known for its hanging pods and the unpleasant odour given off by its leaves when touched. Shepherds believe that the leaves of this plant give a bitter taste to goats' milk. See Nuraghe sas giòlvas. mu

39d7aee008358e34.text: Only a short stretch of the first basal course survives on the side by the farmhouse; around the monument there are two small to medium-sized granite slabs that appear to be pieces of the stele.

39dfd2b566e7dcad.text: It is more likely that this is the nuraghe "Tanca di Monsignori", cited in F. Nissardi's nuraghe map (published by G. Pinza in 1901).

39e5347ddd12465b.text: The nuraghe was completely levelled to build the church of Santa Greca. In aerial images the ground circle that probably formed its foundation is still perfectly clear.

39fd17fe979c252b.text: The nuraghe has completely collapsed and only a few residual stones of the whole structure remain.

39fe262bf01a8a94.text: The Nuraghe Tradori is built of black basalt. The entrance has a pointed arch and is very low. The chamber, from which two low corridors lead off, is circular in plan with a very high false dome (tholos) that is still intact.
