Outside the nuraghe there is a stretch of walling made of large stones; on its outer face, facing south-east, a passage opens that descends deep down and appears to reach beneath the nuraghe.

3a0608707d84e47a.text: The giants' tomb of Sa Presone 1 has a semicircular exedra with a coursed façade. On the right side of the apsidal burial chamber, which is roofed with slabs, a small niche raised above the floor can be seen; it was used for placing offerings or a body in a crouched position.

3a12a687b6f5064c.text: Modest in its entirety, so much so as to be a little jewel; it consists of two walls of almost squared rubble and has a roof of large natural slabs of trachyte.

3a1af257cfd583e5.text: Complex nuraghe with a ruined and buried village whose structure cannot be defined

3a27a1065abcf367.text:
It is striking that the monument is not signposted in any way, in an area where, moreover, there is a sign for every sheepfold. The wall looks out over the Boncaminu plain, and from it one can see the village of Lu Brandali and the site towards La Colba.

The wall looks out over the Boncaminu plain, and from it one can see the village of Lu Brandali and the site towards La Colba.

3a2a0e302a563785.text: A ruined dolmenic giants' tomb of which the perimeter orthostats and a stone lintel survive.

3a3bc8be143f1a13.text: The complex, consisting of the nuraghe and its village, is therefore incorporated within the present-day settlement, surrounded by a terraced park rich in fruit trees, aromatic herbs and Mediterranean scrub. It was built during the Middle Bronze Age (about 1700–1350 BC) on a small rise overlooking the Rio Carrabusu valley.

3a3da2d1915859f6.text: The Acchettas nuraghe appears completely destroyed at first sight; a stretch of the polygonal walls is still visible on the west side. During land-clearing work large quantities of rubble were dumped on the monument.

3a472bc477e7d2a5.text: Another nuraghe completely destroyed, but partially visible on Sardinia maps from both 1954 and 1977.

3a4daf20ccd6887c.text: The area where old maps marked the location of the nuraghe Nuraghessu; one or more dolmens are present in the area.

3a5388315849c685.text: San Leonardo is an old Gallurese village that grew up near the church of the same name, a typical Gallurese country church flanked by a small cemetery. The remains of the San Leonardo nuraghe show that the site was also inhabited in the Nuragic period.

3a9c96cb4b330b07.text:
The second giants' tomb, situated 100 m south-west of the nuraghe, instead has a narrow corridor 6.5 metres long inside, without a roof, the peristalith visible only in part, and to the left of the entrance an orthostat about 1 m high and traces of the exedra.

About 500 m west of the nuraghe there is an area where stretches of walling and surface material emerge, probably of Roman date.

3aaaa41717c6afab.text: Located on the southern edge of the Corraile plateau (480 m a.s.l.), (Ozieri Culture). The eight tombs that make it up, together with a small natural cave, share architectural features similar to those of the main necropolises in the area. Some tombs stand out for their monumentality and for the presence of symbolic elements closely linked to the cult.

3aabbbb96d6cec72.text:
The unpublished proto-nuraghe Crapianu appears to be a decidedly original example among the archaic Nuragic buildings known as proto-nuraghi.

Its most significant peculiarity is that it preserves, inside a large rectangular chamber, unmistakable traces of a supporting ledge (offset) that held up the upper chamber, at a height of two and a half metres.

3abfd23540617b18.text:
Nearby is the domus de janas of the same name. The nuraghe is very ruined.

A short distance from the Florinas–Banari provincial road; the service track of a disused sand quarry lets you get even closer to the site.

3ad7985c7fc6e38a.text: Nuraghe in very poor condition and hidden by dense scrub

3ae2babd755bcf43.text: The proto-nuraghe Friarosu of Mogorella has a sub-rectangular plan with convex short sides, because at the base of the wall mass it incorporates three chambers, two sub-oval and one ellipsoidal, with a corbelled ogival roof.

3af8b1ff08e66d9a.text: The great tomb of Zanchia still has the lower part of its bilithic stele intact, while the upper part lies overturned on top of the other stones of the tomb corridor.

3b0d8118df604cc9.text: This feature is recorded as a Nuragic well and lies near a livestock watering trough.

3b398ed0228f5138.text: A domus de janas necropolis now incorporated into the urban fabric of the city of Carbonia, where 25 tombs of different sizes and types have been identified. Following a major restoration project in which the ancient Sulcitano medau, built in the 18th century, was restored, the site is currently managed by the Cooperativa Mediterranea, which allows free entry.

3b5b43b9fa7c8a46.text: It is an incomplete domus de janas inside a granite boulder.

3b856c958141b99e.text: The giants' tomb consists of two wall faces about 15 m long. Devastated by tomb robbers. Location uncertain.

3ba3992273b035fd.text: The tower of Conca Santinta must have had a significance that went beyond the purely strategic, since large quantities of metalworking slag have been found on the site, and the minerals that make up the hill have properties particularly suited to the working and production of ceramics.

3baea1947137f99c.text: Formed by stones driven into the ground that support a slab measuring 3 x 2 m, surrounded by an elliptical stone enclosure. The Elcomis Dolmen appears to have been built about three centuries after Su Laccu, since its orientation (azimuth 161.9; declination –46.75) would also point towards alpha of the constellation Musca, but in 2100 BC.

3bb2ca43adf39e57.text: Ruined nuraghe enveloped in the maquis. Presumably complex. Several courses of the masonry are clearly visible. The outline of the central tower and some secondary chambers connected to it can be made out.

3bf9d65ea6b424b8.text: Complex nuraghe of the tancato type, with a central tower and a secondary tower with bastions. On the IGM map this nuraghe is confused with the nearby nuraghe sa Tiria.

3c0580f9589c1f7d.text: Unnamed domus de janas, still to be verified

3c1a74f597fd615a.text: It was marked on the old cadastral maps. Probable location; no traces can be found.

3c247545db2b0c60.text: Lost nuraghe, of which a trace survives in local memory and the basal circle

3c2b0edb15364536.text:
The building dates from the 11th century. The remains of the wall enclosing the precinct are visible. The most precious part lies at the centre of the area, with the basin altar. The building was constructed of large, fine isodomic ashlars. Many are T-shaped.

Two "circular rooms" were joined by a sort of trapezoidal vestibule, provided with lateral stone benches. Like the nuraghi, it possesses the triad of internal perimeter niches, the western one larger, the northern and southern ones smaller and symmetrical.

3c5db0fb70eb3c6c.text:
The temple consists of a small vestibule, a narrow descending staircase covered by a stepped lintel roof, and a circular chamber covered by a tholos.

The standing structures are now limited to the keyhole-shaped perimeter wall enclosing the atrium and the well drum. The vestibule, partly paved, has a rectangular plan: the bench-seat is absent. The staircase leading down to the well chamber, with vertical walls, is made up of 12 steps.

3c68c7a262b61266.text: The domus de janas of Bruncu s'Allegau or Sa Domu 'e s'Orku was probably cut from an original natural cavity later adapted for funerary purposes. It consists of a single chamber extending horizontally with an irregular elliptical plan, 2.65 m long, 3.9 m wide and 1.5 m high from the present floor level; the ceiling still shows the small parallel grooves and hollows left by the prehistoric stonecutters.

3c6caecd406fd959.text:
More precisely, it is a proto-nuraghe or corridor nuraghe.

In the maps of the former land registry it is mentioned as Nuraghe Piraruja.

3c6f576af95bbe1c.text: Hypogeic temple in the Pitzu 'e toni area. It faces south. A wide entrance two metres long leads to a fork: the right branch is narrow, the left one wider. The name itself recalls its function. In the early 1960s, during an inspection, Prof. Lilliu found a little necklace made of round animal bone beads.

3c6f6035b2c5165b.text: A completely ruined and buried nuraghe whose structure cannot be determined.

3c869d0c2dd9726b.text: In the Is Noccus area there are two ponds, the first at the foot of the nuraghe and the other about 200 m away. The first, at the south-west base of the nuraghe, was created by using a natural lake basin. The pond is circular and shows clear signs of human intervention aimed at catching rainwater and increasing its storage capacity; boulders of various sizes can be seen placed around the edges of the basin for most of its perimeter.

3cc8ab5bf82c8717.text:
Single-tower nuraghe built of squared andesite blocks in fairly regular courses, in a fair state of preservation. The entrance faces east but the chamber is not currently visible because of the collapse of the monument's walls and roof.

To the south a wall runs in a straight and curving line, perhaps belonging to a recent sheepfold, now dismantled.

3cd4e45ec88fca1c.text: The monument, situated in a predominantly hilly area currently used as pasture, is irreparably destroyed. The base of the outer perimeter can still be seen because outcrops of granite emerge from the ground forming a circle.

3cdc28749352f5bc.text:
It has a single cell.

Another domus de janas should lie nearby.

3d08f5a613491077.text:
Partially brought to light in December 2002, the Sanna nuraghe takes its name from the furriadroxiu of the same name that stands at its feet in the countryside between Santadi and Piscinas. The excavations allowed the Superintendency staff to discover a Nuragic complex, until then forgotten, and to find it in an excellent state of preservation and in a dominant position over the surrounding territory.

Today it is almost abandoned and damaged by the very excavations.

3d480d2c1a0602fb.text: Single-tower nuraghe no longer visible but reported by the archaeologist Daniele Carta in his thesis (ArcheoArte 2012).

3d6e94ee56b6681a.text:
Multi-chambered tomb with a centripetal layout. It was emptied long ago. It yielded material of the Ozieri culture (3200–2500 BC) and of the early medieval period (7th century AD). The former are kept in the "G. A. Sanna" Archaeological Museum in Sassari; the latter in the Nuoro Civic Museum.

Inside the domus de janas, cut into a rock outcrop, access is through a hexagonal doorway; all around the antechamber, with its perfectly worked ceiling, five cells open where the dead were laid.

3d966179322c147b.text: Situated on a small rise in the countryside of the municipality, a short distance from the new provincial road "Ussana, Donori, Barrali". It is a prehistoric wall structure discovered during a survey beneath a clearance cairn. The wall stretch is straight, 4 metres long and 80 centimetres wide, built of large blocks, of which only the uppermost course is visible. It could also be one side of a tomb of the same period.

3d9aa99b30b2a128.text: A coursed giants' tomb, it stands on the south-west part of a hillock. The tomb preserves the outer wall face, the whole funerary corridor including the back slab and a head slab with a doorway (stele?), much of the east arm of the exedra, and an ashlar with circular hollows lying out of place.

3da896765ec82f91.text: Popular belief mixed with the clear memories of the old ancestors and confirmed by the regional Sardinian newspaper of the time “l'ISOLA”, reports the news of a small village where some tombs were found. Among the finds a figurine in the shape of a woman, (ocarina, or Mother Goddess?). MU

3db8015321eb4cf2.text:
A spring above a travertine limestone cliff produces a constant dripping down a sheer wall overhanging the bed of the Flumendosa. The continuous flow of water has created limestone concretions and allowed lush maidenhair fern to grow.

This unusual cascade falls into a pool suitable for swimming in the summer months. The dripping is heavy in winter, gentle and tranquil in summer.

3dbbbc742435b8a5.text:
Corridor nuraghe with an indefinable plan because of its irregularity, and a profile that juts out and recedes.

The main entrance, facing south-east, is rectangular (height 1.70 m – width 1.40 m) with a sturdy lintel and leads into a corridor that cannot be traversed because of the collapse; a secondary entrance, collapsed and blocked, seems to open to the south-west.

The wall face survives to a maximum height of 3.60 m with six horizontal, irregular courses; the blocks are polygonal and only roughly dressed.

3dbd0ce8038934ad.text: The area contains the remains of numerous huts belonging to a Nuragic settlement; some of them were probably reused in later, though still remote, times. Most of the huts are circular and preserve only a few traces of the original structure: some have two or three discontinuous courses, others just a single course, of polyhedral boulders of various sizes. In the north-east sector there is an enclosure containing one rectangular hut divided into two rooms.

3dc79fd99d1c04e2.text: It lies a few dozen metres from the building. It is a fine example of a single-tower nuraghe in a fairly advanced state of decay. Some features can be seen, but they appear to be relatively recent additions and therefore not attributable to the Nuragic construction, which would seem to be a sacrificial altar. Nuraghe of the sprouted site. See Càcchile. mu

3ddbd73b9b2ebe65.text: The complex nuraghe has completely collapsed and is buried. The ashlars were probably removed for the construction of a building nearby. Traces of a village lie all around.

3de303c5422b5689.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe, built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The internal chamber has collapsed in its upper part, but still survives to a height of about 3 m. Inside it two facing niches can be made out, one to the west, the other to the east. The entrance, no longer existing, must have faced south, as can be deduced from the surviving structures. The outer wall face survives to a maximum height of 4 m.

3debafb5cdc62551.text: Tholos nuraghe of single-tower type. Despite its poor state of preservation the circular plan that characterises a fairly small nuraghe can still be made out, built of polygonal blocks of local basalt of which a maximum height of about 2 m of the outer wall face survives.

3e0747a2cf02db33.text: It is a single-tower nuraghe with the characteristic shape of a truncated cone and two superimposed chambers…. Access is through the central doorway facing south-south-east; it has a central chamber with corbelled courses closing the dome, and three side cells arranged orthogonally (90°) to the entrance. A clockwise spiral staircase leads up onto the nuraghe directly above the central chamber, where the superstructure of the second chamber is still clearly visible.

3e1e021c1a497a4e.text: Pre-Nuragic/Nuragic settlement. The remains of two huts were visible until twenty years ago, but one of them was dismantled to make room for ploughs.

3e2df9c05bc0e660.text: It lies within the municipal territory of Furtei. It is recorded by Vittorio Angiu in the Geographical-Historical-Statistical-Commercial Dictionary of the States of H.M. under the entry Furtei as Nuragi-Ais.

3e33bbc38dfd7de4.text: The remains are those of a small complex nuraghe. The pottery found suggests the existence of a small proto-nuraghe that was reworked or demolished and rebuilt as a classic nuraghe.

3e34530d6b2385c9.text:
A corridor nuraghe, affected by a conspicuous collapse, built with polygonal blocks of local stone. Among the collapse of the imposing wall face, the perimeters of the upper portions of some oval chambers can be made out.

To the north-west, traces of occupation from the protohistoric and historic periods are visible, consisting of short, semi-hidden stretches of walling.

Santoni mentions it under the name nuraghe Moru Nieddu B.

3e3bdc8c7d410d6a.text: The monument is in a good state of preservation. It consists of a rectangular lintelled entrance, from which a flight of four steps leads down to a dromos. The ceiling of the dromos is covered with a flat arch of limestone slabs, while the side walls are of dry-stone construction. At the far end of the dromos is the doorway giving access to the well chamber proper, which is permanently full of water.

3e7ac9a64ae5b742.text: Natural cave with a wide entrance followed by a drop and a lower chamber. Inside, material dating to the Neolithic period and the Bronze Age with the Bonannaro culture was found.

3e8f52ec67e7c5a3.text: Domus de janas set inside a granite quarry. Multi-cellular with a double internal pillar

3eab75d4ef2fe041.text:
Situated between the Sas Pireddas area to the east and Riu Mortu to the south, the Domus di Istiolai is a hollow carved out of a single granite block, consisting of an atrium and a burial chamber with a rounded floor plan; the latter has a small, unnatural pit cut into the floor, probably used for votive offerings.

The entrance faces north-north-west, and the workmanship is very careful, especially at the entrance.

3f152310249214cf.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe of polygonal basalt ashlars. Broken lintel. Stairwell on the left from the entrance corridor. Two internal niches visible in the chamber. Traces of huts nearby.

3f1e2774ff8eec6d.text: Evolved complex nuraghe, of which only the central tower can be defined in plan.

3f3aade1fe520260.text: The Piscina Caboni archaeological complex belongs to the Circles Culture of the Arzachena territory, which until a few years ago appeared to be confined to the Gallura region. In the absence of excavation data, the site's occupation can be placed from the 3rd millennium BC.

3f4b1b6b1c03ce23.text: The nuraghe consists of a heptagonal enclosure, with a tower at each corner (still largely recognisable), and a multi-lobed bastion that is hard to interpret, with its opening facing towards Nuraghe Melas, or Fumiu.

3f613fff8c5ac5f7.text: Complex nuraghe with a ruined and buried village

3f6b5fa41cff22df.text: Single-chambered domus de janas on an isolated, emergent rock outcrop

3faab66df808feba.text: Single-tower nuraghe near Nuraghe Arrubiu. It is hidden by vegetation and a small nuraghe, Nuraghe Jana II, stands nearby on the steep slope of the hill.

3fc226fae43de540.text: This is probably a coursed giants' tomb in very poor condition: it is almost indistinguishable from the surrounding rocks. The ashlars at the sides of the central doorway, the burial corridor, the courses to the right and left of it, and part of the outer walls can still be made out. It is clear that many of the stones that made up the central body and the vault have been removed and then scattered all around the tomb or thrown down into the central corridor.

3fdbcda5347d7f4e.text: The complex consists of a proto-nuraghe, a village and a giants' tomb. The proto-nuraghe, of the "corridor" type, has a vaguely ellipsoidal plan and abuts a granite outcrop. The masonry is made of large polygonal blocks of granite.

3fdc99e0b6564629.text:
The remains of this nuraghe lie on a trachyte outcrop overlooking the Rio Tossilo, near the bend where the Birori–Cobercada road passes the nuraghe Urighe.

Unfortunately, only a few large boulders survive, arranged in a double row on just a few stretches. No survey is possible.

3ffbc4b7680e7604.text:
In the Sas Seddas area, not far from the eponymous megalithic tombs site, some ceramic finds of certain Nuragic attribution have been recovered.

No structural traces are visible at the site. The owner of the pinnetta reports that during excavation work an unspecified “channel” cut into the rock came to light, of unknown length and depth; it has since been reburied. The ceramic material consists mainly of cooking-pot fragments.

40080f30db38748f.text: The three granite menhirs stand on the slope of the saddle: the first, aniconic (length 4.25 m; width 0.98 m; thickness 0.60 m) — pointed and split into two pieces — lies on the ground; the second — re-erected in the 1970s — is of proto-anthropomorphic type with an ogival shape and a plano-convex cross-section; the third, also proto-anthropomorphic, has an ogival shape and a flattened plano-convex cross-section. Two menhirs face each other frontally, almost as if marking a passage.

401866645ef8f3c3.text: Hypogeal burial with 10 domus de janas. One worthy of thorough study, in which 10 convex cupmarks can be counted.

40201f34bd7c3ac4.text: The nuraghe, situated inside the equipped area of Girgini, is irreparably destroyed; all that is still visible is the single basal course, while various parts of the nuraghe have been used to build a wall nearby.

4036896550004b59.text:
The nuraghe is a complex type, consisting of a central tower against whose front a bastion with two secondary towers enclosing a central courtyard has been added – with a complete refacing of the structure.

The main tower (diam. 18.00 m) has an entrance oriented to the SE (width 0.80–1.20 m) surmounted by a lintel with a relieving window.

404bce428885a7c0.text: There is no direct connection, yet it is identical to the contemporary Mesopotamian temples and embodies the 'orientalising' belief in the union of heaven and earth: sacred areas on hilltops were regarded as the meeting point between humans and the divine. The temple of Monte d'Accoddi, dating back five thousand years, is a ziggurat unique in Europe for the singularity of its architectural types. It was discovered in the mid-20th century by excavating a small hill that appeared 'artificial' in the middle of a plain.

406208a0b5ba7a80.text: Hypogeic tomb consisting of two chambers. Restructured in a later period with the addition of a dolmenic corridor, it was reused in the Early Bronze Age during the Bonnanaro phase. Violated by looters.

406d95e166cc0659.text: It is a complex nuraghe that was demolished to make way for the Roman settlement.

4070e3fdb3fe099b.text: Prehistoric megalithic funerary structure. Of the part of the monument not hidden by vegetation, only two upright slabs set at right angles to each other are visible.

4073df3c34287cb8.text:
Complex nuraghe, in which several building units, visible only in part, lean against the central body, a tower of trachyte blocks with a circular plan. In the surrounding area, especially to the south-east, there are numerous Roman-period potsherds.

The Sassari urban plan (11 Dec. 2014) defines it as "Nuraghe Arcone II".

4078d0c636beb443.text: Reduced to the level of a ruin, like so many other sites. I am sorry to repeat myself, but the disappointment of finding a cultural heritage that is not protected and is not taken into account imposes on me the civic duty of publicly denouncing this neglect.

4086b201195a7d24.text: The elongated dolmen ('allée couverte') of 'Tramassumele' is probably a transitional monument between the Neolithic dolmens and the Bronze Age giants' tombs.

4095bb8c15d1e14f.text: A complex nuraghe, probably three-lobed, is in such a state of decay that it is almost impossible to identify its structural elements. Around the nuraghe, over a wide area, lie fragments of Punic and Roman pottery indicating the presence of a settlement.

40af5d750898f12e.text: Single-tower nuraghe, ruined, collapsed and overgrown with vegetation

40b265dd7020994c.text: Inside a farmstead it is in a good state of preservation and it is possible to access the top.

40b9034e88c0983d.text: This nuraghe has a partially collapsed tholos; once inside you find the stair entrance on the left and three niches with "stipetti" in the central chamber. The niche on the right, at first sight a normal niche, contains a stair leading to a mezzanine above the nuraghe entrance, with an opening from which you can see the entrance corridor. The mezzanine has a window looking onto the central chamber.

40d0ac406cd8f609.text: These two menhirs are attributable to the Ozieri Culture (4th millennium BC) and, for archaeologists, represent the Mother Goddess and the Bull God, characteristic symbols of other Sardinian prehistoric monuments such as the domus de janas, inside which they were depicted, and recurring also in Nuragic civilisation, especially in the bull-shaped form of the giants' tombs. Over time they have kept their original position and their function as votive monuments.

40df5dde9dd135cf.text: Two giants' tombs once stood in this area, one of which has been completely dismantled. In the area where the tomb presumably stood, about ten ashlars remain scattered inside a mastic thicket. Given the raised ground level, part of the tomb may still lie buried.

40f2d9e9c47278f5.text: A single-tower tholos nuraghe built of local basalt blocks; its outer wall face survives for about four to five courses with a maximum remaining height of about 2.50 m. The interior is completely filled with collapse debris. The building must have been of considerable size (diameter over 13 m) with several superimposed chambers. It now stands next to a modern building made of concrete blocks.

40f7ecbfcc005556.text: It is a vast necropolis of domus de janas, cut into a limestone outcrop. Interesting cart ruts are visible around it. Some tombs are decorated with bull's-head protomes.

412d642c432e7cfd.text: It is in very poor condition and surrounded by dense vegetation.

4133295757a2f664.text: It preserves the intact tholos covered by a large slab. It is a complex structure with a lintelled entrance and a partially collapsed stairwell. On the left an opening leads to another tower in good condition but with the ashlars fallen from the tholos inside it. To reach the upper floor one must use the side facing north-east, from which to admire the 360° panorama over the village with huts still distinguishable amid dense vegetation and among the various collapses.

41354e317df98a75.text:
The necropolis lies within a wider archaeological context that includes a village of dry-stone huts with fortifications – a few hundred metres away – and a megalithic circle (diameter 3.00 m) about 600 m distant.

The funerary complex comprises nine domus de janas with variously articulated ground plans. Tomb I is multi-chambered and has eleven successive chambers.

41504b8b582a0c69.text: It lies to the south, near the boundary with the territory of Usellus. It was presumably a simple single-tower type. It is in very poor condition, although it cannot be ruled out that part of it has been buried over the centuries by natural or human action.

41529ea8dc9e0baf.text: Up to six courses survive for over two metres in height, in large worked sandstone blocks laid and fitted to give the tower perfect circularity. The perfection of the shape is not only horizontal but also vertical. What is visible is the central tower, and it was probably a single-tower nuraghe, but since there is a high mound to the south-east of the visible tower, the presence of something else there cannot be ruled out. The visible tower must have at least four or five courses below ground, judging by the height of the mound of ashlars and earth surrounding the nuraghe.

415811cf2072db82.text: Largely buried but recognisable. Currently being recovered by the Superintendency for Archaeological Heritage, funded by the Porto Rotondo Consortium. The so-called Nuraghe, after archaeological excavation, turned out to be a Punic coastal watchtower (4th century BC).

416a2f5ee47c0b8a.text: "In a field at Luras there are giants' tombs, indeed there are four in the same plot, something I believe is more unique than rare. This site has been known for a long time; one tomb has been almost completely destroyed over the years. Both the Superintendency and the municipality have been informed, but no one has ever lifted a finger" (report).

4172679423d75a91.text: Single-tower nuraghe standing next to an agritourism farm, of which only three courses survive

41a203e06fae9fec.text: Single-tower nuraghe, surviving for only a few courses.

41b5d9954aa1c348.text: On Monte Zara there are nine domus de janas, including a pair known locally as Is ogus de monti, "the eyes of the mountain", a truly fitting nickname. A majestic staircase of about sixty steps, entirely cut into the rock, leads to the summit, from which there is a broad view of the Cagliari coast. Here lies a Nuragic sacred area dating to the 7th century BC, with an altar and several cisterns for collecting rainwater.

41bb89ecfae13e49.text: Area where Nuragic huts are found

41d9d04f62a1a59d.text: A multi-chambered domus de janas with false windows, defined by incised grooves bearing traces of red paint, and straight raised beams radiating on the ceiling to evoke a wooden roof. In the main chamber there is a sub-rectangular pilaster, of which only the lower and upper parts survive, the latter bearing an incised bull's-head protome. A Nuragic village can be sensed in the surrounding area.

420de3fa1b71163e.text:
It is a single-tower nuraghe from which much of the plain below can be seen.

The nuraghe is completely ruined and on private land, but access is not difficult.

The courses below the lintel are buried.

The tholos has completely collapsed inwards, but through the rubble the spiral staircase can be made out on the left of the entrance, and a second staircase whose course is not easy to follow.

It is still worth a short visit.

423ac6ec0b1c6e6a.text: Probably four-lobed, and one of the most imposing in the area. It consists of a central tower enclosed in a bastion with three transverse front towers. The lintel is currently visible at the level of the collapse that fills the courtyard. From inside the chamber the entrance corridor is visible. The stair leading to the upper part of the tower, which very probably had two storeys given the extent of the collapse on the north side, must have started from it.

4266f0b57e0c30e6.text: The orthostats of the large exedra, which lacks its stele, stand out. The stele lies broken on the ground in front of it. A wild olive tree has grown in the stele's place. A small piece of the exedra remains at the apsidal rear, giving an idea of the monument's size.

426b88c180a4a842.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The building is in a fair state of preservation despite the considerable alterations it has undergone. It has a surviving height of about 5 m. The outer wall face is clearly visible and better preserved on the north-east side, while on the southern side it is heavily altered and covered with vegetation. (Pruna on the I.G.M. map)

427297a36a4f8367.text: A single-tower nuraghe in excellent condition, with walls 8–9 metres high, inaccessible inside, surrounded by centuries-old oaks. There is a magnificent view as far as Gallura.

42c76f96b0b436b2.text: A burial of the Nuragic period with isodomic masonry. Of the tomb, partially demolished, the burial corridor, the apse and a few elements of the left wing of the exedra survive.

42e7c676d02159c0.text:
Nuraghe now completely demolished, of which a single course of part of the foundation remains.

Among the evolved nuraghi of Serrenti, this one at Nuraxi and the one at Bruncu Siliqua belong to the concentric-addition type. Nuraxi is four-lobed, similar in form to Su Nuraxi at Barumini (Lilliu's Lower Nuragic I phase), while Bruncu Siliqua has a central tower 14 m in diameter and at least three secondary towers.

42ef9cfb8a9a487f.text: Probably dismantled after the nearby villas were built.

42f404f558829541.text:
The archaeological area of Cuccuru Sa Cresia Arta, in the territory of Soleminis, lies on a hillock about 40 metres above the level of the farm track that gives access to it, roughly 250 metres south-west of Soleminis, in the hinterland of the Gulf of Cagliari.

The archaeological excavation, funded by the municipal administration, forms part of a wider programme to enhance the archaeological areas of the municipality of Soleminis, agreed long ago with the Superintendency.

4306897c75dbf215.text: Remains of structures belonging to a single-tower tholos nuraghe. The building, now almost completely destroyed, consists of a few blocks from the basal course and part of what must have been the left jamb of the entrance, oriented to the south. The building material is local basalt. Nearby, heaps of stone material from the nuraghe's structures can be seen.

432afe4ed89b7c75.text: The monument, built of granite boulders and preserved to a maximum height of 3 m, has a lintelled entrance leading to a corridor with a flat-lintelled roof, passable only for a short stretch because of a collapse.

43639c75be57b7d8.text: The site is completely ruined and buried. The existence of a village, probably Nuragic or pre-Nuragic, over a wide area is evident. Apart from a few spreads of ashlars, only a few walls of a hut or a nuraghe are visible.

436b9db56b8cb563.text: Single-tower nuraghe built of basalt. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

438c85345f112db2.text: From the top of a small hill it overlooks the surrounding territory, where two water mills once stood on a small drop in the Rio Iscanneddu. It is a single-tower nuraghe with a few basal courses of medium-sized stones, only partly dressed. Its name undoubtedly dates from the medieval period when monastic orders settled in the area (10th–11th centuries).

439ecd3bb982c510.text: It is a singular corridor nuraghe, complex and irregular, composed of three large megalithic bodies set side by side and various secondary structures. It has a surviving height of over 6 metres and was built on the outcropping rock with polyhedral basalt blocks laid dry in polygonal masonry. The nuraghe can be dated, in its first construction phase, to the Early Middle Bronze Age.

43a0fee6b414e94f.text: Three metres high. Broken transversely at mid-height and chipped at the base by the impact of a mechanical ploughshare, it tapers at the top into a kind of smooth, sub-oval mask. The design continues linearly along the sides, and at the top appears almost crowned by a distinct pair of bull's horns. The monument is unique on the Island, and perhaps in the sculptural art of continental megalithism as well.

43a69580d87a07fd.text: A heavily ruined cyclopean giants' tomb, of which part of the corridor and the lintel remain. The monument is of the type known as "coursed", consisting of a burial built in courses of superimposed blocks with an elongated rectangular burial chamber, preceded by the entrance, followed by a dromos, and ending in an apse.

43a711757861ccaf.text: Although reduced to a ruin, a few basic elements can be observed that reveal the structure of the monument. The cist is built of various fairly squared stones on which some covering elements rest. The presence of the exedra, composed of stones set on edge, also remains clear, although some of them have fallen to the ground.

43b0722bf661067c.text: It is a complex nuraghe, consisting of a central tower and four attached towers that are not very prominent. The central tower is the only one in good condition, with two superimposed floors, the lower one intact and the upper one missing its tholos roof. On the upper floor there is a large window facing the entrance side.

43b32e1b5d0c10f0.text:
Nuragic settlement, attested by a demolished single-tower nuraghe and Middle Bronze Age pottery.

Decontextualised and illegible site, although the recovery of the materials found on the spot, the relevant documentation, and the contextualisation of the whole are desirable.

43e37ff6ef6bb05f.text: This is a site where the ruins of two single-tower nuraghi (huts) are found; of both, the base survives to a maximum height of one metre and a diameter of about 6

44002dd70b30f08d.text: Only a few stretches of the first basal course, in pink trachyte, are visible of the monument, which is in very poor condition.

443bc1c3b50a819a.text: The Battizzone nuraghe is a three-lobed type, with towers joined by an outer wall that forms an internal courtyard at the front. At present the courtyard and the lateral towers are completely filled with collapse debris, making access to the central tower impossible; the entrance lintel is partly visible. A corridor is also visible in the courtyard area, which probably served as the entrance to one of the lateral towers and is notable for its considerable height.

444f2ff2faa1e407.text: Structures belonging to a single-tower tholos nuraghe. The nuraghe, built of local polygonal basalt blocks, survives in its outer wall face to a maximum height of just over 4 m. The inner chamber has collapsed and the remaining part is filled with the same collapse material. The entrance, identifiable to the south, is lintelled with a height of 1.20 m. The workmanship of the lintel and jambs is fairly rough, with barely dressed blocks.

44683f91e1475a87.text: A tancato nuraghe, with a central tower and an added tower linked by bastions. Traces of a settlement. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

44761aa2a6cacbfb.text: Unfortunately, the destructive action of treasure hunters has endangered most of the sites in the municipality of Chiaramonti. The loss of further historical and artistic evidence impoverishes its cultural heritage even more. The legacy left by our ancestors must be part of our history to help us better understand the path to follow for the future.

44837832b82bffdd.text: Nuraghe partially destroyed by quarry work. The site is of particular interest because of the discovery in the area of three swords, with pistil-shaped blades and a central rib, and a tang to which two wings with holes for fixing the handle are attached, recovered during the 1950s. This typically Iberian type finds comparisons with specimens from the territory of Baunei, and with the sword resting on the shoulder of the “Warrior” of Uta.

449a4fea021d77d1.text: Inside there is a lintelled corridor, a semicircular niche, the staircase leading to the upper floor, and the central chamber; the latter, originally roofed with a tholos but now uncovered, has the classic circular plan with three niches arranged in a cross. The outer wall, up to 4 m high, is built of medium-to-large trachyte boulders.

449af16923ad1f24.text: A badly ruined complex nuraghe whose layout is hard to make out

449dc0bdf48e6b3e.text:
The necropolis comprises 18 domus de janas, all multi-chambered with up to 12 rooms, richly adorned with pilasters, panels, false doors, bull's-head protomes, chevrons and other spiral or wolf's-tooth motifs.

Seven tombs reproduce pre-Nuragic dwellings: single- or double-pitched roofs, horizontal or sloping, with or without central beams and side rafters, supported or not by pillars, all carved in the rock. One has an architectural façade with a carved arched stele.

44afed795e140f3a.text: Nuraghe destroyed by agricultural mechanisation, no longer visible today

44b0fe21de75cbc6.text: Corridor nuraghe, also known as Runalgalva.

44c31a3a2ed72061.text: Unlikely remains of a nuragic site.

44c421e17e12b65d.text: Structures belonging to a single-tower tholos nuraghe. Hard to make out in the dense vegetation, the nuraghe preserves about three basal courses of large polygonal basalt blocks. The rest of the structure has collapsed and the debris fills the lower part. Despite the poor condition, the remains can be interpreted as a small simple nuraghe.

450bb250ccac2834.text: At the foot of the hill, once used as a stone quarry, inside the built-up area of Monastir, in the south-western part, near Via Progresso no. 80, a giants' tomb was found during an archaeological excavation, which yielded numerous human bone remains.

452c8b7e7d12b5e9.text: The probable Nuragic village occupies an area that extends from the edges of the plateau down the NE slope of the mountain. There are remains of several circular huts of which one or two courses and the collapsed structure in the centre survive. The best preserved is an oval hut, very probably reused in more recent times. Enclosures with cyclopean walls are present.

453c90dce40fbaae.text: Situated on a promontory overlooking the municipal road that leads from Villaurbana to the locality of S'utturu su cardu. The tower is largely ruined and inaccessible.

45509bd57a02c0f2.text: Built on the edge of a trachyte bastion, overlooking a natural route, about a hundred metres north of a giants' tomb situated downhill, the monument is a single-tower nuraghe with a stair in the corridor and a chamber flanked by three niches. To the west, in the sector not naturally defended by the vertical rock face, are the remains of a massive outer wall, while the rocky profile on which the tower stands also appears to be reinforced by coursed wall structures.

45535fc8ce5955e4.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal basalt blocks. Despite the dense vegetation the circular plan can be made out, and about five courses, though quite irregular, are visible on the north-west side. The entrance, on the east, has a collapsed right jamb and a lintel set at an angle.

45590c0649438da4.text: It is a complex nuraghe that is not easy to interpret, consisting of a main tower and the remains of two other probable towers. The nuraghe is built of roughly worked sandstone and schist blocks laid in polygonal masonry. On the west/south-west side the walling incorporates a rocky spur.

455cd9030ec9515e.text: A burial of the Nuragic period, almost completely destroyed. The ground plan of the tomb and a few worked ashlars are visible on the ground. In particular, two monolithic arches belonging to the apsidal part of the tomb lie a short distance away.

4568c3e8d90dcc3e.text: It takes its name from the family that owns the land on which it stands. A completely ruined nuraghe, certainly multi-lobed. It lies 600 m from the royal complex of Barumini.

456a5fd1e5c4b81c.text: During excavation it revealed two (perhaps three) sacred wells opening onto a large open paved area, and a hut whose paving has a hole through which flowing water can be seen.

457b38d75045ece3.text: Hardly visible or recognisable, completely engulfed by mastic and rockrose. Numerous large trachyte boulders are present.

45a2f98240b6d5cb.text: It appears destroyed and covered by thickets of brambles and thorny bushes.

45b4dbb0ffb279f6.text: The monument, of simple type, stands at the edge of a small clearing on a granite outcrop that is incorporated into the walls for long stretches. Its outer plan is vaguely elliptical, with a lintelled entrance leading into a corridor 3.50 m long; to the left of this corridor another lintelled doorway presumably gives access to a staircase, or at any rate to a beaten floor that in ancient times must have led to a terraced space.

45d063865911b5e8.text: Complex nuraghe, four towers arranged in a cross around a large courtyard. It consists of a central tower, about 3 m high, linked to two secondary towers by a curtain wall. Some studies describe the complex as a four-lobed structure with concentric additions.

45d96ccba04c1020.text: It is also known by the place name of the adjacent land, "sas Damas", which I believe is the older and more appropriate one, since it is closely linked with sa Domos de sas Fadas which by extension becomes Dama = lady. It was found by chance during extension work on a house, now the Agriturismo Sas Damas Doneddu-Murgia, and was rich in grave goods that were donated to the local museum in Perfugas SS.

45f2b87a2b800f2a.text:
This is a three-lobed nuraghe of particular importance because of its position, size and state of preservation. It lies in the Marghine sub-region, in the territory of the municipality of Bortigali, at an altitude of 785 metres, from which a vast portion of central Sardinia can be seen.

The site stands at the foot of Monte Cuguruttu (867 metres), in a position that ranges from the nearby Monte Santu Padre (1,025 metres) to the more distant mountains

45f86053e1d08373.text: Only the stele and part of the exedra of this burial have survived.

461ecc5251b21d18.text: Complex nuraghe of the four-lobed type. Traces of a central tower and three added towers with the bastion are visible, of which only the foundations survive in very poor condition. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

4653a2d52104b93e.text: Complex nuraghe with a central tower, a refacing with two additional towers. All around are the remains of what must have been the village.

46695eddf95f9043.text: A settlement of which few traces remain, situated on the hill facing Monte Cannas in a place not recommended for visits because it was affected in the 1930s and 1940s by quarrying activity with unfenced dangerous areas. The settlement can be dated between the Bronze Age and the Roman period, passing through the Nuragic culture.

466b848fb94e3e14.text:
A single-tower tholos nuraghe standing in the middle of the dense holm-oak and downy-oak woodland of the Sos Paris area, Codinazza locality. Four basal courses built of large polygonal blocks of local basalt are visible, reaching a maximum surviving height of about 2.50 m. The base diameter of the nuraghe is about 13 m.

The inner chamber has collapsed in its upper part and the surviving portion is covered by a substantial fill of collapse debris.

469c415559be83dc.text: Complex nuraghe of which two towers are still visible.

46ae43563a3ec92a.text: A single-tower nuraghe in relatively good condition with its tholos intact. It stands on the boundary between two properties and can only be reached through a privately owned vegetable garden.

46baf12ec3bf7a27.text: The domus de janas of Bonorchis is a single-chamber tomb, very small, with a wide, well-finished entrance hatch.

46e61f61863ac3c4.text: A heavily ruined nuraghe standing in the middle of the town

46f2805add5ae4f9.text: The Museddu necropolis lies within the Petroglifi Park. It consists of 18 domus de janas with simple ground plans: a quadrangular cell preceded by a small antechamber, or two or three cells arranged longitudinally.

4708cc4a0d698846.text: The necropolis lies in the municipality of Usini. It consists of 3 domus de janas, one with bull's-head protomes and one reused as a hypogeic church.

47562430129750df.text:
Sacred well, situated inside the 13th-century Romanesque chapel dedicated to Saint Anthony of Padua.

Access is through a hatch to a flight of steps leading down to the sacred well, which lies perfectly positioned beneath the Christian altar.

475fbc1687bfb2ec.text: Apparently a single-tower nuraghe. It may belong to the category of "unfinished nuraghi".

476babb9f3ef81e6.text: The nuraghe is located in the COMUNE DI MURAVERA. The entire upper complex, four-lobed with some semi-quadrangular towers, extends along a north-west/south-east axis of about 53 m and an east/west axis of about 20–25 m. The outer curtain wall can be traced only along its eastern stretch and a short southern section: it is an imposing structure with a broad wall thickness that served to close the gaps in the pre-existing natural rock bastion.

476d2ad653c9a359.text: The Punic settlement arose on the site of an earlier Nuragic village, since the structures brought to light by excavation show the reuse of several structural elements of the indigenous settlement. A megalithic enclosure and a nuraghe that was adapted and incorporated into a wall circuit, which in turn appears to be surrounded by a fortified line, are currently visible.

477d09648d89619b.text: Four-lobed nuraghe Alvu, built of squared white stones, with numerous hut bases around it. It shows constructional details in the interlocking of the corner masonry not found in other nuraghi.

477e66a822138930.text: It lies in the municipality of Lodine (NU). A single-tower nuraghe reduced to a heap of ruins. It is situated very close to Sos Nuragheddos 1. Further information can be found in the book *Archeologia in Barbagia* by M.A. Mele.

477f16cae0c51c2c.text: The village that arose in the subsequent Late Bronze Age phase (1365–1200 BC) is characterised by numerous wells dug next to dwellings, some of them sunken into the ground, others provided with a masonry plinth. At present, after the recent excavations, the area has been entirely covered over.

478ae26b633f9ab1.text: Ruined proto-nuraghe covered by dense vegetation

479c023b2950d1f1.text: Remains of the nuraghe Sos Iscaledos, badly destroyed.

47a9825ba1c831f3.text:
The complex stands on the summit of Monte Colbu overlooking the plain of Olbia.

The nuraghe, surrounded by a wall that originally must have exceeded 5 metres in height and has two entrances (one to the north and one to the south), is a single-tower type. The entrance corridor contains a small niche and part of the stairwell that led to the terrace of the upper floor. The central chamber, which has a small well, was covered by a tholos.

47b933232bdf8731.text: Single-tower nuraghe near Nuraghe Arrubiu. It is hidden by vegetation and another nuraghe, Nuraghe Jana, stands nearby on the steep slope of the hill.

47cd6e1d94784cde.text: Nuraghe in excellent condition, though enveloped in vegetation. The internal tholos is intact.

47d6391e9db51e6e.text: Single-tower nuraghe, it marks the boundary between the municipal territories of Villamar and Pauli Arbarei.

47dfca3139fdd112.text: Remains of a single-tower nuraghe built of basalt.

480ad095cbed587b.text: Columnar basalts are majestic basalt formations whose presence indicates submarine eruptive activity or the existence of ancient, now extinct volcanoes in the area. Is Aruttas Santas are a typical example of these basalt formations; we are on Monte Arci in the territory of Villaurbana.

483369ec5dbd5e04.text: It is in poor condition. The closing slab is on display in the Sassari museum, but the tomb is wrongly called Mesu e Rios.

485244015a104d65.text:
The Nuragic village-sanctuary of Abini is one of the most famous and important in Nuragic Sardinia.

It consists of numerous huts and a sacred well protected by an enclosure. The huts are predominantly circular in plan.

48535ab8b8715c3e.text: It is an unfinished nuraghe, remarkable for the size of the lintel that spans the entrance.

488678acdcda55a2.text: At the level of a large ruin, a few polygonal blocks from the basal circles are present, sometimes vaguely dressed. The presence of the main entrance facing south-east is evident. The surrounding area is rich in ancient traces and finds. An interesting sheepfold that may date back a few centuries.

4898294e27b3e2c7.text: Remains of a domus de janas

48bfc2469b1278b1.text: Hidden from view by a granite outcrop, the nuraghe appears half-destroyed. A menhir stands on the spot, from which the settlement and the region probably took their name. A village is likely present.

48c0eb75e1307d5e.text: It is a corridor nuraghe that is hard to survey because its very poor state of preservation and the collapsed rubble prevent it from being read.

48cb34d99c98d1bc.text: It is periodically partly submerged by the water level of the Omodeo artificial reservoir.

48ddcce21cfd8d46.text: At Florinas, amid cultivated fields, we find this small proto-nuraghe called Urzeghe, "characterised by a body of parallel corridors leaning against a small circular tower."

4933310016fb9bd5.text: Three metres of corridor, the headrest to the west, a row of outer blocks, particularly curious is a block with a large cupmark. There would be another stretch of corridor but it is not accessible, let alone documentable, because of trees.

4947399464e6234e.text: Its name comes from the place-name of the land, which in turn refers to the muzzle of the Bull god present in the domus de janas not far away, but also very probably to the more recent medieval or even nineteenth-century period, from the noise made by the waterfall of the same name in winter. “Su mummuttu de s'abba cando sicche addobat dae punta de sas roccas aintro de sa peschina, faghet unu murrunzu mannu. mu

496e40a3934b8373.text:
The corridor tomb has been attributed to the Nuragic period.

The pottery found during the surveys is of Roman Imperial and Late Antique date. Repeated surface surveys have yielded pottery and bricks, probably belonging to a necropolis.

49a6881df945ad6f.text:
Three hypogeic tombs on the slope of a small rise (244 m). The first has a single elliptical oven-shaped cell. The second consists of an atrium, an antechamber and a quadrangular burial chamber with a niche on the right-hand wall. On the left a wider raised cell with two small niches and a relief decoration depicting two human faces.

The third tomb, further downhill than the other two, is of the more regular type with atrium, antechamber and cell.

49bc1faf89643f00.text:
At Sa Turricula the first phase of the Nuragic civilisation is recognised. The site comprises the nuraghe, the village and, a short distance away, two giants' tombs, a well, and the Funtan'e Casu dolmen.

Sa Turricula does not allow an easy reading of the structures. It is choked with vegetation but, once you reach the top of the hill on which it stands, you enjoy a breathtaking view over the whole surrounding territory.

The nuraghe probably belongs to the corridor nuraghe type.

Nearby are

49d50868707bb680.text: The Bau 'e Tanca nuraghe at Talana stands at an altitude of 1122 metres above sea level and is surrounded by a village, of which the courses of some huts and the piles of stones used to build them are still visible. Interesting for the unusual symmetry of the clusters that make up the village.

49d8f3ac1aa70ef4.text: Very little of the nuragic tower remains. The lintel and three courses. Around it lie the ruins of the small village.

49d901b80c02bb51.text: The structure recorded here is of unclear form; it may be a small complex nuraghe built over an earlier proto-nuraghe. Ceramic fragments of the Nur I-IIA/B phases are visible around it. It could also be a small mixed nuraghe.

49e0e7768858b8e5.text: A short distance from the Su Hannavagliu stream and a few hundred metres from the Luduruju nuraghe.

49fa4a5a18aafce2.text:
A nuraghe, a menhir, a wall, and finally a domus de janas with a façade.

Ivano Sotgiu, in love with his own village, was out gathering asparagus when he reported this site where, within a couple of hundred metres, there are monuments dating from the Abealzu culture, between 2700 and 2400 BC, perhaps earlier with the menhir, the Early Bronze Age with the Nuragic wall, the Bronze Age and up to the Roman period, marked by the probable tombs.

4a368c8e43ac695d.text: The site has yielded a two-chambered hypogeum burial cut into the southern wall of the plateau, whose upper part shows a slab of natural rock that, seen from the front, gives the monument a megalithic appearance; a small dolmen; a giants' tomb; a spring; a megalithic wall with traces of later adaptations; and a corridor nuraghe. The corridor wall includes boulders of considerable size, some of which bear linear incisions.

4a3c8687dce3bea3.text:
It stands on a small rise from which the surrounding view can be appreciated. It is a single-tower nuraghe about 11 metres high with a tholos roof. Built of large blocks of dark basalt which, together with yellow lichens, give it its characteristic colouring (hence the name: in Sardinian nieddu means black, dark).

The tower has two openings: an entrance at the base, still partly buried, and, almost at the top, a large window.

4a558d6c0f23a3ca.text: Remains of about twelve huts and a perimeter wall.

4a5686e39fe22e04.text: The Prunaiola dolmen is a funerary archaeological monument situated on a small plateau in the territory of Torralba, in north-western Sardinia. It lies a short distance from the Carlo Felice state road 131 and in the immediate vicinity of the Cabu Abbas giants' tomb and two domus de janas, in an area rich in archaeological evidence documenting the continuity of human settlement from prehistory.

4a8a56abf5529198.text:
It consists of a series of chambers opening onto the western flank of a low limestone hill. The main nucleus, the result of various transformations relating to different phases of use over the centuries, comprises three large cells linked together and arranged in succession from north to south.

The chambers look out onto a narrow terrace; the rock face has two narrow flights of steps by which the plateau above can be reached.

4a94df7e259508fc.text: A giants' tomb completely ruined, lacking its most significant elements. The burial corridor survives.

4a963b471b8faf0c.text: It lies in the municipality of Putifigari (SS). A hypogeal tomb (domus de janas) with a deeply buried entrance, about two metres below the level of the road and the surrounding ground. It consists of a main pillared cell and three smaller lateral cells. The double-pitched roof is still remarkable.

4ab18d99e272d056.text: Part of the nuraghe has been altered and adapted to build a pinnetto.

4ab3285a2a339abc.text: The monument, subcircular in plan, stands almost at the top of a steep, wooded rise, currently used for pasture. Three blocks of the left-hand doorjamb survive, oriented to the north, and two of the right-hand one. The nuraghe is built of roughly dressed medium and large granite blocks in rough polygonal masonry with frequent use of wedges.

4adb4b1c4161cc09.text: About 200 m from the second giants' tomb there are buildings of Nuragic origin whose function cannot be determined, mainly because of later alterations carried out at different times (some of them recent) and the lack of archaeological study. The surviving structures of probable Nuragic origin consist of an enclosure with cyclopean walls built of roughly dressed boulders, and the remains of two probable huts.

4adc98a445b6d976.text: A ruined and buried nuraghe whose structure cannot be determined. Partly under a public reservoir.

4b0789aa767d435f.text: The monument, also known in the literature as “Pranu Nuracci”, is a complex polylobed nuraghe. Two lateral towers, the perimeter walls and the central tower survive. The south-western lateral tower and the northern one survive to a height of about 4–5 courses. The central tower, in good condition, has 12 courses of polygonal masonry with large, barely dressed blocks, a south-east entrance with a monolithic lintel.

4b0ccafc5d314072.text: The dolmen consists of four surviving orthostatic slabs enclosing a polygonal space (1.86 x 1.40 m) bounded above by a large, fairly roughly dressed slab of varying thickness and with a rounded profile.

4b1e53a8412bdd5a.text: Single-tower nuraghe in the territory of Oniferi, situated a few dozen metres from the necropolis of Sas Concas, which lies in the valley below near the stream. Only a few blocks remain visible.

4b20ae9dbb756720.text: The nuraghe, built of schist, is constructed with quadrangular blocks laid in regular courses, set in a layer of ochre-coloured clay. It consists of a main tower and an adjoining chamber joined to the first by a short curtain wall. In the inner wall face of the tower various voids can be seen that must have served to anchor a wooden mezzanine. At the foot of this nuraghe lie the huts of the Nuragic village.

4b59d49cec13321e.text: It is a domus de janas necropolis overlooking the Gulf of Carbonara at the locality Spiaggia del Riso. Of the whole necropolis only one tomb has remained intact: it is a truly fascinating monument that projects the territory back in time by about six thousand years.

4b69da1c8d3c5b17.text: In the fissure there is a staircase of squared basalt stone, one metre wide, composed of three flights, two visible and the third covered by debris, separated by two landings. All the steps consist of two squared basalt blocks cut 'to measure' and laid with a wedge-shaped block inserted between them. Some have circular hollows cut into them, interpretable as cup-marks with a lustral function; on others, mammillary reliefs stand out.

4b83b9c4d583fa39.text: The nuraghe is completely ruined; only a few courses survive amid the dense Mediterranean scrub.

4b869257cb45ac29.text:
A complex nuraghe hidden by a conspicuous collapse. A large village of huts to the south-south-west is entirely covered by scrub. On the southern edge of the village a building with curvilinear walls of squared blocks may date to the Nuragic period.

On the hill to the west of the main rise, a Nuragic building, previously thought to be a giants' tomb, appears in fact to be a circular structure ("tower-hut?").

4b95e982e0dd7c7c.text: The front part has collapsed, while the rear part is fairly well preserved. The rectangular burial corridor is bounded on one side by a slab, while the side walls consist of a series of blocks supporting small stones. The surviving height is about 130 cm. The entire upper surface is covered with a myriad of cupmarks (small cavities with magic-sacred functions).

4bc158a807d60116.text: It preserves the tholos intact except for the closing slab.

4c04b38b2dbd5038.text: The Asusa nuraghe, built around 1300 BC, consists of two towers looking onto a courtyard and has its main entrance to the east. In one of the interior rooms archaeologists uncovered a circular ring belonging to a well or cistern that has yet to be explored.

4c054f99ea10c8fe.text: The dolmen stands on a basalt outcrop on the northern bank of the Riu Coraggiu, about 200 metres north of the Nuraghe Nela. The burial chamber is now bounded by three orthostats, on which a large covering slab rests.

4c0c22c54a3f9bae.text: In a total state of ruin, it takes its name from the place-name of the land or of the landowner. mu

4c23601116c8c738.text:
The tower, circular in plan (diam. 10.65 x 10.12 m), survives to a maximum height of 4.40 m on the north-east side, while the minimum is 3 m on the south-west. The masonry consists of trachyte blocks roughly dressed with some care and laid in fairly regular horizontal courses. The wall thickness is 3.30 m on the north-east, 4 m on the south and 3 m on the north-west.

The interior of the nuraghe is entered through a rectangular doorway (h. 1.70 m – w. 0.90 m), lintelled, oriented to the south-east and slightly splayed inwards.

4c3298150b0d7221.text: The necropolis consists of two multi-chambered domus de janas cut into the limestone, plus a third one that was started (only the dromos was cut) and never finished. One of the two tombs opens in the rock face near the cemetery, while the second, together with the unfinished tomb, opens on the edge of the plateau to the south-east.

4c4b11526e6da6b4.text: It is a fine example of a single-tower nuraghe where the tholos is still intact. Continuing up the staircase, which winds clockwise, certain constructional features emerge that are similar to other sites in the territory of Chiaramonti — a distinction made today that did not exist three thousand years ago, since the territory was a contiguous extension of that of Ploaghe. m.u

4c56e72cac969fc6.text:
Practically unknown and inside a private property. The monument, excavated and cleared in recent times, is perfectly legible and defined in all its components: the corridor, which preserves its intact floor of granite slabs, the apse and the two wings of the exedra.

It lies to the west of Santa Reparata.

The structure is built on a very slight rise with the exedra clearly raised. A linear bench is present in the front part of the exedra, a feature often found in other giants' tombs.

4c65193efb369b76.text: The nuraghe Maletta II, built at 264 m above sea level, is now almost completely destroyed by the continuous agricultural work that has affected the whole area, one of the most intensively exploited in the Sinnai countryside, and preserves only a very fragmentary stretch of the basal course.

4c6bf3553383f463.text: Single-tower nuraghe on a hilltop with only a few courses of stone preserved. From this nuraghe you can clearly see the Nuraghe su Stiddiu, Nuraghe su Bobboi, and the hill where the Nuraghe di Crabili Simoni stood, with the megalithic altar at its foot. A few hundred metres from the nuraghe lies the Mitza Aramu spring.

4c7605f05ffbb555.text: In photographs the Longu nuraghe looks like an imposing single-tower nuraghe. Unfortunately there is no detailed description.

4c777ef88695cc21.text: Nissardi in 1901 (map in G. Pinza's volume) marked a giants' tomb a little to the south-west of the Paule Tolta nuraghe: a nuraghe that actually lies inside the airport perimeter.

4c83f385faf0c067.text: These are the ruins of a structure built of large blocks, completely buried; only a few remains appear on the surface. Some years ago a farm vehicle removed one of the large surface boulders, revealing an opening through which it was possible to enter the structure. It is, in all probability, a silo for water storage or provisions. The shape is a truncated cone with a bulge at the bottom. Diameter at the base 1.55 m; height 2.73 m.

4cc88cf14028a810.text: Until the middle of the last century, remains of several nuraghi could be seen, along with many basalt ashlars of various shapes and sizes.

4cdaef2525334e44.text: A ruined nuraghe for which no description exists

4ce179c7b7b16258.text:
A burial of the Nuragic period in very poor condition.

Of the isodomic type, the corridor is legible and the exedra only with difficulty.

4d01cd06ceed12b9.text: A tholos nuraghe, presumably single-tower, although its poor state of preservation and the dense vegetation cover prevent a full reading of the monument. Built of polygonal basalt blocks, the outer wall face on the west side survives to a maximum height of about 3.50 m. The nuraghe has been heavily robbed, as can be deduced from the heaps of large blocks on the plateau to the north of it.

4d0289164148b3a2.text: A circle of large boulders but without a foundation, so it must be considered doubtful. For the time being this structure has been classified as a "Nuraghe" and assigned the function of a "Meda" for the entrance to the cove.

4d436e46fc4a8194.text:
The building, one of the best known on the island, is a complex type, consisting of a central tower and a four-lobed bastion with an open courtyard.

It was defended by an outer wall, recorded by General Della Marmora, which is now barely legible on the ground surface.

The bastion (height 8.80 m) incorporates four towers linked by curtain walls with a concave-convex profile, built of roughly dressed basalt blocks laid in horizontal courses.

4d4aef7ac582a335.text: Very little of the tomb remains. There are five baetyls, located in the territory of the municipality of Dualchi (NU).

4d6751270a673507.text: The summit of Monte 'E Mesu is a small oval plateau. At one end stands the eponymous nuraghe, built almost sheer on the rock. On a small natural terrace below the nuraghe there are traces of huts and other evidence of the Nuragic period, such as boulders with bull-shaped carvings, lying in a state of total abandonment and looking, one might even say, weary of the multi-millennial life they carry on their shoulders.

4d9eb5370002b8af.text: In 1942 a stonemason from Donori, while breaking up a block of granite to obtain building stones, found 53 coins beneath the block bearing the effigy of Emperor Antoninus Pius, that of Trajan, of Empress Faustina and other rulers with indecipherable names. The nuraghe must have been very large, because despite being considerably damaged and covered by shrubs and various stones gathered nearby, the quantity of scattered boulders is considerable.

4db8ce30e2a9edbd.text: Nuraghe of uncertain type built on the tip of a limestone hill marked by karstic grottoes used from the Neolithic onwards. Three courses of stones up to 25 metres long are visible.

4db938a974ca561d.text: Largely collapsed, overgrown with vegetation, not easily explored. The central chamber, the entrance, and the circular corridor remain clearly visible.

4dc3f12f543471c9.text: The Seruci Nuragic complex consists of a multi-lobed nuraghe with five towers and a central courtyard, and a village of about a hundred huts covering five hectares in a strategic position overlooking the Gulf of Leone. The village is organised into small quarters with streets and central squares. Of particular interest is a hut of remarkable size, probably used for meetings of the heads of families.

4df9cca66f4864c9.text: The tomb is completely covered in vegetation; a few aligned blocks can be glimpsed among the grass. The presence of another tomb on the site is reported, to which a pile of blocks glimpsed among the vegetation may belong.

4e161fa9c0595a4f.text:
These are three hypogea cut into a trachyandesite outcrop inside a private property.

Domus I has a short dromos entrance, an antechamber that opens onto two successive cells along the same axis. The Domus has no particular decoration.

Domus II and III: the first is full of water, but its wide entrance can be admired; the second is completely overgrown with vegetation to the point that it was not possible to explore it.

There are probably other hypogea.

4e223b5ffb9d58b7.text: The tomb is not in a good state of preservation. However, the large stele can still be seen in its original position, of which only the lower, trapezoidal part survives, while the arched top is missing; a fragment of it can be seen fallen inside the chamber. Practically nothing of the exedra survives. The burial chamber, also poorly preserved, is built of slabs set vertically into the ground.

4e359c4ea1c5967b.text: Complex nuraghe, collapsed and of which only a few buried courses remain, where a transverse addition followed the original tower.

4e579a18dbf74d7c.text: The Nuraghe Santu Juanni or San Giovanni lies about 1 km north of Villaurbana in the territory of Siamanna. It is a single-tower nuraghe built of roughly dressed basalt blocks. The entrance corridor is lintelled and leads to a chamber where the tholos is still intact. The upper floor, now collapsed, is overgrown with shrubs and prickly pears.

4e7e65aeb9f77665.text: In 1968, about 150 metres from the entrance, the Treasure Chamber was found: hundreds of bowls were stacked in three large piles. A broken stalagmitic column served as an altar: a bronze tripod, a votive boat, several daggers, bracelets and rings were placed on it. Beside the altar was the hearth, where animal bones were found, evidence of ritual sacrifices. The C14 dating falls between 820 and 730 BC.

4e8adec710a688e5.text: A ruined nuraghe whose shape and dimensions cannot be determined

4e95a7921ae1afda.text: The Aeddos nuraghe stands at 368 metres above sea level on the Sa Serra plateau of Orotelli. The first phase dates to the Bronze Age (1300–900 BC). The nuraghe has a trilobate structure, composed of a central tower and three concentric towers. It is built of large polyhedral ashlars of local granite laid in irregular courses. The height of the visible masonry from the central tower reaches 8.30 metres.

4e9638da32383021.text: The giants' tomb of “Sa Sedda 'e Sena”, known as 'Sa Tanchitta', has the peculiarity of having been built in the Nuragic period by adapting a much older funerary structure, dating to the Early Bronze Age (1800–1600 BC) of the allée couverte type. Of this funerary monument, the burial chamber, about 10 metres long, can still be observed today.

4eada115a6cc4670.text: It is a tomb with an architectural façade, heavily altered and reused in the medieval and modern periods, in which the features of domus de janas and giants' tombs are combined.

4eb7dadd599d399b.text: Nuraghe destroyed by the Scolopi Fathers in 1730 for the construction of some buildings in Chia. Building work in the 1980s erased every remaining trace.

4ee46e53453e5fdd.text: A different cluster of tombs scattered along the islet

4ee4888c8f67703f.text: The monument, considered a proto-nuraghe, is in fact a transitional structure between the corridor nuraghe and the tholos nuraghe. The complex consists of a central tower with a terrace, a bastion, and various huts both inside and outside an outer wall. It now lies beneath a viaduct; indeed, only a few centimetres separate the last surviving stone courses of the monument from the concrete beams that support the road.

4efc11f3400f8123.text: "Domus de giana of Su Adu 'e Sa iana, a short distance from the village, at the ford of Rio Minori, was in the past a hypogean cell, which disappeared many years ago, but the village elders still remember it. On land belonging to Pasqua Sanna, daughter of Isidoro"

4f09ceb5524d0737.text: The building material of the structure, of which the top of central tower A and some wall profiles emerge for a few metres, is basaltic andesite. A dense thicket of mastic covers the exposed part of the structure, showing a curvilinear profile of the bastion which, from satellite images, appears to be at least multi-lobed owing to the addition of at least two secondary bodies.

4f0a772893a434d6.text: Irregular-plan complex nuraghe. Its perimeter wall face encloses a single expanse of collapse debris, from which remains of the central tower emerge to the west. The complex is enclosed by a megalithic outer wall that protects it on the west and, in part, on the north.

4f35423aa7b35eca.text: A nuraghe immersed in vegetation, ruined and partly buried. The entrance is visible but buried almost up to the lintel.

4f3a1d96c07bd529.text: Nuragic spring included in a small municipal park, cut into the rock

4f4d3c2a731bf362.text: The nuraghe was in close topographical and cultural connection with the Biristeddi giants' tombs, which lie about 250 metres from it.

4f4da29b7d9c8928.text:
Zinnuri, in a municipal rural park characterised by centuries-old olive and wild olive trees and a rural shelter. Around the spring there is a picnic area with wooden tables and benches and a car park.

The nuraghe Zinnuri and the spring of the same name are found here.

4f535f9bb38640b8.text: At the western end of the elongated Carronca Simoi ridge, beneath the ruin of a small rectangular building, scant remains of a probable nuraghe can be seen; about 20 metres to the east of it, some stone blocks appear to belong to a round Nuragic hut.

4fa35726e94cf040.text:
Nuraghe set on the double, safe landing of Porto Pirastru.

At present the walls and a cement floor of a recent installation remain.

4fa84aa17cb7e47e.text: Giants' tombs not easily recognisable near the Presethu Tortu sheepfold

4fa96389c9b5db36.text: The nuraghe consists of a central tower surrounded by a wall, against which several secondary towers are built. The central tower, which originally had several superimposed floors, now preserves only the lower floor and the staircase that led to the upper ones, partially blocked by collapse debris.

4fcba6238e4be4b8.text: A tafone of very particular workmanship, probably used as a burial, given the presence of several stones beneath the tafone that probably formed part of the closing wall. A folk legend tells that a chest containing a treasure, a “Scrixoxiu”, was hidden/walled up inside it.

4fd64845a53788cc.text: In the light of all this, an area adjacent to the village of Puisteris must have been established at Serra Neba, probably used for livestock breeding and perhaps also for agriculture. The archaeological material recovered, securely attributable to the Ozieri culture, attests to the occupation of the area during the final phases of the Neolithic.

4fde837a295386a4.text: Almost entirely dismantled, a few ashlars and wall segments of the original structure survive, their layout rendered indecipherable by the dense vegetation and a widespread state of decay. R. Ledda reports the discovery of primary mineral smelting slag, no longer in situ.

4fe04bbc3c9175ad.text:
The archaeological complex "Sa Mandra de sa Jua" – literally "enclosure of the yoked oxen", which in a broader sense indicates fertile land – occupies a modest rise overlooking the Rio Mannu di Ozieri.

The multi-layered site was occupied continuously until the Middle Ages and has been incorporated since the 1960s into the San Nicola district, which lies about 4 kilometres from the town of Ozieri.

The Monument

4ff4738ec107f4eb.text: A fountain whose architectural form shows several certainly Nuragic analogies.

50014d356a110f6b.text: Reduced to a massive ruin. The basal circle of pink trachyte, with vaguely squared boulders, can be made out. Contrary to what has been believed until now, this is not a nuraghe but an important sacred foundry circle of which several forms are evident. One of these, of historical and religious value, consists in its visible part of three steps with a basin. Mu

5024e52f38c479bd.text: A very complex nuraghe. It has a three-lobed outer wall and an internal central tower. Traces of a village lie outside. Its state of preservation is very poor.

503981ba150ecfb1.text: Complex nuraghe, probably of the "a tancato" type with a courtyard and an added tower, built of limestone. The majestic wall faces of the main tower survive largely intact. Inside, on the SSE side, a trapezoidal lintelled opening is visible, preceded by a passage whose course is interrupted by the collapse of the structures. Tampering by looters is evident.

503cb7379a6f1bc0.text: Usanis, situated a short distance from Osidda on the summit of a rocky spur, was a complex structure formed by two towers.

50424d8094e33c2d.text:
It is a large village, presumably of the Monte Claro Culture (Cagliari), which spread in Sardinia around the second half of the third millennium BC. In the centre of the polygon, because of land reclamation, little of the village walling remains, while on the two far sides traces of huts with rectangular and circular plans still emerge.

The plan in photo no. 6 was provided by the archaeologist who directed the excavations.

5067e53eff30c332.text: A well, probably belonging to a Nuragic village. It stands on the summit of a hill, inside a vineyard.

5078696f0296eea1.text:
The tomb was built in several phases. The first dates to the Early Bronze Age, when the Bonnanaro culture was widespread in Sardinia (about 1800 BC). At that time the tomb must have looked like a cist dolmen covered by a mound.

In the Nuragic period the site was reworked into a giants' tomb by enlarging the burial chamber and adding the exedra, composed of 14 slabs among which the central stele, with its entrance, stands out at almost 4 metres high.

508d9c2230dc1f5f.text:
It lies in the municipality of Bosa (OR), inside an agriturismo.

The name may be wrong.

It should comprise two hypogea partly reused.

50c7bcbde8e43c1c.text: Giants' tomb built of basalt ashlars

50de56ae61e06e85.text: Situated on the hill of the same name, from which it overlooks the Bechida valley and part of the coastal strip that leads northwards to the Nuraghe Artora, the structure is poorly preserved. It consists of a circular wall face of modest dimensions that appears to have belonged to a large hut, built of local granite. A large quantity of collapse debris is visible outside the walls.

51209edeb5f3f52b.text: Nuraghe, probably unique because it consists of two side-by-side towers of the same type and size.

514561e86dc6ad1d.text:
Located in the hinterland of the town of Porto Torres, the Sant'Elena nuraghe is one of the best preserved in the municipal area.

The monument occupies the summit of a low rise covered by very dense vegetation.

The central tower has a diameter of about 12 m and a surviving height of 4 m from the present ground level.

The masonry consists of 13 courses of superimposed blocks of white limestone, carefully dressed.
