51491efeb9555328.text: This is a four-lobed nuraghe (municipality of Sardara) that has been completely demolished, of which only a few courses of the basal masonry survive.

516e89cc2275404b.text: The Nuraghe Su Nuraxi of Loceri was built incorporating a rocky ledge. The main tower is well preserved and was built with blocks of local granite, partly rough-hewn and laid in regular courses. Its entrance is raised above ground level by at least three courses.

5184cd9aa5a132c5.text:
Position verified by GPS. The nuraghe is ruined and the entrance is blocked by collapse debris.

It still reaches a maximum height of about 8 metres.

51b95d618efbd074.text: The chamber, roughly circular with a maximum diameter of 1.80 metres on a north–south axis, is enclosed by four orthostatic slabs, though seven can be ideally reconstructed to complete the circuit with the entrance to the south-east. Three of the four surviving slabs support the capstone.

51bac9d26509da7a.text: What remains of a single-tower nuraghe dating from a period between the Middle and Late Bronze Age. Diameter of about 12 m and height of about 2 m.

51bf456df245f914.text: The sacred well is in good condition, despite its basic architectural elements having been tampered with several times. It is built of medium and large trachyte blocks and has a corridor paved with regular boulders, 5.10 m long, leading to a circular tholos chamber with a domed vault that encloses the water vein. The corridor was originally fitted with benches along the side walls.

51d0d67263b7dab6.text: Of the nuraghe Niu e Crobu nothing remains but a squalid testimony. Indeed the monument lies unknown amid the vegetation and a fence that robs it of its dignity, forced to look on as a reservoir clad in its own stone sits beside it, so as not to spoil the environmental impact… ignorance knows no bounds.

51d6b627a361895a.text: The Pranu Muttedu park is one of the most evocative archaeological sites in inland Sardinia. The park area is divided into two parts, for a total extension of about 200,000 sq m. Excavations have brought to light very numerous artefacts attributable to settled communities of the "Ozieri" culture dating to the Late Neolithic (3200–2800 BC). The archaeological complex has the highest concentration of menhirs known in Sardinia.

51fca9d3dee80d93.text:
The skill with which the basalt blocks have been laid is immediately striking. Swallowed by the earth and wrapped in greenery.

The south-east entrance is topped by an enormous lintel and leads into the chamber, where access is blocked by the collapsed tholos.

It must have been an elegant single-tower nuraghe, in a strategic position "guarding" a small, lush valley.

52351d1bc8c123e9.text: The area contains the remains of more than ten huts belonging to a Nuragic settlement. The village area has been completely altered, I would say devastated, during the Second World War, when the structures belonging to most of the huts were dismantled or adapted into military positions.

5295a78ecce03c39.text: Nuraghe never excavated, almost entirely buried

52a34ccf0b0e93b7.text: The Ertas nuraghe is the largest Nuragic monument in the Sassari area. It is a four-lobed structure, completely buried and covered by impenetrable vegetation. From the entrance on the south-east it is possible, by crawling, to reach the main tholos, which is still intact.

52aa0512a1d83680.text: The nuraghe is built on several levels. The oldest part is the central tower; an outer bastion then surrounds the central tower and links it to a second tower. The boulders making up this bastion are of considerable size. The only accessible part is a corridor on the second floor of the central tower, with a “donkey-back” or inverted ship’s-keel roof, whose south entrance is topped by a huge lintel with its relieving window.

52aa2a6ae94218f8.text: In very poor condition, only scant elements of the structure survive amid the vegetation. The location is uncertain, on the left bank of the Canale Orune, next to the water tank built during the Second World War.

52ab57bf8c2a37b1.text: Rocky bank with steps and cup-marks.

52b405b0faf12c2f.text: The nuraghe stands on the top of Monte Nieddu

52bf4dee261ef956.text: Single-tower nuraghe in an advanced state of decay.

52d72466ef1bfe83.text:
The remains of the megalithic tomb lie next to a dry-stone wall that follows the railway line, just 200 metres south-east of Birori station.

Seven surviving slabs of the semicircular exedra (chord 9 m – rise 2.40 m) are visible on the ground, as is part of its outer perimeter (length 9 m – width 4.50 m); nothing can be said, however, about the burial corridor and the arched stele, whose existence can be considered certain.

52db4281f9d7d6d3.text: Nuragic village occupied from Final Bronze Age II to Iron Age I, without a nuraghe.

52e545d54e96830b.text: The domus de janas consists of three large cells with a single entrance.

52fc1adf1ce40675.text: A tomb circle built by stacking polyhedral boulders of various sizes. The upper part consists of 10 large boulders arranged in a circle about 150 cm in diameter. Some fallen boulders lie at the edges and probably belonged to the original structure. The circle is filled with earth and rubble.

52ffb592b35efb22.text: Perhaps a Neolithic burial site; Roman and medieval tombs have been identified there over time. Witnesses report that in the 1940s and 1950s, while ploughing with a wooden plough, numerous human bones and fragments of tegulae and imbrices came to light. This was even more evident when the same person (my father Giovanni, almost a centenarian, now deceased) ploughed with an iron Birindelli plough, which turned the soil at a greater depth.

5310a9c93c17439d.text: An interesting site in the territory of Villa Sant'Antonio. Situated about 2 km south-east of the village, it shows probable remains of domus de janas, channels, cup-marks, basins and a symbol that the locals believe refers to fertility. The whole ensemble suggests a probable cult area of the pre-Nuragic period.

53708d2567fb20b5.text: Tomb II, particularly grand, has its entrance, antechamber and burial chamber cut into two separate rock blocks that were brought to the site and laid on a carefully prepared rubble bed; the fine stonework, done with a pick, and the architectural and planimetric design faithfully echo domus de janas burials.

5373e27763d20793.text: The Benas nuraghe stands on a small hill at the locality 'Tanca sa cresia', north-west of the Jana nuraghe, in the territory of Solarussa, 200 m from the border with Zerfaliu. It is a complex nuraghe, with a courtyard and three secondary towers. The central tower is particularly interesting, preserving the intact tholos roof of the ground floor. Inside there are three niches and a curious staircase on the right-hand side of the entrance corridor.

538676dc621d057b.text: Like the nuraghe Oes, it does not have a traditional tholos roof but one made with wooden lofts.

539274ce292f2cac.text: The Nuragic village of Grutti acqua lies on the plateau in front of the complex nuraghe and consists of numerous circular and rectangular huts. Unfortunately only ruins of the huts survive, and moreover almost all of them are completely covered by dense vegetation that nevertheless allows the structure to be identified, albeit partially.

53c10763af79b6d8.text: The Cala Ostina nuraghe is a low wall following a semicircular course, with a chord of 7.70 m, protected on three sides by sheer cliffs; the wall reaches a maximum height of 2 m in two or three courses of very large stones.

53dd21400e343ebe.text: A group of three Domus de Janas of particular charm. With a doorway carved in the basalt rock and a rectangular exedra below ground level.

53ddeda9f86a7674.text: The nuraghe Loppelìe still stands in good condition despite the collapses. The entrance, well preserved, is triangular. On the left side of the entrance chamber the intramural stairway opens. Moreover, the nuraghe Loppelìe is worth visiting for the splendid view from the top of the structure, which ranges from the village of Triei below, to the mountains overlooking Baunei, and from the bay of Arbatax to the peaks of the Gennargentu.

53f1caf60400d827.text: About 100 metres south-east of the nuraghe are the traces of a giants' tomb: several slabs belonging to the burial corridor emerge from the ground.

541b9b147e2877d9.text: Proto-nuraghe with a village around it. The size and position of the proto-nuraghi of Monti Crastu and Monti Mannu suggest that these may have been the most important centres of proto-Nuragic cantons or sub-cantons in the Campidano, or at least that, together with the other complex proto-nuraghi, they may have controlled a large part of it.

5420e66d0061e680.text: At the locality “Su Tiriarzu” there are two domus de janas about 80 metres apart.

5429273543b4fb14.text: The nuraghe is part of a complex that also includes a second nuraghe about 50 metres away. It must have been particularly grand, judging by the extent of the rubble. Within the collapse covering the central tower a tholos chamber of considerable height can be made out: the upper part of the entrance passage, with the angular cross-section typical of archaic-type nuraghi, can still be distinguished in the profile of the chamber.

54374d8d833f3561.text: On the top of the hill are the ruins of a small nuraghe.

544383c85e5e58ee.text:
Complex nuraghe largely buried.

The central tower, which preserves its tholos intact, reaches a height of about 10 metres on the north side.

5448f6baa078a47c.text: More like a stele than a menhir, having a parabolic arched shape. A dolmen stands nearby.

545f29be84474734.text: A particular site with two different classifications. The first census defined the structure as "Nuraghe Crastu Ruju", the second as "Muraglia megalitica di Giusei", in the style of the more famous wall of Monte Baranta.

5483e628825c4b86.text: It is very ruined and covered by dense vegetation.

549e2e7e04fa83e1.text: Here there was a Nuragic village, of which only a few traces remain.

54b6d8974894ae77.text: Single-tower nuraghe at Sa Cordiola. The outer walls are well preserved, but the interior has collapsed. It has the unusual feature of a double name: the first is "Sa Cordiola", the second is "Giustalassa", the name of the neighbouring locality.

54bfd0af6f9d8c84.text: It is more likely an ancient Nuragic hut.

54c148ffc378f8c0.text: A badly ruined single-tower nuraghe of which only a few courses remain

54ce9dc5fae622b5.text: Situated at the base of a tafone on the south side of the Berchida valley, a small village stands composed of a few huts built with dry-stone masonry. Initially identified as a nuraghe, it does not in fact have the characteristics of one.

54d0fb348ef45af0.text:
It lies in the territory of the municipality of Tortolì (OG).

There are three menhirs lying on the ground, two broken in two and a small one resembling a baetyl.

They are certainly the remains of a sanctuary built with megalithic architecture.

54dadcabd4d40369.text:
The dolmen has a circular burial chamber (1.57 x 1.26 x 0.52 m high above the fill) bounded by ten orthostats of various sizes (measurements of two slabs: 0.68 x 0.27 x 0.50 m high – 0.70 x 0.25 x 0.52 m high), while two slabs placed on one side of the entrance, oriented to the north-east, suggest the existence of a short corridor now destroyed.

The capstone is vaguely pentagonal (2.40 x 2.25 m) and has a maximum thickness of 0.55 m tapering to a minimum of 0.48 m.

54dc5fb3bfa66dd3.text: Located in the Tidula area, it has a niche in the corridor and one in the tholos, which is still intact.

54f6d65ebc61acb1.text: The proto-nuraghi of Monti Proceddu, Monti Tellura, Monti Acutzu and Monti de su Marchesu were very probably placed to guard the borders of districts of the Trexenta, whose most important centres must have been in the present municipal territories of Guasila or Samatzai; the one at Sa Corona (Bruncu de is Angionis Birdis) must have controlled at least the proto-nuraghi of Monti Atziaddei (?), Genna su Carru and those of Monti Cuamnaxi (Coa Margine) and Sa Corona di Villagreca.

550affd40e41d00a.text:
The hill is not easily accessible to visitors because it is wrapped in Mediterranean scrub. The car must be left about a hundred metres from the tarmac of the coastal road from Sarroch to Pula. From here you walk up to the nuraghe.

It is hard even to guess the number of towers that surrounded the central one.

However, it is certain that it must have been a multi-lobed nuraghe with an entrance to the south-east, whose central tower had the three typical internal niches.

550c3651303804f2.text: Single-tower nuraghe with a chamber flanked by three niches, built of basalt. Traces of a settlement.

5548bc32ebc5d79d.text: Complex nuraghe with settlement, village. If this is not the correct identification it may be an unnamed nuraghe listed as number 480 by van Dommelen. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

554ef184a141dc8f.text: It lies in the locality of the same name, about 1.5 km as the crow flies from the SP165. Easily reached by farm tracks, the village covers about two hectares. Among the ruins are several structures occupying the whole area within the visible boundaries of the complex. Some appear to be huts, others are larger and more like enclosures.

5554f8f74af419c8.text: Ispiene was part of the territory of Chiaramonti. About fifteen years ago we ceded two thousand hectares to the new municipality of Erula, and with it a number of nuraghi including Ispiene. That is why "I still feel it is mine", and if you want to find the character of a fortress you must come here, but even more so the imperishable sacred character that pervades the nuraghe with its cells and the sun that at the zenith on the summer solstice penetrates them to join with Mother Earth. mu

55554ba7b6bb122c.text: Inaccessible, with the tholos collapsed inwards

555a0cd14ea92872.text: A tafone that may have been used in prehistoric and protohistoric times as a shelter/dwelling by human families. Here too the walling built by humans to reduce the opening is clearly visible. At least two other more or less similar tafoni in comparable condition lie nearby.

5584bbb34240ae50.text: At the locality 'su pranu', a complex nuraghe in poor condition, hidden and made almost inaccessible to visitors. Around it the remains of a village are clearly visible.

55ac0e01c995711c.text: The place where the oldest human skeletons in the whole of Sardinia were found (8500–9000 BC).

55bf85c749bd5187.text:
You crawl through that opening; the space is tight, the ceiling low because of all that millennia-old earth, and you go on advancing on your elbows, slowly. It consists of at least 12 hypogea, cut into the limestone and provided with various decorations and bull protomes.

These are domus that move you, because their beauty lies in everything they hold.

Then, in the darkness, a shaft of light illuminates a magnificent triple-framed decoration on a doorway still almost completely buried.

562ce041722cf515.text:
The nuraghe, of complex type, consists of a central tower around which a three-lobed bastion was built enclosing a courtyard.

The towers have a curvilinear profile, as in the nuraghe Santu Antine at Torralba.

56380f85ff8feb63.text:
In the illustrated map of Tharros and on the archaeological site it is marked with the number 15.

The tophet was established by the Phoenicians and then by the Punics where Nuragic structures already existed.

5640b9e1a8ecb460.text: The surrounding territory has been heavily settled since ancient times, and sites are numerous everywhere. Often, as is the case with the few visible remains, it is not easy to determine their type. The only proof is the historical memory of the elders, with their indelible recollection of their existence.

56562099af8076f6.text: They are two menhir that have been repositioned in the area.

568aef748b1a3950.text:
The monument, of simple type, stands in an area currently used for pasture; the entrance has a lintel surmounted by a relieving window, while the jambs consist of well-shaped granite blocks laid in decreasing size towards the top.

The entrance leads into a passage towards the chamber, built of very well-worked granite ashlars and covered by an ogival-section roof.

569f9123e678ce79.text: The giants' tomb of S'Ena 'e Sa Vacca is particularly interesting for certain architectural features that in the past led scholars to regard it as a dolmenic structure. The distinctive feature of this burial is the large covering slab, completely unworked, which covers the entire tomb chamber and gives the monument the appearance of an elongated dolmen or "allée couverte".

56b73d0ec9c5a058.text: Nuraghe situated on the mountain called Punta Breigara. Locals call the site "nuraghe de s'omu e is abisi"; the base of a tholos about 1.50 m high is present. Vegetation has completely covered the site and makes further identification impossible. Difficult access; the roads are on private land.

56bb80e01dc1f2db.text: A single-tower nuraghe largely hidden by vegetation, built on a rocky outcrop that merges with the stones of the wall structure. The site dates to the Middle Bronze Age.

56c05568b8707c84.text: It is a corridor proto-nuraghe inside an area where the remains of a larger village are visible.

56f5dd41ff6feb9a.text:
It lies in the municipality of Nuxis (CI).

It was linked to the nearby Nuragic well, as is found at other archaeological sites (Santa Vittoria di Serri, Sant'Anastasia a Sardara, Su Putzu ad Orroli, etc.).

570ef53b43478246.text: The eastern part, which enjoys an excellent view over the whole inner gulf of Olbia, is the best preserved. It rises about four metres from the ground. The lintel is barely visible (see photo) while the entrance is almost completely buried. Traces of the megalithic enclosure are barely visible, but the multitude of remains and collapsed blocks suggest the monument's importance.

57186389eca2ada7.text: The complex consists of several hypogean tombs cut into large isolated blocks of limestone, erratic boulders. Among them Tombs I and IV stand out for their decorative ornaments, represented by spiral motifs carved in relief with the direct pecking technique, and architectural elements typical of contemporary dwellings, such as beams and joists (reproducing a double-pitched roof), frames, pilasters, plinths, steps and false doors, carved in bas-relief.

572350cab0d179ee.text: A ruined and buried single-tower nuraghe whose structure cannot be defined.

5728ad9e9633a5f4.text: One of the best-preserved single-tower nuraghi in the territory of Seneghe

572f8d97ed9ef785.text: Complex nuraghe with a central tower and a bastion with two additional towers. On the north side there are two more towers with a wall, at the narrowest point of the Taccu Ara plateau. Built of basalt.

57482eef30d8250e.text:
Multi-chambered tomb with a centripetal layout. It has long been emptied. It yielded material of the Ozieri culture (3200–2500 BC) and of the early medieval period (7th century AD). The former are kept in the "G. A. Sanna" Archaeological Museum in Sassari; the latter in the Nuoro Civic Museum.

Inside the domus, cut into a rock outcrop, access is through a hexagonal doorway; all around the antechamber, with its perfectly worked ceiling, five cells open where the dead were laid.

5755b06fcf8c2a69.text:
consisting of domus de janas of the horizontal-projection and pit types (1, 2, 3, 4), the other of pit-type domus de janas (5, 6, 7).

Tomb 1 is particularly remarkable, the result of several construction phases: originally of the pit type with an antechamber and a large main chamber, it was later given a long access corridor in place of the pit and enlarged to the right of the main chamber, incorporating three small burial chambers from a neighbouring tomb.

576c408f8c4b8ca0.text: The structure is completely denuded, with only a few visible traces of wall faces. Clandestine excavations have devastated the structure.

576c84f39fcead28.text: The tomb, of dolmenic structure, is now visible only in the burial corridor, the entrance and the right wing of the exedra. Of the tomb body, a single row of medium-sized stones forming the left side of the burial just emerges from the ground.

578b6614f57e17c8.text:
Complex nuraghe, perhaps three-lobed, built of large blocks of local andesite.

Among the vegetation some stone heaps and traces can be seen that probably belong to hut structures.

Reoccupation in historical times is clear, to which numerous pottery fragments, mostly of Roman date, found on the collapse and in the surrounding ground, belong.

57912a17b6ed65e0.text: This is a complex nuraghe over which the buildings of the Boggio anti-ship battery were superimposed during the Second World War. The wall face of the probable central tower is clearly visible from the outside.

57b95555641bd39c.text: Reported nuraghe, immersed in vegetation and not visible from the outside

57c3f5622311978e.text: Underground complex of six domus de janas.

57d6b33f9eb2881d.text: The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM maps; its type is undetermined.

57f0a3505f8b074f.text: Single-tower nuraghe on a basalt ridge, a natural stronghold. A shepherds' shelter was built inside. Today it is abandoned.

57f9d6cc5490e5f7.text:
The nuraghe is very large and I believe it has more than one tower.

It has suffered many collapses; an aerial photograph taken with a drone would be appropriate.

From the nuraghe there is a broad view over the whole surrounding territory as far as the sea.

5829aa34379b4f29.text: Giants' tomb located inside a large olive grove.

585a502d3257b4b9.text: Of particular importance is the cave known as "Su Stampu VI", where pre-Nuragic and Nuragic finds have been recovered.

585ce1843c0f24b5.text: The giants' tomb Sa Dom 'e S'Orcu is one of the best-preserved Nuragic monuments. Built on a slight rise in the ground, it is of the coursed exedra type. The apsidal tomb body, aligned on a SE–NW axis, is 15.20 m long. The masonry consists of medium-sized, well-worked basalt blocks laid in regular courses. In some parts of the walling the use of levelling wedges can be observed.

587ab5c4977fd0ae.text: It is a three-lobed complex nuraghe, with a central tower, three perimeter towers arranged in a triangle and joined by straight-curving curtain walls, and an internal courtyard with an entrance facing south-east. Finds of female-headed incense burners, draped figures and anatomical votives testify to a probable cult of the goddess Demeter.

58900b67ce516ea6.text: Situated inside an area used as pasture, near the course of the stream of the same name.

5890f5bcb01e4a62.text: Located in the territory of Mara, what appears to be a large monolith visible from the SS292 just before the Bonuighinu junction is intriguing. The probably complex nuraghe is unfortunately almost completely swallowed by vegetation, but what strikes me is discovering that the monolith is what remains of a cyclopean outer wall shaped like a V.

589347e6d908a375.text: Natural monument, erosion columns and rock shelters.

58999dc77deee8c1.text:
Small single-tower nuraghe completely destroyed.

The nuraghe was listed under the name Pirastu Fattu, but the owner, Mr G. Raspa, who was born and has lived in those places, states that the real name is Campo Maggiore.

589f9d42024d9df6.text: The settlement, which originally must have extended as far as to merge with that of N.ghe Maiore, consists of numerous building remains that still await investigation by experts. As at nearby Maiore, remains of rectangular-plan dwellings can be seen.

58ab470d149a0487.text: These are three domus de janas, partially eroded and in very poor condition.

58ac6c77c9b2b52b.text: Inside a large tancato in the locality of S. Pietro, next to a farmhouse, little of the nuraghe remains. The building appears to have been erected on top of the nuraghe. The materials used are large blocks of sandstone. The ruins have yielded several hundred fragments of Nuragic pottery, stone tools, flakes and microliths of obsidian, food remains, etc.

58d02ce8b2286369.text: Nuragic sacred well under study and excavation. The reconstruction is hypothetical.

58d1d3d2461005df.text: It lies in the municipality of Florinas (SS), and is a circular single-tower nuraghe with the entrance unusually oriented to the north-east. Very ruined. An old mule track passed practically alongside it, but is now completely disused.

58da18b3cb81e2f7.text: The giants' tomb S'iscra e Lottoni is of dolmenic type, from the Early Bronze Age, and is in a fair state of preservation; indeed it retains the funerary corridor almost intact, with a flat-lintel roof formed by stone slabs laid horizontally along the corridor walls. The large stele consists of a centinated monolith in which the small doorway giving access to the burial chamber has been cut.

58f7b3a62847d2d9.text: A mixed-type complex nuraghe, consisting of a main tower with a partially collapsed inner chamber, a second tower on the SW side, and an imposing structure crossed by a corridor that appears to end in a small courtyard containing a further small tower. The monument is very difficult to interpret, both because of the vegetation cover and the deep deposits, as well as the unusual nature of the building itself.

58fab2fb25ba7fe9.text: Single-tower nuraghe with its tholos intact

5905066d8283229e.text:
The circle, irregular in shape, has been destroyed by agricultural work that has compromised its original form.

The monument consists of about 40 trachyte boulders of various sizes forming an irregular ellipse with a major axis of 17 m and a minor axis of 15 m. Archaeological excavations have brought to light an unspecified number of polished stone axes that have allowed the circle to be dated to the Late Neolithic, placing it within the Ozieri Culture (4th millennium BC).

594ebce339c4ad6f.text: Single-tower nuraghe with the tholos collapsed inwards. Situated next to a sheepfold.

59b3da178c7d2ff0.text: It is a single-tower nuraghe with its tholos collapsed. About ten courses and part of the internal niches still survive, unfortunately used by the local herdsman as a place to store produce and also various plastic waste.

59b473f21b010436.text: It lacks the covering slab and is covered by vegetation.

59b7606a6de7a6de.text: A particularly evocative domus de janas necropolis adjoining part of a larger site that includes a nuraghe with a village and a dolmen. One of the finest domus de janas at Sirilò, until a few years ago it was still entirely underground. From the small entrance you enter the large chamber, inside which there are three more entrances leading to three other chambers.

59be7d1db3aa4618.text: A boulder forming part of a group of five large stones. It is distinguished by its shape, flat on the front and convex on the back.

59d048470d20778f.text: Small Nuragic spring with remains of the original cell built to cover the spring and faint traces of the atrium.

5a014914debd4fc2.text: In the literature, just as on the ground, Su Padrigheddu is closely linked to the S'Uraki nuraghe complex, first mentioned as such by A. Taramelli in 1935. The finds were immediately attributed to a village, settled in the Nuragic period and occupied continuously down to the Republican Roman period.

5a0a72c435280371.text: The site is called Su casteddu de Adeva, named after the mountain behind it, Monte Adeva or Is concas de Adeva. It is a single-tower nuraghe with an outer courtyard, bounded by a wall face that joins the tower structure, on the summit of a rocky spur with which the natural rock is partly integrated.

5a0e95888a8c4e18.text: The tomb was built with large blocks still partly buried and with mostly straight exposed faces. The exedra is no longer visible and the position of the doorway can only be hypothesised.

5a1763feffdfbef0.text: The nuraghe S'Argara is certainly one of the most important at Su Pranu; it is a four-lobed nuraghe, with four towers at the corners of the quadrangular bastion and an internal courtyard facing the entrance to the central tower. From its summit, on the clearest days, one can survey almost the whole of Sardinia's western coast, from Capo Caccia as far as Capo Pecora in the Sulcis.

5a244ac9d2d9fe95.text: The archaeological area comprises a village and two domus de janas on a granite tor partly surrounded by the Tèscere river. The complex nuraghe is distinguished by natural cavities incorporated into wall structures. The two domus are cut into two boulders. The first, single-chambered, is reached through a raised entrance preceded by a short vestibule. The second consists of a single chamber ruined by the collapse of the boulder in which the entrance opened.

5a3a5ecfebdf07ca.text:
Destroyed nuraghe on the summit of the hill of the same name.

Unfortunately little of this monument remains, but it is still of considerable significance.

5a60626c84bf859f.text: The monument stands in the middle of a livestock farm. It is a dolmenic tomb, aligned NW–SE with the entrance to the south-east, its burial chamber tapering towards the rear and open at the front in a broad semicircular exedra.

5a61e008e78e025b.text:
The prehistoric settlement spreads out, adapting to the rock formations, over three natural terraces, the first straight and the other two curvilinear.

These natural features have been reinforced by massive wall bastions built of large and medium-sized ashlars laid with heavy chinking. The proto-nuraghe, built of ashlars laid in irregular, heavily chinked courses, conforms to the morphology of the rocks.

5a862e1cf9b55b10.text: Remains of two sacred wells of the Nuragic period, set about 150 m apart. The first well is almost entirely buried. The second is in excellent condition, with an entrance formed by a semi-buried staircase. Its cylindrical shape has a diameter of about 2 m and a depth of about 3 m; it is built of stone blocks laid in horizontal courses. The presence of two sacred wells suggests a sacred centre of considerable importance.

5a9be3e2121d6c32.text: Together with the Cabonu nuraghe it lies on the boundary between the territories of Ussaramanna and Turri.

5aa30cf4bced3b3a.text: A double circuit wall of large blocks, enclosing an earlier Nuragic structure, the nuraghe Diana, appears to be traceable around the edge of the height.

5ac1cee26104b8ca.text: Partially ruined single-tower nuraghe with the tholos open. It is possible to climb to the last surviving course and enjoy the view over Cala Sinzias.

5acc1702867feec9.text: Located in the Su Fonnesu area (Teulada), at about 300 metres above sea level. It stands on a sharp peak, locally called "punta acuccia", which from a distance looks very much like a pyramid. The stones used are predominantly granite. The view is excellent, especially over the Gulf of Palmas.

5ad172dca5240d9e.text:
Cuccuru Nuraxi is the hill on whose summit a grand complex nuraghe once stood, now largely destroyed.

Even the earliest studies made it possible to grasp the nuraghe's structure. It was the first archaeological excavations, in the early 1960s, however, that gave a more precise definition of the monumental complex. The building consisted of two megalithic towers joined by a curtain wall. Inside, it comprised at least three chambers, one of which formed the main chamber.

5b173e6a82f3f246.text: The tomb shows clear signs of illicit excavation; its structure is hard to make out because most of it is covered by vegetation and soil. The chamber is rectangular and partly buried at the rear; an apse may be present. On the sides and at the back of the tomb there are fallen boulders that certainly belonged to the tomb. Even though it is hidden by the scrub, the wall of the exedra is visible, following a curved course.

5b218e1fc4a03b50.text:
It is built of medium and large boulders laid in rather rough courses; the plan is oval, and it has two entrances and two stairways leading to the upper floor.

The roof is formed of large slabs set side by side.

The east entrance has partly collapsed and was probably connected to the stairways, while the west entrance leads to the central corridor off which open a deep niche and a stairway that has almost completely collapsed. Probable proto-nuraghe

5b26e7ccccd3c98f.text: About 500 metres from the nuraghe of the same name

5b36700158c9998d.text: It is identified as a megalithic circle because there is a single row of unworked cyclopean ashlars arranged in a circle. Diameter about 11 m. It is currently used as a sheepfold. Two menhirs are reported nearby.

5b3d94142e673201.text: Practically a heap of stones; at the top an entrance hatch is visible leading into a passage 2 m long, presumably the lintelled roof of the stair that ran inside the wall.

5b4401594cfcec40.text: Complex nuraghe. Only a few remains of the central tower and bastions survive; it was demolished to build the nearby state road. Many finds from the Roman and early medieval periods attest to the monument's use in those periods as well.

5b51d169ab4df0bd.text: The monument is a single-tower nuraghe built of medium and large blocks laid in regular courses. The nuraghe is not in a good state of preservation. The south-east entrance, which has collapsed, leads into a corridor whose left wall shows the access to the stair (also collapsed). The chamber is circular in plan and survives to a maximum height of 9 m.

5b5636cad1de0592.text: The IGM map marks it as Longu, which actually lies further east, a few hundred metres away. It consists of several courses of polygonal cyclopean blocks whose neat arrangement is astonishing. It shows an opening to the north with a lintel that incorporates the beginnings of an arch. The surrounding area is of interest.

5b90c961a62bffd8.text:
It lies in the municipality of Montresta (OR).

In the centre of the delimited area, on a rocky outcrop, stands what was long considered a Nuragic construction. It is most probably, instead, a Carthaginian fortress of quadrangular shape, at the base of which traces of masonry that completed the defensive structure are visible.

5bb6f064c9ce92d8.text:
It is a bilobed nuraghe built of large trachyte blocks, roughly worked and laid in irregular courses.

Leaning against the central tower, which survives to a height of about (???) metres, is a second, slightly elliptical tower on the east side. From above, part of an internal niche in this tower is visible, faced with perfectly squared limestone blocks.

5bba0711db64d556.text: The Carrarzu Iddia nuragic complex stands on a low rise bounded by a curtain wall that encloses a proto-nuraghe and a nuraghe that appears to be of the tholos type; between the two buildings is a small cluster of circular huts, some of them still well preserved. A few dozen metres away is the eponymous dolmen, and a little farther off the nuraghi of Pranu 'e Ruos and Tittiriolos.

5bc6f480edf0c9be.text: It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan (SE-NW axis 11.75 m; E-W axis 11.50 m) and a wall thickness of 2.70 m to the NW and 3.85 m to the west; the maximum surviving height is on the NW side, at 3.60 m over 8 courses of well-worked, medium and large basalt boulders laid in regular horizontal courses.

5bdd5cc4598480a0.text: It lies in the municipality of Florinas. It consists of two hypogea.

5be402dbd22df328.text: The tomb was restored in 1993, reusing the exedra and the other orthostats and putting them back in their original positions; they were sometimes deteriorated or broken but still in situ. The monument, which shows two different construction phases, was built in both phases in the Early Bronze Age and was used for funerary purposes only during the first phase.

5bff8c977d8741d5.text: Group of three single-chambered domus de janas

5c21695b6d665a34.text: Complex nuraghe, never studied, inside a private property, covered in vegetation.

5c2b11b026b3b790.text:
Four giants' tombs, set a short distance from one another and in varying states of preservation. They are built of local limestone blocks and measure a little over 10 metres in length, except for one.

Because of illicit excavations, no intact stratigraphic context was recovered. It was nevertheless possible to identify a sequence datable from the advanced Middle Bronze Age to the Recent Bronze Age.

5c2ba12597f7afb1.text: The nuraghe Bidighinzu or Su Idighinzu, which in Sardinian means "dry vine shoot", is a single-tower monument that still preserves its intact tholos, located in the territory of Ploaghe.

5c3082d393017706.text: Ruined nuraghe completely covered by vegetation

5cb502b2f5c302ab.text: Probably a single-tower nuraghe. Completely covered by vegetation, making the structure difficult to interpret.

5ccdddcafed81307.text: Single-tower nuraghe, visible only when the water level of the Cuga reservoir drops. It is one of the 20 nuraghi in the Cuga valley.

5cdb619684040110.text: Built on a rise from which it overlooks the surrounding area, it can be seen from the hairpin bends of the SP 6. It is a single-tower nuraghe with a base diameter of about 10 m, built of schist blocks. Part of the masonry on the south side has collapsed, and the entrance, also on the south, is ogival and gives access to the inner chamber, which lacks its tholos roof; a niche is visible inside it.

5cf5c5c0c97954ac.text: It lies about 500 m east of the Menhir Is Perdas Croccadas. In recent times it has been reassembled and restored from three large fragments.

5cf7f3446a0a83bd.text: The burial lies on the south-western edge of a plateau used for crops and pasture. It is about 1.50 metres north-west of the nuraghe of the same name and a few hundred metres south-east of the open-air site of Ruinacchèsos. The monument has its entrance facing north-west, with some blocks of the exedra nearby. The burial chamber is about 3.55 metres long and rectangular in plan.

5d01695078e7d200.text:
The nuraghe is a single-tower nuraghe with a staircase, a corridor niche, and a chamber flanked by two opposing niches. The external ground plan is not fully definable because of collapses and dense shrub vegetation.

The tower, about 12 metres in diameter, survives to a maximum height of 5.30 m (8 courses).

The masonry consists of basalt blocks, medium and large, roughly dressed with some care and laid in regular horizontal courses.

5d1dddce5f2534ca.text:
It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan (diam. 9.60 m) reduced to a heap of ruins. The wall face, made of medium-sized stones laid in horizontal courses, survives to a maximum height of 2.20 m with 3–4 courses.

Because of the collapse it is not possible to know the internal layout of the monument.

5d5252d91a34d630.text: It is a small single-tower nuraghe. The ruin stands at most about 2 metres high and consists of a few superimposed courses of medium-sized, roughly worked stones. The external diameter of the nuraghe is about 11 metres. It is built of mixed basalt, limestone and schist stones. The monument is in a precarious state of preservation.

5d60c694dd5f0dbb.text: The nuraghe is hidden by an impenetrable blanket of vegetation.

5d7fff7dc905a95f.text: Partially ruined single-tower nuraghe. Much of the masonry survives on one side.

5d90f505ce192a95.text: It is also known as Su Canarzu and is recognised as Su Aijanu, which is the name of the plot of land on which it is built. Only the large closure stone and the two jambs are visible. In the surrounding area there are stones worked by man that were used to mark boundaries, and also wild olive or mastic trees.

5d98059efa231513.text: Multi-lobed nuraghe with an outer wall and a straight curtain wall, built of basalt blocks; a Republican Roman settlement on the ruins of the nuraghe. Traces of the nuraghe came to light during roadworks for the construction of the flyover piers: the site was extensively documented and is now completely hidden.

5d9f570d3b451d65.text: The nuraghe, or probably the proto-nuraghe Monte Uri given its features, appears imposing, leaning against and therefore erected in symbiosis with a large granite boulder; it preserves an intact tholos and from its position dominates the Oschiri countryside. For us it was a great surprise to see it, admire it and be able to confirm that where this place-name occurs, remains of very ancient monuments are generally found. (ArcheoUri)

5da4c9283268c34c.text: Single-tower nuraghe built on a rocky outcrop. Only a few courses remain visible, interlocked with the rock, and some wall structures at a lower level but still connected to the nuraghe.

5ddbbe745311d558.text: The nuraghe appears to be formed by three towers; inside, three niches can be seen. On the left a staircase leads to the upper floors, and around it the remains of the Nuragic village are visible, with some red stones from the area. To the left of the nuraghe lies a small necropolis.

5ddf7309b956e91d.text: Situated near the S'Urri valley (where other domus de janas are found), in the Su Linnarbu gorge, on some outcropping rock faces small rock-cut chambers were excavated, of which only slight traces remain because the large natural inlet was used as a dump for inert materials by Italcementi. However, cut into the upper edges that bound the rocky plateau, a few small cavities are still just visible, attributable to prehistoric tombs of the pre-Nuragic period.

5de07489db9c618a.text: It stands on the left-hand side of the Samatzai–Serrenti municipal road in the locality of the same name, on a slight rise of the plateau. It is a single-tower nuraghe with an external diameter of 10 m and a wall thickness of about 2 m. The basal course, formed of large limestone blocks quarried from the surrounding area which is rich in such outcrops, survives almost intact all round the circumference.

5de5cd3b85a6f7b2.text: Also known as "Sa Grutta de Santu Giuanni", it displays the classic ground plan of a giants' tomb. The tomb body (22.10 m), aligned on a north–south axis with the entrance to the south, is bordered on the outside by rows of granite blocks of various sizes. The façade is still partly buried and covered with rubble.

5de675e096ced975.text: The megalithic tomb lies further on, in a small clearing. Of the monument, which consists of a short burial corridor of pink trachyte slabs, only the basal course remains; the entrance is flanked by two carefully worked rectangular slabs, while the outer wall face, following the profile of the burial corridor, is built of vertical slabs with a fill of small stones.

5de7b84081eec217.text: A completely ruined structure whose shape can only be guessed at with difficulty

5df5fabd3bb31dc1.text: Ruined nuraghe, part of a larger settlement. The central tower is ruined; it has a fairly broad terrace running all round the main tower. There is a secondary entrance on the north-east. Hut bases are found nearby at the foot of the nuraghe.

5e376969432acec6.text:
A particular structure is present that appears to be Nuragic and was probably used for observation.

Probable location.

5e44a45e1562bdfe.text: If one favours a defensive function for nuraghi, this one at Elighia I is the clearest example. From an altitude of over 600 m a.s.l. it commands the surrounding countryside for 360° and, like a sentinel, keeps watch over anyone rash enough to venture into these lands. Unfortunately it too is in a ruinous state.

5e6d5e260a68f2a5.text:
Even though the present state is nothing but a series of collapses affecting the site in its entirety, I must admit that it inspires interest and respect for the majesty of the cyclopean stones, few of which are still in situ. The state of devastation is evident.

Nuraghe della Tortorella. mu

5e965265339575b9.text:
The nuraghe is a complex type, consisting of a central tower enclosed by a four-lobed bastion with four corner towers linked by curtain walls with a concave–convex profile.

The bastion (NS axis 17 m) is fairly well preserved on the western side and only partially on the north-western side, while the remaining perimeter appears completely collapsed and covered with rubble.

5e9a02e98549d6cf.text: It is a very beautiful and harmonious trilobate nuraghe in its structure. It is only partly accessible because of obvious and widespread collapses. Construction methods and details of the highest order can be appreciated. The name, which derives from the place-name of the land, nevertheless indicates intense smelting activity. Numerous finds of bronze semi-finished products in the characteristic ox-hide shape.

5eaea2a234f9aba8.text: Three giants' tombs built of schist are present at the site.

5ebe7b8b3a44a0ce.text: The nuraghe stands on the top of a high hill, from which the view extends perfectly over the S'Adde 'e S'Ulumu area,

5ed22969503dba89.text: It is a proto-nuraghe, or archaic nuraghe.

5ef29c5be1f5c7c7.text: All that remains of the nuraghe are a few courses laid in a circle that formed the base of a single tower.

5ef5f9c9d07c4dce.text: It is a ruined nuraghe, of which little is left.

5f22a5aae6913761.text: The Nolza nuraghe is a large four-lobed nuraghe, formed by four corner towers joined by straight bastions and a central tower still standing 13 metres high. Archaeological investigations, begun in 1994 and still in progress, have made it possible to distinguish several construction phases, characterised by alterations and adaptations. In a first phase the nuraghe was built of local schist, the material of which the central tower and two of the corner towers still consist.

5f2a672b3c95e59c.text: Set on the edge of a scarp, less than 400 metres north of the nuraghe "Pattada", and covered by shrub vegetation, it is now reduced to a heap of stones.

5f300937d2a6d5da.text: Structures belonging to a single-tower tholos nuraghe of which three or four courses of the outer wall face survive to a maximum height of about 2.50 m. The inner chamber has collapsed and the collapse material fills it. Built with polygonal blocks of local basalt. No entrance can be identified. The structures are largely covered by vegetation.

5f32bb0d1d452a3b.text: On a mountain terrace at the foot of the Ischiriddé pinnacle stood the village of Sas Funtanas, a very short distance from the Duas Vuccas cave. Lilliu reports the discovery of fragments of millstones and hand-mills and of a two-handled olla containing a copper chisel, and notes the presence of the small village, which is no longer visible today because of the dense vegetation.

5f3dea0954fe4515.text: One of the six coastal nuraghi on the island of Sant'Antioco — a single-tower nuraghe with an adjoining probable hut or other room — stands on the rocky outcrop of the same name, in a strategic position in the cove “Su Portu de su Casu”. A few courses of the original tower and a short stretch of walling to the east of it survive. The line of the inner face of the chamber can no longer be traced, as its interior is completely covered by vegetation and collapse.

5f43f83f3cd1bf95.text: The Menhir Terra Coccoi stands on a rise about 1 km north-east of Nuraxi Figus. It has a surviving height of about 2 metres.

5f71a32876f1818d.text:
It dates to the 11th century BC. A temple built of isodomic limestone ashlars, it is a work of fine architecture. The outer walls are decorated with rows of bosses carved on the ashlars. Water is channelled into the well through channels and from there into an external basin.

It has some affinity with the Predio Canopoli well at Perfugas.

5f77e41c033d6fb9.text:
Only a few courses are still visible at the Peidru nuraghe, a probable single-tower nuraghe located on the SP8 near the old cantoniera of Ponte Oinu.

An interesting boulder with three holes can be seen at the base of the monument.

5f79057a17ef5290.text: The nuraghe, probably of complex structure, was built on the same rocky ridge as the corridor nuraghe, to the north of it. It shows a very extensive collapse. The central tower can be identified thanks to the presence of two courses of boulders that survive in their original position. On the rocky ridge there is a curvilinear wall running from the west side round to the south-south-east side. On the south side stretches of walling, not well defined because of the collapses, appear to link the two nuraghi.

5f8e57a148de858c.text: About 150 metres from the Bigozzi nuraghe, to the north-west, lies the giants' tomb of the same name. Built on a small platform made of small stones, the burial retains the tomb corridor of orthostatic granite slabs; the roof is missing and the apsidal slab lies on the ground, while only a short stretch of the exedra is visible outside.

5faaa1bfb25db07d.text:
A Nuragic complex consisting of a central body with a bastion and four lateral towers. Bronze Age, 2nd millennium BC.

A large nuraghe on the hilltop overlooking the Colostrai lagoon, in an area that was heavily settled in the Nuragic period. A landing place and two river mouths, partly navigable, completely controlled.

5fb476c574eef11d.text:
The distinctive features:

the complete absence, at the entrance of the tombs, of the exedra; the resemblance to an upturned ship's keel that can be seen or compared with funerary monuments called "navetas", typical of the Talayotic civilisation of Minorca and the Balearic Islands.

These large structures are built of limestone slabs laid in courses that corbel progressively further inwards towards the top, and the roof was formed by a series of slabs serving as lintels.

5fb4f13df6f996fc.text: It is the uniqueness of the place in seeing so many ceremonial circles that one might believe in a constructive exaggeration without any purpose. It is thought instead that the importance of the place derives precisely from so many ceremonial circles where there was certainly a numerous population.

5fbf0f937c924f60.text: It is a complex building consisting of a main tower with a staircase, a corridor niche, and a chamber flanked by three niches arranged in a cross, plus an addition that is not easy to interpret typologically. The tower has a circular plan (diameter 11 m on the north-south axis) and survives to a maximum height of about 6.50 m.

6015c9ad35beae2d.text: Domus de janas built around a rocky outcrop on which the traces of a hut or megalithic circle survive

6026d659ae30458a.text: Basal part of a nuraghe near the old fire lookout, built of schist blocks.

6043637ab6672650.text:
A burial of the Nuragic period. The tomb body can be identified, partly hidden by the covering soil, together with the funerary corridor and the exedra.

The construction technique is coursed, using sub-squared polygonal blocks of granite.

6072213d7ebf795f.text:
A nuraghe in the territory of Ulassai, in the province of Ogliastra, is the second largest after the nuraghe s'Ulimu in the same municipality. It belongs to the complex in the "Neuletta" area, where besides it there are two other nuraghi and a small megalithic village, called Nuragheddos in the local Sardinian.

The nuraghe was built in the period between the Middle Bronze Age and the Final Bronze Age, therefore around 1400–900 BC.

60bf8d0fb719884f.text: Structures belonging to a complex tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The central tower has its lower chamber intact and the base of the upper one; the northern part of the bastion is visible, with two towers, while the whole southern part is covered by vegetation. The other two towers, not yet located because they are hidden by vegetation, may lie to the south of the central tower.

60c4b8337286b641.text: Built mainly of boulders like those of the Arresi nuraghe, four towers are visible, plus one almost completely destroyed. Some elders still remember the north-west tower intact. They say it had a well so deep that you could not hear the stones they dropped hit the bottom.

60d8821446f0b7dc.text: It is a group of six domus de janas tombs, five of which, of the single-chamber oven type, are in very poor condition, while the sixth has a sub-square antechamber giving access to the adjoining rectangular cell.

6109c31be6d0a334.text:
A buried Nuragic building, partly hidden by Second World War anti-aircraft positions. Between south-west and east there are traces of the Bronze Age village.

Chronology: Nuragic Bronze Age (for the nuraghe and the village); contemporary period (about 1942-43: for the military position).

6152c21b393c6105.text: A completely ruined nuraghe of which only a few traces remain on the surface.

615e864d0e703da9.text: A completely ruined nuraghe whose layout is difficult to determine

618d5b709508455b.text:
A veritable necropolis of giants' tombs – it comprises four or perhaps five burials, two of which have an arched stele, and they are still preserved in good condition.

The main burial has a broad arched exedra – with barely indicated wings – that joins the tomb body without a break, with a concave-convex wall face.

619eadf033e61b57.text: The nuraghe is a complex building consisting of a central tower against which a bastion with three secondary towers linked by curtain walls with a concave-convex course has been built: two towers stand on the front, the third is set off-centre to the right (towards N). The bastion has a curved eastern front (height 5.00 m) in the centre of which the entrance opens (width 1.10 m; height 1.60 m), now partially blocked.

61b02a7d2b303c13.text: Nuraghe overgrown with vegetation and ruined

61b675635fccbd53.text: Prof. Ercole Contu reported in 1992, about twenty large baetyls lying halfway up the south-east slope of Monte Cachile. I consulted some geologists who partly ruled out a natural geological formation. The site has been known to local people since time immemorial, and a legend is handed down orally that first-time mothers were brought there to give birth.

61c5fc904eb19132.text: A ruined multi-tower nuraghe, not interpretable, part of a larger settlement.

61de255ac5304d26.text:
More precisely it is a proto-nuraghe.

A boundary wall of a small house has been built against the nuraghe.

61f03582616032a1.text:
It lies near the campsite of the same name.

It consists of 25 menhirs, 22 of which are standing (but only 5 in their original position, since the others were re-erected by the archaeological excavation team).

620c5ccf808a9f07.text:
Funerary megalithic structure consisting of three vertical stone slabs orthogonal to each other.

It has been interpreted by archaeologists as a dolmen, although like all the other surrounding monuments it requires more thorough scientific investigation.

621d2dbeb7675245.text: A Nuragic village never studied or excavated, lying inside the Gutturu Mannu park, in the Assemini administrative enclave, on the left bank, opposite the springs of the same name. It is completely enveloped by holm-oak woodland, making it almost invisible from the outside.

6248aadab4ed254f.text: In the area, where a site of Nuragic origin probably existed, a lime kiln was built which, in recent times, was reused as a dwelling. Adjoining it are the ruins of a recently built house. The kiln was most likely built at the end of the 19th century or the early 20th: many other kilns erected on Sant'Antioco date from that period.

625ae3ca646d6515.text: No trace of the nuraghe remains except in the stone buildings that mark the property boundaries. Numerous pottery finds are present instead.

626223723c7c0a65.text: It is a ruined giants' tomb in a state of relative neglect

627fc051917f84fa.text:
The monument appears as a large sub-circular enclosure (diam. 18 m), with a wall thickness of 2.50–3 m and a maximum surviving height of 1.50–2 m, showing two courses.

The masonry consists of large polygonal blocks laid in horizontal courses.

From what can be seen, it is most probably a corridor nuraghe.

628271bb90ac5109.text: Complex nuraghe composed of a central tower and two towers with a courtyard.

62a5fea14262cb0a.text: The burial, situated near two nuraghi and a village, still preserves the tomb body. This encloses a burial chamber built of granite blocks of various sizes, shaped obliquely on the exposed face and laid in irregular courses with the use of chocking wedges.

62c88bbe66d99297.text: The nuraghe is in a state of considerable decay; artificial structures are also present inside the nuraghe.

62cbf61345ad9eb6.text: South of the nuraghe and near the village huts there is a rectangular structure cut into the ground to a visible depth of about 150 cm, about 120 cm wide and about 250 cm long, lined with trachyte boulders of various sizes. The interior is almost entirely filled with collapse boulders and vegetation, making it difficult to determine its dimensions and structure correctly.

62fadff2b58ec710.text:
It is a small artificial cave cut into a single rounded block of limestone. The oven-mouthed entrance faces south-east and leads into a longitudinally developed space, divided into several chambers, which must have formed the rooms of a hypogeal burial.

The tomb shows no decorative motifs and has yielded no grave goods. It is dated to the Late Neolithic and demonstrates the occupation of the territory from the pre-Nuragic period.

6338d1dce4862369.text: Certainly a central-tower nuraghe of note. The central tower soars, and from what can be made out it must have been a four-lobed nuraghe with a village around it. The tholos has collapsed inwards.

6347717477fdd088.text: The structure is built onto a natural rocky outcrop and forms an enclosure about 50 by 32 metres with an average height of about 3 metres. Access to the interior was through two lateral portals on the north and south sides. The entrances are followed by a walled corridor. Inside, a large granite boulder, which some say has the features of a mother goddess, leads them to hypothesise a temple function for the area.

6349de2ae427dba5.text: The Tomb of the Three Hundred is the most remarkable monument and part of a larger necropolis discovered during construction of the SS 131. It takes its name from the number of skeletons found inside the walls surrounding the inhumation area.

634ee5dc99e94aa4.text:
It is one of the many prehistoric monuments that make Seneghe one of the Sardinian municipalities with the highest density of material evidence of that remote civilisation.

Single-tower nuraghe, partially collapsed and covered in vegetation

634ef1fcbc9a2242.text: A hypogeum of the Monte Claro culture discovered during work on the "new 554". It consists of two hypogea with a vertical access shaft and several grave goods.

635c6dc3311feafc.text: Dr Aste maintains that Su Doladorgiu was originally the fortress he has reconstructed, which was equipped with towers and a nuraghe. For strategic defence reasons it was built in the Nuragic period to keep watch over the whole valley, since attacks by enemies and invaders were feared from the sea.

638e0b2c0bc6045b.text:
Romanzesu is one of the most important settlement and cult complexes of Nuragic Sardinia, with about a hundred huts, five cult buildings — a sacred well temple and four "megaron" temples — and a large ceremonial enclosure. It is built of local granite.

The area develops around the sacred well temple, built into the rock from whose fissures spring water emerges. It has an access stair and a circular chamber built with regular courses of carefully worked blocks.

6392c7218f11e912.text: It lies above the church of Santa Lucia. Little is visible, in particular a wall of the tower (I think it is single-tower) on the north side and various courses.

63a34e2c6de8db70.text: It has a quadrangular plan with a rounded profile and a maximum surviving height of 3.65 m on the south-east side, with five courses, while on the north-west it is 2.00 m with four courses. The masonry consists of large, barely dressed boulders laid in very irregular horizontal rows. The building has two coaxial entrances, the first to the ESE and the second to the WNW, linked by a corridor that runs orthogonally to the structure's long axis.

63e6ec33e83522ce.text: Nissardi in 1901 (map in G. Pinza's volume) marked a giants' tomb a little to the south-west of the Paule Tolta nuraghe: a nuraghe that actually lies inside the airport perimeter.

63ef5fb02a417e88.text: A ruined nuraghe whose tholos has collapsed at the top. It stands in a wood.

63fccd20ee293649.text: Nuragic village almost completely covered by collapse debris, vegetation and stones from cleared fields.

64057d35d3f71662.text: The structures suggest the remains of a probable proto-nuraghe. Viewed from a raised position at least two rectangular rooms can be distinguished, while the rest is hidden by vegetation. Unfortunately, various field-clearance operations, with the subsequent piling of stones on top of the ancient structures, cast doubt on the true nature of any other buildings.

6418fa53230d8467.text: Collapsed nuraghe but with the interior accessible. The doorway and about five courses of the masonry survive.

64194bea6a6a099c.text: The few known finds from the A1 rock shelter at Monti Crastu, used as a burial and violated by clandestine digging, are attributed to the Abealzu phase. The size and position of the proto-nuraghi at Monti Crastu and Monti Mannu suggest that these may have been the most important centres of proto-Nuragic cantons or sub-cantons in the Campidano, or at least that, together with the other complex proto-nuraghi, they could have controlled a large part of it.

642f951df74196f5.text:
Situated a short distance from the rural church of S. Gavino and about a hundred metres to the north-west of the Nuraghe Toscono, with which it had a close cultural relationship, the tomb of Santu Bainzu is of the dolmenic type with a monolithic arched stele, aligned along the SE-NW axis and with the entrance to the south-east.

It was recorded by Lamarmora, whose drawing still shows the orthostats of the exedra in situ, whereas they are no longer present in a later plan sketch by Mackenzie.

6444c2f12129d861.text:
It is a single-tower nuraghe in a state of serious deterioration. The perhaps improper description comes from the fact that these monuments speak and shout like living beings. History of our forebears, of a great people who managed to express their own culture of peace and solidarity among small shepherd-kings federated in a single great state. What was said elsewhere for the many monuments in the territory of Chiaramonti applies here.

(photo Mario Unali)

6468b1895ff850a2.text: The very poor state of preservation does not allow a clear reading of the building, which nevertheless appears to be a single-tower nuraghe of elliptical shape.

647880e609c6a9d0.text: Two multi-chambered domus de janas are cut into the limestone ridge that bounds the Baddenare plateau. Both have an antechamber, a main chamber and two side cells. One is entered through a long dromos, the other through a raised doorway above ground level. The domus with the dromos entrance preserves two fine columns in the main chamber and an incised inscription (L M S), probably Roman or medieval in date.

647f613dec78cda4.text: The slow retreat of the water, caused by drought, reveals what normally lies submerged. All around, clear Nuragic traces are visible, such as the sacred huts and other rooms typical of the period. On a small promontory stands another nuraghe, “Sa tanca 'e sa Mura”, and a little further on a third, “Tudera Alto”, of which, unfortunately, only a few of its cyclopean stone courses have survived.

64ac278d9b02f40c.text: Ruins of a circular megalithic structure with an apparent entrance portal.

64b5c9ca66adec5d.text: Ruined nuraghe whose tholos has collapsed

64e4b48052df25f5.text:
It lies in the municipality of Goni (CA).

Although the signage highlights the presence of a giants' tomb, the construction type (the monument has two opposing apses) finds few parallels in a funerary context.

It may be a cult enclosure.

64f66b18309b5192.text: At first sight a single-tower nuraghe, in reality a complex one with buried structures covered by vegetation. The original tower preserves its entire perimeter circuit. On the SE side there is perhaps a raised entrance. The interior of the tower is blocked by boulders and earth. To the SE an obvious attempt at illicit excavation has exposed the outer wall face of the tower. To the S and SW circular curtain walls can be seen that may belong to two further towers.

650b0c22b492ca29.text: Domus de janas on a trachyte ridge, decorated inside with a false door and a probable carved hearth

651c2be9b1cfbcf4.text:
It lies in the municipality of Monastir (CA).

The archaeological area was discovered during earthworks for the 131.

6534a1b5e2cf9e96.text: A ruined nuraghe of which a good stretch of walling about 3 metres high survives.

6535dcb4afbd2f4f.text:
Throughout the area there are settlements and hut remains ranging from the Neolithic to the Medieval period.

This nuraghe, too, lies in a state of total abandonment; no restoration work or excavations have ever been carried out to highlight or bring to light any finds.

6580e25bf154b7be.text: Built of limestone blocks on a rocky outcrop, it consists of a main tower, an added section where the remains of a corridor can be seen, and the remains of several huts on the west side. It is not in a good state of preservation.

658374abb4ab4b59.text: Vittorio Angius calls it Fumìu: "It is a design of such a kind that no idea of it can be given without having drawn it." He goes on to state that several nuraghi make it up: "Above the door opening towards the sirocco-levante there is a loophole, and not far from it a second door opening to the sirocco and two metres high, which however, being high above the ground, looks like a window: on one side of it the gallery within the wall thickness opens, leading to the upper floors or the terrace."

65a0cdcee9399deb.text: The monument stands on a natural terrace in a hilly area used for pasture. About 300 m to the north-west lies the giants' tomb of Funtana Morta. The nuraghe is almost completely destroyed and only the external ground plan, vaguely circular, can be made out.

65c6585f25731054.text: The nuraghe retains an intact tholos, but the collapse at the entrance means it cannot be visited. The chamber has four niches, making it one of the very few nuraghi known so far with this feature.

65ca6fdef2c2ee84.text:
Dolmenic burial with an apsidal corridor.

It lies in the municipality of Narbolia (OR).

65d441c6d88faf0c.text: The nuraghe is semi-subterranean, probably single-tower and single-chambered. The outer wall face is exposed in places. The inner face retains three courses that completely roof the circular chamber. The entrance lintel has been set into a dry-stone wall.

65e5952e3a03e8a1.text: It is a large Nuragic village; very little of it now remains, only mounds and scattered stones around the nuraghe of the same name can be seen.

65edfcedaef5f094.text: The nuraghe has been almost completely dismantled; only a few courses of stones remain.

65ef4a53027a1bf7.text: Probable domus de janas, currently used as a dog kennel. There were probably other domus de janas in the area that have been destroyed by building activity.

65f88d12f3d9a627.text:
This nuraghe has unique features, such as the three different helical staircases that led from the ground up to the upper levels.

Today, very little of what once stood remains. The height of the central tower and the massive scale of the building can be inferred from the diameter of the tower, the imposing size of the ashlars, and the extent of the whole footprint of the main structure.

In this case, too, a village of considerable size must have developed around it.

660167fb7777fe1c.text: It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan. The nuraghe stands on a basalt platform on the summit of Monte S. Antonio, to the south-west of the rural chapel dedicated to the Saint. The monument rests on the sheer edge of the height, which acts as a natural bastion for the nuragic tower along the whole western arc, before sloping down towards the NNE where the building rests on the open ground.

6604a7b0274216dd.text: six domus de janas on the site.

660fc159d3c39a44.text: It is a small single-chamber tomb of the oven type, circular in plan (depth 0.55 m – width 0.62 m), entered through a finely shaped doorway (width ….. – height 0.42 m – thickness 0.12 m) preceded by a short antechamber (depth 0.32 m – width 0.75/0.48 m). The orientation is to the south, the walls are perfectly smoothed and the ceiling slightly hemispherical.

661319f1b2172355.text: It is visible from the SS131 and immediately strikes you as a special nuraghe. Special because it combines the features of a nuraghe with an elongated, upturned-boat-shaped chamber and a truncated-cone nuraghe. On entering, you find yourself in the long chamber, which has two large niches and is about 7 metres high; at the far end a doorway leads to a staircase that, plunging into darkness and enclosed by the nuragic walls, spirals up to the upper floor.

66309609d4e5cb8e.text: The nuraghe, in a good state of preservation, consists of a main tholos to which other masonry parts were added later. A long corridor and a staircase lead off from the entrance. In the main chamber, where the roof has collapsed, there are several niches. The nuraghe, datable to 1500–1200 BC, stands on a hill whose slopes show the remains of circular and oval walls, probably belonging to a village.

66481ae229fabb1a.text: Complex multilobate nuraghe, of which very little is left

6648d6cc6bccf073.text: The nuraghe is multi-lobed, consisting of a central tower surrounded by five towers, some of which are in a good state of preservation. The towers have lost their tops; originally the tower summits must have been crowned with stone battlements, which were recovered at the base of the structures during the most recent archaeological excavations carried out on the monument following the collapses.

6649f3b1cb29415a.text: A "tancato" nuraghe has on the front of the main tower a wall structure of varying shape that encloses a smaller tower and a courtyard set between the two towers.

665970e04e53254e.text:
It is a nuraghe that is hard to classify typologically because of the collapse and the dense shrubby vegetation covering it.

The masonry consists of medium-sized stones laid in regular horizontal courses. The few features observed do not help to understand the ground plan of this structure, which excavation might reveal to be a proto-nuraghe rather than a classic tholos nuraghe.

669b9a3a6991872c.text: Two nuragic towers at a very short distance from each other

66b47f91916c0a9c.text: It is a complex nuraghe, whose ground plan cannot be deduced because it is largely buried. A tower to the west is faintly visible, showing up to five courses. Elsewhere various circular courses emerge here and there.

66be76584516d532.text: A ruined, never-studied nuraghe of which a few courses remain. A singular and remarkable worked stone near the proto-nuraghe, above a few completely unidentifiable ruins, could be interpreted as a fragment of a shaped tumulus originally located above a domus de janas with a façade, or as a covering element of a giants' tomb.

66cb74c5a0fab348.text: It is a domus de janas cut into the base of a trachyte outcrop.

6700174566a64b82.text: Single-tower nuraghe of large blocks of white limestone, situated in the courtyard of a private house. About three courses survive, with a maximum height of 3 m and a minimum of 2 m. Diameter at the base: 15 m. The structure is collapsing overall; state of preservation: mediocre.

6713c64deb9753cf.text: There are not enough elements for a reasoned classification; however, despite the latest alterations, I believe it is a Nuragic spring.

67155568138260e3.text: The tomb, because of the collapse of its side structures and the lush vegetation that covers most of it, does not clearly show its layout. However, some ashlars still in their original position suggest a rectangular plan. At the sides and in the surrounding area there are heaps of earth mixed with boulders and rubble that probably belonged to the tomb structure, clear signs of the violation carried out by clandestine diggers.

67598d2324934d65.text: It appears on the 1844 cadastral map of the Royal General Staff as Nuraghe Numassi.

677956d7acb63f5c.text: Only a few worked ashlars of the monument, now destroyed, are visible; they show that the tomb was of the coursed type in isodomic masonry.

67cb1ef57bf88eda.text: The monument, inside the village of Sagama near the parish church, is a single-tower nuraghe with a stair, a corridor niche and a central chamber flanked by three niches arranged in a cross.

67e1067a7f42000a.text: Circular single-tower nuraghe with the entrance to the south topped by a lintel stone. The central chamber, oblong, is distinguished by the unusual presence of four niches: one on the left side, one at the back opposite the entrance, and two (as a pair) on the right side. All have a semi-elliptical plan; the section is trapezoidal, like that of the entrance passage. The cone survives to an external height of about 3 m.

67e9a808c544cedf.text: another nuraghe in the territory of Segariu, albeit neglected and ruined

67f504832ed0aa7a.text: Situated on a plateau next to the Caddare stream, the tomb lies a short distance from the Lettu Rucratu site. Before excavation and restoration the burial had suffered heavy disturbance by mechanical equipment that removed part of the chamber and the exedra; it was built with orthostatic technique. The site has yielded material datable to the beginning of the Middle Bronze Age.

6833037cfdc0b3b4.text: It consists of about ten metres of megalithic wall made of large boulders placed on the ridge north of Monte Zennaru, facing Runaghe Paulusedda or Palusedda, in the centre of which the Rio Murrone flows as a winter torrent. The construction gives the impression of being intended, almost, to watch over that river crossing. On close examination there are no traces of any other building in the vicinity.

6844f183f79790d5.text:
The nuraghe is a single-tower nuraghe built with large, well-worked boulders.

The entrance is topped by an imposing lintel and leads into a corridor with a niche on the right and the stairwell on the left; the latter is largely filled with rubble. At the end of the corridor the circular chamber opens, its tholos vault still intact, containing three symmetrically placed niches.

684f06e6ef141592.text: The nuraghe is completely ruined, reduced to a heap of blocks about 2 metres high.

684fa7de19e47212.text: Two-tower complex nuraghe with settlement. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

6875625bc164c04c.text: Around the parish church the remains of an important settlement have come to light, including three wells and Hut 5, interpreted as a council hall. The discovery of terracotta casting moulds in the area outside "Hut 4" proves that metal artefacts were produced on the spot. By the threshold of "Hut 1", also of the Final Bronze Age, a clay bowl containing ox-hide ingots was found, deposited in the Iron Age.

68786d9114bdf062.text: The nuraghe is located on the summit of a steep rise, characterised by dense woodland, and stands on a rocky granite outcrop that commands an excellent view of the surrounding territory. The monument, in a serious state of decay, is a simple nuraghe with a roughly circular plan, barely recognisable because of the extent of the collapse.

6888f5cd956acb4a.text:
Small dolmen consisting of two upright slabs supporting a well-shaped covering slab.

The back wall is instead made of two base stones on which small stones rest to close the chamber.

For the enhancement and public use of the monument, the surrounding area belonging to it has been fenced and linked to the municipal road network by a fenced path as well.

68a64104c726e378.text: Single-tower nuraghe of which part of the tholos and the reworked entrance portal remain

68d83c82bcdd6275.text: These are a few wretched ruins and some boulders of the nuraghe, which is completely overgrown with vegetation.

68e5f92fcb3e8652.text: Single-tower nuraghe; located inside a military area. The tholos survives intact. The site is now accessible (it is still advisable to ask for "authorisation" at the "Bechi Luserna" Barracks).

68f8ed78d7ee1cc9.text: Only a few courses of the nuraghe remain. It stands in a lookout and signalling position from which the view sweeps 360 degrees over all the surrounding mountains and nuraghi.

6900ff05eaccf2dc.text: The menhir Sa Perda de s'Omini stands on a promontory at an altitude of about 230 m above sea level. It is a monolith whose shape is probably the work of weathering. It has the appearance of a human face. Some believe it was connected with the ancient cult of the Mother Goddess, especially given the presence of remains of ill-defined structures next to one of the two monoliths. In ancient times, and still today, it is regarded as the centre of the Island.

690fd6fbbe951729.text: The well, situated to the south of the cave and a short distance from it, is oval in shape. It was cut into a rock outcrop that defines its north side and, partially, the east and west sides. A masonry structure built of parallelepiped blocks completes the east and west sides and the whole of the south side.

691ee05cf10ef2b1.text: The burial stands on the flat summit of Planu Borgolo, about 50 m east of the line of the SS131, which separates it from the settlement to which it belongs. The tomb's layout and the funerary corridor, formed by several large orthostatic slabs, especially at the far end, are still discernible; only a few elements of the exedra survive.

692fee2f043a86a5.text: Ruined, buried, little known and never excavated, it is visible from the SS 131.

6945f079120a1ebf.text: The uncovered tomb has the outer profile of the central body with concave wall faces. The exedra has curved wings. The burial chamber is oblong. The facing course of the apse can be seen.

69696041360cb29d.text: Complex nuraghe with masonry of worked ashlars of similar thickness. Ruined, collapsed and partly buried.

696d13a6d8f48621.text: Partially ruined nuraghe, with about ten courses still standing, situated next to two rural buildings.

6981ddb1ccff9f27.text: Tafone/luttoni – a rock shelter probably used in prehistoric and protohistoric times as a shelter/dwelling by human families. Its identification is not certain for lack of thorough study, so information is scarce. The only clues pointing to such an identification are other rock shelters nearby (three to be exact) and a giants' tomb a short distance away.

6996399ccaf60c1c.text: It is a jewel of architecture, harmonious in construction and full of sacredness. In front of the mound, turned over from below and above, visited several times by tomb robbers, the exedra develops in a double row of roughly worked stones. From the wings of the exedra the circle of single stones begins, with a diameter of 15 m.

69c0f776ae03b9d0.text: Simple proto-nuraghe, of which very little is left

69e5ffa1b97081b4.text: A single-tower nuraghe of which very little, if anything, remains. It was inhabited until the Recent Bronze Age. After that, life at many nuraghi apparently ceases, as they have lost their original function.

69e65c7e0c766b16.text: Built of squared limestone blocks, it stands at least six courses high and has a well-defined, legible façade even from a distance. It was investigated in the 20th century with unsystematic excavations undertaken by the then Honorary Inspector Cornelio Puxeddu.
