About 25 m west of the nuraghe and at a lower elevation, a building of uncertain purpose was erected in modern times; it has a cemented stone wall with an iron door and an upper skylight.

6a1bac3a3c22935c.text: The archaeological site of Bruncu Suergiu lies in the Giara Park. Hidden by vegetation and hard to reach. Traces of ancient routes, a large settlement with production facilities, and defensive structures characterise the site. Besides the huge quantity of material, a broad terrace looks out over the Campidano, offering a breathtaking view. Only the panorama repays the long and difficult walk. The archaeological area, which is protected, covers about 11 hectares.

6a2121e8b343a424.text:
A particularly evocative proto-nuraghe for the beauty of its protohistoric architecture. The entrance to the original tholos survives, incorporated into the rocky mass.

On the outside of the granite block, and in plain view, there are hollows that form natural sculptures; inside there is a rock shelter that was probably already used in earlier periods.

6a2bc7ccb8092782.text: Twenty-two Nuragic villages, large and small, are known in the municipal area, and not all were occupied at the same time. They are often found near a nuraghe, as at the Bruncu Pubusa site; in other cases (Giuanni Acca, Sattu Divisu, Bruncu Abis and Sa Serra) they lack one.

6a2c8b0ba2e2ab9c.text: Neolithic burial composed of two chambers connected through a doorway that has, at the top, a probable double bull's-head protome.

6a4214210a8b6a67.text: Hut or nuraghe base, not marked on the IGM map, now reduced to a pile of rubble

6a630e9080899c09.text: A short distance from the Sant'Andria nuraghe, to the north-west, lies the domus de janas, cut into a granite outcrop. The entrance has collapsed, so the hypogeum is reached through an irregular opening that leads into a small antechamber from which the second chamber opens. Fragments and flakes of lithic material can be found around it.

6a69c8f17414948b.text:
The monument stands about twenty metres from a second giants' tomb and about 200 metres from the eponymous nuraghe; it is not traceable in the outer perimeter because of its very poor state of preservation.

A fragment of an arched stele (height 0.46 m; width 1.25 m) with a raised frame, 12 cm wide on the left and 15–17 cm on the right, reused in the paving of the nearby church of Santa Sabina, probably belongs to this tomb.

6a6d13e1576fabf0.text: In the area of Monte Sa Scrocca Manna, on the boundary between the municipalities of Sant'Antioco and Calasetta, there are several structures that originally most likely formed part of a Punic and/or Roman settlement. Unfortunately, during the Second World War military works irreparably damaged their walls. Some stretches of walling, still fairly well preserved, survive, together with various squared and moulded ashlars reused in the military constructions.

6aa974f09d6c166c.text: A ruined single-tower nuraghe, not marked on the IGM map.

6ad28b4d97bacb67.text:
A burial of the Nuragic period. The monument is practically destroyed. On the ground one can make out a course of the stones that formed the funerary corridor and blocks belonging to the exedra.

The most visible distinctive element is the terminal slab of the funerary corridor, still in its original position. The construction technique must have been of the coursed type, using polygonal blocks.

6adf301083235435.text: One of the very many dolmens found in Sardinia. Dolmens (from the Breton tol-men, stone table) are funerary monuments erected presumably during the Late Neolithic and Early Chalcolithic (3400–2700 BC).

6ae3f76b0aa2ac2e.text: Unfortunately, very little of the tomb remains: today the central corridor of the burial chamber can still be made out, its walls once formed by courses of stones laid neatly as in nuraghe corridors; the stones that framed the central doorway are also present, together with many other stones scattered all around. Finally, a single stone slab (or orthostat) survives which, set in a row with many others, formed one of the two wings of the exedra.

6af0be8720cc9c6a.text: A burial of the Nuragic period built of polygonal trachyte blocks. Little of the tomb is visible because of the vegetation; the corridor and the exedra survive. From what the remains and the vegetation allow one to see, the two arms (running straight) that define the exedra consist of two superimposed wall faces of different widths with a set-back that presumably served as a seat. mu.

6b0429ccd1085386.text: The remains of the nuraghe are hard to make out; it has certainly been dismantled and the ashlars may have been used to build the retaining walls and boundary walls found in the area where the nuraghe probably stood. From the booklet “Ritratto di nuraghe eredità di un'isola …” by Sara Muscuso we read: “All that remains of the nuraghe is a curvilinear wall face made up of one or two courses.”

6b10177fdebe1a02.text: The Nuragic village of Neulè lies in the area of the same name, a few kilometres from the settlement of Dorgali. The site contains numerous still-intact huts, a sacred well and a nuraghe.

6b131317526a1666.text: Leaving the village of Irgoli towards Onifai/Orosei, just before a small bridge, turn onto the road for Capo Comino. After only 300 m, at the junction for the bypass, a municipal asphalt road begins on the right. Follow this road for about 5 km until you see two prominent granite pillars on the left. Walk on until you reach the Domus de Janas Sa Conca 'e mortu.

6b1ef0ccd7fd1bd6.text: No trace of the nuraghe remains except a large quantity of collapse material hidden by the vegetation.

6b48d2cdd29e2fa7.text: The monument must have been a far more complex and articulated structure than one can imagine today, looking at the surviving ruins, which nevertheless still retain a semblance of their original monumentality. The first tower, circular in plan, has its foundations set on a bedrock surface; the inner chamber has an oval layout whose elongated end joins the wall face of what must have been the main tower.

6b5078cf2a9b0331.text: Probably a single-tower nuraghe covered by collapse and vegetation. Only a single course is visible.

6b523dfb7260d951.text: Isolated menhir, on the back of which is an alignment of cupmarks.

6b5fd112e3ebacd6.text: In an advanced state of abandonment, the wall face running east–west, built of medium-sized stones laid on edge, is still visible. There are few traces of the probable exedra. Worth noting, however, is the presence of a baetyl stone with several holes whose meaning is unknown unless related to the female essence.

6bab7ec9df851d13.text: In a dominant position above the Riu Liscoi, on a spur of granite rock, a corridor nuraghe is visible, elliptical in plan and built of pink granite and trachyte; the interior cannot be visited because of collapses, and it is flanked by the remains of several circular huts.

6bc21beaa72f5dff.text: It is a proto-nuraghe or archaic nuraghe

6bd8a79bac96bb6b.text: "Nuraghe s'Omu e s'Orcu" lies near Santa Giusta. The Nuragic stronghold consists of a bilobed central tower, characterised by a lateral tower and a second tower situated in the central part of the complex; the towers are circular, about 7.50 m in diameter, and built of medium- and small-sized quadrangular and polyhedral ashlars laid, with chinking, in regular courses.

6bdc801fc57ea11f.text: Structures belonging to a nuraghe, presumably of the archaic, corridor type. The monument lies inside a private courtyard on the northern outskirts of the present-day village of Bonarcado. Four or five courses of polygonal basalt blocks can still be seen among recent structures of small blocks and cement that lean against the nuraghe. The building technique of the few visible remains would suggest the nuraghe's antiquity.

6bde8a1bfaf5b013.text: At the entrance to the village of Bari Sardo, on the hills of su Pranu, lies the necropolis of Funtana su Rettore, composed of three domus de janas. The domus, of the bicellular type, date to the Late Neolithic, 3500–2800 BC. The tombs, well preserved, are set at almost the same level on the rock face and retain the marks of the tool used to excavate them.

6bef691fe3324eb4.text: Arched stele from a giants' tomb, used as a gatepost for a metal gate

6bf7d017e3025723.text: The monument stands on the Planu Is Ciaexius plateau, in the Sarcidano, a region of south-central Sardinia. The megalithic tomb of Aiodda, which follows the classic giants' tomb layout, was discovered during agricultural work. The entrance, facing east, is preceded by a large semicircular exedra of limestone orthostatic slabs, about 6 m wide.

6bffb266d4c180bb.text: The central tower is elliptical, typical of a proto-nuraghe. The towers are more regular in shape, suggesting they were built in later phases, as was the curtain wall of the courtyard, which encloses a system of stairs and silos (presumably for storing agricultural produce). Some parts of the towers show a smaller-scale fabric in the curtain wall, with flatter, more regular stones.

6c03ef37b8a6ac62.text: Single-tower nuraghe of trachyte blocks; three courses survive. It appears destroyed and completely hidden. It takes its name from the mountain on which it stands, where a convent of nuns stood in ancient times.

6c079978b2c6249f.text: Lacking visible structures and a vestibule. It consists of the linear continuity of the staircase (28–29 steps) and the water chamber, which together form a rectangular void 8.12 m long and 1.25–1.10 m wide. The "bottle-shaped" section of the well, elliptical in plan (1.82 x 1.25 m, height 5.12 m), also sets it apart from the sacred wells of Sardinia. The internal masonry is of polyhedral type.

6c2670cfb1612d42.text: “Sa Pedraia” consists of five hypogea set close together on a short rock face. One of them has an antechamber with a sloping roof and grooves showing the run of the beams. In the same chamber two bull’s-head protomes have been carved naturalistically to show that the fertility god would guarantee rebirth in the new life. The adjacent domus on the left has a cell with a central pillar and a raised lying-in floor.

6c4016261d4b20c0.text: From the second giants' tomb, moving 450 m northwards, one finds an area where the presence of polyhedral boulders of various sizes, only roughly dressed, suggests that a cult area was located there.

6c44e8ba58b7a295.text: A tomb with its top missing, its walls emerging only a few centimetres. Width about 4.50 m, calculable length about 7 m. The burial chamber, apse, and outer perimeter wall are discernible.

6c520e10a6c9f7cd.text: A subtriangular proto-nuraghe built of basalt. It lies a short distance from the nuraghe Su Pranu to the west.

6c537bf64dd5f25b.text: A jewel set among the mountains of Padria, where the Ancient Sardinians quarried the rock and carved extraordinary protomes on an entire wall, enigmatic guardians watching us in silence.

6c7422dd3dd0ee20.text: Mighty and fascinating even under a grey winter sky, the Nuraghe Sa Dom 'e S'Orcu rises from a massive rocky outcrop amid a superb landscape, with broad views over the whole of the Parteolla as far as the Gulf of Cagliari and the Iglesiente mountains. It dates to the 2nd millennium BC and is the principal monument in the territory of Dolianova, where numerous other prehistoric remains are present.

6c75f2cf0e4c437b.text:
It is completely covered with earth and vegetation; one would not even notice that it is a nuraghe were it not for a few limestone blocks laid one on top of another visible on top of the hillock.

On the side away from the sea, a few metres from the summit where the central tower stands, inside a hollow one of the towers of the nuraghe can be seen, in which its tholos, sectioned in half, is visible, built of sandstone and limestone blocks.

6c864ee046e23017.text:
It is a complex nuraghe of which the central tower and three other perimeter towers are visible (the presence of a fourth on the WSW side is not ruled out), joined together by a wall following a straight and curvilinear course.

The last excavation campaign ended in 2009.

The masonry is built of cyclopean basaltic andesite boulders, averaging 3 quintals each, with small stones and mud mortar also used in the interstices.

6c931c087da53fb0.text: Two giants' tombs side by side, from two different building phases. The first is of the dolmenic type, the second is coursed.

6cb510b92060149b.text: Location of the remains of the nuraghe Tattari Pizzinnu, of which only the foundations survive, a Roman villa built with stones from the nuraghe, and the rest of the Roman-period settlement.

6ce39dae2e5193a4.text:
The “Domus de Janas” is cut into a modest, irregularly rounded granite outcrop that barely rises above the surrounding plain.

The plan is reduced to a single cell of modest size; the entrance, which opens to the south, is preceded by a short dromos cut into the rock face, characterised by a sub-trapezoidal plan and bounded laterally by vertical walls that decrease in height from north to south.

6cf84c1648258f8d.text: Single-tower nuraghe, with traces of a settlement around it. The famous Tzricottu bronze tablets were found at this site.

6d12c9ac6baff369.text: The village, lying east of the two nuraghi, occupies a broad flat area and consists of several structures. An apsidal hut is visible, rectangular in plan with a forecourt vestibule, in good condition, together with a probable circular hut and two enclosures. The area covered by the village is currently being excavated, bringing further structures to light. The structures were certainly reused up to recent times.

6d234b2b67f8516d.text:
These natural cavities are among the largest and most beautiful in Sardinia: their rectangular entrance is set in a lush holm-oak forest.

The caves, easily visited, were according to ancient legend the dwelling of three janas (fairies) who were turned to stone by God for killing a friar.

The cave walls are covered with marble-like flows and draperies. From the ceiling it seems almost as if a storm of white stalactites hangs over the visitor.

6d2512265670dcde.text: The village of Sa Muralla, whose name comes from the late medieval walls built around the village and the Castle in 1365, may be linked to the ancient toponym "Nuragonnos" on the northern outskirts of Sanluri; the latter probably referred to the hills on which the present town stands, perhaps already inhabited during the pre-Nuragic Monte Claro phase, as indicated by the Cukkuru Poddinis hypogeum.

6d345b4e8dce70a3.text:
Funerary structure of the Nuragic period.

Form to be completed.

The monument lies in the municipal territory of Norbello (OR).

6d38c3197717aaf3.text: The oldest nuraghe in the Villa Sant'Antonio area is Nuraghe Spei, a corridor nuraghe with a central body consisting of an ellipsoidal structure measuring 22 x 7.5 m, on whose eastern side open the three lintelled entrances of the internal tholos chambers, which are connected to each other by intermural passages. On the opposite side a second, larger ellipsoidal body abuts it, also with three lintelled entrances, now blocked.

6d3cb00219d5b31f.text: The remains of the nuraghe "CULZU" lie in the municipality of Torralba (SS) in the Su Segadu area, a few dozen metres from the nuraghe Longu, in the so-called Valley of the Nuraghi; it is a single-tower nuraghe built of basalt with a chamber flanked by three niches. It has the entrance and the entrance corridor to the chamber; the tholos is missing its top and various trees growing inside the central chamber protrude from it.

6d421014769de527.text:
It lies west of the village centre, along the boundary with the territory of Villaurbana. It is a simple, single-chamber type. It is undoubtedly the best preserved and presumably among the most recent nuraghi in the municipal area.

Oral tradition holds that this nuraghe suffered a dynamite attack in the 1930s; the arrangement of the dome's ashlars and the condition of the western side would support this theory.

6d4b3a357404fc66.text: Near the remains of a church dedicated to the saint after whom this nuraghe is named. Built of basalt blocks in polygonal masonry, it has a surviving elevation of about 3 metres. It is covered by several bushes that prevent the entrance from being identified.

6d7d0fdb313cc7b0.text: The Nuraghe Anulù belongs to the settlement of the same name, a large village dating to the late Nuragic period, composed of about thirty circular huts of medium and small size, interspersed with several walls.

6d8e25da80977a40.text:
Of this megalithic tomb, which must have been closely linked to the nuraghe of the same name, only the upper part of the arched stele survives, in fragments.

The monolith, now incorporated into one of the many dry-stone walls that criss-cross the area near the Serbine nuraghe, measures 1.68 m in height and 1.15 m in maximum width; the frame that defines its outer profile is 0.11 m wide.

6d8f56e551596e0a.text: The nuraghe is in very poor condition, reduced to only a few courses.

6db0af65fe88df78.text: The monument, in a very poor state of preservation, does not allow the original layout of the structures to be identified; one can only hypothesise, judging by the line of some wall stretches on the south side where two courses of granite blocks survive, that it was a simple tholos nuraghe.

6dcbd768492bf225.text: Nuraghe completely destroyed by land-improvement works. Possible location.

6e2c2a4eef76c29f.text: A short stretch of slightly concave wall made of not very large stones is certainly worth observing, because whoever built it did so to meet a family need for a dwelling or for hunting. Assessed within the context of sa Mesana di sos Pianos and the nearby Cudinatos, contemporary with the Domus or the following period, it would take on a different identity. mu

6e40ae5d1d908406.text: A single-tower tholos nuraghe, visible beneath a dense thicket of wild olive and mastic. Apart from a concentration of scattered blocks, a few basal courses of the building remain, built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The surviving structures are filled with collapse debris.

6e59bebbf9b43caf.text: The Nuraghe Bruncu Mannu of Villa Sant'Antonio stands on a rise a short distance from the SP 37. At first glance it looks like a single-tower nuraghe whose top is missing and whose interior is invaded by the flowing crowns of several shrubs. Along the perimeter the entrance can be made out, topped by an interesting lintel. The interior is choked with collapse debris.

6e6301488d8136df.text: Group of domus de janas hidden by the scrub

6e6e58187e87a064.text: A small part of the masonry, built of medium-sized boulders on two or three courses, still survives in a very ruinous state.

6ea5d8590fedd235.text: Situated at about 176 m above sea level, marked on the topographic map as Nuraghe. This complex of dry-stone walls has a variable height between 40 and 110 cm. The plan of these walls is circular in some rooms and squared in others.

6ebf32dc5cc4e514.text: Chance find. Tomb cited in Annalisa Uccheddu's 1995 degree thesis, University of Cagliari, located inside the Villa Siotto Park. Tomb with its top missing and buried. Probable original length about 10 m. Illicitly excavated with the covering removed.

6ed77c025a78a2f8.text: The necropolis consists of four domus de janas, of which the "tomba dell'architettura dipinta" is particularly well known, characterised by relief and painted decorations. The hypogeum, with a T-shaped ground plan, consists of a long dromos ending in a rectangular atrium, an antechamber, a central chamber and two side chambers.

6edd1fa3f0129621.text: Complex nuraghe of the lateral-addition type. A main tower is visible with a secondary tower alongside it on the east side. The entrance to the main tower, facing south, is lintelled and buried for more than half its original height. The entrance corridor, with the typical ogival section, is about 4 m long and built of perfectly worked basalt ashlars, showing a level of construction skill rarely found in other nuraghi in the area.

6f00c4bd48e27299.text: Right next to the electric company village there are two nuraghi and this exceptional giants' tomb belonging to them, called Pira Onne. Here too the stele with its three recesses for the trinity that usually stood above the exedra of coursed masonry stands out; the blocks are slightly squared.

6f1adb74dc4b36ed.text: Nuragic complex with an uncertain plan, in which a very large tower and a series of wall structures of uncertain function connected to it can be recognised. The site was also occupied in the Punic and Roman periods.

6f2f0737aa6cb203.text: Three or more granite menhirs arranged near the nuraghe of the same name

6f99d23c5b92fec4.text: The necropolis consists of six domus de janas in poor condition. One, however, has two pillars carved in the rock with herringbone decoration. The ceiling, also carved, represents the roof of the hut.

6fdc79a1fbf208fc.text: Unfortunately the nuraghe Longu is no different from the desperate state of most of the nuraghi of Chiaramonti. Its study and architecture are interesting, placing it at the centre of attention because it belongs to the type with a sub-floor chamber. Mario Unali,

6fea63746dc425af.text:
It stands on a high rocky spur whose shape has strongly influenced the appearance of the monument, which in its surviving part shows a portion of an internal room with a sub-rectangular plan and rounded corners.

The surviving wall face of this room is about 3 m long and 1.55 m high.

For the rest, the whole nuraghe is reduced to the collapse alone, which is very extensive and located mainly on the southern slope.

701530fd1b68960d.text: Only a single ashlar with a curvilinear profile belonging to the apsidal area is visible of the monument, which is now destroyed, and it indicates that the tomb was of the coursed type in isodomic masonry.

7028bac9da2f2b1a.text:
The monument, of complex type, consists of a central tower and a bilobed bastion.

The central tower is entered through a lintelled doorway. The bastion probably enclosed two towers, one to the east and the other to the south-west:

703cb7e5c0919145.text: Complex nuraghe consisting of a central tower and a bastion with three towers. The original tower survives, filled with earth and collapse. To the south-east stands a tower of which part of the wall structures can be seen; the inner wall face is barely visible because of collapse and vegetation. A curtain wall links this tower with another oriented to the north-east, of which almost the entire wall outline survives. A third tower oriented to the south-west preserves its external perimeter almost intact.

707bb43abefc7022.text: It is a single-tower nuraghe 9.90 metres in diameter whose entrance, still intact, leads into a corridor now open to the sky, off which the guard chamber opens, also intact. The circular chamber (diameter 3.50 m) has lost its top at 3.50 m above the present floor; it has no niches, and the doorway to the stair that led to the upper floors opened above ground level.

707c5cc433c39ac4.text: It is a couple of hectometres from the church of Santa Lucia. At first glance it looks like a single-tower nuraghe, but it could simply be the top of a large complex nuraghe buried inside a hillock formed over the millennia. What is visible is somewhat ruined: a few courses, a cavity that may be the top of the central tower or the end of the stairwell.

70a6588391fca3f7.text: It preserves an intact tholos. A Nuragic settlement surrounds the nuraghe.

717d7ff25025e857.text: Giants' tomb dating to the Middle Bronze Age with a stele, probably bilithic, of a dolmenic giants' tomb partially buried

71878b3f5eb591bd.text: Ruined nuraghe, probably also destroyed during work on the municipal road.

71adc4d1ceccabd1.text: Among the heaps of stones the main tower emerges at the highest point, where the entrance is topped by a bare lintel. The open-air entrance has the niche on the right intact and on the left the collapsed stairwell, passable up to the upper floor from which the interior of the tholos with its two side niches can be seen. On the north-west side a double chamber, partly underground, is entered; it probably connected with the central tower in the lower part, which is now below ground.

71d00273eabf764b.text: Domus de janas entirely cut into the schist, consisting of a single chamber with lateral benches.

71e851cb303a26d2.text:
It lies within the municipal territory of Nule (SS).

The nuraghe is a single-tower nuraghe with a staircase, a corridor niche, and a central chamber flanked by three niches arranged in a cross.

The tower has a circular plan, while the roof has collapsed.

71ed755c83a04f0b.text:
The massive excavation work, the architecture of this monumental hypogeum, dates to the period of the first spread of metals on the island. In this "domus de janas" one sees the result of an evolution and it denotes the consequences of the formation of powerful family nuclei under tribal chiefs, capable of imposing a greater volume of work on their dependants.

The cells opened at a considerable height above the flat rock floor, inaccessible without a ladder.

7200116fa8425f07.text: The monument has been badly damaged by a thorough and indiscriminate clearance operation. Beneath the many piled ashlars that cover the structure, the corridor and one wing of the exedra appear to be distinguishable. Among the ashlars (which show that the tomb was of the coursed, isodomic type), made with great care, the so-called dentilled stele and several curvilinear-profile elements belonging to the apsidal area can be observed.

722159a4b0613854.text:
The nuraghe stands on the edge of the Corte plain, south-west of the town. You follow the Nuoro–Orani farm track and stop at the little bridge that crosses the Rio Su Saju.

On the left, about 200 metres away (near the shepherd's hut), lies the nuraghe. The site occupies a dominant position over what was a possible access route to the Corte plain and made use of the water from the nearby stream, which in ancient times was much more abundant.

Altitude 510 m a.s.l.

7221cdd7a824ba6a.text: Only a few ruins of the nuraghe remain, at an altitude of 599 metres.

7235748baa4d59db.text: Nuraghe to be verified, as it may be an enclosure

7264c64df7e2756b.text: The sacred well of Sa Brecca is located in the locality of Sàrrala é Sùsu in the Marina di Tertenia (Ogliastra). The site takes its name from the Rio Sa Brèca (Sa Brècca on IGM maps) and from the goat sheepfold of the same name (Coìli 'e Sa Brèca) that stands on the remains of the pre-Nuragic settlement. The watercourse is one of the most important on this slope and flows out onto the beach of Fògi Mànna.

72961311a5e39289.text: Corridor nuraghe, a hypothesis supported by the shape of the entrance (lintelled). The site is easily accessible and visitable. Traces of pottery on the outside suggest unauthorised excavations. About 200 m away there is an allée couverte giants' tomb, which some scholars describe as an unfinished work.

72bec0280606cc5a.text: The giants' tomb lies next to a river and is largely destroyed. A stretch of the open corridor is visible. The area is interesting because it is rich in springs. Several nuraghi lie near the giants' tomb. It stands at the foot of Bruncu Salamu, where there are several springs, sacred wells and the Nuraghe Sa Dom'e S'Orcu.

72d09f537fca2a8f.text: Only the outer perimeter of this nuraghe is clearly visible. The rest of the structure is barely discernible. Its plan is rectangular with very rounded corners, and its maximum height to the north is 4 m with six courses of roughly dressed boulders. The western flank consists of a rock face that drops sheer into the valley.

72d9c66bf0b8cd2e.text: Single-tower nuraghe, with its tholos intact. The lintel above the entrance measures about 3.30 x 0.90 x 1.85 m, for an estimated weight of about 16,000 kg.

72dec1afdab3dbff.text: Built by the Sardo-Nuragic people, the well is presumably about 2,700 years old. It was discovered in 1883 during earthworks for laying the state railway tracks; it is assumed that valuable finds were lost. Of the original 40 steps, 22 remain. Various finds such as rings and coins were recovered, all now kept in the Cagliari Archaeological Museum.

72e6751bfcb9859e.text: Nuraghe very ruined, with tholos and walls collapsed

72e9cf6fe89a1532.text: Immersed in the dense vegetation stands the sacred well “Su Presoni”, so named because tradition says it was used as a prison in past centuries. The sacred well is a building linked to the water cult, composed of an underground part (well chamber) and an above-ground part (atrium) connected by a flight of steps. The monument at Cardedu is well preserved; the side walls of the atrium are still clearly visible to a surviving height of more than a metre;

72fd7f2db1d22296.text: Corridor nuraghe. The structures are completely covered and hidden by dense marsh vegetation. The building stands on a small alluvial rise between the Rio Cispiri and a parallel stream. As for the structures, only a few courses of polygonal basalt blocks can barely be made out.

73334df075f2d40f.text: Giants' tomb immersed in vegetation and ruined

734086524c8fca93.text: Single-tower nuraghe in ruins with the tholos collapsed inwards

734d66bde75261ec.text: Hidden Nuragic well. It has been completely sealed with bricks and cement so as not to be detectable.

734f9bcf152baaa5.text: It is an anthropomorphic rock whose appearance is likened to the face of the Egyptian sphinx.

736d818f2d07e30d.text: Three domus de janas. With an imposing column inside and protomes carved on the walls. Very difficult to locate

737672d5524245fe.text: Nuraghe coinciding with a medieval settlement

7386479130ff1b77.text: Partially ruined nuraghe overgrown with vegetation, on the edge of the village near a country church.

7399d94471fe4e98.text: Easy to find and hard to understand, because of its REINFORCED CONCRETE roof that only the local administrators can fathom, not to mention its pitiful state of abandonment. Apparently the giants' tomb was used as a powder magazine during the construction of the SS131, which is why it was fitted with a reinforced concrete roof and an iron door that is no longer there.

73b2467c836df360.text: The most important domus de janas of the Pozzomaggiore area are here. The necropolis has at least 20 rock-cut tombs: some are only roughed out and were never finished, others are buried or badly damaged.

73cd4faee7ca9591.text: This nuraghe has also been completely destroyed; only traces of a single course of a single-tower nuraghe about 9 metres in diameter remain. Many potsherds and basalt lava querns were found on the surface.

73df64cfff64c8e4.text:
Originally there were three, but only one remains standing.

Probable location.

73e9cf8690369397.text: The necropolis, situated along the southern slopes of Monte Corona 'e Teula, consists of 11 domus de janas distinguished by the complexity of their ground plans and decorative schemes. Only one of them is single-chambered, while the others are composed of several cells arranged in an increasingly complex layout.

73f39e579f8c6456.text: The archaeological area includes Nuragic tomb circles at 990 m above sea level, and later structures, among them old cattle enclosures and old sheepfolds called "Pinnetus".

73f579e1cc7b2851.text:
The megalithic monument, 13.5 m long according to the 2005 survey, does not depart from the traditional model. The long corridor was entered through a doorway cut into a generally arched stele, flanked on either side by stelae of decreasing height joined together (exedra).

Despite the collapse of the vault, the corridor is still preserved; the tomb entrance, however, is covered by a dense mastic bush, which prevents verification of the stele's integrity.

74329d8506d9cc99.text:
The necropolis, situated on the southern slopes of Monte Corona 'e Teula, consists of 11 domus de janas distinguished by the complexity of their ground plans and their decorative schemes.

The Tomb of the Hourglasses, on the other hand, comprises 10 chambers; the walls display geometric motifs in relief.

7434a3e7350da766.text: Partially buried nuraghe with a distinctive, worked lintel, now broken in two. The eponymous dolmen is also nearby.

743eac0415527a97.text: Single-tower nuraghe whose layout is hard to determine because of the collapses and the dense vegetation. Even so, the outer wall face of the central tower can be made out. A probable refacing is visible on the west side of the central tower, with two or three courses surviving in places.

749b7cedce716136.text:
Single-tower nuraghe now called “Su Nuraxi”, though it was once better known as “Cocconi”.

A second tower is suspected to have existed in the past. A distinctive feature is that a Byzantine burial complex has been brought to light inside the central tower: a sacred use from which the monument evidently never strayed. Indeed, another of its long-standing names was “Sa Parrocchia”.

74c86c6f6e5f9fed.text: The Furcadizzo nuraghe stands on the small promontory. The monument has suffered heavy collapses. Around the area, wall structures of mixed curvilinear and rectilinear plan can be identified.

74c8837cacc4c8ac.text: Little of this nuraghe remains, only a few large boulders in a circular arrangement. Perhaps the first course of stones of the foundation.

74e3d56d62179238.text: A Chalcolithic necropolis discovered by chance during public works for the new Cagliari aqueduct. Three oven-type tombs were identified and investigated: of the first, found on the lowest part of the ridge on which the site extends, only the cell cut into the sandstone bedrock survived; 5 m to the west of the previous burial a second tomb preserved the vertical shaft and the oven-type cell with an elliptical plan intact.

74e4d95cbbbd6044.text: The tomb corridor survives. It has five courses of stones on the west side and six on the east, a maximum length of 7.40 m and a width of 1 m.

74ece7918ca5c915.text:
Single-tower, single-chambered. With its top missing, the chamber completely filled with collapse debris. The south-east side of its outer wall face, where the entrance opened, has completely slipped away. The highest surviving part of the monument reaches three metres in height and consists of six courses of roughly dressed boulders.

The well-finished entrance lintel lies isolated on the ground a short distance away.

74f038de5b807b48.text: Single-tower nuraghe consisting of a chamber with an intact tholos roof and an internal staircase linking the various levels that make up the complex structure.

74fea0fd06c9c81b.text: The highest part of the Posada crag was occupied by a corridor nuraghe, and on its south-eastern slopes, at a noticeably lower level, a village also stood, probably arranged on terraced levels. The village began about 90 m in a straight line from the nuraghe and extended from an altitude of about 42 m down to about 25 m above sea level, over a difference in level of around 17 metres. (Sanciu 2010)

75026ecfadd78c0b.text: At this site, within a distance of a couple of hundred metres, there are monuments dating from the Abealzu culture, 2700–2400 BC, the Early Bronze Age with the Nuragic wall, and the Bronze Age up to the Roman period, marked by the probable tombs.

7526a2b2655ec8b6.text: In 1788 the community council of Villaputzu complained that the cove of Murtas, where the sea penetrated a long, deep inlet, was unguarded. Corsairs hid "behind large boulders at an ancient nuraghe called Nuraxi de moros", which they used as a base for raids: in 1767 they enslaved two farmers; in 1779 two peasants; in 1781 four; in 1788 two men who were making charcoal for their own use.

75325c73b8774128.text: Single-tower nuraghe with a small surrounding village.

7536faae0508f20a.text: A village of which little or nothing remains because of building work right up to the immediately surrounding areas.

7548806599755d66.text: A nuraghe recorded in old writings (Taramelli) and in the place name known to the village elders. Reported by Costantino Corongiu.

754db59ab6b1fa5a.text: Single-tower nuraghe of which megaliths remain, regularly "ploughed" in which a few sherds of the Final Bronze Age

755308bfc2bedf30.text: Arched stele of a giants' tomb called “S'Artare de su Moro”; the base of the stele is still in situ, while the upper part has been broken off and incorporated into the wall of the little house.

75557b4f530c409a.text: Collapsed nuraghe whose shape cannot be determined

75562bb2d7f67371.text: Sos Monimentos is circular in plan, with a chamber measuring 1.80 x 1.00 m, surrounded by a dry-stone wall of granite. At the entrance to the structure two rectangular slabs stand about 0.60 m high. On these slabs rests the roughly circular covering slab, measuring 2.50 x 2.25 m. Its possible astronomical orientation has not yet been recorded.

75cb095abb7e67dd.text: The two domus de janas, between which a large tree stands, are about 1 km from the village of Goni and are cut into a rock formation about 4 metres above the ground level.

75d63320cb24a1fd.text: Nuraghe whose south side has collapsed but whose tholos is still intact

762889fec822b8ae.text: Single-tower, it is a newly identified feature because the central chamber has imploded and the wall face has collapsed to the west. Some characteristics of the Nuragic masonry can be observed. Nuraghe of San Pietro. Local tradition does not recall a church dedicated to San Pietro in this place. It probably refers to a property linked to the church of San Pietro that stood in the village located at Elva nàna, the name of which has not survived. Mu

762d5a39bab34bce.text: The remains of the funerary structure are completely covered by a thicket of mastic. A circular hut built in recent times on the tomb remains is present; part of the exedra, formed by five basalt boulders arranged in a semicircle, is visible.

7645cfa7b9052a0c.text: In its upper part the corridor appears to have been cut by excavating into the sandstone rock. Below it is covered with soil; the depth is unknown but the distance between the walls is certainly greater further down. Of the conical structure of the well proper, parts made of worked ashlars are visible, especially on our left and in the upper part straight ahead, while the part on the right and the central lower part seem to have been emptied of ashlars, as if they had been taken for other uses or had collapsed. The lower part of the spring is covered with mud.

76d0d21c8da19546.text:
At present a circular tower (diam. 1.50–2 metres) can be seen at the centre of an irregularly quadrangular fortified bastion that follows the rocky contour of the hill.

The entrance to the bastion, on the south-east, has a rectangular opening (width 0.80 m – height 1.05 m above the fill) and is topped by a massive lintel. This doorway leads into a short corridor (depth 2.50 m – height 2.05 m – max. width 1.75 m) that turns left and then stops where it has collapsed.

76dd18c64282c2b5.text: "Giants' tomb of Araene, of the long cell the dense stones of the sides and large slabs of the roof are seen. In the land of Carta Luca, it was Luigi." From Taramelli's description, the tomb of Araene must certainly have been the best preserved among those in the territory of Lodè; unfortunately the monument was destroyed in relatively recent times, as a result of the usual land-reclamation works, which spared practically nothing.

770c3144182a3f41.text:
In an initial phase several villages of quadrangular huts belonging to the Ozieri culture settled in the area; they are associated with a necropolis of hypogean domus de janas tombs and a probable sanctuary with menhirs, stone slabs for sacrifices and stone spheres.

It consists of 8 hypogea, among which the "tomba del Capo" stands out for its importance.

77132f8bf28e67e7.text: Nuraghe of undetermined type. The nuraghe has an unusual staircase which, about halfway along the entrance corridor, at a height of 2.20 metres from the floor, projects diagonally for over 5 metres with a remarkably steep incline leading onto the terrace. The chamber's vault is intact.

77221d85049ccaa6.text: A single-tower tholos nuraghe, unfortunately in an advanced state of decay, protected by a broad outer wall with an overhanging cliff beneath it, which still makes it an inaccessible stronghold.

772fafe891d8aba8.text:
It is a single-tower nuraghe with a guard niche, a probable stairwell, and a chamber with three niches arranged in a cross.

The tower, circular in plan (diam. 12.70 m), survives to a maximum height of 5 m on the west side, with 7 courses, while the minimum height is about 2 metres in the section affected by the entrance, to the south-east, which has completely collapsed. The masonry consists of roughly dressed trachyte blocks laid in horizontal courses with numerous packing wedges.

777912f696f381d4.text: Complex nuraghe consisting of a primitive tower and a bastion, perhaps four-lobed. The entire outline of the central tower survives, although hidden by vegetation and collapse. The structures of two chambers belonging to the central tower survive. A curvilinear curtain wall forms the link between two peripheral towers oriented NNW and ENE. The NNW tower is connected by a curtain wall to another tower oriented WSW, of which much of the outer outline survives.

77b642f048942d06.text: The giants' tomb of Sas Melas stands about 200 metres as the crow flies from the nuraghe of the same name. The tomb is completely buried and in very poor condition; only a few orthostatic stones are visible, protruding just a few centimetres.

77cd0f541baea384.text: on the edge of the hill of the same name: a very ruined tomb, perhaps the only hypogeum left of a small necropolis.

77d7ef31279f1b32.text: Domus de janas for which there are no photographs and whose condition is unknown

77e316e2b1deef19.text: Artificial rock-cut chamber with an entrance, pseudo-square and large.

77f9091d57ea9e86.text: The area preserved the settlement, which was brought to light in the early 1980s. The land was expropriated and archaeological investigations were started, uncovering a series of rooms for domestic use occupied at least until the early medieval period, the traces of a complex nuraghe, and what has been identified as a sacred well, still to be excavated.

78061533a1471bce.text: It is a complex nuraghe situated on the hill called Pettu 'e Murtas, from which it takes its name. Nearby are the remains of several huts, also of Nuragic date.

780d52a5a4b8fcc4.text: Nuraghe with a giants' tomb next to it

7837da5987240a5e.text: Single-chamber domus de janas situated beneath a work of art on the SS 131 dir N.O.

7856b2c653c33ea3.text: Remains of a nuraghe of which only the bases survive.

786a396bedadd1c2.text: Particularly eroded single-chambered domus de janas

7895017e9863cd80.text: Probable proto-nuraghe consisting of a tower sector leaning against a tafone. Probable entrance to the south-east. From the top of the rock it leans against there is a view of the archipelago to the north-east and of Rena Majori to the north-west.

789517f4e77023b6.text:
Nuragic settlement with Middle and Late Bronze Age pottery. Following deep excavations for industrial purposes, the site has recently undergone profound changes.

The single-tower nuraghe has been demolished and the building stones have been set aside; the materials are still visible.

7897702b29e37dd4.text: The archaeological site was discovered in 1985, entirely by chance, during clearance work for a vineyard. Excavations, which continued until 1988, identified the main core of the sanctuary, consisting of the sacred well, a rotunda that characterises part of the large building in isodomic masonry, and two cylindrical structures, interpretable as altars.

78b3cdc10c3a2202.text: It is a nuraghe with a square-plan chamber that was never finished; only the base has been built and the lintel has been set over the entrance. It is interesting because all around lie the boulders ready to be used on the nuraghe, making it valuable for understanding the building technique employed.

78b5930da4036ea9.text: Partly hidden by Mediterranean scrub, the tomb is oriented north–south, with an exedra facing south of which about three courses survive, composed of large quadrangular granite blocks laid in alternating rows, to a surviving height of 90 cm.

78e50c766a67248a.text: Complex nuraghe with settlement; no traces remain on the surface.

78e9b4c1e2b973b9.text: A group of domus de janas on the limestone scarp overlooking the Bunari valley (Abealzu culture).

78f049c42021dc2d.text: A large area belonging to a probable Nuragic village. In the surrounding areas potsherds and other surface finds are easily found. The village extends a good way south from the indicated point and towards the stream to the west.

790aa9345e001bb1.text: The namesake nuraghe near the unique monument, composed of two superimposed towers, stands alone on an extremely high and impressive cliff overlooking the great valley of the Rio S'Acqua Callenti, right near its junction with the Flumendosa valley.

7915c504c9bfedce.text: Catalogued as a probable Roman-period tomb, lined. A superficial part of the monument is visible, next to a hollow in the ground, with a granite lintel and, beneath it, three walls of small and medium ashlars forming dry-stone masonry. It recalls the features of a spring.

792587ac94812cec.text: The giants' tomb of Iscrallotze is particularly ruined. From what remains visible it appears to belong to the dolmenic type of giants' tomb.

79426168b6fc1f48.text:
The Santu Scioni, San Lussorio nuraghe stands in the countryside of Pabillonis, on a hillock from which much of the Campidano plain can be seen towards Monte Linas and above a bend of the Flumini Mannu.

Originally it must have consisted of a central tower and a series of other towers that are now by no means easy to identify, since all the wall structures have been levelled and covered by human activity around the sacredness that the site still retains today.

7960b0b5eef0f3d1.text: The nuraghe has almost completely collapsed. The entrance with its lintel and traces of two corridors remain. A niche in the rear corridor can also be seen. Nuraghe Budas is an example of a proto-nuraghe.

796168d124b3fa96.text: Well of undefined period, often described as Roman but perhaps Nuragic

7983e112784784c1.text: Ruined and buried, so that its structure cannot be defined.

7993b044e93c4d44.text: Single-tower nuraghe, collapsed and stripped of stone, of which only scattered ruins on the ground remain

799c8d9699757d1c.text: The nuraghe Abba Noa stands on a granite spur at an altitude of 178 m and has the particularity of being built in mixed masonry: both local granite and basalt from the surrounding hills were used in its construction. The complex plan consists of two diametrically opposed towers joined by a bastion, straight on the west side and curvilinear on the east, running along the edge of the summit.

79bdbc0867b5f32e.text: A nuraghe of which very little survives externally, collapsed and never studied.

79fb5ddd50813cb9.text: remains of the nuraghe Sa Domo Ezza

7a2a8949e802a487.text:
Small nuraghe, located on a high crag of Monte Dominigu.

Nearby, to the west of the nuraghe, is the megalithic circle of Monte Dominigu. In the maps of the defunct land registry it is marked as Nuraghe San Leonardo.

On the current Sardinian Region CTR it is named "Nuraghe Sa Pedra Pertunta".

7a69d3c5dede37cd.text:
The Lu Brandali nuraghe is of mixed type, with features of both a corridor nuraghe and tholos nuraghi.

The entrance opens in the north-western part of the latter, its length marked by several watchtowers that make use of rock outcrops.

Outside the curtain wall the village extends; Michele Careddu's 1967 survey recorded 36 huts, mostly circular. Period between the 14th and 10th centuries BC.

7a6ba66d84024f55.text: Nuragic megalithic enclosure, probably for defensive use, reused in the Roman period as shown by the presence of potsherds on the ground

7a708dbaa573f236.text: Single-tower nuraghe in very poor condition; only two courses remain.

7a80b5407e370cc2.text: Nuraghe/proto-nuraghe characterised by a sturdy, broad central tower and the remains of two other towers that are barely visible. The nuraghe stands on a hilltop, in a natural stronghold that commands an extensive view, so that the ruins of the castle of Las Plassas can easily be seen with the naked eye.... traces of Punic/Roman pottery suggest the overlapping of several civilisations.

7a814efc9da6f91b.text: Nuraghe, probably a simple tholos type. The structures are very difficult to interpret because of the dense vegetation, the poor state of preservation, and the presence of recent structures leaning against the remains of the building. A few aligned polygonal blocks can be seen, while the rest consists of a heap of jumbled blocks overlain by small stones.

7abf865f400ffb57.text: Discovered by the great cartographer A. Lamarmora in 1840. It is covered in dense mastic vegetation, has collapsed inwards and filled with earth over time. The stones used for the construction are white with yellow patches of dry moss. The surviving height of the tower exposed to the north is about three metres. If visited in summer, the desert-like landscape of the area adds to the fascination of this imposing megalithic monument.

7ac8e088bc943c00.text: Nuragic giants' tomb, fine corridor and partial section of the exedra.

7acd6817ab200e1c.text: The Nuraghe Su Guzzu is a single-tower nuraghe built of limestone blocks with basalt reworkings. It lies about 7 km south of Paulilatino and, together with the Nuraghi Forreddos, De Mesu and Codas, forms a quadrilateral between the territories of Zerfaliu and Paulilatino. The lintel giving access to the inner chamber is very interesting; the tholos is intact but unfortunately the chamber is cluttered with a good deal of collapse debris.

7ace1279234d0420.text: The area, located on the north-western slope of the municipality of Giave, includes the remains of a nuragic tower, with a probable giants' tomb, and an associated settlement.

7ad6153a4bdef6a7.text: Single-tower nuraghe incorporated within Medau Su Conti. In recent times it was used as a support for the masonry of a house. It is partly stripped of its outer stones but overall retains a good height. It is the only accessible nuraghe in Carbonia, even though it lies inside a fenced plot.

7aed96d632277f10.text: Probably a three-lobed nuraghe, of which only the basal courses survive.

7b0b30d92fac3c58.text: This nuraghe is only one of the countless examples found within the territory. Its condition is appreciable, but a maintenance intervention by the municipality was necessary because of some landslides.

7b28191e0ed2bf32.text:
Complex nuraghe, with a bilobed bastion

The central tower has a mezzanine floor.

7b530fcbc5b7f3f3.text: The tomb has its top missing and is of orthostatic, coursed construction. Part of the exedra, the lintelled doorway, the burial corridor and part of the apse survive. Length about 12 m.

7b67b06be8f19eb5.text: Nuragic settlement area. A Nuragic site has been located with clear signs of human presence (1300 BC).

7b90345baaaa84cc.text: It lies within the municipal territory of Collinas. The Regional Commission for the Cultural Heritage of Sardinia, by its Decree no. 155 of 14 December 2017, declared the property known as the “Nuragic Tomb of Sa Terra de Su Muru” to be of particular archaeological interest.

7b971a19d6a9316d.text:
The nuraghe is a single-tower tholos nuraghe, built of roughly dressed trachyte stones, with a circular base 12 metres in external diameter, a surviving height of about 6 metres, and walls sloping at 7 to 11 degrees.

The entrance, oriented to the south-east as in most nuraghi, is topped by a lintel made of two separate blocks and leads into the corridor, roofed with transverse slabs.

7bb5d84b33f249d2.text: The stone of Sant Eliseo is a large erratic boulder on the lower slopes of Monte Santu, in the territory of Mores. Used in various periods, it was first a Prehistoric Tomb of the Neolithic, then adapted by the Romans, and finally became a Byzantine church dedicated to Sant Eliseo. The domus has a ground floor and a first floor, reminiscent of the houses of the fairies (in Sardinian, precisely, Domus De Janas).

7bfebc9880a6962f.text: Single-tower nuraghe; the entrance is not visible, and its diameter is about 9 metres. It belongs to the Su Padru nuraghe complex.

7c14da6520431c61.text: The monument, built of limestone, has an internal diameter of about four metres, small by known standards, but not excessively so when compared with the width of the spur on which it stands, which extends for just over six metres before ending at the edge of a cliff.

7c38ca4975ec7cb6.text: Masonry of barely rough-hewn blocks alongside others that are well shaped, of various sizes. The side towers: the one on the left is better preserved than the others, rising from the ground for four courses of blocks of considerable size; the tower on the right is barely visible on the surface, with two courses partly buried; the third tower, its footprint covered by collapse, stands opposite the entrance.

7c3cb4e9daccceb9.text: Nuraghe that could belong to the category of "unfinished" ones

7c58d30eb6130184.text:
The monument is in the Mandras locality (Campeda), 600 metres north-east of the Mura Sauccu nuraghe and less than 300 metres west of the Mura Sauccu B nuraghe.

It is a single-tower nuraghe surviving to a maximum height of about 6.50 metres. The masonry consists of large and medium-sized blocks.

7c918c0968785213.text: Of the monument, of the coursed type in polygonal granite blocks, the corridor and part of the outer profile of the tomb body are visible.

7cc1c6b8018f93d3.text:
Despite the very dense vegetation and the collapses the monument has suffered, the ruins of a central body flanked by two towers, built of pink trachyte boulders, can be made out.

A short distance away, to the south-west, traces of several circular stone structures are visible.

7cd6235b2c1e7848.text: Complex nuraghe. Access to the upper floor is via a staircase that passes under the SE tower.

7cd870a56f53943d.text:
The monument has a complex plan in which at least two bodies can be distinguished, one leaning against the other, developing along a north-east–south-west axis 16.50 m long.

The perimeter of the north-eastern body, which has almost completely collapsed and is partly buried, can be traced only at the point where it joins the other tower and in part on the western side.

It may have been an elliptical element whose major diameter measures about 7 m.

7cddc2b81b58910e.text:
It is a two-chambered domus de janas, oriented south-east, with a largely broken-in ceiling (opening 1.06 x 0.86 m) and lacking the partition that separated the two chambers, demolished in recent times to create a single, more spacious room.

The hypogeum is entered through a quadrangular hatch (height 0.44 m – width 0.50 m – thickness 0.22 m) finely shaped and fitted with a triple frame for the cover slab.

7ced4863bf2b3751.text:
Sa Pedra de Nunnale. A picturesque and colossal tower of bizarre shape, at the base of which stands the eponymous Nuraghe. The nuraghe, though imposing, appears incredibly tiny compared to the immense rock that looms over it.

This single-tower nuraghe is built of barely dressed megalithic blocks, even larger at the base. Around the rocky mass it is possible to make out the huts of a small village.

7cf73674873c1848.text: This is a domus that has probably suffered the collapse of its forecourt, leaving only the entrance chamber and the inner cell.

7cfe7e178bba8f0e.text:
A rather massive towered structure can nevertheless be distinguished. This tower stands off-centre in relation to a kind of walled “enclosure” that appears to have been very thick and abuts it on the northern side, while a facing of large blocks involves the western sector of the tower.

Another outer wall is visible from north-west to south-east, almost doubling the tower’s perimeter.

7d05c4e0d889acec.text: Nuragic settlement or sacred place reused up to the Roman period. The foundations of several structures from different historical periods are present.

7d0c7098ff859ee7.text: In an irregularly shaped granitic rock ledge, two single-chambered domus de janas have been cut. The surrounding area is characterised by a dense oak wood. The two hypogeal burials, about 1 m apart, are cut respectively into the north and west sides of a granitic ledge.

7d233f1cd7313ba6.text: Nuragic settlement with particular attention to the lithic industry. Among other finds, polished stone axes, hammers and mace-heads have been found here. One of the most unusual finds is a depiction of a dagger on pottery.

7d28584c1acddc63.text: The site consists of a three-lobed nuraghe, still largely buried, and structures probably of Roman date.

7d3c1bb3a802b614.text:
The complex consists of a "cromlech" and other menhirs. In the surrounding area, an underground necropolis attests to the intensive occupation of the territory in prehistory.

The "cromlech" is made of large rounded boulders (trachyte, grey granite and pure white quartz) transported from considerable distances.

The complex is attributable to the Final Neolithic (3200–2800 BC, Ozieri culture) and the Early and Middle Chalcolithic (2800–2400 BC, Filigosa and Abealzu cultures).

7d3d3a06ff742cd1.text: It lies in the territory of the municipality of Nuoro. It is a single-chambered domus de janas, well finished inside. Difficult to locate because of the dense vegetation. It opens onto a low granite outcrop.

7d443d672f585b48.text: North-west of the nuraghe there is a small pond fed by spring water, which is present even in summer, albeit in very small amounts. The pond has a completely natural, irregular triangular shape. The deepest point reaches the overflow level at about 120 cm.

7d59e78cab0ec01c.text: No official records exist, but locally it is said that a complex nuraghe and a very large village lie buried beneath the hill, as suggested by the traces left by tomb robbers.

7d5a807ad5898dc0.text: Multi-lobed nuraghe; the central tower (which has a mezzanine) retains its intact tholos roof over the chamber.

7d863c6c44e1f7b7.text: The finds show that it was occupied from the Middle Bronze Age to the Recent Bronze Age. It is built of large limestone blocks and preserved a chamber with two niches and a staircase. Now the collapse blocks the entrance. Near the nuraghe the remains of a hut can be recognised, consisting of a circular room and an atrium.

7d86a2c7e08394af.text: The tomb is in excellent condition, both inside and out. The façade, built of well-squared medium-sized blocks laid with care, has a low rectangular entrance doorway at the centre (about 50 cm wide and 60 cm high). The burial chamber reaches a height of about 1.80 m at its highest point; the apse that closes the rear of the chamber is also very well preserved.

7dbe34d1a0d27d5a.text:
His Majesty ERGULIS, the largest of the nuraghi in the Cuglieri area, is a single-tower nuraghe at 106 m above sea level and survives intact in both its masonry and its vault.

It has two opposite niches just beyond the entrance lintel and two inside the chamber, while the niche that would face the entrance is missing.

The lintel has a relieving window facing south.

7dc188d410891d65.text: The Golunie nuraghe stands on land owned by the Guiso family (former Barons) exactly on the boundary between the territories of Orosei and Dorgali, in the Cala Osalla area, and looks out both towards the Marina beach in the area of the second pier of Osalla (Orosei) and towards the beach of the same name (Dorgali).

7dd0a845dba3da57.text: Typical Nuragic spring with jambs made of stone ashlars and a closing lintel. Interior with a water-collection basin.

7de53b7e6aedb211.text:
The small necropolis of Ovau consists of three small domus de janas. The first is the one with the largest chamber and a doorway frame; the third, on the other hand, is very small inside.

Nearby are two unusual superimposed menhirs, very well worked. The first menhir

7e133945f8f3d096.text:
Single-tower nuraghe of which only the ground-level courses remain.

Twenty-two Nuragic villages, large and small, are known in the municipal area, not all occupied at the same time. They are often found near a nuraghe, as in the case of the Bruncu Pubusa site.

7e48b0377f887cc4.text:
The nuraghe, collapsed internally, shows a fairly irregular plan, typical more of proto-nuraghe than of true tholos nuraghe.

7e6486e20e39b408.text: It spends most of the year beneath the waters of Lake Cuga. Destroyed single-tower nuraghe; only a few courses of the original structure are visible. During the excavations before the dam works, the archaeologist Contu found an important Nuragic model boat here.

7e6f797e2c77924c.text: In the territory of Sanluri there are the remains of as many as 15 nuraghi, three of which are of the complex multi-tower type: Corti Sa Perda, Geni, Nuraxi Candelas.

7e79bafee054cb25.text:
THE PISCINA'E SALI SITE. The archaeological area is reached by following an agricultural track that starts from Via Cimitero, continuing straight on at the junction at Gedilis and crossing the Pranu Corongiu plateau until the right-hand side road.

The area certainly played a prominent role in the past as regards religious manifestations; no fewer than ten menhirs have been found in the valley and are associated with the funerary contexts of Pranu Corongiu

7e7a3b0c5a011c65.text: The Pastoris nuraghe is a simple type, situated to the north-east of the settlement, near the municipal water reservoir, next to which some buildings belonging to a livestock farm were erected a few years ago; these do not really harmonise with the Nuragic presence.

7e93987d182f67e6.text: It is a massive andesite nuraghe with a three-lobed plan, the result of adding two secondary towers in front of the central tower, linked by walls that enclose a central courtyard. Not far from the nuraghe stands a hut of considerable size; nearby there is also a well carefully lined inside, also probably dating to the Nuragic period.

7e95ee0ad54c1ce7.text: Partially destroyed and close to the Portoscuso industrial zone.

7ed0bdad34442b0c.text: A collapsed and buried tomb whose structure cannot be defined

7eeeb7d33221049c.text: The tomb has been considerably disturbed, partly because of illegal excavations; it preserves (a rare case for the area) a (probable) large fragment of the central stele of the exedra.

7ef45367926eb7d6.text: Of the two giants' tombs, both relatively ruined, the burial chamber and the exedra can be recognised.

7effd430be5af0ab.text: This complex nuraghe, with five towers and a curtain wall as long as 450 metres, rises imposingly on the eastern edge of the Abbasanta plateau. The general layout of the Santa Marra nuraghe is complex and three-lobed, with a concave-convex perimeter, similar in type to the Santu Antine nuraghe at Torralba and the Losa nuraghe at Abbasanta, but reworked in an original way.

7f04ce2fd6363de6.text:
Nuragic well in the territory of Guasila about which no significant information exists.

It is simply noted that the construction is of isodomic masonry and has, in its upper part, a crowning of T-shaped ashlars, a feature found only in far more famous monuments of the highest quality.

7f1f971cc3192b6e.text: Here too there is a mezzanine and a subsidiary staircase, raised inside the right-hand niche of the chamber. A nuraghe whose layout reminded me of Crabia at Bauladu.

7f27d3e53b5a77ef.text: This nuraghe was identified through a letter written to NurNet by a reader of the page. The nuraghe appears destroyed and incorporated into a large rural building. Hence the name "Medau Mannu".

7f5a2c7d36d4204f.text: The site is characterised by a quadrangular courtyard that was originally the main chamber, now collapsed. It is entered through a granite arch of rare beauty, and from there into what remains of the original domus de janas: two chambers, one quadrangular and aligned with the entrance, the other irregular in shape on the right.

7f9098052b19ca61.text:
The necropolis consists of 14 domus de janas, considered among the most beautiful in Sardinia for their architectural conception.

Twelve of them are cut into the rock in a horizontal row, the other two opposite the first ones. The façades are striking for their monumentality and the precision of the workmanship: in particular that of tomb 3. A drainage channel cut into the rock, still visible, protected the burials from rainwater infiltration.

7f9de465cff952e7.text: Megalithic enclosure with an overturned menhir inside.

7fa413f806fde21c.text:
A single-tower nuraghe (mostly remains) is present on the ridge of the hill Cuccuru S. Eremilis, very close to the road.

Position to be verified

7fade875b4639b87.text: The nuraghe cannot be detected on the ground because of dense scrub covering a possible destruction layer. The presence of abundant pottery nevertheless indicates the Nuragic origin of the site's occupation.

7fe710208d526fe5.text: Giants' tomb with a bilithic stele of which only the lower part remains; the monument has been disturbed over the years by looters and stone-robbing.

7ffa59388d9f37e9.text: It may be the same nuraghe that some books call Thorcodossile, marked 500 m further west. Only a few ruins remain on top of the hill.

8013714e42ae323f.text: Nuraghe Artòra dominates the Capo Comino spur from 120 m above the sea and performed the watchful function of the present-day semaphore. Situated a short distance from the lighthouse that dominates Capo Comino, it is described by Relli as a complex nuraghe on the summit of the same name, but is barely distinguishable because it is covered by a concrete platform built for military purposes during the Second World War.

80170f61eb05eec7.text:
Single-tower nuraghe; the tholos roof of the chamber survives almost intact.

It is one of the few nuraghi equipped with a mezzanine or intermediate floor above the entrance corridor.

80195b3358c48d7e.text: It is a complex structure consisting of a main tower (or central tower) and two subsidiary towers flanking it to the south. Its entrance has partially collapsed, making access difficult.

806567e0252adb7f.text: Possible origin of the name: nuraghe of the scolca, which in the Judicate period was a guard post. On a small rise at 70 m above sea level there is a heap of stones and basalt boulders, traces of tombs, Roman pottery and obsidian flakes.

8078fc654046dcab.text: Small and single domus de janas

808526370313d697.text: The nuraghe Thorra, like the nuraghe Sas Melas, stands on a low hill rising at the bottom of the valley, surrounded by higher ground; from this position it closely controls an important ford on the Rio Torra, a tributary of the Rio Mannu. Three hundred metres away to the west lies the eponymous giants' tomb, recorded by Taramelli who, strangely, makes no mention of the nuraghe at all.

80e2883b898d197b.text:
The construction is extensive and complex. The area outlined in red is the highest and is well enclosed by typically Nuragic walls up to two and a half metres thick.

All around, however, the existence of other walls can be discerned; they defined a much larger surface, with terraces stepping down towards the impluvium to the north.

The building dominated the valley, now completely built over, which takes its name from the little church of Santa Barbara.

80e7bd9418e716a6.text: Single-tower nuraghe near which traces of a settlement and a well are found.

8100fe508a82a8f9.text: Given its commanding position over the surrounding countryside, it is thought to have been a very important and complex nuraghe. Unfortunately, only two curved stretches of wall are now visible, one to the north and the other to the south. Many basalt lava querns have been found nearby.

810ef39c5126548e.text:
The monument stands on the edge of a steep rock face that drops sheer to the south, in an area of particular interest for the presence of numerous archaeological monuments, both prehistoric and Nuragic.

The building has a roughly quadrangular plan and is crossed by a through corridor flanked by opposing pairs of large niches; the corners are rounded, the walls where the entrances open are straight in profile to the ESE and slightly concave to the ENE.

81302f5d3c8147a7.text:
Probable location.

There are two underground tombs.

81310aa1c1f00435.text:
The monument consists of a central tower against which, on the north-western side, a second ruined tower leans.

The main tower, built of basalt blocks of various sizes, survives to a maximum height of about 8 metres. An internal staircase leads to the upper level. An extensive village, indicated on the surface by stone rubble and numerous ceramic finds, extended around the nuraghe.

813f62f6f295eba7.text: The context is unusual because the rock-cut stone appears “isolated”, surrounded by holm oaks that camouflage it; the entrance faces south-west, the chamber is circular and its walls contain squared niches, the surrounding ground slopes, and a few metres away to the west there is a fine rocky escarpment.

8147ae29e3075826.text: Complex nuraghe; its poor state of preservation and the fact that the structures are heavily buried mean it cannot be confidently assigned to any defined type.

8162d36833239887.text: The Sisini nuraghe stands on the summit of a low hill in the countryside at the entrance to the hamlet of the same name. It has an original and uncommon plan that follows the model of sacred wells. It consists of a tower with a circular base preceded by a massive square bastion.

8180ead9bf5b3806.text: The nuraghe, built of basalt blocks, is in fair condition. It consists of a main tower and two others leaning against it, though the structure of one is unrecognisable because of collapse. Through a lintelled entrance you enter the main tower, where a niche and the remains of a staircase can be seen. From the nuraghe there is a splendid view over the bay of Cea.

81a5237036541632.text: One of the many nuraghi, hidden by the earth, in the territory of Oschiri

81a76b2df2c6da79.text: It lies on the south slope of Monte Lerno. The structure is in a state of serious decay. Nevertheless, part of the wall is easily recognisable because one of the entrances is still in good condition. At first glance this could be mistaken for a dolmen because of its particular structure, with a massive flat stone resting on the walls. A short distance further downhill there is another building, resembling a hut.

81b03c7500ded028.text: Village – scattered across the area are several stretches of walling that may belong to the village huts; unfortunately the dense vegetation does not allow a broad view of the area and makes it difficult to identify the structures.

81b3ae51a8171068.text: The domus de janas, which exists in the immediate vicinity of the nuraghe, marks the continuity of occupation of the site over the millennia.

81b4bce6e8ad73f7.text: Complex nuraghe with a central tower and three added towers with bastions (three-lobed). Around the nuraghe are traces of a settlement.

81b76175724dd560.text: Excavated in an amphitheatre of trachyte rock on the southern flank of the 'silent' hill of sa Pranedda, it consists of over 40 tombs of various sizes and plans, aligned along the rock face in a symmetrical arrangement that appears pre-planned. The necropolis of Montessu is one of the most significant and fascinating pre-Nuragic testimonies on the Island, in use for a millennium and a half, from the Late Neolithic (3200–2800 BC) to the Early Bronze Age (1800–1600 BC).

81b8c07b765b0153.text: Considerable difficulty; ascent not recommended. Several overhanging sections. In some places there are walkways and cables to use as handrails.

81c3177e971c93d1.text: It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, 11 m in diameter, preserved to a height of about 2.5 m over three courses. Cyclopean walling of barely dressed boulders. The entrance, to the south-east, lacks a lintel and leads into a corridor about 2 m long.

81d209ea94cd6f19.text: The menhir, known as Su Furconi de Luxia Arrabiosa, stands alone on a small plateau. It is quadrangular, tapering towards the top into an almost conical shape, and measures 3.60 m in height. On its main face, which faces east, twelve small cup-marks are carved.

81e28b0675eef0dd.text: At Baratè, on a low rise in an area used as an olive grove and partly as a vineyard. On the north side four courses survive (height 1.80 m) of trachyte blocks; on the south side the remains of the elevation are covered by vegetation. Boundary walls lean against the nuraghe.

81e5e27fbac886f3.text: Only a few traces of the structure remain; the site is neither accessible nor easily legible at present. Following the penetration of the Greek Church, Greek Orthodox monks and hermits taught the inhabitants the production of sun-dried bricks in the eastern manner, made of mud and straw (ladrini), which were used for building houses, using the stone taken from the nuraghe Zira as a foundation.

81e6856957d28340.text: It stands on a rise, in a panoramic spot overlooking much of the Ogliastra territory. Of the structure, which is in poor condition, only a few courses of limestone blocks are legible.

81fcbc280e6a9834.text: On a hillock beside the Atzara–Belvì provincial road, blocks of granite have been found, almost completely buried and arranged in a circle, which are thought to belong to a nuraghe.

822541bc6b7ab710.text:
The Maiore nuraghe (14th–9th century BC) is a single-tower type, currently standing more than eight metres high, with a clear taper towards the top; it has a single entrance on the south-east side. From the entrance a corridor leads to the central ground-floor chamber, which has a tholos roof, while on the left a stairway gives access to the upper level.

Because the tower suffered a major collapse before the 1980s, restoration work became necessary.

8227992fceab608b.text: Complex nuraghe or nuragic palace, apparently six-lobed, completely razed to the ground, of which only the low courses, partly buried, emerge. From it one dominated much of the Marmilla.

8237978d36df3440.text:
The domus is cut into a limestone face that is almost sheer above the valley below. It has a façade 2.60 m high depicting a simple stele. On the stele are the three typical recesses.

Like most architectural-façade domus created from scratch, it has a single chamber; this has a semi-elliptical plan. Inside, on the left, a wide niche opens whose function is unclear but which was presumably used for depositing votive objects.

824022900d8905f7.text:
The nuraghe consists of a main building with a three-storey central tower, against which a bilobed bastion on two levels is built, enclosing a courtyard and two secondary towers. It is surrounded by an outer wall provided with towers and by a sacred area.

Its tower has the largest diameter of any known nuraghe.

825207b3af858e70.text: An enormous, tall building of huge, very dark basalt blocks, cyclopean, worked just enough to fit them together and give the structures perfect circularity. The central tower, very broad, and two other towers are visible, one to the south-east and the other to the north-west, plus a stretch of wall linking the central tower to the north-western one. The maximum visible height of the tower walls reaches 3 metres. The eastern part of the complex is covered with earth and vegetation.

826c34e947bdec43.text: Dolmen I consists of a large slab resting on stones that originally must have been set on edge to support the roof. Of Dolmen II the ceiling slab and a few wall boulders survive. In the same area about sixty hemispherical hollows are also recorded, clearly artificial and perhaps linked to ancient cult practices connected with the prehistoric monuments just described.

82837c38a2c5482d.text: A village already inhabited in the Iron Age. According to the PUC the site continues to be affected by quarrying activities and, in particular, by a large dump of equipment and inert materials. A quarry where 10,000 tonnes of toxic waste from Portovesme S.r.l. were illegally buried.

8297d6a6d955ba1d.text:
The existence of the village, belonging to the nearby nuraghe of the same name, is attested by the presence of a few circular huts and other alignments of stones emerging from the ground.

The settlement lies in the municipal territory of Macomer (NU).

829ace6260d3f0ab.text: It is a “corridor nuraghe” standing at the centre of a broad outer wall within which the ruins of a large village can be made out. The monument stands on the basalt plateau that stretches between the settlements of Dualchi and Borore. About 180 metres to the north-east lie the remains of the giants' tomb of the same name, while to the north-west is the giants' tomb of Putzu Iu.

82bfa9476bb00be5.text: Complex nuraghe with traces of a village around it and major collapses on the slopes. From here there is a significant view and control over the village with the temple of Irru.

82cb39628fc500a7.text:
Built entirely of granite, it is of the central-corridor type, with a mixed layout that combines the plan of corridor nuraghi and tholos nuraghi with a central corridor and paired chambers; the structure is massive and irregular. The tholos is intact.

The bastion is reached by a staircase accessible from the courtyard. The entrance leads into a central corridor, covered by an ogival vault, which runs the full length of the building and opens onto a large courtyard.

82d2b69b360ef99f.text: The area is heavily built up and rich in remains. The presence of this wall, built of medium-sized polygonal boulders, others only roughly shaped, does not seem to follow a pre-planned direction, but is by no means random. The surrounding territory is rich in features from which its importance can be inferred. The freely interpreted drawing is a partial ideal vision of the sites in that territory.

82f0d84e6ad28898.text: The site consists essentially of two parts: the first, formed by the well temple, a sacred well dating to the Nuragic period, with structures attached to it: a meeting hut, an enclosure, and other smaller huts. The second part of the complex, about two hundred metres to the south-west, consists of a single-tower nuraghe, some elongated stone huts of uncertain date, and a Nuragic village, still to be excavated, of which only a few emerging elements are visible.

831e367f36eaec84.text: Single-tower nuraghe with an attached village. The original tower survives, its interior choked with collapse and vegetation. About four complete courses of the original structure remain. To the south there is a curtain wall with an entrance topped by a lintel; because of collapse and vegetation its function cannot be determined. To the north-west of the tower a cyclopean wall is present, breaking off abruptly, apparently the north wall of a corridor.

833bf4c6f2f60103.text: The nuraghe was built in the advanced phase of the Middle Bronze Age (1500–1400 BC) on a granite base surrounded by a series of massive boulders, adapting the building to the irregular shape of the hill. It is a four-lobed nuraghe, with a central tower and four other towers added concentrically.
