Access is made easy by a ramp leading to the entrance, which in turn opens into a long corridor with corbelled walls forming a pointed arch.

8342c3ac24f9e115.text: Oral sources insist that a nuraghe stands on the summit of Bruncu Zinnibiri, without specifying whether it is a single tower or a more complex structure. Immediately below the few ruins of the “nuraghe” the village extended, also the target of continuous illicit digging; one of the surveys carried out led to the discovery of a cultural deposit near which charcoal remains were observed and where abundant ceramic material was collected.

834e76b0e7970f6d.text: Nuraghe currently under excavation. It is thought to consist of a central tholos and four surrounding towers enclosing a courtyard. An extensive village of numerous huts, also used in Punic and Roman times, spreads around it, protected by a massive system of walls up to 6 metres thick. Great importance attaches to the discovery inside the village of a glass-working workshop. The site is not open to the public.

83513fcd96d1c93f.text: The necropolis consists of eleven domus de janas, both single- and multi-chambered. The largest originally had five chambers, now a single space after the partition walls were demolished. It is distinguished by two distinct phases of use: the first in the Neolithic and the second in the Middle Bronze Age (1700–1300 BC), when at least three hypogea were converted into "domus a prospetto architettonico".

8367345caeb83466.text: A ruined nuraghe of which only a few courses survive in elevation, set into natural rock masses.

8375f645498b8e92.text: The tomb is small and built with orthostatic technique. Disturbed by illegal digging, during the excavation and restoration work carried out in 1996 fragments of a carinated bowl of a particular shape were found, which has no parallels in Sardinia; in 2008 various glass-paste necklace elements were recovered.

838be6dc8474df98.text: A ruined nuraghe of which very little survives, situated at the junction of three boundaries.

83ced32001881340.text: Necropolis consisting of four domus de janas cut into erratic boulders

83d1d8a64e2f75cf.text: This site lies in an olive grove and was studied in the past. It is now completely destroyed and it is unclear whether any village remains survive underground. Some hut or nuraghe shapes can still be made out. The farmland is covered with squared stones and stone fragments. Most of the stones of various sizes have ended up in the many dry-stone walls that surround the site.

83d512f6de506d9b.text: In the immediate area behind the mouth of the Mannu River, the complex nuraghe Monte Aiveghe survives to a height of about 1.2 m with three courses of limestone blocks belonging to the upper parts of the two towers. Around it the remains of at least three huts belonging to the probable associated village can be recognised. A scatter of Roman-period pottery is also attested.

83f3894ad6fcd03c.text: This hypogeal tomb, cut into an erratic boulder, lies about 300 m from the village sports field. Other boulders with cupmarks can be seen nearby.

83f477bc8ff4d066.text: There are three giants' tombs, of which the first is the most important and the best preserved.

84026b5e5d9ca8e0.text: The investigations have identified traces of human presence at the site dating from the period between the Late Neolithic (3300–2700 BC) and the Chalcolithic (2700–1700 BC). The most monumental evidence consists of the menhirs present at the site: single, in pairs, in triads, in spectacular alignments formed by as many as 20 menhirs, and in circles. Walking through the site one can see menhirs lying on the ground everywhere, whole or in fragments. The site must originally have been larger than it appears today.

844719993f47d5a7.text: An apparently single-tower nuraghe cleared of vegetation in 2022. It was previously recorded as a single-tower nuraghe, but it now seems more likely to have been a four-lobed one. A considerable quantity of Roman pottery (terra sigillata) lies around the nuraghe.

845d3ca5e4e1ea1a.text: The Lorenzu Origa nuraghe partly incorporates the pink granite spur on which it was built into its wall face. The monument appears as a truncated-cone tower about 11 m in diameter, preserving a surviving height of at least 2.80–2.50 m. The other opening, topped by a lintel, leads into a space that is actually a sort of corridor roofed with blocks laid in steps and may be part of a stairwell.

846642c6282f93ab.text: A single-tower nuraghe, partly in good condition, standing on the ridge of a small hill.

84b15019b36fb12a.text: The site is hard to locate. It appears to the visitor as a heap of buried ashlars, only very partially exposed. It is reached via the mid-slope path behind the settlement of Capoterra,

84b557dfaff9d7b0.text:
The giants' tomb lies to the south, about 500 metres from the nuraghe; only part of the inner wall face of the chamber and traces of the peristalith are visible.

In an area of about 2000 sq m around the giants' tomb, numerous structures are visible of which only the basal courses remain; in particular a wall stands out that encloses a roughly rectangular area, inside which there are traces of various types of rooms, some semicircular but mostly quadrangular.

84c8f552e740643e.text: Single-tower nuraghe with an addition that is not easily legible. Surrounding village.

84cf04d8b566f687.text: Enormous single-tower nuraghe, not accessible, built on a rocky ridge; walls up to 4 metres high remain above ground. Reached on foot via the road to the Forestry Service lookout. One of the highest points in the area, it commands a beautiful view.

84e9f853f83d1907.text:
Its entrance is unusually oriented to the north-east.

By now it is covered with earth and sand, although the top of the nuraghe still shows the chamber with its top missing, from which part of the internal masonry can be glimpsed.

84ff8079e9fb8de0.text: The cave is reached by a staircase built with Nuragic technique and covered with lintels for sixteen steps, very similar to the one used inside nuraghi. The cave consists of two large chambers and a small single-cell room at the top of the cavity. On the floor of the cave there are ceramic fragments of the Nuragic period. The site is generally classified as a hypogean temple or as a refuge.

8518e13c448dbcaa.text: The monument is quite imposing: it measures 22 m overall; the exedra has a chord length of 18 m and almost all the boulders remain, set on edge, some of them very tall. The burial corridor is 16 m long, 1.30 m high and 1.40 m wide; it is roofed with horizontal slabs, one of which is missing, allowing a view of the interior, whose cross-section is rectangular.

852acd05cc7c6024.text: The village lies at the foot of Monte Perdas de Fogu, in the locality Sa Costa de su Lurdagu. The structures survive as disordered wall remains; in some cases two rows of boulders are arranged in a pseudo-circular form. All the structures contain fallen boulders and rubble inside, making it difficult to determine their original perimeter and shape. Numerous potsherds of various kinds are visible on the surface throughout the area.

852f16d8d985536b.text: Complex tholos nuraghe. Completely enveloped by vegetation, it is a large nuraghe whose features can only be vaguely guessed. It appears to consist of a central tower and two added towers, with an internal courtyard now filled with collapse blocks. Built of large blocks of local basalt, it survives in good condition, although it is hard to observe because of the bushes that envelop it.

85401d129d2ca0de.text: At Funtanazza, on the Lampis family's land, lies the giants' tomb of Bruncu Espis, a place where a Roman village once stood. Well preserved and looked after by the landowners, it has a corridor about ten metres long and a little over one metre wide, and is completely covered by the earth above which some ancient structures still appear.

85629a0f51e8b232.text: Single-tower nuraghe, covered by a canopy of vegetation, its tholos still intact

8589650ab91db3fd.text:
Practically in the town, on a ridge overlooking Tossilo, this completely derelict single-tower nuraghe stands out. Its layout is the most classic one, with a niche to the left of the entrance to the south-south-east, and the staircase to the upper floor on the left. Inside the tholos, though completely covered in brambles, the three typical niches can be made out.

A splendid spot for sunsets of nostalgic meditation.

858992b85b1c16dd.text: Once you have “crawled” your way inside, the tomb reveals itself in all its beauty: the column, the bas-relief protomes, the cells, the antechambers, the door to the afterlife, the symbols and signs of an archaic devotion that intoxicate both soul and spirit.

85a1c349b9085472.text: The village includes three sacred wells and a series of circular huts. The best-preserved well lies in the northern sector of the area. Built of medium-sized blocks of local schist, it abuts a small natural rock face to the south-west. Access to the chamber is off-centre relative to the axis of the tholos. The tholos has collapsed on its northern side. The area in front of the entrance chamber is bounded by a series of curvilinear walls at different levels.

85f2a426195c131d.text:
Inside a pastoral farm, at the centre of a circular sheepfold bounded by a dry-stone wall, stands a unique and exceptional proto-anthropomorphic menhir fixed in the ground. The pillar, 1.77 m high, shows a summary rendering of a head set off from the body below by a short neck, and may symbolically evoke the phallic symbol.

It lies 500 metres north-west of the hypogeal necropolis of Monte Ozastru.

8606324f17341d23.text: The temple was built in isodomic masonry, that is, with blocks of basalt expertly squared and dressed with the appropriate slope where needed. The rocks in the surrounding area consist mainly of schists or granites, and the volcanic rock used was brought to the site from rather distant locations, probably from the territory of Dorgali.

860f89d966f4035c.text: The archaeological area lies on the edge of the Santa Lucia basalt plateau, east of the Monte Arci massif. It includes two complex nuraghi with a village, set about 50 metres apart. The nuraghe to the east is also complex, in better condition than the previous one; it preserves the central tower chamber, with its top missing, with several niches in the walls and the stairwell opening off the entrance corridor.

8623547e0c115955.text:
Tholos nuraghe.

The main tower currently preserves its chamber, which is sub-circular in plan and filled with collapse debris from the tholos and the upper part of the wall face; a first block marking the start of the corridor is visible. About 8.50 m to the south there is a secondary tower surviving to a height of five courses, laid in polygonal technique and in an irregular manner.

865687fd2c3fbc54.text: The location of the nuraghe reported by Taramelli on the hillside can be presumed. The nuraghe was already demolished in Taramelli's time and is no longer visible. The location is not precise.

8693d32834b08d93.text: It now appears as a modest rise. Probable "tancato" complex nuraghe (two towers with an intermediate courtyard). Stretches of wall survive. Destroyed by the opening of the municipal road.

8694c5b4aa5867a2.text: Easily visible next to the municipal road, the upper part of the tower is almost destroyed; there is an entrance covered by shrubs.

86c0086b33f07f97.text: Nuraghe Abbaia (Acquaviva); it stands halfway up the mountain of the same name, near two abundant springs. This nuraghe, of which only scant remains survive, also served to watch the coastline in visual contact with Nuraghe Ottiolo.

86dab82870f7f473.text:
It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan (diam. 12.50 m) and an entrance facing south-east; the tower survives to a maximum height of 4.80 m on the south-east side, with six courses, while the minimum height is on the north-west side at 2 metres with three courses. The masonry consists of carefully worked blocks laid in regular horizontal courses.

In the surrounding area the circular structures of numerous huts from the Nuragic settlement are clearly visible.

86dd54fc1a0e946c.text: Single-tower nuraghe. About 100 metres from the monument there is a Roman hypogeum, partly cut into the rock and partly built of brick with a barrel vault.

86f42518434a190d.text: Location according to ancient maps of this nuraghe of which only scattered stones are found today.

8710668f7587c7cf.text:
A burial of the Nuragic period. The monument is fairly well preserved, though partly hidden by vegetation; its outer profile, the funerary corridor and the right wing of the exedra can be seen.

The construction technique is regular coursed masonry using sub-squared polygonal blocks.

8724fa70b12fc476.text: The central tower, which at its top has a diameter of about 8 m, is clearly legible. It survives for nine courses of regular sub-squared masonry with medium-sized blocks wedged with stone chips. The upper interior is completely blocked by collapse. Added structures can be made out, though with difficulty, hidden by vegetation.

873f78d54a0f0148.text:
The nuraghe, almost completely demolished, is traceable in its entire ground-plan profile (diameter 11 m, surviving height about 2 m).

Near the nuraghe, scattered over an extensive area (about 12 hectares), the remains of a great many circular structures (generally more than 7 m in diameter) and rectilinear ones can be seen, attributable to the ancient settlement and probably also belonging to a sacred area.

8746908ae8c291f0.text: A large Nuragic complex comprising three structures identified as water-cult buildings. The Superintendence marks the third as a probable nuraghe.

874f380519baa735.text: It is situated on the north-east slope of Monte Sozu, just below Su Casteddu where the nuraghe of the same name stands. It is the largest giants' tomb in our territory of Chiaramonti. The burial cist, about 15 m long, is built of stones of various sizes roughly shaped, and is covered with large trachyte slabs laid flat. Mu

87521610f8d1f860.text: It consists of at least four domus de janas, still being excavated.

8771bb3ddd23d00b.text:
It is in a poor state of preservation.

It is a proto-nuraghe; the tower survives to a maximum height of 5.50 m.

Within a radius of 400 m there are three giants' tombs, a Nuragic spring, and five baetyls.

877260810e55e77c.text: Two opposing dolmenic tombs. One has been excavated and consists of two chambers, with the entrance facing south. The other is unexplored; its covering slabs are visible, and the entrance faces north.

878d15915ef7aefb.text: With the filling of the Oliai artificial reservoir, it reappears on the summit of a small islet.

8799c12b16150fc1.text: Small giants' tomb, belonging to the Appiu village context. Never excavated, it appears to belong to the cyclopean type of giants' tomb, even though it lies in an area where the type with an arched stele is prevalent.

87aa554490418714.text: It is a two-chambered domus de janas with a short antechamber cut into a trachyte outcrop. The chambers are arranged along the longitudinal axis and have carefully smoothed walls and slightly hemispherical ceilings; the entrance faces south-east.

87aba838b149e43b.text: Between 1950 and 1960 a lime kiln was built, whose structure was very probably made using stones from the village.

87de76843d0aca7d.text: This is a complex nuraghe, with at least the ashlars of the upper courses masterfully worked in sandstone. Unfortunately it is difficult to visit and document because of the vegetation.

87e7eac82f9a7341.text: The nuraghe Su Cuttu stands on the Alghero–Ittiri provincial road. It is a single-tower nuraghe that has suffered considerable disturbance. Only a few boulders remain in their original position. It belongs to the complex of nuraghi in the Cuga valley.

87f660e9a29263e0.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. The structures are completely enveloped in vegetation, so that they look like a small natural rise covered in brambles, bushes and scrub. Although the monument's type can only be guessed at with difficulty from observation, it is likely that if cleared of vegetation it would prove to be in fair condition.

881647d8baa379be.text: Complex nuraghe with a frontal addition and lateral development, with a central tower and two added towers with bastions, and a courtyard between them serving as a connecting space.

8819c63e5660577a.text: The Prunittu necropolis is in the Sorrana area. The complex consists of two clusters about a hundred metres apart and contains 27 domus de janas in total. Most of the hypogea are easily reached, but some, cut into the vertical face of a trachyte bench with their entrances set well above ground level (up to four metres), can only be accessed by lowering oneself from the plateau above.

882028d065d86e04.text: A few remains of a single-tower nuraghe built of limestone. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

883743940e5fb5a3.text: The attribution of the site to the Nuragic period is not certain.

883f034a05109c58.text: Collapsed remains of a probable single-tower nuraghe

884b762848e5cda8.text:
It stands on the highest point of Florinas (517 m a.s.l.).

Unfortunately it has now collapsed inwards.

It has a central tower and two added towers.

884f7669f49de708.text:
A single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal basalt blocks.

The building is completely covered in brambles and climbing vegetation, so that only a few stretches of the external wall face can be seen. From above one can observe the collapse debris filling the inner chamber. Modern and contemporary structures, enclosures and shelters, lean against the nuraghe on the west side.

8853127344c1c3a9.text: Complex nuraghe; the central tower is visible, and inside it there are three niches. It has been heavily disturbed by agricultural mechanisation and the incessant activity of tomb robbers. An extensive village was attached to it, reaching as far as the giants' tomb of Sa Pedra Longa.

885842d1e767c62e.text: The nuraghe is built of soft trachyte blocks, not very large. The foundations rest directly on the bedrock, which also forms a natural bastion that was then finished and completed by the nuraghe's builders by adding large blocks. Nearby the base of a Nuragic hut is visible. Single-tower nuraghe with village and outer wall with probable seven towers

8861785dd22406a5.text:
Popular memory records the existence of a complex nuraghe beneath the Su Pisu Fort.

The reconstruction commissioned by the Region for the Phoenician Sulky project shows a Nuragic village on the hilltop overlooking the harbour and the ancient city.

88726d1720fb1b71.text: Reported as a nuraghe, it turns out to be a high pile of stones. Very useful for hikers because, coming from Magola along the cliff edge, it marks the turning point to pick up the path below the walls. Watch out for sheepdogs!

887589c464cd286d.text: These are three baetyls of truncated-conical shape, about a metre and a half high with a diameter of about 60–80 cm, lying on the right-hand side of the tomb. At some unknown date the central baetyl was overturned and turned into a trough.

8875f87e19b01d2f.text:
The site dates to about 3000 BC and was used for about 1500 years, from the time of the Ozieri culture to that of Bonnanaro.

It takes its name from the large number of skeletons (more than 200) and the rich assemblage of weapons – datable to about 1650–1600 BC – consisting of swords and daggers in arsenical copper (19 in all). The swords, with triangular blades, range in length from 27 to 66 cm and show some similarities with the swords of the El Argar culture (Spain).

8878fdebdd388f78.text: Single-tower nuraghe; it faces the nuraghe Su Nuraxi on the opposite bank of the Rio su Gaffu.

88914d40bc7fe058.text: The name would indicate a probable three-lobed nuraghe, almost completely destroyed, of considerable size; above the central tower there is an entrance covered with shrubs.

88976154d099e122.text: A natural cave consisting of a single chamber inside which prehistoric potsherds are visible. The cave has been heavily disturbed by clandestine excavation.

88be519d1323c5f2.text: Nuraghe with a large village and associated giants' tomb. Ruined and overgrown with vegetation. The shape is difficult to identify.

88c05bce9563fc54.text: The “Tittiriola” at Bolotana is a single-tower nuraghe built of basalt blocks, bounded by an outer wall and set within a village whose traces are still appreciable. It has an internal stair chamber that is currently impassable because of collapses, and on the upper part, corresponding to the entrance, a large window surmounted by a lintel is clearly visible. Near the structure a sacred well is visible that appears to have been covered over in relatively recent times.

88d9a109ae8cda4c.text: Two domus de janas at the foot of the hill called "Sas Monzas". Cut into Miocene limestone.

88e19494d38a8f3b.text: Ruined giants' tomb belonging to the nuraghe and village of the same name

88e84835013e9645.text: Located on a picturesque natural crag near the Nieddu nuraghe. It appears ruined and hard to interpret because only a few courses remain in situ. The main tower and a smaller secondary tower, probably added later, are visible.

88f044de5f09228d.text: It has a fine intact tholos and, at a height of about four metres, two niches that certainly communicated with the staircase leading to the upper floor. The boldness of the construction is evident, since the two niches should weaken the ogival structure, which instead appears solid and strong in all its beauty. Part of the upper floor, accessible from the outside, is also visible.

890eb5f7a40d4579.text: The nuraghe is in a state of complete abandonment. Half buried and completely overgrown with vegetation.

890f048030b5196c.text: These are the ruins of a site and a settlement that must originally have been of medium-to-large size. One can indeed make out what must have been the imposing central tower (only the base, the side walls and the entrance lintel remain), at least three other towers, and extensive fortifications running all round the perimeter of the low hill on which the site stands.

8919634a7358cc2a.text: Remains dating to the Nuragic period situated on Isola Rossa, about one kilometre from the coast of the municipality of Teulada. The area forms part of the Capo Teulada military firing range.

891b4f5102377522.text: The Pranu Narbonis Necropolis consists of a group of three domus de janas still in an excellent state of preservation, cut into a single large outcrop of granitic rock.

89494ba1f15853ac.text:
Of the megalithic burial, of isodomic type and oriented south-east, the funerary corridor can be measured (length 4.20 m – width 1.05 m), consisting of four blocks per side and one at the end, all finely worked; the layout of the exedra and that of the tomb body are less clear.

Among the scattered stones in the exedra area lies a dentilled ashlar: it is trapezoidal (1.85 x 1.15 x 0.75 m high), has a slight rebate and the usual three vertical notches.

894b96583b2e93c0.text: The village consists of three sacred wells and a series of circular huts. The best-preserved well lies in the northern sector of the area. Built of local schist blocks, it abuts a small natural rock face to the south-west. The entrance to the chamber is off-centre relative to the axis of the tholos. The latter has collapsed on its northern side. The area in front of the well's entrance chamber is bounded by a series of curvilinear walls at different levels.

8974fcab08c004b0.text: Remains of a probable Nuragic settlement now lying in the centre of a road-junction ramp

8987b76e41c3ac78.text: The high, lintelled entrance leads into what must have been a sheltered space built on the edge of a sheer drop. On the left as you enter there is a circular room; on the right of the corridor only the perimeter wall survives.

898cca40919711f4.text: It is a complex nuraghe, consisting of a main tower surrounded by a four-lobed bastion that includes four corner towers and an open courtyard. In the north-eastern area the remains of the outer wall and the ruins of the annexed settlement are visible.

89af1ba9e7a5d05a.text: Neolithic huts of circular form, characterised by large boulders up to 1.00–1.20 metres high resting on the bedrock.

89d315f30a378464.text: A short distance from the hypogeal tomb of Putzu, on the other side of the farm track that crosses the locality of Busola, two menhirs have been identified. One of the menhirs is still fixed in the ground in its original position. A second menhir, with a pointed lateral profile and an elliptical cross-section, flat on the longer side, is incorporated into the doorpost of the field entrance.

8a0be753a7a08799.text: The tomb is covered by enormous flat stone slabs, including one more than four metres long.

8a225f2452816252.text: The monument, of complex type (four-lobed), comprises a main tower to which four secondary towers have been added, linked to the north and east by straight curtain walls, while the connecting wall structure to the west is curved.

8a27f8c2f1d48fa2.text:
The monument lies about 200 metres from the nuraghe of the same name.

The tomb has been partly demolished with the removal of all the worked ashlars that faced the burial chamber.

Nevertheless, despite the very poor state of preservation, the usual ground plan of this tomb type can still be read on the ground: a rectangular body with an apsidal rear, a semicircular exedra at the front, and a rectangular burial chamber.

8a3351f43e8a2410.text: Among the few remains of the nuraghe, the lintel deserves special mention; it appears almost suspended in mid-air.

8a3b9b687f111427.text: The tomb opens a few metres from the remains of a small single-chambered domus de janas (Tomb III); it is very likely that Tomb II was also originally a small domus de janas, later transformed into the form of a façade tomb. The stele now lacks its upper part with the lunette frame, which lies overturned a few metres from the entrance.

8a56c6f0dc294e96.text: Nuraghe forming part of the complex of nuraghi in the Cuga basin. Apparently bilobed, but a third, semi-destroyed tower beneath the lake waters cannot be ruled out. All around, the remains of a vast Roman settlement are clearly visible.

8a5b8384ad6b11f8.text: Probable complex nuraghe, completely collapsed and slipped.

8a63e89d8447490e.text: The Ortei nuraghe is a three-lobed type, consisting of a central tower, still in a good state of preservation, and two lateral towers whose remains are almost completely buried and overgrown with vegetation. The peculiarity of this nuraghe lies in the fact that the chamber of the central tower, which has a circular plan, is provided with three particularly deep niches, especially the central one, which has a large lintel with a small window above it.

8a6d1a32de3d8926.text: They are three hypogea cut into a low limestone ridge.

8a7b1f979b75dcd9.text:
The tomb is built with coursed masonry. The tomb body contains a rectangular funerary corridor, closed at the far end by a single shaped head slab with an arched top.

The exedra survives only in part: the hemicycle is bounded by orthostatic slabs of reduced size, at the base of which runs a low bench-seat, also incomplete, intended to receive offerings.

The rear wall face of the exedra joins the tomb body without a break.

8a878bf830ca952c.text: It consists of five hypogea, one of which is underground and one difficult to locate.

8a8e71474c221cfe.text: Domus de janas on the edge of the village, next to which a house has been built.

8a9226598ad04adb.text: Small dolmen closed on three sides with a single covering slab.

8a98614405b54f31.text: The reliefs at Sa Icu in Dorgali are on the basalt cliff overhanging the Cedrino, 1.2 km east of provincial road no. 38, and are attributed to the Chalcolithic. They consist of 57 geometric figures covering an area of 10 x 12 m, carved mostly in high relief (only one is incised) on three basalt blocks that protrude on average 30 cm above ground level. The figures depict: simple parallelepipeds, truncated terraced pyramids of three tiers with simple rectangular plans or with a semicircle on the longer side of the base parallelepipeds.

8aa6fdb28e3d2888.text: Nuraghe named after the locality "Sa tanca 'e su padru". Of imposing size but completely destroyed and not appreciable. Until a few years ago it allowed internal access.

8ab6d8af7af45de5.text:
A large cavern extending for about 40 metres, with an archaeological deposit disturbed by guano diggers and clandestine excavators.

From the disturbed layers come ceramic materials ranging from the second half of the 5th millennium BC to the Republican period.

8ab7ddf510c88b29.text: It is probably the closing slab of a domus de janas.

8ad5ddc43032f1e4.text: The necropolis consists of three domus de janas.

8ae20d05fb32a010.text: A ruined single-tower nuraghe of which only a few courses survive

8ae99d90f8b5aadb.text:
Possible single-tower nuraghe; the doubt arises from its small size, but it could be a small nuraghe placed on a height with the sole role of a lookout.

Near the structure there are two tombs, perhaps of Roman date, built of limestone slabs; inside, two skulls and other human bones can be seen.

8aeb7b39fc9ca14e.text: It is one of the many nuraghi in the Thiesi area, of which only a few remains can be identified today.

8affd99fff66cae1.text: A tomb circle built of large, semi-worked slab-like boulders of various shapes, mostly triangular. It differs from the others in the size of the slabs. The circular structure is broken on the north-west side, where presumably three or four boulders are missing. Nine boulders remain in their original position, covering three-quarters of the construction. Some recumbent slabs lie at the edges and very probably originally closed the circle.

8b1387a597181fc3.text:
In its present state of preservation it is only possible to hypothesise, on the basis of the few identifiable wall stretches, that the monument developed on several levels following the different levels of the rocky peak on which it was built.

Perhaps its major axis was oriented north–south, but the position of the entrance and the plan layout of the chamber remain undefinable.

8b1e1b4b21858f01.text: A complex nuraghe that is hard to define because of its degraded state and the considerable burial of the structures. It stands on the Capo San Marco height with a commanding 360° view.

8b45b03db155062f.text: The Nuragic spring of Su Musuelu lies about 600 m east of the Nuragic sacred spring of Is Molineddus. From the little information Spano was able to gather, its temple consisted of a rectangular building with the entrance on the western side, built of large blocks laid dry. Behind the building a spring rose from the rock and collected in a round well, also made of large stones.

8b60279ab8ed73bb.text: Complex nuraghe with three towers probably added later. Limestone ashlars. Nearby are the remains of a village and two giants' tombs.

8b65044db8954ac9.text: What remains of a giants' tomb located in the picnic area of the Santa Barbara forest

8b848d0934b4810f.text:
A burial of the Nuragic period. A monument of considerable size in a good state of preservation, legible in all its components except the entrance area, which has now been altered and retains only two residual fragments of the original stele.

The construction technique is of the coursed type, using polygonal blocks of granite.

8b84d0c8cd626ed5.text:
Two domus de janas about 2 m apart. An antechamber with a semi-elliptical plan and an irregularly flat ceiling. In the back wall of the antechamber a quadrangular doorway, also with a rebate, gives access to a chamber with a flat ceiling.

A doorway with a rectangular opening and a rebate for a closing slab gives access to an antechamber with a sub-elliptical plan and a flat ceiling.

8b88e15ab7753425.text: The Cuccurada archaeological complex stands on the southern tip of the Mogoro basalt plateau of “Sa Struvina”, in a position commanding a wide view over the Campidano plain and the Rio Mogoro valley. Excavations carried out from 1994 to the present have revealed the presence of monumental structures attributable to different periods: a megalithic wall and a cyclopean structure with an elliptical plan (Cuccurada A), attributable to the developed Eneolithic (Monte Claro Culture, 2700–2200 BC).

8b88f17f0e5c676b.text: Artefact submerged by an artificial lake

8b951ea2a36be01d.text:
The Nuraghe Biriola lies at Dualchi, about four hundred metres from the Nuraghe Piddio. It is a complex nuraghe that looks like a veritable fortress of considerable size (about 38 by 22 metres). The central tower contains a large circular chamber with a corbelled roof; niches, partly accessible, are set in the central part of the structure.

A village once stood around the nuraghe, and traces of it are still visible.

8bb010f32a356bd4.text:
It stands on the summit of a hill in the Marmilla. The structure is a complex type, formed by an original central tower built in the Middle Bronze Age, to which four more towers and a bastion were later added. One of the four towers was subsequently sacrificed during a further building phase that presumably also saw the construction of the massive hexagonal outer wall.

In the Early Iron Age a new village developed on the site.

8bf5479ed3f26aac.text: Menhir located about 40 m from the Nuraghe de Chirigu. The menhir has three faces: the two opposite ones are roughly semicircular with a flat surface, while the third, rear face is convex. Natural fissures and hollows can be seen, together with smooth areas that are probably not natural.

8bf9062aaddc2558.text: Built of basalt blocks, the construction has a trilobate layout, with a central tower and three secondary towers arranged around a sickle-shaped courtyard. The structure was surrounded by a massive outer wall – clear traces of which survive – composed of five towers and straight curtain walls, except on the north side, which was naturally protected by the Giara ridges.

8bf9cfba40da64a7.text: The alignment of closely spaced stones at Serra Pillonadori stands on the south-western slopes of the Su Niu de is Crobus ridge and west of the Baccu Ungroneddus, in a position from which the valley of S. Barbara and the Rio Solanas can be taken in at a single glance and which is visible from practically every point of the inner ridges and valleys below. The five granite stones of which it consists are arranged on a north–south axis and face east.

8c163f822bfa4e7a.text: A large natural cave on whose eastern side several smaller cavities open; their morphological features would lead one to classify them as domus de janas, a hypothesis supported by the presence on the summit of the cave of channels and cupmarks used for both functional and ritual purposes.

8c27698951ab5b79.text:
It is probably a corridor nuraghe against which various elongated huts and numerous dry-stone walls were later built, making it particularly difficult to survey.

From this heap of rubble overgrown with vegetation a circular tower (diam. 11–12 metres) emerges, with a surviving height of 4 metres.

At the top, where the tower is missing, short stretches of corridor can be made out, but they cannot be defined because of the collapse.

8c5cd6af648a6110.text: The Nuraghe Dom'e Biriu lies about 1.5 km north of Genoni. Largely ruined, a tower of roughly square plan can still be made out, built with horizontal courses and almost squared blocks.

8c86be6426246128.text: It is recorded in the historical memory of those who worked on the construction of the Madau artificial reservoir in the second half of the 1900s. No evidence of obvious buildings or foundations of any other kind exists in situ.

8c8f592a10901388.text: The largest nuraghe in the territory of Illorai, mentioned by Taramelli, G. Lilliu and Angius-Casalis, consists of a central tower probably of two storeys with its tholos still intact; on the south side is the courtyard with the entrance partly collapsed; on the north-east and north-west sides are the two lateral towers (with collapsed tholoi) but their internal walls are in excellent condition. Collapses inwards are minimal, while those outwards are substantial. Contact AGRIS for access to the area.

8c973c77e93b2b08.text: Originally it must have formed, together with the nearby Nuraghe Ena Ortu, a single extensive settlement.

8caaefdddd31f327.text: Giants' tomb in very poor condition; the chamber can still be read clearly, while the exedra is partly incorporated into the enclosure wall. It lies inside a fenced plot a short distance from the country church of Santa Cristina. Easily reached.

8cd5a56b1dad06ee.text: Complex nuraghe built of schist (Stintino stone). Three towers are still visible, with a massive outer wall encircling the structure. Around the nuraghe there are clear traces of huts and collapses of associated structures. The tholos survives almost intact, except for a few courses.

8ce5f57c95f85a72.text: Complex nuraghe of which the central tower and a bastion, perhaps three-lobed, survive. The original tower retains almost its entire outline. The interior of the tower is filled with collapse and vegetation. To the NNE there is a curving wall that reaches its maximum height to the ENE, where five courses survive; it may be a tower. To the W–SW a wall can be made out, probably belonging to a lateral tower. A further tower was probably located to the SE. Ceramic fragments are present, attributable from the Nuragic period to the medieval period.

8d0a7646f05f6dfb.text: Complex nuraghe, ruined and overgrown with vegetation. The tholos is intact. Surrounded by an important outer wall.

8d13d1896fa9e569.text:
Collective burial of the Nuragic period.

Of the monument, hidden by a thicket of mastic, the apsidal area with the terminal part of the corridor is visible.

8d1c6dd59b61d075.text:
Santa Vittoria is one of the most important cult complexes of Nuragic Sardinia. Covering more than three hectares, it is protected to the south/south-west by a natural cliff and to the north-west by a wall that follows the rocky edge.

The sanctuary has four main groups of buildings: the two temples and the "priest's hut", the "festival enclosure", the "double baetyl" enclosure group, and the east-south-east group

8d38456f080a447a.text:
What is visible is only a small portion. The rest is completely buried and covered by vegetation. A circular structure on several levels.

A little lower down an ancient wall, cut into the rock and formed of very large stone blocks.

8d640e1766c944c5.text: Included in the Municipal Urban Plan. There are no authoritative scholarly sources on the structure. Local oral tradition says it has an entrance on an inclined plane/steps for a couple of metres down to a base, then a vertical drop of about 20/25 metres. The landowners in that area sealed the entrance with a large boulder/slab.

8d84d4ec05e26245.text:
In a wooded area, cut into trachyte rock. The interior is decorated with a false door and an overlying probable bull's-head protome.

It comprises 7 hypogea in total, known.

8da24ee84bd04f1b.text: Of the practically destroyed monument, the outer outline of the tomb body and the exedra are still visible on the ground. Shaped ashlars worked on their exposed faces lie on the ground, showing that the tomb was of the coursed type in isodomic masonry. During the last site visit (Jan. 2012) it was found that the two so-called dentilled stelae that lay next to the burial are no longer present.

8da6e04882651802.text:
Nuraghe "CASTEDDU" located in loc. Pozzo S. Nicola (Comune di Stintino).

It could be a trilobate or quadrilobate nuraghe; at present it is buried.

L.L.

8db28d14ca80c3bd.text: In this area, used for cultivation for many years, eight monoliths were found during ploughing; five of them still lie on the ground today. These menhirs, all made from a single block of local trachyte, have an average height of 180 cm and present one flat face and one convex face.

8db4146460198c4b.text: Nuraghe submerged by the lake basin on the Temo

8dc6449e6dbd4c13.text: Only the central corridor of the structure can be recognised. All around lie scattered ashlars that cannot be immediately linked to the tomb.

8dd09721ba09b137.text: The monument retains a good part of the internal corridor. The outer wall face can be traced as far as the exedra, of which the right-hand side is visible, while on the left there are only two upright stones corresponding to the entrance. A short distance away lies the megalithic stele, unfortunately cut, and what appears to be the closing slab.

8dd38400d708d7e6.text: The monument's wall structures are clearly visible: those of the central tower, plus other towers, plus a probable one. The outer wall with its lintelled entrance is clearly visible. The central tower's structure survives for as many as seven courses.

8de61a176bf25107.text: Nuraghe destroyed at the time of the land reclamation in the area. Large boulders (not found in the surrounding area) remain on the site; they were used several decades ago to build terraces. Pottery sherds probably of Nuragic date and fragments of millstones from the same period have been noted in the area. It is impossible to determine its exact location and dimensions.

8df16460ebc746a0.text: About 250 m from the Nuraghe Noccus, on a rocky outcrop, there are: a very unusual tafone, now partly collapsed; three large monoliths (about 250 cm high), set a short distance apart, which could be menhirs; numerous boulders of various unusual shapes, in some cases next to the monoliths, in others scattered without a clear order but close to them. In the opinion of a (female) archaeologist, the menhirs do indeed seem to mark out the funerary space.

8df50dc3c051752a.text: The shape of this single-tower nuraghe is still clearly visible, although unfortunately only a few blocks have survived.

8df74754790fb377.text: A collective burial of the Nuragic period. The structure has been largely destroyed and is also covered by vegetation and rubble.

8dfb25bdc5b6cd09.text: The ceramic finds recovered date to the Monte Claro phase and correspond to those from the nearby nuraghe Trobas. This stands on a rise flanking the prehistoric track to Villanovaforru and has an unusual layout with a large semi-underground chamber and four adjoining rooms.

8e01f05f032248d9.text: The collapses and dense vegetation do not allow the structure to be defined perfectly, but it appears to have an elliptical plan and to be of mixed type: a corridor nuraghe, probably flanked by a tower built at a later date, to which a further circular tholos structure may have corresponded.

8e738b76d5b88de5.text:
The complex consists of an extensive settlement defended by a wall (length 120 m; maximum height 5.00 m): the north-eastern end is better preserved, where a tower is incorporated. In the central sector, probably protecting the entrance to the acropolis.

Halfway up the slope are the remains of a second fortification, built of large squared blocks. The village extends over the summit of the plateau and has numerous huts; the complex is datable to 1400–1000 BC.

8e74eb40453f5d72.text: The nuraghe Santu Antine, also called Sa domo de su Re ("The King's House" in Italian), is one of the most majestic nuraghi in the whole of Sardinia and also one of the most important of those still standing. The entire complex is a major example of prehistoric Mediterranean architecture, and its original height is thought to have reached between 22 and 24 metres, the tallest for that period after the Egyptian pyramids and the central tower of the Nuragic palace of Arrubiu, which measured between 25 and 30 metres.

8e789743acc61c92.text: A complex nuraghe of the four-lobed type; the central tower is surrounded by a bastion with four towers enclosing a courtyard. Around it are traces of a settlement and a defensive wall.

8e7a61f892f2d6df.text: The Nuragic village of Perdu Isu (one nuraghe and traces of about 11 huts) and the cistern-like cache known as "Su scusorgiu" lie at an altitude clearly above 1000 m a.s.l. The village stands on the crest of one of the tacchi, in visual contact with the better-known site of Serbissi and with the valley where the complex of "Is Tostoinus" stands.

8e8e19bab6ae95b3.text: Complex consisting of 9 domus de janas. Probable location.

8ea0f582168973b8.text: The structure of the nuraghe is clearly complex; the compact mass of the monument is immediately apparent, dominated by the central tower. To the north-west of the nuraghe, about ten metres away inside the enclosure, stands a large stone which, because of its shape, is thought to be a stele; its presence gives the site its name, and also the name of the Nuraghe Istelai, or "place of the steles". All around, traces of the ancient human settlement are evident, ranging from the pre-Nuragic period back to the Neolithic.

8ea4155b10d13fa7.text: Generally known as Su Corrazzu dessu Estiu, it is so large that its circuit measures no more than a hundred ordinary paces, and it is built of enormous stones with the wall about 30 palms high on one side and half that on the other. Inside and around there is a great mass of ruins. The simple folk who live there believe an evil angel dwells within, so many fear to approach it, and only the most courageous dare go there in September to search for some marvellous flower of prodigious virtue that benefits whoever picks it. But all who have gone have laboured in vain, because the spirit of the place hides it. This place and this spirit are the subject of wondrous tales among the people of Fluminimaggiore, and anyone who tries to dissuade them speaks in vain.

8eca328bde420779.text: The nuraghe takes its name from the light colour of the stone used to build it.

8eca6f87337bc156.text: The complex nuraghe Diana consists of a tholos and two minor towers linked by a curtain wall to form an overall triangular shape. In the centre is an open-air quadrangular courtyard giving access to the various rooms.

8ed62323df7f05e0.text:
It lies in the municipality of Buddusò (OT).

It comprises at least 10 hypogea.

8ef2a9e9dcffab73.text: Only a few medium-sized boulders of the basal circle survive in a ruined state; inside them the entrance facing south-east can be seen. With the main structures of the nuraghe missing, it is likely to be classified as a tomb.

8eff65e9a28f886d.text: A tancato nuraghe with a central tower and an added tower opposite. The nuraghe lies near the necropolis where the great statues of Monti Prama were found.

8f123f5d4bd877c2.text: The probable Nuragic village occupies a large area on the eastern slope of the channel called S'ega Langonis. Despite the dense vegetation, more than 30 circular and rectangular huts can be counted. All have collapsed or imploded, partly because of illicit digging; even so, several courses of the perimeter walls survive on some of them. All the structures were built of small- and medium-sized polyhedral boulders, laid dry in more or less regular courses.

8f297746da765c2b.text: Nuraghe in a poor state of preservation.

8f3399b222075658.text: The nuraghe stands in a commanding position over the broad Modolo valley, in the Planargia region of north-eastern Sardinia. The building, of particular interest and grandeur, is a corridor nuraghe. It has an irregular elliptical plan, crossed longitudinally by a through corridor with opposed entrances.

8f4533db60aaeca1.text: Structures belonging to a single-tower tholos nuraghe. The building stands on a low rise in a commanding position over the surrounding plain. Three to four courses of the outer wall face, built of polygonal blocks of local basalt, can be seen, while the inner chamber is destroyed and not visible. The maximum surviving height is about 2 m.

8f5296aa02bb0459.text: Single-tower nuraghe forming part of the complex of nuraghi in the Cuga valley. At present almost invisible and impenetrable because of the scrub.

8f5333befdd60973.text: The slabs of the burial chamber and a small portion of the outer wall face on the east side are visible. The chamber has been partially dug out by looters, who also excavated in the mass of fill making up the tomb mound, between the left wall of the burial chamber and the course of stones of the outer wall face, wrongly believing that the two walls enclosed a second burial chamber adjoining the first.

8f6a608f41bfbc8b.text: It is a small dolmen that is still intact.

8f72432eac5bb9ab.text: The nuraghe, an archaic corridor type, built of large polygonal blocks of local basalt, has a quadrangular–elliptical plan. It shows two communicating entrances, on the north and south sides respectively. The entrances are lintelled and vaguely trapezoidal. The internal corridor is visible and in excellent condition, with the usual roofing of slabs laid flat.

8f7e1a42f3276baf.text: Complex nuraghe with a singular plan. Known on the IGM map by the erroneous name "Giaga 'e Puliga" (which is the name of a nearby nuraghe).

8f8d74d0e7dad6c6.text: Domus de janas reported via the Nurnet page by an anonymous source. From the photographs it appears as a two-chambered tomb, used by the landowner as a livestock shelter.

8f8e009bda3ff2c1.text: It consists of four domus de janas.

8fa275bd68008dfc.text: The nuraghe stands in the middle of a wheat field with very poor visibility. The structure of the nuraghe is visible in the middle of the field, but the extent of the village area is not.

8fcec670daeff6e9.text: Domus de Janas on the SS125 junction

8fe8ecdf9272df21.text: An imposing Nuragic site. Various hypotheses and recent analyses suggest the remains of a four-lobed (or five-lobed) complex nuraghe. Currently open to the public; the north tower can be visited. A central opening leads to internal chambers and continues into precarious passages that suggest a complex, articulated structure.

8feecb0754c99fc0.text: It consists of at least 19 tombs, including one that is barely begun.

8ff526154df5fcef.text: The monument, built of trachyte, has a rectangular plan (12 m x 7 m) with an L-shaped corridor inside, and shows a substantial collapse both along the west wall and on the south side.

9014b538e4d75611.text: The chamber is single-celled, with a sub-elliptical plan and an entrance offset to the left of the chamber's median axis. It has a flat floor and a curvilinear vault, almost oven-shaped. It shows two phases of construction: in the original layout the chamber and the rectangular doorway, marked by a groove, were cut; later a small dolmenic corridor was added.

9016bebfa285818c.text: A collective burial of the Nuragic period. The monument, of large dimensions, is barely legible in plan because it is almost entirely buried. Of the orthostatic structure, parts of the outer wall face and the exedra are visible, as well as fragments of the large arched stele lying on the monument.

903f87564829e2ec.text: Prehistoric tomb of the Nuragic period. Unfortunately the tomb has been partly demolished by shepherds to build a livestock pen.

90433b495cfeccb9.text: The central tower is visible for four courses of cyclopean blocks. It is likely that at least four more courses lie underground. To the east and north are the remains of two secondary towers, of which little can be seen. Some wall connections are visible on the surface.

90462dcd1344d596.text:
The Punta Unossi complex is one of the most important in the Florinas area.

It consists of an extensive settlement within which a large circular building stands out (external diameter 11 m, internal diameter 7.60 m) displaying typical features of the so-called "meeting huts": a circular bench against the walls and a central circular base on which a tower baetyl originally stood.

905f903cfdb0c8de.text: It is the prehistoric necropolis that gave its name to the first phase of the Early Bronze Age in Sardinia, the so-called Bonnanaro Culture (1800–1600 BC). It consists of seven hypogea, one of which, Domus I, the most important, lies about 600 metres to the north-west (outside this polygon). Two of the above hypogea are more properly burials in rock shelters.

90675713a5eeb406.text: Village attached to the nuraghe Lu Padru

908c6c64a9785684.text: Probably a complex nuraghe, largely collapsed

90b795e9b0d619c0.text: Two giants' tombs stood in this area, about 100 m apart. The second is the one that survives in a more legible state, although for most of its extent it is covered by vegetation and its walls are blocked by collapse. The tomb whose structure is harder to make out very probably has a rectangular chamber built of large boulders of various sizes, only roughly dressed.

90e7d468da4a7a3e.text: Nuraghe completely ruined and immersed in vegetation, never studied

910cc10955f6a78a.text: The village lies on the slope of Capo Su Moru, north-west of Torre Canai. The area is strewn with trachyte blocks of various sizes and, in stretches where the Mediterranean scrub is less dense, quadrangular and circular wall traces can be glimpsed, signalling the probable presence of a village, if not a temple.

912e0703133e795e.text: A multi-chambered domus de janas with a dromos that has probably collapsed. Inside the main chamber there is a pillar with carved capitals.

9151136b1ec96d72.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. It stands on a rocky spur overlooking the whole western slope of Montiferru down to the sea, and is almost completely hidden by tree vegetation. It is built of polygonal blocks of local basalt and survives to a height of about 2.60 m. The inner chamber has collapsed and the remaining part is filled with its collapse debris.

915bfb3f8ccb410b.text:
Domu de Orgia of Esterzili is the largest Nuragic "megaron" temple known so far.

The building is enclosed within an elliptical perimeter (48.50 x 28 m; wall thickness 1.50 m) reduced to the single foundation course, with an entrance to the west.

This and other information:

915d0c91ee2e0f3c.text: The Middle Bronze Age material (at most fragments of cooking pots and carinated bowls), almost all of the S. Cosimo facies and found on the surface, comes mainly from Monti Crastu, Monti Atziaddei, Monti Ibera, Monti Porceddu and Monti Acutzu; material of the Monti Mannu facies, which needs further specific study to be better understood, is found only in the Serri locality that gives it its name.

9177b7d35323f85e.text: Of the coursed monument in isodomic masonry, the tomb body, the corridor defined by several shaped and well-fitted ashlars, the apse, and part of the exedra survive. A shaped ashlar, but probably damaged, may constitute the so-called dentilled stele.

917bec6392c243bf.text: To be brought to a scholar's attention. They appear in random order, and if they ever had one it is not the present one. It is clear that they were put to a use connected with the herdsman's needs.

9183aaf2d0c28f7b.text: Giants' tomb dating to the Middle Bronze Age (14th century BC). In very poor condition, very close to the eponymous nuraghe better known as Nuraghe Gorroppu.

91861ba699349247.text: Unfortunately the nuraghe is smothered in vegetation. It is thought to have a well-preserved tholos.

91cbfd040ec11032.text: The nuraghe must originally have been quite tall. At present the tholos has collapsed inwards. Note the presence of two giants' tombs not far from the nuraghe.

91dd3e2ff3286bf2.text: On an isolated hillock about 40 metres south-south-west of the nuraghe Su Sonadori the ruins of a complex nuraghe were observed; at present it is hidden by heaps of clearance blocks.

91e8215f49e1c0c3.text: Nuragic sacred spring, a short distance from the Ardasai nuragic complex.

91ebd5489bf92219.text: Excavated inside a limestone boulder turned pink by iron veins. Single-chambered tomb

91ec6d17ae29125c.text: Set on a trachyte plateau at 152 m above sea level, from which a vast territory can be controlled, Monte Baranta consists of a pre-Nuragic settlement characterised and protected by a tower-enclosure, a long and massive wall that encloses a group of rectangular huts, separating them from a sacred area with menhirs and a megalithic circle.

9231b56b5be94a7e.text:
At the foot of the hill, a short distance away, lies a lake basin, an important water source for the nearby village.

The banks show clear signs of human regularisation, with blocks and boulders carefully arranged to frame the so-called “Nuragic pond”.

928bc523cf95f081.text: The structures of the nuraghe, of the simple tholos type, are buried and covered by dense vegetation. Some courses of local basalt blocks emerge partially on the summit of the small rise formed by the structures and the earth covering them.

92963658cd635194.text: Ruined complex nuraghe enveloped in vegetation, difficult to define

92992ea3ffc4f7b3.text: The only evidence of this megalithic burial is the presence of numerous shaped ashlars of various forms incorporated into a dry-stone wall for a length of about 200 metres. All these monoliths are remarkable for being perfectly worked and shaped, indicating that the destroyed tomb was of isodomic type. Among these stones, most of which have lifting recesses, a monolithic arch is of particular interest (arch span 1.72 m – rise 0.80 m – height 0.68 m).

92b7e1311fafbdba.text:
It is a domus de janas in basalt. It consists of an antechamber and an adjoining chamber.

A small niche is cut into the right-hand wall of the antechamber. The floor has a well-made "hearth".

It lies on a low basalt ridge in the shade of some holm oaks. Easily reached a few dozen metres from the road.

92b8f542c02f1e10.text: Single-tower nuraghe. The corridor leading to the circular chamber, which lacks a vault, has a staircase about 1 metre wide on the left. Nearby is another nuraghe called Lobaos II, visible in the photo.

92d13efddfc09cce.text: It is in a state of total abandonment. The structure is built of limestone and schist. Part of the tholos wall face is visible, along with some added structures that suggest a complex monument. Around the structure there is a heavy scatter of material surfacing, almost certainly belonging to a village leaning against the nuraghe.

92da30c0c5539ad0.text: The nuraghe stands on a small hill beside the church of the same name (17th century). It is in fair condition, rising to about 4 metres, with a south-facing entrance that is partly blocked. Inside, two pointed-arch niches can be seen. Single-tower nuraghe built of basalt blocks.

9313192255aa9230.text: Single-tower nuraghe, of which very little is left.

932fc80fe057dbbf.text: Single-tower nuraghe used as a quarry for building walls and "pinnettas". Today only a partial course of boulders is visible.

935b8f161d91e7bd.text:
The Nuraxeddu nuraghe stands on a hillock that is now isolated in the middle of a stretch of land used as pasture for sheep flocks.

The masonry is built of roughly dressed parallelepiped blocks laid in fairly regular courses.

937371254f2b6caf.text: It is a complex nuraghe, partly ruined, standing in the centre (mesu) of a broad valley at the foot of the Alto Oristanese plateau.

937387a72cd20ab9.text: This is a monument that is probably Nuragic, in which the remains of a cistern can be identified, perhaps originally roofed with a tholos, and an adjoining building of elongated rectangular shape, built with rubble-core masonry.

937a7e105a9b6c1f.text:
A complex nuraghe, difficult to read in its ground plan because of the dense vegetation and the conspicuous collapse, made up of large andesite blocks.

Traces of a village of Nuragic huts can be seen, especially to the south-east, and of an open-air Neolithic village in the area between the nuraghe and the Neolithic hypogeal necropolis of Serra Maverru.

937c79d04faa2ddc.text: On the main summit of the rocky outcrop, beneath the remains of a small modern rectangular building, the ruins of a probable nuraghe can be seen, almost unrecognisable.

93842d727701f562.text: Only scant remains of the nuraghe survive.

938b7a79c4dc5f2d.text: Single-tower nuraghe belonging to the complex of nuraghi at Su Padru. Partially destroyed

938d2770ae9116b9.text: The complex consists of two sacred wells, a large hut and other rooms. The various structures are bounded by dry-stone walls built in a herringbone pattern.

939f7f03cfa84d1e.text: The cave contains wall remains and artefacts inside; its use as a smelting site cannot be ruled out.

93a123e18f17d748.text: Structures that are hard to read because of the dense vegetation, probably belonging to an archaic corridor nuraghe. A few blocks of the upper part can just be made out among the vegetation. The plan appears vaguely elliptical, with a straight section facing south, in which a doorway with a monolithic lintel opens onto a flat-roofed corridor about 4 m deep. The nuraghe is built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. A

93eb3a9b9186a786.text:
About twenty metres north-west of the large tomb described in record no. 50 lie the remains of a second megalithic burial that has been largely destroyed by a dry-stone wall cutting across it transversely.

Only a short stretch of the rectangular body can be measured (4.30 m long – 3.20 m wide); the construction technique uses orthostats, while several large overturned slabs inside show that the roof was flat-laid.

940dc700349a00d4.text: This is one of the two hypogea in the Campu Marinu area. A dolmen also existed on the site in the past (presumably destroyed).

941d8f0905efc825.text:
The Barrancu Mannu giants' tomb, also known as "Sa Tuerredda", displays the classic ground plan of giants' tombs: an apsidal tomb body, a covered corridor, and an arched exedra.

The outer wall face consists of large, roughly dressed blocks of yellow-pink granite topped by irregular courses of variously polyhedral stones of large size.

Of the apsidal circuit, originally finished with ordered rows of tailed ashlars, two or three courses survive.

945856e0777d3643.text: The San Pietro nuraghe stands on the summit of a hill on the immediate outskirts of the village of Ussaramanna and takes its name from the church of the same name, which has now disappeared. A complex nuraghe consisting of a central tower and a quadrangular bastion with towers oriented towards the four cardinal points.

946316e3e9105740.text: The archaeological site, dating to about 3500 BC, lies near the provincial road and consists of three tombs. The first, isolated, was cut into a rock outcrop that rises behind a small building; the other two, close together, are instead situated further south in a granite monolith that runs alongside the road. All three domus de janas are of simple type without an antechamber and have a rebate in the entrance doorway.

947db635af230088.text: The nuraghe, datable to the Middle Bronze Age (15th–14th century BC), has a single-tower structure and a truncated-conical shape with a diameter of twelve metres and a surviving height of ten metres. It is built of well-worked limestone-schist blocks laid to form the tholos, which has lost its top courses. The entrance leads into a corridor four metres long, equal to the wall thickness, which opens into the main chamber, circular and over five metres in diameter.

948709a629ff55e6.text: Information from Wikimapia: remains not visible

949463f2cde0ca6c.text: The Perda Lada nuraghe stands on a hill used for grazing and cultivation, very close to the Crastutorro nuraghe. All that remains of the monument are large granite blocks which unfortunately do not help to identify the type of monument or its various features, perhaps also because of the stone-clearing work that has affected the area.

94e2de9e0bb7fccf.text:
It appears as a large heap of rubble covered by dense shrub vegetation that in no way allows the ground plan of the monument to be read.

The surrounding ground is strewn, over a wide area, with the remains of the Nuragic settlement, which was also reused in Roman times, as shown by the potsherds scattered on the ground and several cippi.

The nuraghe was defended by an outer wall that still survives for about sixty metres in length and to a height of about 1/1.50 m.

950adef3a4e753b4.text: The Nuragic village lies at 1200 metres above sea level and is one of the highest in Sardinia. Part of the village is fenced, but the gate is open. The three-lobed nuraghe is surrounded by springs and mountains and set in an unspoilt landscape. Inside the nuraghe a staircase leads to the upper floor and the central tower, whose tholos is intact. The remains of the circular huts that made up the village and the nuraghe are of granite.

952ce4bfe4fbbe2a.text: The basal courses of the single-tower nuraghe can be glimpsed among the shrubs.

952e397bd74fd3ab.text:
This nuraghe lies on the edge of the Teulada military training area.

The geoportal shows that walls still survive around the nuraghe of Monte Idu, built for who knows what reason. The place is magical, both for the presence of the monuments and for the breathtaking scenery it offers the visitor. Its landscape value is exceptional.

The nuraghe appears to be a single-tower nuraghe

953d90fcfaaa5476.text: Hundreds upon hundreds of ruins, huts and towers linked by little lanes, catapult us back thousands of years, showing how imposing and important this site was in the Nuragic period. Two things stand out in particular. The first is a kind of amphitheatre, a majestic horseshoe-shaped building; the other is the spring.

95461be8e9c55172.text: Situated about a hundred metres south of the Borore–Sedilo provincial road, the Pedru Feghe enclosure is roughly circular, with a surviving height of 2.45 m to the north-west and 2.05 m to the south-east, with four and three courses respectively, while the wall thickness varies from 1.45 m to 2.46 m. The masonry consists of medium- and large-sized polyhedral blocks laid in fairly regular horizontal courses.

9554ca352a2eedab.text: Nuraghe no longer visible; a house was built on the site in the early twentieth century, now in ruins, using basalt blocks from the nuraghe.

9555966dbc5b54b6.text: Only a few foundation stones of the aforementioned tomb emerge, with a piece of stele nearby, suggesting that a giants' tomb may have stood there.

9570634998d88661.text: STESSEI, indeed almost against the nuraghe on the east side, the remains of a Nuragic village are clearly visible, covering an area of at least ten thousand square metres and consisting of numerous huts partly hidden among piles of stones. Among the huts there are at least three wells (or cisterns).

957d58e2eba5cc86.text: On the Monte Narcao plateau the remains of several prehistoric huts built of large boulders are still standing. Obsidian flakes are not uncommon all around.

958e9151f93ddc17.text: What remains of the probable nuraghe rests on a granite outcrop, of which some stretches were very likely incorporated into the wall face. At present only half a circuit of roughly dressed, medium- and large-sized granite blocks survives in plan. At the base of the outcrop, at a slightly lower level, two short wall stretches survive, whose function cannot be determined because of the monument's state of preservation.

95932cc7fa2380cf.text: The building consists of a central tower and a four-lobed bastion with an internal courtyard. The outer wall face of the main tower, of which only a single course belonging to the first-floor chamber is visible, is built in isodomic masonry with sandstone blocks. Inside, the opening of the mural staircase can be seen to the south.

95bc847b5b4b3dd1.text: A short antechamber (depth 0.45 – width 0.77) preceding the doorway (height 0.48 – thickness 0.18 – width 0.40). The chamber measures: depth 0.98 – width 1.16/0.90 – height 0.44/0.80.

95e293449ded00c4.text: Few but clear ruins of a giants' tomb. The mound is still partly in situ, as are the two pillars incorporated into a dry-stone wall. The surrounding area is rich in Nuragic remains.

96185f56c6428c27.text: A giants' tomb of which very little remains, almost completely destroyed.

96320b36e2c78eec.text: Two giants' tombs situated near the nuraghe of the same name and the Nuragic village. A dolmen is also attested nearby.

9649095589d69c6c.text:
A burial of the Nuragic period.

Of the monument, practically destroyed, the funerary corridor can be seen, formed by two parallel alignments of ashlars emerging from the ground. Other ashlars are detectable in the immediate vicinity.

The tomb's construction technique was of the isodomic type, carried out with finely shaped ashlars.

966466032dce8576.text: They are on the left bank of the Rio Oloitti. They develop in an L-shape, numbering three chambers with an antechamber. The photograph showing the King's throne "sa trona de su Re" is not far away and arouses curiosity for its shape, which ergonomically suits the substantial backside of a commander.mu

96adc973d72f6645.text: It is a simple nuraghe with the typical truncated-cone shape, probably a single-tower tholos nuraghe. It is built of large granite blocks. About seven courses can be counted at the highest point, but it is clear that others lie below the floor level.

96c902fd7bbc0f4f.text: Nuraghe on the SSW slope of Monte Arbus, on the hillside facing the S'Acqua sa Canna area. Complex nuraghe with a three-lobed bastion and an internal courtyard. The towers of which traces remain are positioned to the N, SSE and SSW. Because of the collapses and the vegetation it is difficult to make out the outline of the walls clearly. By contrast the outline of the courtyard is well defined; at first glance it appears pentagonal; in some stretches up to three rows of boulders of various shapes and sizes survive.

96cb2a9d66a0f562.text: The best-known nuraghe is undoubtedly the one found in the Santa Maria area during excavations beneath the sacristy of the country church; its foundations were discovered in 1843 and some nuragic boulders are incorporated in the low wall enclosing the churchyard.

96e5587ef33337c7.text: Remains of a single-tower nuraghe and village.

971268343aa5b85e.text: The complex, datable between the Late Neolithic (Ozieri culture, 3200–2800 BC) and the Chalcolithic, stands on a broad outcrop of tuff and consists of 26 domus de janas. The domus de janas are arranged on the ridge at different levels and are multi-chambered, i.e. composed of several rooms; most have a dromos entrance (a corridor cut into the rock) while only a few have direct access.

971c203326a000b7.text: The Nuraghe Murartu or Sa Menta lies in the territory of Silanus, about 2.2 km from the village. It is almost completely hidden by vegetation. Of complex type, part of the central tower emerges for a height of 2 metres.

9728cc5bed969357.text: The Nuraghe Cae is a complex nuraghe, with a central tower and at least two towers joined by a bastion; the presence of another two towers on the south-east side is probable, and a semi-underground gallery is also mentioned. A small village and signs of the area's reuse in Roman times are also present.

973427de639f24b2.text:
It is a single-tower nuraghe with a staircase, a corridor niche, and a chamber flanked by two opposing niches.

The tower cannot be fully defined in its outer perimeter because of collapses and dense shrub vegetation, but a circular ground plan about 10 metres in diameter at the base is to be assumed. The surviving height is 6.50 m on the south-east side and 4.80 m on the north-west side. The masonry consists of medium and large basalt blocks laid in horizontal courses that are not always regular.

9776820ce0919735.text: Structures belonging to a giants' tomb built of local basalt. The funerary structure stands on a small rise overlooking a small river valley, between the nuraghi Campu Scudu and Piricu (Santu Lussurgiu). Some blocks of the funerary corridor and part of the outer wall face remain visible. The tomb is oriented east–west and survives for a total length of about 8 m. In the front part a few displaced blocks can be seen that originally must have formed part of the exedra.

97d6c1ae4babbb06.text: It lies near the country church of San Pietro, about one kilometre from the village. Its name, S'Acqua 'e is dolus, means "the water of sorrows", from an old folk belief that the water in this small cave has miraculous powers; a legend also tells that during one of his journeys San Pietro took shelter in this artificial grotto and prayed there for so long that the imprint of his knees was left forever in the rock.

97ddf9d39b4f4ae5.text: Nuraghe built by fitting masonry and tholos among emerging rock masses.

97fb05255399cd25.text: A complex tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The structures are overgrown with vegetation, but a central tower and an added tower with a courtyard can be made out, of the so-called tancato type. The added tower appears to be smaller than the central tower. From the top of the latter the interior of the chamber can be seen, still well preserved except for the collapsed upper part.

9807c62f2b2f7f00.text: Six hypogea of the domus de janas type. The immediate proximity of a tuff quarry, on the edges of which a few traces of other hypogea can be seen, suggests that the site originally extended further than it does today. Of the six domus present, one is almost completely destroyed, three were converted into farm buildings in historical times after substantial alterations to their plans, and only the last two (Tombs V and VI) have preserved their original structure.

984110b7f75960f3.text: In total ruin, only a few large roughly squared boulders remain. The oldest villagers remember its existence, even if only a few basal circles were left. When the Sassari–Tempio dual carriageway was built, the earthworks for it affected more than one site, in total disregard for the enormous historical value they represented, to be used as sub-base for the road network.

984d0b545b996e5d.text: Complex nuraghe with its tholos intact. Part of the outer wall face has collapsed.

9857cbf3930176e1.text: The area where old maps marked the location of the nuraghe Evrassu, in the territory of the municipality of Pozzomaggiore (SS). What remains of the nuraghe Frassu (territory of Pozzomaggiore).

98728b59823cac15.text: From the aerial photograph it looks like one of those nuraghi belonging to the "unfinished" category.

98971556fcd91c65.text: From the second giants' tomb, moving 50 m westwards, one finds an area where the presence of polyhedral boulders of various sizes, only roughly dressed, suggests a zone set aside for worship.

98a0a109dcffcf2d.text: A collective burial of the Nuragic period of dolmenic type. Of the tomb, now completely destroyed, the exedra and the apse are partially legible, while some fragments of the arched stele are present both on the facade and in the surroundings.

98a5d6480ff422b3.text: The nuraghe stands on the summit of a hill, from which the view extends over the whole surrounding territory and especially over the valleys below and the course of the Rio Mannu. It lies inside a cultivated olive grove.

9944ae4e3107961b.text: It is a simple nuraghe, judging from the few remains highlighted by the stones scattered here and there inside and outside a centuries-old thicket of mastic. The boulders are of medium size and some appear vaguely dressed. Few are the surviving courses, which do not yield sufficient results for a survey.

9947264f248248f9.text:
The necropolis of Sos Laccheddos is an archaeological site in the territory of Sassari, in north-western Sardinia. It is divided into two groups of tombs lying a short distance from each other, located between state road 127 bis and the new provincial road to Anglona a few kilometres east of the town, in the direction of Osilo.

To the 32 tombs recorded in the aforementioned work, another 19 were added following more recent investigations.

995a951a0cd8dff0.text: Single-tower nuraghe in excellent condition. Corbelled entrance corridor with a left-hand intramural staircase.

995afcf67463d1ff.text: A multi-lobed nuraghe largely covered by vegetation. The central tower can still be visited from above. It proves to be a much larger complex than it appears at first sight.

9960cc61577055d6.text: A ruined complex nuraghe enveloped in vegetation. Its outlines are hard to make out. It may be a four-lobed one.

996a77d73e3e2a70.text: The nuraghe Su Mamuccone is now completely ruined; it stands on a limestone monolith near the sheepfold of the same name, in an ideal position for overlooking the whole area.

9973278cbb9d9f92.text: Nuragic village of Su Putzu, composed of about a hundred huts surrounding a well temple, precisely Su Putzu. The temple has a long ramped vestibule; the staircase leading to the spring vein is missing.

99c1e22e591c37bb.text: Nuraghe reported on Wikimapia but flagged for deletion. To be verified.

99d6d4e14f3f5c60.text: Nuraghe and a structure of uncertain type

99dc44e5b0a78132.text:
The monument, located on the immediate northern outskirts of Birori, has a circular plan (diam. 12 x 12.30 m) with an average surviving height of only 2.75 m and two courses; the blocks, polygonal and roughly dressed, are laid in horizontal courses.

Because of its very poor state of preservation it is not possible to identify the internal structure of the monument.

99e792ae088a8d86.text: The I.G.M. marks it as a nuraghe, but there are strong and well-founded doubts about classifying it as such. It stands on the boundary between the territories of Chiaramonti and Ardara, in the area called Pittiri, at an altitude of 440 metres above sea level, and on the boundary with the areas of Truncu Nieddu and Serra di Monte Pittu. The construction is atypical and hard to classify: it is not a nuraghe but difficult to class as a hut.

9a2aa32bfa878587.text: A place of rare beauty. The complex, of particular charm, comprises a complex nuraghe with an attached village, a cave with two entrances, two giants' tombs and two single-tower nuraghi.

9a377e93d37c99d1.text: Now almost nothing is left but large stones that have been moved and used in the nearby dry-stone walls.

9a5f2be3240ab10f.text: Nuraghe of unidentifiable structure. Unfortunately only a few traces of the nuraghe remain because it was completely demolished to make way for a RAI antenna. At the foot of the antenna various boulders lie heaped haphazardly. At the edge of a hollow, next to what must have been the base of the nuraghe, are the remains of a probable hut.

9a6830d5b17e778e.text: Nuraghe with an extensive collapse on the east side, making the ground plan hard to read. Adjacent huts belonging to a probable village.

9a88f3364762788d.text:
The monument lies less than 900 metres south of the Nuraghe Suerzu.

It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular, slightly flattened plan, with a surviving height of 2.15 m over four or five courses of medium and large stones, only roughly dressed and laid in irregular courses.

Because of its very poor state of preservation, the collapse and the shrub vegetation, it is not possible to determine the position of the entrance.

9a951394f9210566.text: A complex nuraghe, but heavily ruined and never studied. It is completely overgrown with vegetation and not easy to interpret. It shows a probable internal staircase and remains of external masonry belonging to secondary rooms.

9aa1569e53343429.text: Nuraghe in very poor condition and entirely covered by scrub.

9ab0bbbdf395f200.text:
