A single-tower tholos nuraghe. The building stands on the summit of a bend in the Rio Cispiri and rests on a solid rocky base partly incorporated into the structures, as can be seen on the north-facing side.

The nuraghe is well preserved on the north and north-east sides, with an external wall face of large polygonal basalt blocks reaching a maximum surviving height of about 12 m, while the south and west sides have collapsed.

9abc03a3ee40f8c4.text: (16th–13th century BC), it is built of trachyte. It has a corridor with a spiral staircase on the left and a guard niche on the right, and a vaulted chamber, perfectly preserved, with three niches arranged in a cross. The entrance jambs of the nuraghe are 1.52 m and 1.24 m high respectively. The tower reaches a maximum height of 8 m and consists of seventeen courses of stone. The entrance faces east; its perfectly worked lintel is 1.60 m long, 0.70 m high and 0.80 m wide.

9acb5d49ca0a45b3.text: The monument is a single-tower, single-chamber nuraghe. Its entrance and the whole of its base are badly damaged, although clear traces of a staircase and a guard niche remain. The north-western wall face is the best preserved, standing about six metres high with eight courses of roughly dressed blocks. Along the corridor, itself practically destroyed, the traces of two facing niches can be seen.

9ae30688b5fe4be4.text: The nuraghe stands on the summit of a modest isolated rise. The area is covered by almost impenetrable vegetation. Some alignments of granite blocks of the monument are visible.

9ae454109cd71a92.text: A semi-destroyed nuraghe of which only a single underground chamber built of masonry can be observed.

9ae83b043a68868e.text: It is slightly elliptical, with a diameter varying from 20 to 30 m. Some stones no longer stand in line along the perimeter but lie fallen inside or outside the circle; however, most of them are still well aligned with each other and some are still perfectly upright. It is astonishing that, despite thousands of years having passed, the state of preservation is still relatively good.

9b25e4f96699414c.text: These are the remains of a sanctuary built in megalithic technique, set in the centre of the saddle about 100 metres from the other site to the east; at present the dense vegetation allows only four or five menhirs lying on the ground a few metres apart to be visited. I remember from a visit I made to this site many years ago that the menhirs were far more numerous, but now the thick vegetation makes it impossible to tell whether any others survive.

9b33042eb3f6000c.text: Fortification or nuraghe also called Staderis or Giolza. It lies in the Montiferru, near the summit of a high spur of bare, rugged rock facing Monte Urtigu, where the remains of an imposing megalithic wall survive with seven courses of roughly dressed basalt boulders. The straight line of the ruin suggests an original quadrangular defensive structure around the level top of the rock, rather than the wall face of a hilltop nuraghe.

9b505a166440da3a.text: Inside there is a pillar on which a bull's-head protome is carved in high relief.

9b506c319214dcf3.text: Only traces of the structure remain, as it has completely collapsed.

9b5e1cd47b9576f4.text: Ruined nuraghe. The central tower is clearly visible for 10 courses. A possible trace of an outer wall preceding the north tholos is present. The south-east turret has completely collapsed. The nuraghe appears to have imploded on itself in non-recent times. A short distance away a structure can be identified that suggests it may be a dolmen.

9b625cc5768c4579.text: In Serrenti Nuragic villages are often found near a nuraghe, as at the Bruncu Pubusa site; in others (Giuanni Acca, Sattu Divisu, Bruncu Abis and Sa Serra) they are not.

9b6d926e25cfdebb.text: This complex nuraghe consisted of a tall central tower and three towers joined by a bastion, now not very well preserved. The tall central tower, on the other hand, is in perfect condition, with a surviving height of 14 m, not much less than its original height. It rises on two storeys, both intact and each roofed with a tholos.

9b793c1c6d2cc40a.text: It is a corridor proto-nuraghe built of basalt.

9bb23c1d423d4667.text: The church was built on the remains of a nuraghe called Nuraxi Mannu, and Nuragic remains are found throughout the village. The decision to build the church stemmed from a desire to give sacred continuity to a particular place. The church is a small building with a rectangular plan and a single nave. In the white façade, a round-arched doorway with a frame opens, surmounted by a small circular oculus.

9bd3c30675e59d05.text: Nuraghe by the road. Partly collapsed. The tholos is open and its constructional details are substantially visible in section.

9c0791fab6b72aa3.text:
150 m from the second group of domus de janas, at the foot of Monte Corru Tundu, stands a colossal monolith of trachyte tuff with a truncated top (surviving height 5.75 m). The menhir, one of the largest in Sardinia, is strongly tapered, with one face flattened and the other rounded; on the latter three circular cup-marks appear to be visible.

The monolith and the necropolis served the settlement of Monte Padrillonis. (San Michele culture, 3200–2800 BC).

9c14bc9ade3fb27b.text: The Nuraghe Norampè has literally almost entirely disappeared; only a few boulders incorporated into the bedrock remain to testify to its excellent and commanding position.

9c2ba2e623a1bbb4.text: Between Tratalias and S. Giovanni Suergiu near Is Loccis. In very poor condition.

9c2fab168b6f39f7.text: The remains of the nuraghe lie inside the Orguglioso castle.

9c31f6f263cb272e.text: The nuraghe stands on the hill of Cala Francese, in the locality “Serra is tres portus”. It may originally have been a complex nuraghe built of limestone boulders. The outline of the original tower survives discontinuously; its interior is covered by collapse and vegetation.

9c5539f745cb7e73.text: Single-tower nuraghe built of large blocks, situated on top of the hill. On the hill slopes there are tall wall structures of the same period. The site was used from the Bronze Age to the Roman period.

9c5dd88b9ad951aa.text: Built on a slight basalt outcrop less than 200 metres south of the Riu Corte, the monument is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, now largely demolished around its outer perimeter. Because of the collapse, the construction details of the corridor and the chamber cannot be made out.

9c83328b5ed8a4da.text: The monument was built in two phases. In the first, dating to the Bonnanaro culture period, the allée couverte tomb – a kind of elongated dolmen – was constructed; later, around 1600 BC, it was turned into a giants' tomb with exedra and stele, traces of which you can still see.

9c91609f5e0be651.text: A well built of boulders of various sizes; its outer structure has been completely demolished, probably belonging to a sacred well temple fed by a spring.

9ca85495547a9b07.text: Set in a striking wood of monumental wild olives, the nuraghe has a complex, four-lobed plan, with a corridor, an access ramp in the upper part, and a trapdoor leading to an underground chamber. The only accessible lateral tower is the one to the north, and it is visible from the upper part of the central tower.

9cabd3f3436a4bba.text:
This domus de janas came to light in the flood of 18-11-2013.

Covered by vegetation until then, it was certainly known to the local shepherds. A road runs above it.

9cd8f95aed53c105.text:
The giants' tomb is covered by dense scrub, and only one covering slab leaning to the north can be seen outside.

Rock shelter opening in a huge granite boulder, a spacious cavity with a wide main entrance flanked by two orthostatic slabs and already partly closed. The main interest lies in the geometric figures on the exposed rock that forms the shelter floor, and schematic anthropomorphic figures on the back wall.

9ce54b7a9816c9ad.text: A collective burial of the Nuragic period. The monument, like the other tombs in the area, is in very poor condition. The corridor formed by two parallel courses of stones is still legible, and the outer profile can be recognised in some stretches. Some regular ashlars incorporated in the surrounding dry-stone walls may belong to the tomb.

9d092b238d67b5e1.text: A burial of the Nuragic period. Of the monument, half-hidden by vegetation and collapse debris, the outer perimeter, the funerary corridor and part of the exedra are visible.

9d0ec0666288c646.text: Complex nuraghe belonging to the nuraghi of the Cuga valley. The associated village and the outer structure are heavily altered. It allows access inside as far as the tholos, which is still perfectly intact.

9d2b34a98e9be4ab.text: More precisely it is a proto-nuraghe, and it has a circular plan.

9d4607b08ddb23c6.text: Probable location. In a grazing area, hidden by a large thicket of mastic, in poor condition, some blocks are visible. Adjacent to the sewage treatment plant, it may have suffered damage during the recent installation works.

9d4e70031a153abb.text: A wild gorge, cut by a stream in porphyritic granite, leads to the Nuragic village of Praidas. The structures are in a state of severe decay and have slipped significantly.

9d61a90994db4b00.text: "Monte sa Perda", it is thought there was another nuraghe that dominated the whole gulf of Palmas, probably destroyed for the construction of "su forr'e sa cracina" (lime kiln) situated in the immediate vicinity.

9d7d519b7b353b6d.text: Its position relative to the terrain's orography is really strange! Or rather, it is clear as day, since the fortified wall facing it on the slopes of Monte Zennaru declares its function of control and surveillance.

9d96625f0ea60afb.text: The first photos show the section of the tholos, unfortunately half-collapsed. The splendid niche is also visible. It is easily reached even though it is on private land. It lies a few hundred metres from the Romanesque Cathedral of Sant'Antioco di Bisarcio.

9d9ba7bdf8b76bfd.text: A small circular structure, built in Nuragic technique and classifiable as an atypical nuraghe.

9dc6a44e930ff657.text:
The monument appears as an artificial hill at the base of which the material produced by clearing the surrounding fields has been piled up.

Its very ruined state, the fact that it is buried, and the rubble that partly covers it do not allow a correct reading of the building's ground plan; nevertheless, it must have been grand and of complex type, as the very name Tresnuraghes attributed to it also suggests.

9dcbf1992a366b49.text: It is a fine example of a single-tower nuraghe with a collapsed but easily accessible tholos chamber. The nuraghe displays a variety of constructional and architectural features. Facing north is an entrance that was clumsily walled up in recent times; it lies about 2.00 metres above the present ground level.

9dd4319bac171a78.text: Complex of 5 domus de janas in the Rio Mannu Canyon. Excavated in Miocene limestone. Some have suffered collapses.

9ddb3e32fd24a92b.text: Single-tower nuraghe in good condition near a small farm

9dedb873ade9ab03.text: Hypogeum of the Monte Claro culture. The site was also frequented in the Nuragic, Roman and medieval periods.

9def887a26b97392.text: Originally built of medium-sized basalt blocks, it uses the bedrock as a foundation. At present it is almost illegible because of the conspicuous collapse, held in place by vegetation consisting of wild olives and prickly pears.

9dfce14b398f1197.text: Nuraghe Alvu di Nulvi: "alvu" = white. A four-lobed nuraghe, very beautiful, although in a fairly degraded state of preservation. Human and institutional neglect, together with the harshness of the elements, contribute to its deterioration. Let us remember that present-day municipal boundaries make no sense when referred to the Nuragic period, and future generations will have one piece fewer with which to reconstruct the historical and cultural period of our forebears.

9e1efba9f53094b7.text: Single-tower nuraghe with an elliptical plan; the nuraghe's plan is difficult to read.

9e2b9d2e742e296c.text:
A nuraghe bearing an inscription carved on an ashlar that marks the boundary between the territory of the Ilienses and the Balari.

The inscription reads "ILI IVR IN NVRAC SESSAR M C", i.e. the rights of the Ilienses of Nurac Sessar. Its importance also lies in being one of the earliest attestations of the name given to Sardinian towers.

9e3f337d5dd372f8.text: Near the nuraghe a Nuragic spring is visible. It lies on the Pedruitta plateau. It is immediately clear that this is a very archaic spring of the Nuragic world.

9e3f5320dd1e3661.text: A rectangular niche cut into the sedimentary rock, set against a quadrangular space bounded by four large upright stones with dry-stone walls. In the lowest Bell Beaker levels three cist structures were identified, sealed by limestone slabs and containing human skeletal remains attributable to several individuals. Above these lay further deceased individuals accompanied by grave goods such as objects in ceramic, metal, stone, bone and a gold necklace.

9e4ac7177d26a911.text: A small single-tower nuraghe; around it is a small domus de janas necropolis, in which there are decorations of carved bull's-head protomes.

9e784daf54e7ae26.text: It stands on a basalt spur accessible from only one side, west of the village of Sagama. It has a polygonal plan with a straight, slightly convex façade to the north-west where the entrance opens. In the centre of the main wall the main entrance opens with a rectangular opening and lintel. On entering there is a straight corridor; in the right-hand side of the first stretch two niches open side by side.

9e7cd1e25b672454.text: Reduced to total ruin, only the base circle can be traced, where an opening to the north is visible. There are not enough surviving structures for an exact classification into a precise type; it is thought to be a corridor nuraghe. An interesting area because of the presence of large stones set on edge, which gives the impression of standing before a giants' tomb.

9ebba98be615d7ec.text: It lies in the municipality of Guasila, inside a private plot planted with Mediterranean scrub.

9ec3f7b3bc0c5966.text: Two blocks of the exedra and the right-hand inner wall face of the chamber are visible. Illegally excavated and damaged.

9ecc85edb37ec0f9.text: The “rotunda” of Sa Corona Arrubia in the territory of Genoni, also known locally as “Santa Maria S'Ungroi”, is a unique sacred building of the Nuragic period at Sa Corona Arrubia-Genoni. Of the monument, mentioned by Taramelli who considered it a Nuragic sacred well, the entire base ring survives, consisting of an isodomic basalt wall face with two and in a few places three courses preserved, with a small niche and a few blocks belonging to a bench.

9ecedd7c3aeea508.text: See Giuseppa Tanda's book “L'arte delle domus de janas”, page 97.

9ef4c48e64361d27.text: The tomb has its top missing; it has a rectangular plan and no longer shows any trace of the apse. Its length is about 12 m. At present some blocks of the left arm of the exedra, the entrance, and the perimeter wall can be observed.

9f0729673a25d122.text: Around the building extends a large village of circular huts, while a short distance away there are two giants' tombs. There is also record of a well that existed in ancient times, of which no trace remains today.

9f0c5b089b59bfab.text: The "Domus de janas" are hypogean (underground) burials of the pre-Nuragic period, datable to 3500–3000 BC, consisting of one or more chambers and used up to the Nuragic age. On Monte Arista, in the municipality of Cardedu, there is a necropolis composed of ten carefully made tombs in an excellent state of preservation. The tombs are cut into isolated blocks of granite. The hypogea are of two types, single-chambered and double-chambered, and have a longitudinal layout.

9f146dd60d8e8856.text:
It is hard to interpret because it is not clear whether it consisted of a single tower, which in that case would have been of a large diameter, or of several towers on different levels.

All that can be seen are high walls of massive construction, built of roughly squared blocks and spread over a wide area.

It also appears that the wall faces of the monument enclose a space already bounded by rock outcrops that are incorporated into it in several places.

9f1d5729c9463f00.text:
It lies within the municipal territory of Quartu Sant'Elena (CA).

Of a most unusual shape, the nuraghe is now almost completely destroyed.

9f1de417e1c03ec6.text: Situated in the Bèrchida valley, it shows use and occupation from the Nuragic period, with a substantial surface scatter of pottery fragments of Middle-Late Imperial date. It was inhabited until the 1950s. Among the dwelling remains, the ruins of a small religious building are of particular interest; it is already attested in 14th-century documentation.

9f2c4361ac2bfdd4.text: A proto-nuraghe later remodelled into a nuraghe. On the highest hills of Serrenti, overlooking the valleys that lead to the Trexenta, stand the simple proto-nuraghi of Monti de su Marchesu, Monti Acutzu, Monti Ibera and Monti Proceddu.

9f425edca8a431f4.text: Complex nuraghe; because of its state of decay and the considerable burial of the structures it cannot be confidently assigned to any defined type.

9f7f605d50b16afc.text:
It is of tufaceous trachyte (L 5, W 2.50, H 2.70 m), consisting of a rectangular chamber (4.18 x 1.14 m) bounded on the sides by two orthostats, by a front slab with an entrance hatch with rounded corners facing south-east, and by a flat covering slab.

Inside the western lateral orthostat a rectangular niche opens (L 1.22, W 0.88, D 0.50 m). To the left of the monument's front slab there is a small niche, cut into the thickness of the western orthostat.

9fa1161b074af6b6.text: A collective burial of the Nuragic period. The structure is hard to see because, besides being swallowed by the usual thicket of mastic, it is also covered with small stones from the clearance of the surrounding ground.

9fbf26d21d1083c2.text: It appears to belong to the category of "unfinished" nuraghi, but the dense vegetation does not allow a proper definition.

9fc5a0b4cae6015f.text: The site is partly ruined. The entrance corridor and part of the staircase remain. The nuraghe is thought to have been in use from 1550 to 900 BC.

9fc7922b96a500ea.text: The nuraghe Paiulu (IGM) or Paiolu stands perched on a basalt bastion at Costa Pisu, on the west flank of Monte Arci, on the boundary between the municipal territories of Oristano, Palmas Arborea (Tiria) and Villaurbana.

9fc9469ad2883f6c.text: Single-tower nuraghe; the few remains are covered by thick vegetation.

9fe70c616d486780.text: Probable nuragic tower of which only the entrance lintel survives, besides the collapse heap.

9fff7918ad9d973c.text: June 2021, report. The foundation has collapsed and they have strapped the stones to the fig tree with iron rods; if you zoom in you can see them.

a01d5a61f973e98a.text: The sources available to us report that the proto-nuraghe was studied by the archaeologist Ercole Contu, before the construction of the Cuga dam, around the 1950s/60s; unfortunately the same texts tell us that the body of the nuraghe was dismantled for study precisely because it had unusual forms. Subsequently, with the approval of the Ministry, it was used as a foundation for the Cuga dam. The tower was 6 metres high.

a0203407efef8981.text: Single-tower nuraghe, with traces of a settlement around it. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

a02fdd30f0459c89.text:
It stands on a ridge from which it is possible to control the valley where the Nurritani people were settled, bounded by the Roman boundary stone found in that area by Prof. Mastino.

The region lying south of the Tirso extended between Orotelli and the sources of the Tirso east of Benetutti, and bordered the Goceano to the north and the Barbaria to the south.

a03dd77413b10cdb.text: The site includes an undefined structure (WHAT COULD IT BE?) at the edge of a sheer drop; on the front it once had (now disappeared) a hollowed-out boulder like a holy-water stoup, a tiny domus de janas, the giants' tomb of Pascaredda; a dolmen, the Monti Di Deu nuraghe, the Agnu nuraghe, and the Nuragic spring of Li Paladini. The Pascaredda tomb and the Agnu nuraghe are easily reached; everything else has been left to itself and is hard to locate and reach.

a0548905676bbea4.text: Nearby and closely associated with the Miuddu nuraghe, no more than a hundred metres to the south-east, stands a giants' tomb displaying the usual architectural layout of this tomb type: a semicircular exedra (chord 10.05 m – sagitta 2.25 m), a slightly apsidal rectangular body (length 9.75 m – width 2.50 m) and a rectangular burial chamber (length 4.60 m x 0.80 m wide x 0.75 m high above the fill).

a055d01b83acae13.text: It takes its name from the place-name of the land. Like most of the nuraghi and other features at Chiaramonti, it too is in a state of degradation that is irretrievably compromised. Certain particularities emerge that lead me to consider it as belonging to the nuraghi with a basement level.

a05787575fb7ec0e.text: A beautiful domus de janas necropolis consisting of eight domus, four of which are grouped together (5-6-7-8); Domus IV lies near the group of four tombs, Domus III about 200 metres to the south, and Domus I and II close together about 100 metres east of the third.

a06d0de84771c63b.text: Single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan (diam. 12.80 x 12 m) and a maximum surviving height of 2.55 m.

a0907cbaa62bc212.text: The Bia nuraghe now appears as a ruin. It is not a single-tower nuraghe (although the most visible tower is very probably the central tower), since other walling can be made out to the south.

a09ce11fd8a88c30.text: The few remains of the nuraghe have ended up, following land reclamation and improvement works, beneath a blanket of brambles and other shrubs, and behind a curtain of barbed wire. Nevertheless, traces of the monument are evident through the large stones of the basal circle.

a0aab8069f58e5a0.text: A few surviving courses of the Crastu nuraghe, inside the hamlet of the same name

a0ca319a0baab44c.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The monument preserves three to four courses of blocks of the outer wall face, reaching a maximum surviving height of about 2.60 m. At present it is not possible to identify the entrance, partly because brambles and mastic partially cover the remains of the nuraghe. The inner chamber has collapsed and the material that formed it completely fills the remaining parts of the monument.

a0dd61818557c0d5.text:
A monument of exceptional value belonging to the final Nuragic period, when towers were no longer built and various "federal sanctuaries" were created, which frequently included sacred wells built of isodomic ashlars and enriched with architectural sculptural elements.

Unfortunately the sacred well is not looked after and is not kept constantly clean.

a0f0f4b7d02c7863.text: Single-tower nuraghe. On the IGM map this nuraghe is confused with the nearby Nuraghe Molas. Around the nuraghe there are traces of a village or settlement.

a137fbf519536e09.text: The De Planu or Don Micheli nuraghe has a diameter of 12.50 m and a wall thickness of four metres. The circular chamber, 3.80 m in diameter, is reached through a corridor 4.50 m long, blocked for two metres. At a depth of two metres fragments of vessels with handles of different shapes and a mould hollowed out in the centre came to light; at a depth of one metre fragments of tableware, human bones and a cremation burial were found.

a15ac0e12e9a2ed9.text: The proto-nuraghe Bardalatzu stands on the western end of a basalt plateau, in a rugged and hard-to-reach area, overlooking a narrow, deep valley where the Riu Murtazzolu and the Riu Cuguttu meet. The monument is of considerable size, with an irregular ground plan that adapts to the triangular profile of the hill on which it was built.

a15e673b881e195e.text:
Complex nuraghe.

Although marked as Nuraghe Brundette, it is actually known (even by the village elders) as Nuraghe Chentucheddas, and stands on the edge of the rock of the same name.

a186769eb41f771a.text: Of complex plan, it is built of basalt in a structure of well-squared blocks laid in regular horizontal courses so that the joints of the upper blocks fall at the mid-point of the lower ones. The stronghold probably consists of three towers enclosing a small courtyard with an entrance to the south-west.

a1962477e723448d.text: The complex consists of a nuraghe and a village of about 90–100 huts spread over 5 hectares. Because of its great extent and the number of buildings, the site is considered unique in the Gallurese Nuragic context.

a1a633c8cf9f4a4c.text: Single-tower nuraghe that re-emerges from the lake only during periods of drought

a1d7960fa75a7248.text: The nuraghe that once stood near the church forecourt has been demolished and no trace of its former presence remains. Some shaped blocks are incorporated into the church dedicated to Santa Petronilla. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

a1f5e21914697d41.text: Probable nuraghe (Ugas 2022), situated beneath the remains of an eighteenth-century fort later used as an anti-aircraft position. Some archaeologists believe it was a four-lobed nuragic palace; others consider this unlikely. Further studies are awaited.

a200db2ae7441a62.text: It stands on the top of a hill, right on a watershed. From this favourable and strategic position the nuraghe commands the whole plain below.

a2021f270b30daeb.text: A four-lobed nuraghe whose excavations yielded many intact finds. The nuraghe's period of occupation appears to have been very short.

a235b92de614ffdc.text: A multi-lobed nuraghe in which a bronze figurine and the mast of a bronze model boat, shaped like a four-towered nuragic fortress, were found.

a238e0b37b7948e8.text:
Nothing of this monument remains, as it was buried over time and subsequently covered by houses and streets.

Some sewer excavations and the accounts of the inhabitants indicate the presence of a complex nuraghe and the village. We are also 300 m from the site of the warriors' tomb of Sant'Iroxi, known for the two hundred skulls and the swords.

a258913f11c4f353.text:
The Written Boulder, carved.

Giants' tomb at Santu Micheli whose stele is framed, precisely, by a low-relief border.

a2713c40ca6b9ee2.text:
Nuraghe, probably complex, with a village.

Later occupation after the Nuragic age is also evident in the area, shown by the scatter of historic-period pottery fragments on the ground.

The complex, which is difficult to reach, is currently covered by dense vegetation that hides the hut structures, making a correct reading of the plan and its layout difficult.

a28e51b6e1b27115.text: Wikipedia lists this nuraghe as one of the last to be built, with ever less pronounced slopes on the outer wall face. The tholos survives almost intact, except for a few courses.

a2ab2cd36492bf70.text: Situated in the locality of the same name, in the countryside around the village, a Nuragic sacred well of which only a few remains are visible today. The monument is of isodomic type and therefore of very refined workmanship. Numerous blocks of the sacred building can be recognised scattered near a recently built well that has effectively replaced the ancient one.

a2af53bb761abfd0.text: Complex nuraghe of Mont'Elva with an adjoining village. It is reduced to a ruin because of the work on the water mains of the Alta Nurra aqueduct carried out from the 1950s onwards. Still recognisable are: the central tower, partly buried, with a surviving height of about 2 m; a secondary tower, to the south-west of the main one, reduced to just two courses hidden by dense Mediterranean scrub.

a2c74cb5dced0fee.text: Structures belonging to a mixed-type complex nuraghe, consisting of an archaic corridor nuraghe linked to a single-tower tholos nuraghe. The complex as a whole is very imposing, formed by a large building with an elliptical – sub-quadrangular plan with rounded corners, about 22 m long and a little over 17 m wide, oriented N–S.

a2d779d329297f14.text: The Nuraghe of Busurtei stands on top of the hill of the same name, from which there is a breathtaking view. Near the nuraghe, in the medieval period, stood the small village called Busurtei, Busateri or Buzarcheri, which belonged to the diocese of Santa Giusta in 1224. About a hundred metres north of the nuraghe there is a spring whose water is said to be the best of all the springs in the territory of Sedilo.

a2d97e0949b1db55.text: Complex nuraghe with frontal addition and lateral development: the added structures are arranged not only in front of the main tower but also to its sides. There are two minor towers, linked to the main one by curtain walls; the courtyard lies between them as a connecting space.

a325ecd50ff446dd.text: Multi-chambered domus de janas containing carved decorations representing a bull's-head protome. In the centre there is a pillar created by cutting away the rock.

a333a7b48d4e9021.text: Nuraghe Busoro lies in the municipality of Sedilo, about 1.5 km north of the village. It is a single-tower nuraghe, built of basalt; the internal tholos lacks its uppermost courses.

a3622f4944227ffe.text: There is a considerable quantity of potsherds in the area. Visible amid the dense vegetation, one hut is still intact; a first tower and a second, perhaps the remains of a multi-lobed structure; a magnificent well or cistern with a basalt ring at the mouth.

a367867eb4cf1ba0.text: The Bau su Matutzu Tomb (3rd millennium BC) lies inside an olive grove within the Ecoserdiana landfill site.

a3696c5f3c602360.text:
The nuraghe S'Ulivera is of mixed type; it has corridors, and above them rises a tholos chamber with niches that has partly collapsed.

Around the nuraghe some remains survive of what was once a village. A few metres away, several well-worked basalt boulders are visible, which almost certainly belonged to a building of cultural significance.

a3772359fd80eea1.text: approximate area of the Nuragic village of Codula Manna

a394e028a98298b0.text: Two Nuragic huts are in a good state of preservation; the rest of the village is a ruin. On the south-west edge lies the pond (Paule – from which the site takes its name), which probably served as a water reservoir.

a3adaf466c6d2ba6.text: Complex nuraghe, completely ruined and buried

a3d0c272f5bdf880.text: It appears to be a nuraghe whose construction was never completed.

a3dccc79a7d06fc1.text: It is a bilobed complex nuraghe in granite with traces of a wall enclosing the monument. It sits among the rocks at an elevation of 245 m on top of a hill.

a3e6506240c44d26.text: On the flank of Monte Cumida. It consists of eight domus de janas, variously articulated and characterised by decorative motifs on the walls. In Tomb VI, which has seven chambers, a false door of trapezoidal shape is carved into the back wall of one of the cells. In Tomb VIII, the main cell has a double-pitched ceiling and, on the front wall above the hatch giving access to one of the secondary chambers, double horns are carved in low relief, now barely legible.

a3ec0c6ce86b892e.text: Here too the situation is critical because the remains of the nuraghe are a shapeless heap of stones, yet they still reveal some of the monument's constructional features. As is typical of most Chiaramonti nuraghi, the entrance — with both jambs and the lintel still visible — faces east-south-east.

a41013587fac6505.text: Around it one can see the remains of the ancient village and the granitic rocks in their varied shapes. Near the building, of which only a few courses and the lintel facing Monte Novo remain, the traces of the granite quarries are very evident. Within an area of 1 km there are nine domus de janas; some lie near the Nuraghe, the others, on the same granitic outcrop, lie near the Sau family farmhouse.

a416d6f46532c891.text:
It is a proto-nuraghe; the tower survives to a maximum height of 5.50 m.

Within a radius of 400 m there are three giants' tombs, a Nuragic spring and five baetyls.

a42b5c6c31af1f74.text: Beside the provincial road the low course of a probable giants' tomb survives, its typical structure clearly visible.

a42c02195677bf69.text: It is a mere ruin. Some basal-ring boulders, though barely discernible, are set into the natural bedrock to form a single whole with the entire structure.

a43f83f30dfb7440.text: Single-tower nuraghe with an ellipsoidal plan. Other wall stretches of uncertain function are present. The site was also occupied in the Roman period.

a44bb6177309ed64.text: Single-tower nuraghe incorporated in a bastion. Four courses of enormous sandstone blocks of the retaining wall are visible, for a height of almost 2 metres. Climbing onto the retaining wall you can see the ruined top of the tower.

a45c5c3c68787a2c.text:
Only shaped ashlars of the monument can be identified, from which it can be established that the tomb was of the coursed type in isodomic masonry.

Some of the ashlars (perhaps those belonging to the exedra) are incorporated into the walling of a recent hut, and others lie scattered nearby, hidden by vegetation. In particular, the so-called dentilled stele of considerable size is present.

The baetyls now placed in the forecourt of the Church of Santa Caterina appear to come from it.

a45e3017c8916a0f.text:
On the summit of the limestone outcrop at 191 metres above sea level stands a monumental Nuragic complex that makes use of the natural rock ledge to the west and a sheer drop on the eastern slope.

The monument covers an area of about 1000 sq m and extends in plan along a longitudinal axis oriented north-west–south-east, with a probable entrance to the north.

From north to south the following can be identified: a tholos; a sub-rectangular block; a semicircular room; walls following a curvilinear course.

a460a7f7bcfbe647.text: Visitable, collapsed in on itself, central tower with a tree inside, large walls of limestone tuff. Used in the Roman period, as shown by the presence of roof-tile sherds. In the rocky outcrops nearby there are laccus. Traces of a village around it.

a47bec8478559f00.text: The monument lies about 200 metres north-east of the Nuraghe Figu and less than 350 metres south-west of the Nuraghe Bighinzone. It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, a wall thickness of 4.00 m on the east side and 3.60 m on the west, and a height that varies from 3.05 m to the north-north-west, with six courses, to 1.75 m to the south-south-west with three or four courses. The masonry consists of polyhedral blocks laid in horizontal courses that are not always regular.

a490349148fb125f.text:
Complex nuraghe of which only some wall stretches of the towers and probably of an outer wall are visible. The collapse and the dense vegetation make it difficult to interpret the spatial development of the complex.

A modest Early Neolithic village extends to the south-west.

The complex shows interesting superimpositions, including the ruins of an old medau with buildings constructed of dry-stone walls.

a4b7ad5569f87ebd.text: A few megalithic stones indicating a probable nuraghe, perhaps a circle. Witnesses certainly report that many stones ended up forming a hardcore layer during the reclamation of the marsh. Nuraghe of the marshes, of the swamps. See Paùles and Cunvéntu nòu.mu

a4c2703d195d189b.text: The archaeological park contains a hypogeal necropolis made up of about fifteen domus de janas (the fairy houses), the prehistoric tombs cut into the rock faces of Sa Carona Arrubia (red rock face) and into the large basalt erratic boulders, and a few single-tower nuraghi.

a4d47b8acf558a1d.text: A group of domus de janas, the most important of which bears a chequerboard motif, bordered on one side by a zig-zag band, representing the depiction of fabric hangings found in the dwellings of the living and reproduced in the houses of the dead.

a5015661dbdb7053.text: The nuraghe is marked as "Chessalzu" on the maps of the former land registry. It is ruined; only a few buried courses remain.

a50d659dc67aa32d.text: A ruined nuraghe of which it is difficult to say whether it belonged to the category of unfinished nuraghi or single-tower nuraghi

a51926cb866a1b2e.text: The construction is atypical and hard to classify: it is not a nuraghe, yet it is difficult to call it a hut. Traces of later human intervention from various historical periods can be found, and these have certainly altered the original structure, creating the difficulty of classification.

a54e87c6d8b49cca.text: Reported by a resident of Osilo. Domus not photographable, hidden by brambles and shrubs. To be verified.

a58d98130a6619d3.text: It is a single-tower nuraghe standing on a cliff that overlooks the whole area of the Tirso river below the village of Villanova Truscheddu. The tholos has collapsed inwards and the nuraghe is not maintained and has never been investigated.

a5931941e0916b3d.text:
Nuraghe consisting of two towers and a courtyard on the south side. Built of large roughly dressed blocks of red trachyte. A megalithic double-faced wall runs south from the nuraghe, of which about 35 m of the basal courses survive. To the north, and partly to the east and south, a village of huts extends, of which various basal circles remain.

A few metres west of the nuraghe there is a well now blocked by collapse debris.

a594f789c493731a.text: This is one of the countless nuraghi destroyed over the millennia by vegetation, ploughing, land reclamation and stone clearance for other uses. It must have been a multi-lobed nuraghe, perhaps with a double frontal addition. But it is hard to say without cleaning and excavation.

a5a283e691e0407e.text: Located inside a private property, among the very numerous domus de janas of the Ozieri area, they are the largest in the territory and beyond; they are also the only ones that display symbols of the bull god carved in such a clear manner.

a5ea087f180e766a.text: The nuraghe Su Nuraxi of Gonnosnò lies about 400 metres east of the village, near the industrial area. It is a single-tower nuraghe largely destroyed and covered by its own rubble and vegetation. Only a few courses remain.

a62e22d864f0c50a.text: Situated a short distance from Sa Unta and Sa Tumba, in the locality of Sculta 'e Muru, it appears as a heap of rocks in total abandonment.

a6875cf62fb69713.text:
Proto-nuraghe Mura Barbaros. The monument consists of an outer wall that encloses, for at least three-fifths, a building of rather irregular shape. On the level of the collapsed top a short stretch of corridor to the south-east can be made out, partially closed by four lintelled slabs, while to the south-west the lintelled entrance of a second corridor is visible.

Almost a continuation of the previous one.

a6946ce0bc088ff4.text: It has an elliptical plan and is built on a bed of granite rock. The interior has completely collapsed, suggesting the existence of a chamber to the north with a curvilinear layout. The entrance is not currently visible, but it was probably on the north side, as that is the most accessible. During clearance work, several early medieval ceramic finds decorated with "stampiglia" were recovered.

a6c7c5a6c2f87d12.text: It is a single-tower nuraghe that still has its tholos intact. It almost certainly belongs to the type with a sub-floor chamber, which is easily recognisable. The entrance has collapsed but it can be entered carefully by sliding over the lintel astride the guard chamber.

a6e4b0b0f775a0a3.text: Only a few traces of the settlement survive, having completely slipped downhill. Excavated by looters. Remains of the wall faces are visible.

a71c8af1e0ea75c3.text: The protohistoric settlement of Via Monastir–Via S. Giovanni in San Sperate extends over an area in the present north-eastern sector of the modern Campidano town. It was identified at several points within the same UGAS; it developed along the interfluvial strip between the north bank of the Riu Flumineddu and the south bank of the Riu Mannu, at elevations not exceeding 46 m above sea level.

a763ba22801b0b3d.text:
It is in very poor condition.

It is a circular single-tower nuraghe (diameter 11.50 m), built with massive limestone blocks. At present the wall face survives to a maximum height of 1.80 m over three courses of stones on the south side and 0.80 m over a single course on the north side.

a77fb27ddf71f730.text: Remains of a complex nuraghe built of basalt.

a78baf752f284cfb.text:
It is a single-tower tholos nuraghe of trachyte with some elements in granite, circular in plan and about 11 metres in diameter, surviving to a maximum height of 5 metres.

The monument has an entrance topped by a lintel, a corridor with a trapezoidal cross-section that gives access to a niche and the stairwell, as well as the central chamber with two opposing niches; however, the whole is difficult to reach because of the collapses.

a797b386e0eeba7d.text: Remains of a giants' tomb of which only the basal courses survive.

a79b155e90515036.text: The nuraghe stands on Monte Perdas de Fogu at 230 m above sea level. It is a complex nuraghe of which the wall faces of the central tower survive. The entrance to the monument, trapezoidal in shape, lies to the SSE. A narrow corridor with an ogival cross-section leads directly into the central tower's chamber.

a7acefc6b503fc1b.text: The monument is built at the foot of a rocky outcrop where a spring vein is present. The structure is made of trachyte boulders of various sizes expertly worked. Access to the well is through a vestibule leading to a staircase that ends in the well chamber; this has a façade preserving a rectangular entrance opening surmounted by a lintel. Because of collapses and its precarious state the site has been fenced off.

a7b1a955b5da72e1.text: According to legend it was one of the seven villages destroyed because of the beautiful Maria Cadelana.

a7b7b0d5639af710.text: The nuraghe "Serra de Chigulas" was formerly called "Su Tangarone" and is mentioned in Canon Spanu's book. The monument has a complex plan.

a7d18f784698fc37.text:
Imposing three-lobed nuraghe with the two added towers collapsed but the main tower in good condition, although largely buried. It must have served to defend the nearby village with the nuraghe of Pettu 'e Murtas, only 200 metres away as the crow flies, and to guard the Badde valley below.

For further information:

a7f2b566d648084d.text: It is a nuraghe that is more than ruined. It appears as a shapeless heap of stones which, on its least damaged side, preserves three basal courses of the original construction.

a7fe1104a67ce84b.text: In this hypogeum dating to the Middle Neolithic (4600–4000 BC) several interesting finds were recovered, including a tetrapod limestone dish with a bull's-head protome. This is described as one of the oldest depictions of a bucranium in Sardinia. A bucranium is the figure of an animal head with the horns pointing upwards. On display at the Cagliari Archaeological Museum.

a7feace4e4217caf.text: The antechamber is quadrangular; the walls are concave while the ceiling and floor are flat, and the height of the chamber is almost the same as that of the doorway. In the back wall is the doorway leading to the main chamber, which is sub-quadrangular in shape and set irregularly in the wall. The main chamber is sub-ellipsoidal (1.80 x 1.24 m); the walls are concave and the ceiling is flat.

a804c5e55978b832.text: The sacred well was wrenched open by tomb robbers with a bulldozer, and they found numerous bronze figurines which were sold on the black market. The well is now in very poor condition, covered in brambles and mud.

a80847fd522ab682.text: Collective burial of the Nuragic period. The structure has been largely destroyed. Some alignments of stones belonging to the corridor and the exedra help to identify the monument's plan.

a835b5d38e89723c.text: The tomb is set into an earthen mound. The burial corridor is 7.65 m long. It lacks an exedra. The excavation yielded Roman-period finds and, below them, Nuragic ones.

a855b80e52e55cb2.text: They are two hypogea: a two-celled domus de janas and a three-celled domus de janas.

a85be7448f6b2eed.text: Located near the Monte Ladu quarry, on the banks of an artificial pond. The base is visible, still partially intact.

a8af3b5d126edf0a.text: North-west of the nuraghe Sa Scrocca Manna, a probable menhir of prismatic shape with a triangular base lies on the ground. The boulder has a flattened front face, probably produced by pecking the surface. The two rear faces show signs of working and smoothing.

a8afd9564c737464.text:
The megalithic burial lies less than 200 metres south-east of Nuraghe Pattada, which stands in a higher, commanding position on the sheer edge of an extensive trachyte formation.

The monument, of isodomic construction, with a coursed exedra and a lintelled entrance, repeats in plan the ground-plan common to this tomb type: a rectangular body with an apsidal rear profile, preceded by a semicircular exedra.

a8f07125c272d1e5.text:
The structure is badly damaged and only a circular alignment of large stones, set on the natural rock, remains, with an estimated maximum diameter of 11 m; no other details or planimetric articulations can be determined.

The surviving basal course consists of large, roughly dressed blocks whose dimensions range from a maximum of 1.04 m long by 0.41 m high down to a minimum of 0.35 m by 0.17 m.

a8f18cf3de392617.text: It lies within the municipal territory of Sassari. It is very ruinous and covered by dense vegetation.

a92a9b5be9af49b5.text: This is the original location of the menhirs now at sa Figu. Here they were heaped in disorder, perhaps as a result of land-improvement works, as reported by local herders.

a939020cb6f5fbb4.text: The Caìu nuraghe is certainly the remains of a tancato nuraghe, that is, two towers enclosing a small internal courtyard, probably datable to the end of the Recent Bronze Age. It lies near the Genna Salixi Necropolis.

a9694b872e7d6eb4.text: Complex nuraghe, collapsed and of which only a few buried courses remain, where a frontal addition followed the original tower.

a97dc43119a3655c.text:
They lie in the municipality of Fonni (NU).

The site comprises 5 tombs, of which 2 are well preserved. Four tombs are close together while a fifth (in very poor condition) lies about 400 metres to the north-west.

a982c65902c0d434.text: 2 domus de janas with an architectural façade, a typical funerary architecture very common in the Sassari area

a9a01cfa60c3d1ed.text: The necropolis consists of three corridor burials and two giants' tombs without a stele. A fuller description is given in the document "recupero dei siti archeologici nel territorio di Castiadas".

a9b692d68ac4ca81.text: It is in poor condition, disturbed by stone-clearing and earth-moving work. In the apsidal area it preserves a baetyl with a single "ocellar" hollow that is not fully defined.

a9bc502e53a2df29.text: Apart from the central tower, the complex is largely buried, making it difficult to interpret the parts that compose it. Around the nuraghe several circular rooms can be seen, perhaps the remains of a village. Also nearby is what may be a sacrificial area, called by the people of Samatzai “Sa piscedd' 'e su casu” because its particular appearance resembles a cheese form.

a9d037328394e046.text: group of menhirs scattered on the ground

a9eca8afd1ffb65c.text: Typical single-chamber domus de janas with a carved stele on the limestone façade

a9f8e9d90aec9d28.text: Remains of a small single-tower nuraghe built of limestone.

aa1d7df2fc6db611.text: It consists of a central tower about 7 metres high and two lateral towers linked by a bastion that wraps around and protects the whole structure. The central tower still has its intact corbelled dome (tholos), while the lateral towers have collapsed. Access is from the south-east, through a small triangular courtyard that leads straight into the entrance of the structure. On the left, after a short corridor, a staircase opens that leads to the top.

aa35f0a49e8beb58.text: The nuraghe stands on the summit of a granitic rocky outcrop; it is a small single-tower nuraghe in an advanced state of decay, and the dense vegetation makes it impossible to reach and visit.

aa82885afd42cbac.text: On a hill, consisting of a central tower and a bastion, with a large village that the dense vegetation conceals almost entirely. Two large huts survive, one identified as the 'meeting hut'; at least four more can be glimpsed in the scrub.

aa972c1dfc3a4ef3.text: Contiguous with the area where the corridor nuraghe of the same name stands, it consists of dozens of quadrangular huts, sometimes divided into several rooms and apsidal, bounded by blocks set on edge. Sometimes affected by illegal excavations, the fragile pre-Nuragic dwellings are located both inside the wooded area owned by the municipality and, in greater numbers, outside it, in a large area used as pasture.

aaf0a133c0400de7.text: It stands on Cuccuru Cireddu at 130 m above sea level. It is not in good condition and is almost completely covered by mastic. It is in visual contact with the Nuraghe Monte Eghedda about 1 km away and the Nuraghe S'Omu e S'Orku about 2 km away as the crow flies. Documents from the Municipality of Maracalagonis also report a necropolis, perhaps "Roman"; indeed, a large amount of material is present all around the nuraghe over a wide radius.

aafd007f48f2d40b.text: Single-tower nuraghe with its top missing and the vault collapsed inside. The best-preserved stretch stands four metres high with eight courses. To the south-east the lintelled entrance survives with its relieving window.

ab0dc26fa59379d1.text:
Domus de janas reused in modern times for other purposes.

It should comprise 9 domus de janas.

ab0e6175a7ff3822.text: Nuraghe Mannu stands on the summit of the beautiful Cala Fuili beach. The importance of this site lies above all in the Nuragic village of Nuragheddu, which is one of the largest in Sardinia and consists of more than 200 huts of various shapes and sizes.

ab11d6aac44a8857.text: Reported to the Superintendency of Ca-or on 17 May 2021 by the Nurnet Foundation

ab172037023d8e3e.text: This domus de janas takes its name from the bas-relief carving of a ram's protome on one of the interior walls. The other distinctive feature is the dolmenic corridor in front of the entrance.

ab285e36cbef122d.text:
It is a single-tower nuraghe roofed with a tholos, still in good condition: it survives on the N-NE and N-W sides to a height of 10.50 metres, while the SE side, corresponding to the entrance, has collapsed.

The external wall face, of 26 courses of stone, is formed by large polygonal blocks in the base, which has a diameter of 14 metres, while in the upper part the blocks are sub-square and of modest size, becoming more regular as the height increases.

ab3ae37d49394b68.text: The building stands in a strategic position on the limestone plateau of Sas Seas (482 m a.s.l.), from which it dominates the surrounding territory. The ground plan of the nuraghe cannot be clearly defined because of the collapses. Inside the structure part of a rectangular chamber survives that was probably originally roofed with a truncated ogive. The same roofing system has been hypothesised for the Fodde nuraghe at Bolotana.

ab5306207025dee8.text: A vast and complex archaeological site, with at least two villages, a probable necropolis with an attached building that may be a place of worship, and a kiln a short distance away.

ab7d2bf27b431c4b.text: Mixed nuraghe of which little remains, partly covered by vegetation. Perhaps enlarged and restructured.

ab7e0a4908ac304d.text: Of the megalithic tomb, which was very well preserved until the 1970s, only the northern side and the right arm of the exedra survive, and only partially; a short stretch of the burial chamber can also be made out, while a few metres away some enormous slabs that formed the flat-lintelled roof of the tomb are visible.

ab89dd9a84d34442.text: It now appears as a single-tower nuraghe, surrounded by well-cultivated fields; it is imposing, with free-standing walls about seven metres high. To the right a steep helical staircase leads up to the top of the nuraghe; to the left a niche overlooks the entrance area. Inside the circular chamber three further niches can be seen, clearly defined. The view from the terrace takes in the woods and the well-tended lands of the industrious people of Samugheo. It deserves to be visited and enhanced.

abb8b0f8b18c338f.text: Apparently detached from the nearby tomb, it must certainly have been built in relation to it, or vice versa. The place is also known as Culu de Muru.

abc1a6b035f3aa2e.text: At the foot of the nuraghe of the same name – in the east-south-east sector – wall remains probably belonging to the village are visible, though partly hidden by the scrub. One can clearly make out: the entrance to an enclosure; the remains of a rectangular hut; cyclopean walls adjoining the hut structures and the nuraghe itself. The structures were almost certainly reused in relatively recent times.

abc430a475acfcfa.text: The giants' tomb Su Niu de su Crobu stands on a rocky rise, not far from the sea, in the locality Sa corona de su crabì. The burial, of the “coursed” type, consists of an apsidal funerary corridor a little over 10 m long and 1.20 m wide on average; the stones composing it are roughly worked, laid in irregular courses and wedged with numerous chocks.

abd2e5da6c30fc78.text: Located near the nuraghe of the same name, a few giants' tombs can be seen, hidden by the dense vegetation that also partly conceals the nuraghe.

abe29e6bf2912d65.text: Situated about a hundred metres north of the Rio Merchis and less than 300 metres west of the proto-nuraghe known locally as “Nuraghe Magossula”, the monument is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan (diam. 13.70 x 11.70 m) that survives to a maximum height of 2.00 m with four courses on the north side, while on the south-west there is only a single course and on the south-east, where the entrance must have been, the wall face is entirely absent.

abe3cb188b09c769.text: Complex nuraghe, apparently four-lobed, with the central tower's tholos intact

abee9d7422c12098.text: Unusual rectangular plan with a probable entrance on the south side, which has collapsed completely. The north, west and east sides remain visible. Built on the edge of a steep slope, it is probably a temple dedicated to the water cult, as suggested by two springs (long dry) at the foot of the structure on the south side. One spring is covered by an almost intact tholos with its entrance partly blocked by a collapse, while the other, triangular in plan, shows clear traces of a spring at its apex.

ac30d8b330f5adb9.text: “Nuraghe Sas Melas, a short distance from the hill called Fruncu Sas Patatas, at the ford of Rio Minori. It is the best nuraghe in the municipality; it still has two storeys; solid construction, accessible doorway like the corridor and the lower chamber; shepherds’ refuge; the stair leads to the upper storey, with a domed cell; windows wider than they are high. In the lower chamber a stone table. On land belonging to the heirs of Luca Piras, son of Angelo.”

ac60de420955cb0e.text: Complex nuraghe of two towers joined by a corridor, built of basalt.

ac905da6ed6aab7b.text: Nuragic huts along the south-western coast within the municipality of Arbus. Little remains visible, but it is an important testimony to that civilisation.

aca7110d2b1d00dc.text:
Cut into a tufa cliff inside a narrow valley traversed by a tributary of the Rio Mannu, just outside the village, to the right of the road to Allai.

The domus de janas lie on private property, fenced and closed by a gate; the owner is very often working in the vegetable garden and will not hesitate to let you in and accompany you to the site.

acf7fbeeecede4e6.text: Multi-celled, extensively altered and used as a shepherds' shelter.

ad169d6781c351c7.text:
Small watchtower.

Nearby there is a hut with a "rotonda" fitted with a basin.

ad3404b285e4dd5d.text: The tomb is built in isodomic masonry with a coursed façade. The burial chamber, squat and symmetrical, apsidal, tapers slightly into a broad semicircular exedra edged with benches, facing SSE. Of the monument, in local basalt, the basal course of the burial chamber survives, part of the basal slabs of the façade and of the bench seat, and a good part of the extradosed roofing of monolithic arches.

ada7409facdba3a2.text:
The dolmen lies about 250 metres north-west of Nuraghe Arghentu and less than 500 metres south-east of Nuraghe Interenas, on stony ground with abundant shrub vegetation.

The tomb, built partly on a basalt outcrop, now consists of three orthostats that enclose a quadrangular space (1.16 x 1.26 m; height 0.92 m) and support a large covering slab, now slightly tilted to one side.

adbcbd704c58fdb4.text: A ruined nuraghe overgrown with vegetation, near which a dolmen is reported.

adbf3e18078c98fd.text:
It is a single-tower with a circular plan  

(axis SE-NO 11.75 m; axis East-West 11.50 m) with a thickness of 2.70 m to the north-west and 3.85 m to the west; the maximum remaining height is in the north-west, measuring 3.60 m on 8 courses of basaltic stones, well-worked, of medium and large dimensions, laid in regular horizontal courses.

adc9676e8f088f8e.text: The type of nuraghe cannot be determined; a tower with its tholos still intact is present, surrounded by collapse debris amid the dense scrub.

adef3851df435ef0.text: The tower is missing its top and the perimeter has an irregular circumference. The internal diameter varies from 4.2 to 5.6 m. There are traces of clandestine excavations.

ae01d19c24a3ba42.text: Single-tower nuraghe, ruined with its tholos collapsed and overgrown with vegetation

ae0bbc681c522b0f.text: The nuraghe is a complex type, consisting of a five-lobed bastion enclosing the original tower and a courtyard. The central tower, circular in plan (13 m external diameter), survives to a maximum height of over 12 metres. The wall face is built of blocks laid in horizontal courses. The lower chamber is filled with rubble, laid transversely to the helical staircase — also blocked — that started from the ground floor.

ae218d79e1243485.text: The Orgono nuraghe at Ghilarza is a remarkable monument whose structural development tells the evolution of Nuragic architecture: from the archaic nuraghe with an elongated, upturned-boat-shaped chamber to the truncated-conical tower with a circular tholos chamber. The consolidation and excavation work carried out so far has allowed at least partial recovery of the monument, which was already seriously unstable and in danger of collapse.

ae312519fed91a26.text: Only a few large boulders that formed the basal course remain of the monument, which is largely covered by a farm track built over it; from these it can be deduced that the ground plan was circular.

ae38f105abd43da6.text: The complex consists of two domus de janas cut into a south-facing sandstone rock face; they lie to the south-east of the new church of San Giovanni.

ae5a0ceb36b37b66.text: Situated on a rocky spur near the road between Thiesi and Romana, it dominates the landscape below, where the nuraghe Majore stands out in particular.

ae60012e460b9a03.text: Complex nuraghe with a village and a sacred well nearby

ae6ea4a9ac070e0b.text: Domus de janas reported to the NurNet editorial team. From the video it appears to be a rocky outcrop where a more extensive necropolis is likely to exist.

ae759644c7006e86.text: The nuraghe stands on a rocky ridge west of the Domus de janas and is completely hidden by dense vegetation. The outline of the central tower can barely be made out, but a few partially visible courses suggest a single-tower structure.

ae7c21c6f9727706.text: Nuraghe inside the town centre, single-tower, partially collapsed

aec5d2cd9d74183a.text: At the end of the Geometric phase the number of occupied sites continues to fall: evidence for the 7th and 6th centuries BC is found only at Monti Crastu, Is Arruinalis and Monti Angurdu, where decorated sherds of the Archaic phase have been observed. In this later phase it is likely that the centre of Is Arruinalis grew to a “proto-urban” level, as is known to have happened at other settlements in the Campidano and Marmilla (Tuppedili, San Sperate).

aec7e336cd75948c.text: An almost completely destroyed nuraghe, of which a semicircular stretch of walling survives.

aed3b993e8b02f21.text:
It stands imposing in the locality of Pauli on a limestone plateau. The monument consists of a central tower almost 7 metres high, against which two further added structures lean, now almost completely collapsed. From the entrance you enter the main chamber, partly covered by collapse debris.

The nuraghe is surrounded by an outer wall and the remains of a village, whose huts are used as goat shelters. A few hundred metres away lie the remains of two giants' tombs.

aee7e191c7488f95.text: A ruined nuraghe, notable for its proximity to several other Nuragic megalithic monuments.

aee90228c89f101e.text: Two giants' tombs a few dozen metres apart

aefad4ebd990fda5.text: About 100 metres west of the nuraghe, a small settlement has been recorded, consisting of the remains of a cluster of at least five circular huts and a rectangular building. South of the nuraghe, about 500 metres away, the basal courses of two circular huts and other short stretches of curvilinear walls in trachyte are visible, while about 400 metres south-west of the nuraghe lie the remains of a circular hut.

af1cca68f83765ad.text:
A pre- and proto-historic complex comprising a modest Early Neolithic village, a complex nuraghe enclosed by an outer wall, and its village of huts. Inside the village a well for water supply has been dug, of uncertain date.

The buildings are constructed of blocks of local andesite.

Above the Nuragic hut village a fine sheepfold has been built, bounded by dry-stone walls.

af207b243c1b42e0.text: The monument, situated a short distance from the Giants' Tombs of Su Piccante and Su Ittichinzu and the nearby village of Lettu Rucratu, stands at the foot of a hill where it appears as a small spring cut into the ground, where the water table presumably emerged naturally, and lined with blocks of rough basalt.

af475417d567f1bc.text: It is a sacred well almost completely buried and partially disturbed by illicit digging. It can be identified in the middle of dense, invasive vegetation that nevertheless does not prevent the presence of wall structures forming the upper part of the well's tholos and the upper structures of the vestibule from being observed.

af5ccc6c740c54ff.text: The nuraghe stands on land used for grazing and partly for vineyards. It has been irreparably destroyed by illicit excavations in the area. Only a short stretch of wall can be seen, which does not allow its dimensions or construction type to be determined any further.

af601c4ae20f7af7.text: Reported to the NurNet editorial team by an enthusiast from Osilo. A single-chambered structure standing on a limestone outcrop from which it takes its name, near the settlement of Santa Vittoria.

af623f91f0934921.text: Single-tower nuraghe of simple type, built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The building, camouflaged among the dense vegetation and overshadowed by a large clump of prickly pears, retains about six courses of superimposed blocks. The entrance, to the south-east, has a large, well-squared monolithic lintel. The jamb blocks are also quite carefully worked.

af64eac4e2fa0335.text: The nuraghe is completely ruined, probably also known by the name Tostoinus.

af6bf30c757e0870.text: Simple dolmen, with a rectangular plan and the entrance facing north-east. The right-hand wall consists of a rectangular slab, the left-hand wall of two roughly worked boulders resting on natural rock. The capstone is flattened on its underside and left natural on the upper surface. DATE: Ozieri Culture (3500–2700 BC).

af7a186c5b7f4668.text: Nuraghe of which only a few traces remain

af7bedb82930f301.text:
Not easily accessible, it is reached after a steep climb through arid, rocky pastures, among protruding stones that hint at the ancient existence of a large village.

Nothing of this monument appears to have been excavated, and only the tholos of the second level alone is accessible.

The courtyard in front of the main tower appears completely buried under ashlars and brambles.

af8d3bc9984c50ab.text: The territory, today almost entirely devoid of vegetation, must have been greener and richer in water at the time of the nuraghi: the springs, now neglected, were clean and well kept until thirty years ago. Even then it is likely that small circular structures were built around many of them, made of large blocks and covered by small vaults with an opening for the water, to keep them clean, as we can see in the remains of Funtana Gureu.

af9c3e6af131c1da.text: The Complex lies within the territory of Villaputzu. It comprises the two towers known as N.ghe Monte Arrubiu I and II, which must be considered part of the same structure, and the Nuragic village that spreads out on the plain below. From the summit there is a wonderful view. There are various rocks that take on distinctive shapes.

afb4d83418826461.text: Complex nuraghe with a central tower and bastions, probably with a second tower. Nearby are the remains of a settlement and the Giants' Tomb of Li Mizzani. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

afc7e0e6fdd224e3.text: One of the most important historical testimonies near the municipality of Arbus is the nuraghe of Cugui, one of the most original in Sardinia. Set on the summit of a hill in the direction of Fluminimaggiore, the nuraghe of Cugui is easily reached from the Canau area, known for its spring. The nuraghe has three towers, one of which is accessible, although taller people may have considerable difficulty getting inside.

afe8a4a0f729ece4.text:
It lies in the municipality of Cagliari.

The final part of a domus de janas (Neolithic hypogean tomb), near the cave of the same name, destroyed by the limestone quarry.

afed8acf6ff6f247.text:
It should preserve an intact tholos.

An imposing complex nuraghe, today it appears as a wooded hill.

On the summit a staircase allows access to the interior chambers, probably the central tower.

I advise against an internal visit; because of the large roots of the vegetation it hosts, the nuraghe is very unstable!

affe51a749d174b0.text:
The central tower dates to the 15th–13th century BC, while the bastion, the outer wall and the curtain wall date to the 13th–late 12th century BC.

Already in the Early Iron Age the finds show a declining use of the site, though it never fell completely out of use.

It was also used for funerary purposes, as attested by finds of the 7th–8th century.

b0477bb27e92831f.text:
The remains of what appears to have been a classic-type Nuragic sacred well lie against a dry-stone wall marking the boundary between the territories of Birori and Borore, a few metres from the Bau Cannas hypogea.

At present only the circular base profile (diam. 1.40 m) and a masonry of two courses of well-worked stones are visible; the bottom, as far as can be seen through the standing water, seems to have paving slabs.

b076ad8ea62a58d5.text: Only the floor, made of large stones, a few perimeter stones, and the quite evident exedra remain.

b08189b4cc9575e7.text: A circular single-tower nuraghe with three niches. It stands on an island in the middle of Lake Cuga, which was spared when the dam of the same name was built. It cannot be reached by land; the only access is by boat or canoe after a journey of 20–25 minutes. Each time one lands there after the winter season, the rebirth of the flora and fauna is revealed anew, forming a natural frame for the archaic shapes of the nuraghe. The quantity of incisions and cupmarks is striking.

b0974ea8b643c694.text: Situated on the side of the ravine of the same name where the stream of the same name flows during the rains, it originally stood on an isolated spur in a raised position above the valley below. Some courses of medium-large blocks are present. A few metres further downstream large quantities of collapse are visible; the structure is now almost completely destroyed.

b0ba63faaca93405.text: Three-lobed nuraghe, reused in the Roman and medieval periods. The village around the tower, now practically non-existent because of agricultural mechanisation, is one of the most extensive in the territory of Uri.

b0cb5ddcfbcce376.text: Composite nuraghe. At present it is impossible to read its plan because the whole site has been churned up by mechanical diggers, even though until a few years ago it was possible to go inside by lowering oneself from above. One thus entered a long corridor with corbelled walls; a further bulldozer operation has probably piled more material against the nuraghe and blocked the entrance. The hope is that the burial has protected it from this devastation.

b0fa6b8bbf288f0a.text:
A. Sanguinetti, who in 1970 complained that, among other things, it was partly buried under stone dumps caused by the reclamation of the surrounding farmland.

The author nevertheless described a single-tower nuraghe with an elliptical plan and an entrance facing north-east, and hypothesised a straight access corridor.

b10def6f34c38df9.text:
Situated just outside the town of Arzachena, it appears as an imposing structure, although the upper floor has partly collapsed.

It is built of large blocks of granite and dates to around the Middle Bronze Age (about 1600 BC) on the basis of the numerous finds recovered during the excavations.

The walls of the nuraghe lean against a large granite boulder; for this reason the nuraghe has an irregular plan that gives it a "pseudo-nuraghe" appearance. (MIBACT)

b1139bbdfa02be4a.text: The site can only be reached by crossing a difficult path. Of the ruined monument, which is not easy to interpret, a section on the east side survives with 11 irregular courses of masonry.

b1377630f0c0325f.text: Nearby there are also some Nuragic huts.

b137f9b29d3b3a16.text: What remains of a small nuraghe very close to Santu Sciori. An ancient church was built on top of it. Mentioned in the writings of Vittorio Angius for the discovery of some giant bones.

b14861155ad2eb2a.text: Structure of uncertain interpretation built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The building stands on a small natural rocky spur and has an elliptical plan. It measures about 17 m in length and about 11 m in width at the central point. The northern, western and eastern parts consist of one to two courses of large and medium-sized polygonal blocks, while the southern part has three courses built with the same technique.

b15bc2089f6f2adf.text:
Situated at the foot of a hill along the course of the Rio Caddare, in an area covered by dense vegetation, the remains of wall structures belonging to the village can be seen emerging from a section of the hill eroded by the elements; these are not, however, the only evidence relating to this settlement.

Venturing into the vegetation it is in fact possible to identify the presence on the ground of numerous circular structures.

b163f4ed2018f712.text: Near the namesake nuraghe on the ridge that descends towards the Stupàra stream there is a giants' tomb built of flat schist stones. The tomb is about 7 metres long and about 2 metres high. No exedra is visible. Its state of preservation is nevertheless fair.

b17749259b5508b2.text: It was the earliest settlement in the Villanovaforru area. A short distance from a spring, unfortunately no traces of it remain. A Bonnanaro Culture tomb was found, dated to the Early Bronze Age between 1700 and 1600 BC, together with fragments of a tripod vase and obsidian arrowheads; no osteological remains or tomb structures were recovered. The isolated find is to be interpreted as an open-air site or a funerary deposition.

b18d7aa2733daec4.text: On 10 July 1205 Maria de Thori, wife of the nobleman Pietro de Maronju and aunt of Comita, judge of Torres, gave the church of S. Maria di Orria piccinna, near Chiaramonti, together with the nearby church of S. Giusta, with servants, houses, woods, lands and animals to the hermitage of Camaldoli, and for it to the prior Martino, granting, among other things, to him and his successors the free election of the rectors of the donated churches and the burial of the monks.

b199f0dec53fa729.text: In Goffredo Casalis's historical dictionary the nuraghe is recorded as Sa Corti deis Bacus.

b1a35b3931d0d0a9.text: Nuraghe built of white limestone ashlars on a rocky outcrop rising from dense woodland. The masonry survives to human height.

b1af3f1ace8db3cc.text:
Sa Pedra de Nunnale – Orune. A village built around the picturesque and colossal tower of bizarre shape, at the base of which stands the eponymous Nuraghe. The nuraghe, though imposing, appears incredibly tiny compared with the immense rock that looms over it.

This single-tower nuraghe is built of megalithic blocks only roughly dressed, of even larger dimensions at the base

b1b28c638d2cd2c3.text: Serra is Araus is a multi-layered site, known for a rock-cut necropolis (domus de janas) of the Neolithic (Ozieri Culture), Chalcolithic (Monte Claro Culture) and Early Bronze Age (Bonnanaro). The 2013 excavation brought to light two new hypogea and the first evidence of the Nuragic village. In particular, traces of a building were found inside which a large model of a nuraghe had been placed.

b1e43aaec3ab3e9b.text: Nuragic wall (200 m long, double-faced). It enclosed a Nuragic village.

b1e70ef0ea9c93b8.text:
The nuraghe still has an accessible tholos, although its top is missing. The entrance lacks its original material all the way up to the top of the tower, perhaps because of a collapse that affected the load-bearing structures of the wall in the past. The masonry has been rebuilt.

The nuraghe was almost certainly used both as a shelter and as an animal pen, and this has allowed it to be preserved in good condition.

The monument has the stairway on the left, with 13 steps still in place.

b22e099dd645b905.text: Remains of a simple single-tower tholos nuraghe built with basalt blocks from Montiferru. The structures survive to a height of 5–6 courses. The nuraghe stands on the summit of a dune of what was, until the 1950s, the Is Arenas desert. It has direct visual contact with the large four-lobed nuraghe of Tradori, on the opposite side of the road.

b23ae3d818bd84a2.text: Archaic corridor nuraghe. The nuraghe stands on a hillside and is laid out on two different levels, adapting to the lie and slope of the ground. The structures are largely covered by vegetation, but the north-west and west parts can be seen in particular. The north-west part follows a semi-circular course, while the west part consists of a massive wall that extends in a straight line towards the south.

b24a2111bcb1276b.text:
The nuraghe has been dated between the 14th and 12th centuries BC.

It is notable for the use of large basalt blocks carefully squared, in particular the jambs and lintel of the entrance.

At the entrance, on the left, is the ramp that led to the upper terrace, while on the right there is a niche in the walling. In the chamber one can see the three large ogival niches in the walls, the central hearth, and the tholos that forms the ceiling, still intact.

b25bd43329214241.text:
It is cut into an erratic limestone boulder, worked on the outside as well, roughly trapezoidal in shape. On the main façade, which has an entrance, an arched stele almost 4 metres high was carved, on top of which three small baetyls were originally placed. On the rear façade another small entrance can be seen, perhaps from an earlier period.

The material culture found during the excavations is of the Bonnanaro type (Early Bronze Age).

b2662ba178526c3a.text: Single-chambered domus de janas with a façade

b27804e5b11675c0.text: An almost completely destroyed nuraghe of which only a single course remains visible. Covered almost entirely by collapse and vegetation, its ground plan cannot be determined.

b283ffcb72a32112.text: The site consists of the nuraghe, formed by the central tower and two towers, various buildings all around that would suggest the presence of an important village in antiquity, and finally a building that appears to be an ancient sanctuary.

b28649a52ddf91e8.text:
This nuraghe stands on a hillock opposite the village of Mara.

It is signposted yet completely neglected. To reach the monument one has to pick through tall scrub that makes it almost invisible. For this reason it is hard to describe, especially for a layperson.

It appears to be of the corridor type.

b298512c9614edbf.text: A ruined nuraghe, buried and covered in vegetation. It appears to be a single-tower nuraghe.

b2ae0631cc6284fd.text: Nuraghe built of trachyte blocks; the lintel still survives, but the rest has been destroyed, its stones probably used for the dry-stone walls in the area.

b2b1c3fa13dbbed8.text: The nuraghe, probably of complex structure, is now covered by dense vegetation and preserves only a few courses of the original building. A cyclopean wall of circular shape, about 10 m in diameter, is attached to the nuraghe. Its state of preservation is very poor.

b2c0b85275518823.text: It is largely buried. One can thus make out a central tower with an irregularly circular perimeter, containing a central chamber, also circular. Along the outer perimeter of the monument stretches of walling can be seen that suggest something about its more complex articulations; for example, to the east-north-east one might hypothesise terracing works, if not the actual presence of huts or enclosures.

b2c1d1358d15e4b2.text: The probable nuraghe stands halfway up Monte Sa Corona Arrubia. Its structure cannot be determined: a large quantity of collapse boulders lies in disorder, and dense vegetation prevents an overall view. A few courses with a circular alignment are still visible in their original position, probably belonging to the central tower. Numerous potsherds lie on the surface in the area.

b2fc02b92143f7c7.text: Nuraghe completely dismantled, according to S. Ghiani in La Trexenta Antica.

b31138f4dad3343d.text: The discovery of the Monte Idda hoard (Decimoputzu), which took place towards the end of 1914, was described by Taramelli as “perfectly accidental”, and on this subject the famous archaeologist wrote that “two shepherds from Desulo, who were grazing their herds on the mountain known as Sa Idda, found under some loose granite boulders, inside the remains of a terracotta vessel, a mass of bronze weapons and tools, together with ingots and ingot fragments, slag and scrap pieces of the same metal…”.

b33a3f2f89abfed4.text: The corresponding Nuragic settlement should also be present at the site.

b380a2551a7678eb.text:
The megalithic complex consists of a central body, built of rubble laid in irregular wall courses; vaguely quadrangular in plan, it contains three small circular chambers.
