These rooms, enclosed within the wall face (about 2.10 m high) that defines the central body, quadrangular in plan, have been subjected to conspicuous illicit excavations carried out at an unknown date by looters.

b391a3030a57e989.text: Domus de janas with an architectural façade, interesting graffiti

b39e9eb95a75a722.text: The necropolis of S'Isterridolzu occupies a flat area, crowned to the east by a steep rock face. It contains ten hypogea cut into low limestone outcrops, one in an erratic boulder, and a last, unfinished one on a rocky spur: they appear distributed over a wide area (about 10,000 sq m); the distance between each hypogeum varies from 10 m to about 200 m.

b3c25d057f71bc68.text: Reduced to a great ruin, it still shows some constructional features of that period. The foundation traces and part of the wall fabric are clearly visible. Land-improvement work has contributed greatly to its disappearance by piling up the stones.

b3c5a01a4ea1f821.text: Only the first two basal courses of the monument survive. It may be the Nuradorzu nuraghe.

b3dc6718fb005ebd.text: Single-tower nuraghe covered by sand. Around it, traces of a settlement and a well cut into the rock are clearly visible.

b3e2c959989680e0.text: The nuraghe has almost completely collapsed. The entrance with its lintel remains.

b3ebb824a4a2f647.text: Initially, probable rock shelters became domus de janas as needed, with the addition of the appropriate modifications. Others remain to be recorded. The surrounding area is rich in fossils and limestone formations. Photo Mario Unali

b42104e8706113a4.text: It appears to be a single-tower nuraghe. Survey is difficult because thorny shrubs have colonised the whole structure. Traces of the Nuragic village huts are clearly visible, scattered around the central tower in a limited area, not as incorrectly reported by others.

b44a3a147b8e82dc.text: In the maps of the former Cadastre the nuraghe is called "Mesu 'e Tancas Paulis".

b44bc02630bdbd94.text: This domus de janas is single-chambered with a pseudo-quadrangular room and curvilinear walls. The domus de janas lies against the perimeter wall of the cemetery with its opening facing that wall. The nature of some apparent "reliefs" on the ceiling should be investigated further. A second tomb is present next to it.

b496248a64bfbaa0.text: It lies to the south-east of the village, not far from the Tirso River. Its state of preservation is very poor, being almost completely destroyed, like the Jana nuraghe. However, the extent of the rubble, about 25 x 18 metres (1), suggests a complex of considerable size. Nor can one overlook the fact that the very long fence enclosing the field in which it stands is built entirely from the stones of the nuraghe itself.

b498f505e9b14da3.text: There are four of them (but one is destroyed)

b4cb22658db8ff92.text: A single-tower nuraghe of broad diameter of which only the courses survive up to about 2.50 m in height, with the entrance and lintel.

b4e7e5ebc2f00c1a.text:
This is an archaeological area that cannot be defined because of the collapses and the vegetation. However, the data collected lead me to determine that it is a complex nuraghe, consisting of an ancient tower surrounded by a massive wall (bastion) with a continuous, concave-convex profile that probably encloses a courtyard, and some minor towers.

All around, the remains of walls (outer wall?) built with blocks of considerable size are visible.

b4f865834e3685b4.text: Generic position in the locality of Li Casacci

b4fa73fdb0633674.text:
Complex tholos nuraghe, of the tancato type, with a central tower, a small courtyard and a secondary tower. The complex is built of polygonal blocks of local basalt, but is distinguished by the extremely careful working of the entrance blocks (jambs and lintels).

The central tower has a maximum surviving height of about 4 m, while the added tower has largely collapsed and survives to a maximum height of just over 3 m.

b5002cb8a36c2233.text: The probable Nuragic village, about 200 metres west of the nuraghe, appears to consist of about 10 huts, two rectangular and the rest round. Unfortunately all the structures are in very poor condition and in some cases barely distinguishable. The huts were built of small and medium-sized polyhedral boulders laid dry. Several pottery sherds are present in the area.

b536e9d0e623f4b4.text: More precisely, it is a proto-nuraghe.

b55c7ac33bf53602.text: Usanis, situated on the summit of a rocky spur, was a complex structure formed by two towers.

b561753331cde68c.text:
The monument lies less than 200 metres south-east of the giants' tomb of Santu Bainzu, which must have been the reference funerary area.

It is a single-tower nuraghe at the centre of a large village bounded by an outer wall that can only be traced in part. The tower, circular in plan (13.12 x 2.75 m; diameter at the top of the surviving masonry 11.90 m), with wall thicknesses of 4.30 m to the east and 3.60 m to the north-west, survives to a maximum height of 7.25 m and 12 courses to the south-east.

b57fb9db9546f400.text: Single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan and a surviving wall face reduced to 2–3 courses.

b599844b55326968.text:
A particularly evocative domus de janas necropolis adjoining part of a larger site that includes a nuraghe with a village and a dolmen.

One of the finest domus de janas at Sirilò, until a few years ago it was still entirely underground. From the small entrance you enter the large chamber, inside which there are three more entrances leading to three other chambers.

b5d2555313ccb4cc.text: Few remains of a giants' tomb. The site has been heavily settled since ancient times and is thought to be as rich as the nearby Pisciu Accas. mu

b5e56f79fea033a5.text: The proto-nuraghe Su Cannuju (formerly S'Alzola Trigale) has a quadrangular plan, with a single longitudinal corridor.

b5f2218df15baf31.text: It is almost certainly a single-tower nuraghe standing on a cliff, as if to emphasise its impregnability against a probable enemy attack. About twenty courses of ordered stones are visible in the circles. The inaccessible tholos is probably intact.

b5f2a87a61169839.text:
It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan (diam. 13.30 x 13 m): the wall thickness is about 4 metres, while the surviving height is 1.75 m with three courses.

The entrance, facing south-east, leads into a corridor (length 4 m – width 1.50/1 m) in which the existence of the stair and the opposing guard chamber can be discerned.

Of the circular chamber only the base diameter (5 m) can be measured, while it is not possible to determine whether it was lined with niches.

b5f707ded2265e66.text: A well of probable Nuragic date and probable sacred use, situated 70 m west of the quadrangular tower. The well is built of well-shaped ashlars in limestone and volcanic rock, has the remarkable depth of about 30 m, and has yielded a large quantity of material of Nuragic, Punic and Roman date.

b6009d8cbfd2bc64.text: Near provincial road 25 to Aidomaggiore stands the tancato nuraghe called “Sa Jua”, shown here in the fine photographs of Nicola Castangia. Professor Pittau derives its name from the Latin “iuga”, meaning a herd of cattle. I would point out that in ancient Egypt cattle were also called “iwa” (jua), plainly similar to the term “ju” or “juale” used in Sardinian for the yoke.

b623d284c47f8927.text: The only tomb in the territory of Dolianova attributed to the Bonnanaro culture and dated to 2200–1800 BC. Pottery, two tripods and a cup were found here. The tomb was destroyed during quarry work.

b6875af4e1757122.text: The tomb is hidden by vegetation, blocked by fallen boulders and earth. Despite the collapse, the entrance can be identified and faces east. The exedra and the apse are hard to make out, also because of the violation by looters. For the exedra, the few clues are some semi-worked stones still in their original position at the sides of what remains of the probable entrance. To the rear, boulders arranged in a semicircle formed part of the apse.

b697711008f0584b.text: A domus de janas on the hill facing the Ortali 'e su Monte complex, below a smaller nuragic tower with the same name

b6b1f1f32a82e8a0.text: To reach it, follow the SP 63 from Sindia towards Scano di Montiferro for about 4 km until you see the beautiful single-tower nuraghe Serrese on the right. The dolmen lies 750 metres north of the nuraghe.

b6b2607db4c8eff5.text: Sa Turricula shows the first phase of the Nuragic civilisation. The site comprises the nuraghe, the village, and, a short distance away in the territory of the municipality of Osilo (locality Funtana 'e Casu), a dolmen.

b6bd886326ae10b5.text: The nuraghe itself no longer exists, although a stretch of the perimeter walls can still be seen on the hilltop. The shape of the hill suggests it conceals more than it reveals.

b6e1f369ea042d41.text: Single-chambered domus de janas on a limestone outcrop

b6e9959de4932da6.text: This tomb, cut into trachyte, shows – in the antechamber and the main chamber – a painted ceiling reproducing the roof of a hut according to two different typological schemes. Of particular interest is the “reticulated” motif running along the walls of the main cell.

b73a96cce9b209b8.text:
The monument stands on the summit of a low hillock, in an area currently used as pasture.

Of the simple nuraghe, which rises on a granite outcrop, only the outer wall face is visible, for 1.50 metres.

The chamber plan is sub-circular and rather irregular because a roughly trapezoidal rocky spur, projecting slightly into the chamber, has been incorporated into the wall face.

b73ef0fcbb8604fc.text: In the Nuragic period, during the Final Bronze Age, a small sacred well temple dedicated to the water cult was built. The building follows the ground plan typical of this type of monument elsewhere on the island, consisting therefore of a vestibule, a stairwell, and an underground chamber. The circular chamber, originally roofed with a tholos, and the stairwell, which survives with six steps, have wall faces built of perfectly fitting isodomic sandstone ashlars.

b73fbbe2d6b417bd.text: The structures, most likely to be interpreted as the remains of a single-tower tholos nuraghe, are literally hidden by a thicket of mastic. A few basal courses, made of polygonal blocks of local basalt, can be glimpsed on the south side. The nuraghe is practically destroyed.

b75fb1760cb89a24.text: Single-tower nuraghe. Only the first three or four basal courses, built of polygonal blocks of local basalt, are legible on the side facing west. The structures are covered by dense vegetation and can be seen only from the farm track that runs alongside them.

b790cf1a85079e43.text: The nuraghe is completely invisible, partly because of the vegetation but mainly because its stone components have been dismantled and reused to build dry-stone structures nearby (also abandoned). This also makes it hard to locate.

b7a67eea03190549.text: It is a domus de janas cut into a flat rock outcrop and consists of two roughly circular chambers – on the same axis and opening to the south-east – separated by a partition with a hatch; the walls are carefully finished while the ceiling is slightly hemispherical.

b7a8baf260042eb4.text: The Lu Brandali nuragic complex consists of a nuraghe with an outer wall, a village, a giants' tomb, a series of "tafone" tombs and rock shelters. To reach the Lu Brandali Archaeological Site from the traffic lights on Via Nazionale in Santa Teresa Gallura, turn left towards Capo Testa; after about 700 m the main entrance is on the left.

b7caa24aab685c50.text:
They are in the municipal territory of Busachi (OR).

At least four Domus are visible.

The necropolis should comprise at least eight domus.

b7cc65d96dc11247.text: Baetyl with two concavities almost on the "head". Probably for the insertion of stone horns.

b7d38f312df38140.text:
The collapses affecting the Nuragic monument make it impossible to identify the entrance.

Collapses are also visible in the upper part, preventing any view of the inner chamber.

In this area a few courses of stones can be seen leaning against the bedrock.

On the northern side, next to the central tower and a rock outcrop, there is a structure with an entrance that appears to belong to a courtyard or a Nuragic hut.

b7de56d28c2cd368.text: It is a sarcophagus similar to those of Su Cannau and Sos Terrelas. Ready for a burial, or simply ready to be delivered to the client? Roman period or simply medieval? Or belonging to the Judicate period, part of the personal or family estate of one of the judges or kings of Torres or of Logudoro.

b7e327308f520206.text:
The complex currently consists of 15 domus de janas.

The hypogea, set at a considerable height above the surrounding ground (from a minimum of 0.60 m to a maximum of 4.00 m), were originally reached by footholds cut in the rock; collapses and fractures in the rock face now make access particularly difficult.

b7ef931dfa0bbebb.text: A splendid single-tower nuraghe, partly collapsed. It has an intact tholos and a counter-clockwise staircase.

b7f1c8a020d7e56d.text: It lies near the Nuragic spring of su Musuleu. It appears to be a structure of the Nuragic period.

b80afdadd84c0c8e.text: The Nuraghe Aresti lies on the boundary between the municipal territories of Narbolia and Seneghe, about 1 km north-east of Narbolia, a short distance from the SP 11. It is a complex nuraghe in a fair state of preservation. The central tower is accessible and has a fine entrance with a corbelled corridor and an intact tholos over the inner chamber.

b8189615e83deb90.text:
It consists of a few basal circles that nevertheless define its construction character precisely; this character belongs to a broader human context in the surrounding territory with numerous other features close by. Its function as a lookout, or if you prefer as a defensive post, is paramount.

- Nuraghe del mestolo. In the matter of kitchen utensils it is curious that this nuraghe lies about one kilometre as the crow flies from Nuraghe Cogàlzos (see entry) which means "spoons (of bone)". See Truddàriga.mu

b8202a3e98db4c54.text: De Chirigu Village, the one to the north-west of the nuraghe of the same name, even though immersed in dense vegetation, shows several clearly distinguishable wall stretches belonging to probable huts, mostly rectangular in shape. At the far end, to the north-north-west, there is a circular structure (diameter about 10 m) that probably served as a meeting hut, against whose south side a rectangular structure is abutted. Numerous pottery fragments from various periods are present.

b82058234bfe80e2.text: The tomb is buried in vegetation; to find it you have to follow the dry-stone wall on the west side.

b826d2f5a9e8b964.text: It was a smaller tower (about 8 m in diameter) than the nuraghe de Susu. It probably served as a lookout. It was certainly reused in the Roman period, as shown by the presence of terraces, pit graves and lithic material in the area. After bulldozer work during reforestation, few traces remain.

b84a7e8f942c5906.text:
It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan that reaches 29 m in length including the collapse debris closest to the monument.

Its state of preservation allows the structure to be followed in general around its entire outer perimeter, which was not affected by any refacing of the masonry. It is difficult to identify where the entrance opened, probably to be located in the southern quadrant.

b85b7fd8cefe8b12.text: Ruined, only the first courses are visible. It must have been of considerable size, with a base diameter of about 15 metres.

b87ef8467826af4b.text: Only a few worked ashlars of the monument, now destroyed, are visible; they show that the tomb was of the coursed type in isodomic masonry.

b87fa4e0f4ec2130.text: A burial of the Nuragic period. Of the monument, in poor condition and partly hidden by vegetation, only the funerary corridor, the exedra and numerous shaped ashlars remain, showing that the tomb was of the coursed type in isodomic masonry. The ashlars, very carefully made, include the so-called dentilled stele of considerable size, and an element of uncertain definition on which one face has a framed, raised boss.

b897a50228feb0fd.text: All around the monument the Nuragic village extends over a wide area, with in particular two huts in a good state of preservation. At the south-west edge there is a pond (Paule – from which the site takes its name) which very probably served as a water reservoir.

b8c1cac5d496a796.text: Remains of a nuraghe perhaps never finished

b8cec15197d60037.text: A singular funerary monument, a prehistoric tomb entirely cut into the rock. Discovered not many years ago, archaeologists regard it as a collective burial datable to the end of the Middle Bronze Age and therefore include it among the Nuragic-period giants' tombs. Its structure, however, is completely different from the usual giants' tomb types, both the coursed ones and those with a stele.

b8fa8812ed2f0d80.text: Scant remains of a small nuraghe

b9353b2353f3610b.text: Two other domus de janas are visible nearby

b93fa229a94c87b6.text: It lies about 300 metres below the associated nuraghe. It is built of isodomic ashlar blocks. In the vestibule in front of it there are stone benches, and in front of the entrance a hole cut in the rock acts as an overflow for the threshold level. The spring is still active and functioning. A temporary structure of concrete blocks has been built all around the spring to protect it from the weather, vegetation and animals.

b94e51cc9956ff4e.text: The nuraghe Tutturuddu stands on the first promontory after the nuraghe Nuridda, guarding a path that descends towards the village of Tuili. Only a few traces of this Nuragic monument survive. The name Tutturuddu comes from the Sardinian word tutturu (rolling pin), referring to the shape recognisable in the remains of the ancient structure.

b957464684163884.text: Nuragic settlement with a single-tower nuraghe built of sandy limestone blocks. Middle Bronze Age pottery. The landscape setting of the nuraghe has been radically altered since the site was recorded; nevertheless, traces worthy of protection remain.

b9952e66bd57cb10.text: The domus de janas that make up this necropolis, one of the most extensive and important in Sardinia, are cut into the vertical face and the plateau of a trachyte outcrop — about 10 m high and facing south — and consist of some twenty burials arranged mostly at a certain height above the surrounding ground level.

b99dce64c1e7ee15.text:
Reduced to a state of total ruin, most probably as a result of road excavation and land improvement works. It merges with the one not far away at Pedru Canu.

Nuraghe della smilace (Smilax aspera). This is very probably a Paleo-Sardinian term. It indicates that when the name arose the monument was covered in smilax, a thorny climbing plant.

b9acef5c068dddc1.text: Domus de janas with one chamber, whose ceiling has collapsed.

b9aeceb16c7814fc.text: The Orconale complex has a towered bastion with a courtyard. The main tower has an ogival corridor. All around lie the remains of a large Nuragic settlement with a megaron temple where a model of a nuraghe was found, perhaps belonging to a basin similar to that of Su Monte Sorradile.

b9bc25c9d33a3bd1.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The entrance, opening to the south, is lintelled and gives access to the corridor; to its left opens the stairwell of the helical staircase that led to the upper chamber, which no longer exists. The inner chamber is well preserved except for the top of the false dome, which has collapsed. Two facing niches open inside the chamber, oriented respectively east and west.

b9cd9a454a25f28a.text: It was a large stone cist dug into the ground, oval in shape, with its walls lined with stone slabs; inside were the remains of 15 inhumations and various grave goods typical of the Early Bronze Age (Bonnanaro Culture).

b9e345ce7d81c0fb.text: Built of local granite boulders, it has a roughly triangular plan and shows mixed features of corridor nuraghi (the most archaic type of nuraghe) and tholos nuraghi (an evolution of the former). The central chamber with its tholos roof is still intact, while the side chambers have partially collapsed. The building has two entrances, one to the south-west (the main entrance) and another to the south-east.

ba0596bed0707867.text:
Collective tombs of the Nuragic period, 1600–1800 BC, built in the final phase of the Middle Bronze Age, 1500 BC, and used until the Final Bronze Age phase, 1100–900 BC.

The elongated burial chamber has side walls of limestone blocks laid in corbelled courses, closed at the far end by a slab set on edge. The outer wall face is apsidal at the rear. The entrance, facing east in Tomb no. 1 and south-east in Tomb no. 2, is preceded by a semicircular exedra space.

ba08a618a34f0d16.text: Unfortunately, there is a great deal of damage, most of it unwitting, caused by people trying to reclaim a few square metres of pasture.

ba1064d73c69c007.text: Archaeological area comprising various features including cart ruts; menhir; cupmarks of various kinds

ba121513dfb54522.text: The central tower, almost completely destroyed (maximum surviving height 2.70 metres), is built, like the rest of the visible structures, in polygonal masonry, using exclusively granite blocks. On the south side a trilithic structure survives that could be interpreted as the remains of the entrance to a mural staircase giving access to the tower's terrace or to a possible second chamber.

ba15d29618f3ad6f.text: An allée couverte is also present at Chinzana. It is a tomb consisting of a rectangular corridor with a surviving length of 5.20 m and a width of 0.95 m, formed by slabs set on edge, seven of which are still in situ; the covering slabs have disappeared. Around the tomb, on the NW, W and SW sides, some stones of the peristalith emerge.

ba39eeb662820204.text: Granite nuraghe, of large and medium blocks. It appears to be a tancato nuraghe with two towers, which can be documented: a stretch of the central tower wall on the north side, three courses high, and the interior of the upper part of the secondary tower.

babf7ecc86d213bf.text: Single-tower nuraghe, formerly leaning against a farmhouse. Very close to the paved road.

bad298d783bce6e4.text: Built of granite blocks quarried on the spot, the nuraghe consists of a circular tower about 4.5 m in diameter and an added pseudo-elliptical body (with a major axis of about 12 m and a minor axis of about 8 m). No traces of huts are currently visible, but it is likely that some structures were built against the site's perimeter and that the natural tafoni were exploited for various uses.

bad5820016839520.text: It comprises at least eight domus de janas, of which only three can be traced in plan.

bae16389dbc7aac8.text: Remains of a probable quadrangular fortification built by the Nuragic people. It survives as a large megalithic wall running along the eastern edge of the plateau that forms the mountain summit. The wall is broken by an entrance leading to a corridor parallel to the wall and roofed with basalt slabs laid flat. The place name “Sa Rocca 'e su Para” given to this mountain may refer to the use the Camaldolese friars made of the fortress in the Middle Ages.

baf0cf45ff29ed69.text: Necropolis consisting of three clusters, one tomb of which is decorated inside with a carved spiral

bafe6ef79e8a34ff.text: There are about ten tombs of various forms, from the simplest single-chambered ones with an antechamber and a single cell, to those with a circular plan with several loculi, a hearth, and small pillars separating the cells. They are cut into the soft tuff rock. Threatened by clandestine archaeological excavations,

baff369c9d99db4a.text: Half-ruined. Twelve courses of stones remain, with a breach to the south-east, perhaps the entrance. The prismatic shape of the stones made it easy to fit them together, so they are joined precisely, but they are not laid in horizontal layers. The outer wall is vertical and hard to reach, so it is not easy to get inside.

bb46772a7f080c00.text: It is four-lobed, with a central tower surrounded by a bastion against which the other four towers are built. In places it is quite ruined, yet it still reaches a height of more than ten metres; the ground floor is well preserved, while the upper floor lacks its roof although the masonry survives to a certain height. As often happens in multi-storey towers, the upper floor was characterised by a large window.

bb6b4981a20909cb.text: The necropolis consists of two groups, of 7 and 31 units, of hypogean domus de janas; only one is single-chambered while the others have more complex plans and one of them contains as many as eleven chambers. They are of the "vertical and horizontal projection" type, that is, accessible through a vertical shaft or a descending dromos, almost always provided with steps leading into the vestibule.

bb6cf49935423a21.text:
It is also called Sa Pinnettedda.

The circumstances of the discovery and the finds date the monument to the end of phase II of the Nuragic civilisation (1500–1200 BC).

bba03d5d90e849d5.text: Giants' tomb reported in an article in Gallura Oggi, already included in the Geoportal, next to which a wind turbine has been built.

bbc059560b397eee.text: Single-chamber domus de janas located near the municipal road

bbc4d1b409b31f3a.text: Nuraghe covered with prickly pear plants and disfigured by a building that has sprung up alongside it.

bbcec42aa2c704fc.text: Situated in the hollow of San Simplicio, only a few fallen stones survive on the ground.

bbe01eb28c39fa97.text: The excavation revealed a rectangular building divided into two rooms and set inside an enclosed area. It is thought that the building had a religious function. The excavations yielded finds datable between the 8th and 7th centuries BC. The setting is bleak and typical, with abandoned military structures (built inside the sanctuary), an abandoned restaurant and a large tarmac car park.

bbfcfab4cd667700.text:
The Margone nuraghe stands on the summit of a hill and is largely hidden by dense vegetation, especially prickly pear and wild olive.

Its important function is emphasised by the complexity of the structure: it is a three-lobed nuraghe with a central tower 12 m in diameter. Around it one can trace stretches of polygonal masonry, built of medium-sized limestone blocks, that link three secondary towers to the main tower.

bc0c588d1554968f.text:
The archaeological site stands on a rocky cliff of granitic nature, bounded by three spires lying about 30 and 50 m apart.

The area covers about 2.0 ha; the settlement is hard to read in plan because of the vegetation and its very poor state of preservation.

The site is surrounded by an outer wall that encloses the nuraghe, the two watchtowers and, in the centre, the Nuragic huts, while other huts lie outside the wall on the east side.

bc425ca14ddccfa5.text:
The site where Sa Murta 'e Pizzus stands, at 520 metres above sea level, is beautiful and evocative, set in the greenery and silence of an area little touched by man. Numerous grey-pink granite rocks sculpted by time are present, and the Gulf of the Angels can be seen from the hill.

Near this funerary complex there are some stones marking the circular perimeter of several Nuragic huts,

bc44d6fcf3e3cc38.text: It has a distinctive shape, because part of it merges with a huge boulder that has been partly hollowed out and adapted for funerary use.

bc6e8b697ddd1934.text:
There are nuraghi that are not only grandiose in themselves but also for the landscape in which they stand.

The nuraghe Iscolca is one of these: it dominates the Semestene valley and those of the surrounding villages. Not easily reached, it is accessed after a steep climb through dry, rocky pastures, among protruding stones that hint at the ancient existence of a large village.

Nothing of this monument appears to have been excavated, and only the tholos of the second level is accessible.

bc704cb0d407c6de.text: It is a single-tower nuraghe and is in an advanced state of decay. Some elements of the construction are still visible, however. For the moment it shelters a few domestic animals right on the main entrance. I want to exorcise the situation by thinking of the great people of the nuraghi… "from the stars… to the stables" if institutions and civil conscience linger and persist in abandoning our monuments. mu

bc914836ef57d764.text: Cut into a low trachyte formation, it has a bull's-head protome in the antechamber.

bc9c4009dd4aed35.text: "Domus de gianas of Gianna Oria Porru or Solottos; a short distance from the bed of Rio Mannu or Rio Posada, on the opposite bank from Nuraghe Eritta (no. 5). Two small chambers cut into the limestone, each with a low doorway with a raised border. Empty. In the land of Antioco Sanna" (Taramelli, 1933).

bd31e143145d02c6.text: The nuraghe, next to a farm, has a small added tower.

bd31fe65032d4215.text: Probable Nuragic well in very poor condition and relatively isolated. The perennial spring vein is still active inside it. Reported and photographed by Sergio Melis.

bd3efac46119921e.text: A proto-nuraghe later transformed into a single-tower nuraghe,

bd666f58ec88dfc2.text: Not far from the three domus de janas of the same name: an elongated chamber structure with walls built of courses of medium-sized stones, small ones, and a roof formed by the rock into which it is cut.

bd89cea477199659.text: Nuraghe with a village almost completely covered by earth and vegetation. The most visible part has been destroyed by excavations. Surrounded by greenery and many rivers, other nuraghi are visible from here, including Sa Dom'e S'Orcu.

bd8a26fff2c72351.text: A village composed of several circular huts of which only a few courses and the collapsed structure in the centre remain, plus two of complex structure. Of these two, the first, rectangular, consists of five rooms: four roughly circular ones at the four sides and one rectangular one in the centre, perhaps a courtyard; the second, oval, has four rooms, three of them round and the fourth formed by the wall joining the three rooms, perhaps a courtyard. Enclosures with cyclopean walls are present.

bd8adc19a336be54.text:
The nuraghe is surrounded by a square wall, inside which the circular remains of huts can be seen, perhaps forming a small village.

The upper part of the perimeter of the enclosure wall shows several stretches of a walkway cut into the thickness of the wall.

bd949709db071e94.text: It was marked on the IM map but has now completely disappeared.

bda639a19c1d7913.text: Collapsed nuraghe covered in vegetation. Probable single-tower nuraghe.

bda6be9db0252fb1.text: It is a tower with a circular outer perimeter, a maximum diameter of about 10 m, and an internal chamber that is approximately elliptical, as far as can be judged from its present state of preservation. The whole northern sector is badly damaged, and the east and west sides have been affected by illicit excavations that caused further gaps in the perimeter, later patched by an attempt to “restore” the masonry in the eastern quadrant carried out by the Sisters of the Good Shepherd.

bdb2b91d16001669.text:
It lies to the south, near the boundary with the territory of Usellus.

It is of the simple type and has been heavily disturbed.

bdb701105df8dd5f.text: Single-tower nuraghe in blocks of sandy limestone. Nuragic settlement with finds of Middle Bronze Age pottery. The site is currently neither accessible nor easily understood; a study for its philological reconstruction would be appropriate.

bdc49df8637c89ca.text: The domus has an ESE-facing entrance and a cruciform ground plan. The tomb structure consists of a trapezoidal doorway leading into a sub-rectangular antechamber and then into a rectangular main chamber, on three sides of which are three raised parietal niches. The niches are oriented SSW, NNW and NNE. Originally they were decorated with small pilasters set in the centre of each niche.

bddbcd9c9189ca2d.text: A wall of clearly Nuragic workmanship, of undefinable function. In the centre of the site there is a singular structure consisting of a sort of silo cut into the rock, with straight walls except at the bottom (at 2.65 m) where it narrows; the rim, partially worked and squared on the outside with rebates, has some irregularly shaped cupmarks.

bddf50e93c0348a7.text: Of this monument, reported by Lamarmora and other authors but not by Taramelli, every trace has disappeared. It seems to have been located not far from the railway and to have been destroyed by the very works connected with the building of Borore railway station.

bde94254e20a320e.text: The nuraghe has an irregular elliptical shape; the total circumference is about 50 m. This massive structure is crossed lengthwise by a corridor 15.2 m long, running right through with opposed entrances and lined on both walls by wide openings that lead to large niches — that is, cavities — or to the stairwell that gives access to the upper floor. The straight corridor has a trapezoidal section with a flat ceiling formed by 11 slabs.

bdf51dd330ca05d4.text: Complex nuraghe; it cannot be confidently assigned to any defined type because of its degraded state and the considerable burial of the structures. Nearby are traces of a settlement, a village.

be11dcce95c72723.text: It consists of a façade and a small vestibule. The lintelled opening of the water-collection chamber opens in the façade. The chamber has a semicircular plan and slightly corbelled walls.

be1da0546fea6195.text: In this sacred well, of which nothing more is known and which was probably destroyed, several bronze figurines of considerable importance were found, including the standard above the votive sword and the warrior with shield and four daggers.

be2d63c873279540.text: Nuraghe in good condition, built of reddish granite boulders. It has a spiral staircase. Probable complex nuraghe.

be5f807049fc0485.text: Nuraghe of which very little remains because of building on the immediately adjacent land

be6253725e0803f3.text: In a fairly large area there are numerous sarcophagi obtained from large parallelepiped-shaped blocks of trachyte and basalt of considerable size (2.50 x 0.90 x 0.90). Since they are positioned here and there without any defined or reasonable order, one is led to deduce that this was a place where they were made.

be7ff15717b10bc4.text:
The nuraghe, which stands at an altitude of about 794 m, is of mixed type, meaning it has features of both corridor nuraghi and tholos nuraghi. It consists of a central tower against which a three-lobed bastion is built.

Around the nuraghe there is a village of huts and, a short distance away, two giants' tombs and a dolmen.

be99aebc35660776.text: Single-tower nuraghe built on the crest of a scarp, almost completely collapsed, walls about two metres thick, used in the past as an animal shelter.

be9a5273ef7db97e.text: The menhir, situated inside a flat field, is about 1.67 m high, with cup-mark decorations.

bead79495695649c.text:
It is a large archaic single-tower nuraghe, with some accessory buildings, built of enormous blocks of red basalt.

Because of the collapses it is only possible to enter the interior partially.

bebc3a915037d093.text: The upper part of the structure is visible because it is buried. It consists of a larger tower joined by walls to a smaller tower. The best preserved and most documentable details are on the north side, where two or three courses of the towers and the wall joining them emerge. The stone used is limestone.

bebe5d083b3343c2.text: Later than the neighbouring Monti Pintau II, about seven courses of heavily wedged ashlars survive.

bed31693db829149.text: A nuraghe distinguished by its limestone lintel, white against the dark walls. The tholos has collapsed inwards.

bedbd488d5086143.text: The nuraghe is easy to locate because it lies near the tanks of the drainage plant of the Central Sardinia Reclamation Consortium. Large schist blocks outcrop on the eastern slope of this hill, but a more detailed reading of the site is not possible because its state of preservation is very poor.

beed40f4013e5018.text: This is the nuraghe Monti di Deu, still partly buried, in a good state of preservation; it stands on the summit of Monte di Deu on the Limbara massif, on the Calangianus side.

bf14ec8b16a4a59d.text:
On the site and in the surrounding area there are several alignments formed by large basalt blocks and at least two large clearance cairns resulting from the destruction of structures during agricultural work carried out in the past in the area.

Obsidian flakes and knapping debris outcrop near a path and in the exposed section relating to the left-hand side of the same, to the north of the Temannu nuraghe.

bf4fbccfb84f205f.text: Nuraghe with a system of outer walls around it, visible from the adjacent lane.

bf62c9098b2ea8ad.text: Some roughly squared granite blocks, in two courses, attributable to a Nuragic structure, are present.

bf6cc3755e85b910.text: Nuraxi – Pauli Onigus shows few and uncertain traces of a settlement in its immediate vicinity, while remains of a village can be seen at Pauli Onigus, a locality about 200 m to the south but separated by the course of the Riu Cardaxu. The extent of the villages, based on the materials visible on the surface, almost always varies between 7,000 and 10,000 sq m, apart from the village of Is Arruinalis, with remains mostly of the BFII-FI phase, which covers an area of about 4 hectares.

bf7ef95e7f5fcc3c.text: The Nuraghe Mura Craba lies near a quarry about 2 km east of Bauladu. It is a single-tower nuraghe built of basalt blocks in a fair state of preservation.

bf8e5111a6734ab8.text: The area has been heavily settled since ancient times. The importance of the site stands out from the numerous remains and their particular nature, which find no parallels in other parts of the island. A project focused on the architecture of the giants' tombs is currently being studied by female researchers who will shortly publish a specific book on them.

bf92e484a11b4390.text:
The nuraghe is very ruined.

Nearby lies a pre-Nuragic settlement dating to the Chalcolithic.

bfb710779d21c1e3.text: The Nuragic complex of Tamùli is an important archaeological site dating to the Middle Bronze Age (1500–1200 BC). The site was already well known in the first half of the nineteenth century, thanks largely to the description given by the scholar General Alberto Della Marmora in his Voyage en Sardaigne, published in 1840. In the accompanying atlas he illustrated the nuraghe, two of the three giants' tombs present, the baetyls and several ashlars on the spot with numerous drawings.

bfb96f65a207cb25.text: A natural cave characterised by a large hall used as a sacred area where various votive offerings (lamps and miniature pots) were found on a natural rock altar shaped like a bench. It was frequented from the Neolithic to the Iron Age and includes the San Ciriaco, Bonannaro and Nuragic cultures.

bfbec558c02d98b7.text:
Complex nuraghe. A bastion formed by at least three towers was added to the main tower, but a fourth tower probably existed as well, though it is not visible today because dense scrub covers the whole nuraghe.

The tholos survives intact.

bfca1b6f9b97023c.text: The Tuppedili nuraghe, situated along the road to Mandas, is also of particular archaeological importance. Still awaiting full study, the site has so far yielded a large number of artefacts datable to the Nuragic and Roman periods.

bfdba63136e3370d.text: Partially collapsed single-chambered domus de janas

bfdd7ba25394ac2c.text: Two tombs partially collapsed and eroded beneath a striking natural dolmen

bfe4e1f5f7f2057f.text: A ruined nuraghe near a complex of domus de janas

c042b2c11794450b.text:
Only a few basal courses of the nuraghe remain visible, up to a maximum height of about 2 m, formed by large polygonal basalt blocks laid in a circle.

What survives of the inner chamber is completely blocked by collapse debris and covered by a dense layer of vegetation, with brambles and shrubs. The entrance, no longer visible, faced south.

c0733884b213b71d.text:
It lies in the municipality of Bolotana.

Single-tower nuraghe with a chamber.

The nuraghe is cut by a recent dry-stone wall.

The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

c07a742c970361d0.text: It lies in the municipality of Orani and consists of 8 domus de janas.

c086d5e01785f29d.text:
The building, set in a commanding position at the eastern end of the hill of the same name, is a three-lobed complex nuraghe with a village around it.

Here too there must have been a king who ruled the whole plain.

The finds suggest that the Romans arrived later as well.

c0957a3840de8697.text: A complex cave with three entrances (two of them artificial), heavily disturbed and stripped of its formations because it was partly used in the past as an onyx quarry and as a wartime shelter. It was frequented during the Early Bronze Age. A small park has been laid out at the entrance, managed by an association that periodically organises guided tours.

c09b3c1b05c0cb03.text: It is a single-tower nuraghe, with a stair and a corridor niche, a ground-floor chamber flanked by two subsidiary rooms, and a further room above the corridor. It probably had an added structure (a courtyard?) and an outer wall enclosing various related structures of the adjoining settlement. The nuraghe is easily reached from the road called Valle dei Nuraghi, following an unsurfaced track that lies on private property, so access is not guaranteed.

c0e9f9d5ca9035e2.text: What makes the area of the Nuraghe Su Angiu even more interesting and distinctive are the nearby Punic and Roman villages whose remains are still visible today.

c101770e312e6522.text: It lies in the municipality of Pula (CA) inside the archaeological area of Nora.

c12b9a140cba8c6c.text: A ruined nuraghe near which stands a Nuragic spring, in good condition. It consists of a rectangular lintelled entrance (about 0.95 x 0.90 m) giving access, via a stair of four steps with a tread of 24 cm, to a dromos (length about 1.00 m; width 1.06 m; height 1.82 m).

c14ea2c53f9027de.text: It is also known as Matzone (Maxia records Massone). Su crastu covaccadu probably comes from the presence, not far away, of a giants' tomb that had a trilithon and a cist covered with a flat lintel, hence su crastu covaccadu. It is a single-tower nuraghe and its features cannot be made out because it is completely covered by plants and bushes. However, the Nuragic spring that supplied drinking water (so the owners told me) until a few years ago is noted.mu

c18993cbc9a3c3b5.text: Called the nuraghe Coarittos, but there is no trace of that kind of monument.

c19c6c1da4f53754.text:
It is practically destroyed. The few remains that allow it to be identified consist of two courses of stones, just emerging from the ground, that define the tomb corridor. In the area of the exedra (itself more guessed at than actually present) lies the so-called dentilled ashlar, not in its original position; its presence indicates that the burial was built with squared ashlars laid in courses, like the nearby Sa Presone II.

The monument lies in the municipality of Bultei (SS).

c1a9f1fb0a5a5226.text: Single-tower nuraghe with a giants' tomb nearby

c1d0e04376ca37f0.text: On the summit of the nuraghe ruins, a sentry box for the powder-magazine guards was built after the war. Single-tower, ruined, collapsed and buried.

c1f3da4885e4c01a.text: It is in a very degraded state. Covered in brambles and scrub, it is inaccessible. Built of trachyte. From the outside a small window is visible, high up, facing east. The walls still standing are about four metres high.

c1fbf6b751123a8d.text:
It is a village of considerable size; dozens of circular structures can be made out on the ground, mainly to the south-west of the nuraghe of the same name.

Given the presence of four other nuraghi within a radius of just a few kilometres and an exceptional view over the Gulf of Asinara (on clear days ships off Porto Torres are clearly visible), the village probably played a strategic role.

c23a530dbdefcb8a.text: With the presence of two nuraghi, the remains of a village and a giants' tomb, it forms a significant complex for reconstructing the historical events of the territory. The single-tower Nuraghe Corru 'e Oe stands on a small plateau visually linked with the four-lobed Aidu and with three others that appear to have belonged to a single defensive and territorial surveillance system. Near the nuraghe the remains of a village have been found, consisting of circular huts;

c24fd14c0f4d26e8.text: Cyclopean giants' tomb whose corridor is in good condition, while the exterior appears buried and partly ruined.

c26ce1d43afa2cb5.text: It lies a short distance from Lake Cuga; as the photos show, two or three courses of the foundation stones remain, giving a clear idea of the internal layout of this single-tower nuraghe.

c2789e572285a7a7.text: The monument takes its name from the ancient name of the area where it stands (Nixias) and from the unusual hole on the right of the great stele, which was thought (perhaps wrongly) to have been used in historic times for tethering horses. The monument is of considerable interest because it is a rare example of a giants' tomb with an arched stele in the centre-south of the island.

c29e463b3791083e.text:
The nuraghe is inaccessible because of a high metal fence.

Nearby there is a menhir, also inside the fenced field.

c29e717c57f74c69.text:
A semi-circular exedra oriented to the south-east, bounded by large orthostatic slabs; an elongated body (length 6.15 m – width 3 m at the junction with the exedra – and 2 m in the terminal section) with a burial chamber 4.43 m long and 0.55 m wide.

In the centre of the exedra the lower part of the bilithic arched stele is visible, truly majestic (width 1.10 – thickness 0.22) with a trapezoidal doorway (width 0.24 – height 0.20).

Another arched fragment of the stele lies overturned on the tomb.

c2b13a1ba1170022.text: It is a nuraghe that is particularly dear to me, not least because it was the site of a find of an object that I donated to the Sanna Museum in Sassari, and which has unfortunately disappeared. I have monitored the nuraghe over the years and reported its imminent collapse. I have visited it inside and I believe I am one of the few who know the nature of its masonry.

c2b96c451968dadd.text: Tomb I has an elongated, apsidal tomb body containing a burial chamber and a broad semicircular exedra in front of it. Tomb II, lying to the south-east and buried under collapse and earth, still shows the outline of its apsidal tomb body and exedra. Tomb III, perhaps a dolmenic burial, is in very poor condition.

c2bf05a03a0e7582.text: A pre-Nuragic menhir about 5 metres high, still standing upright. The menhir was named after a giantess who often appears in Sardinian folk legends. The presence of many other menhirs in the area testifies to the widespread diffusion of religious practices linked to megalithism.

c2e335b02b7b45d2.text: Single-tower nuraghe completely collapsed and robbed. A few stones of the outer wall face and the circular base alignment survive; no other elements are visible.

c2e5532a26f68d3d.text: It consists of a central tower and three auxiliary towers linked by stairs and corridors that are now partly impassable. A stair on the right gives access to the ground floor and the upper floor, which now lacks a roof. The ground-floor chamber, of considerable size, is distinguished by three other large niches reaching 4 metres in height.

c2ed22b31cc3f192.text: The probable Nuragic village consists of several structures that were almost certainly reused up to the last century. The huts, whose remains can be glimpsed, were probably originally circular and rectangular in shape. Parts of the walls survive, built of semi-worked stones of varying sizes. The very dense vegetation, which in places has grown inside the structures, has contributed to their collapse. About 200 m to the east lies the Noccus pond.

c3189371f2675a01.text: It consists of four hypogea. Probable location,

c3217b8ab15431f8.text: Dismantled complex nuraghe of which the lower courses remain

c3687b62d49f4f3b.text: The complex corridor nuraghe Sa Conca ‛e sa Cresia originated as a corridor nuraghe in the Middle Bronze Age and was remodelled into a tholos nuraghe in the Recent Bronze Age. The surrounding areas were landscaped in the 1990s. From the tholos one enters corridors dug by tomb robbers that lead inside the tholoi. Outside, to the west and south, two elliptical vaulted structures, now ruined and of uncertain purpose, are reported.

c37b50af9963126b.text: “Su Posidu”, meaning treasure. A very unusual well set between two enormous granite boulders, about 60–80 centimetres apart and 5–6 metres high. A series of schist steps, set between the two rock spurs, deliberately worked and cut, form a double staircase that allowed easy access to the central part of the well, where the precious liquid was found: water, what treasure was as precious to the people of that time as water?

c38e1f17ac2b81b4.text: A large four-lobed complex nuraghe. Never excavated and lying inside a private property, it is therefore inaccessible. It is distinguished by certain particular artefacts inside it, including a menhir.

c3d7d29689185372.text: Single-tower nuraghe of tuff, with an attached megalithic wall surrounding the promontory. Inside a private estate.

c3f49bddc3abf3e4.text:
It lies in the municipality of Muravera, a short distance from the Cuili Piras menhirs and near the boundary with the municipality of Castiadas.

More precisely it is a proto-nuraghe.

Of particular interest is an entrance whose lintel survives well preserved.

c40f2c48f6283743.text: Possible corridor nuraghe, rectangular in plan, with the entrance to the south-east and a spiral staircase on the left leading to the second level, now ruined. Studied by Lamarmora in 1830.

c420ff0b01683318.text: Mixed-type, tancato complex nuraghe, with a central tower and two added towers. The central chamber, slightly elliptical in shape, has two niches and a roof of slabs instead of a tholos, which brings it closer to a proto-nuraghe. Built of granite. The position of the nuraghe is not confirmed; it is not marked on the IGM map.

c422caa459b7ecdd.text:
The complex consists of a nuraghe and a village of huts. The nuraghe comprises a central tower refaced by a bastion with a straight-convex-curvilinear profile that incorporates two minor towers to the ENE and SSE.

The village, dating to the early Iron Age, extends to the NW of the nuraghe. The dwellings, sub-circular and sub-rectangular in shape, are arranged in "blocks" with several rooms that generally connect onto a central courtyard.

c46aea889e9e24d5.text: Almost imperceptible remains of the nuraghe

c47174acb8a32eb0.text: Clandestine excavators have uncovered some courses of the wall of a small ellipsoidal chamber.

c4792e1605fa1159.text: It was a tomb of the "architectural façade" type. The façade is completely ruined and hidden by vegetation. It now lies beneath the overpass of the new Uri–Scala Cavalli road. Source: Wikimapia

c49e5ddcf0d4d103.text: The domus has an ESE-facing entrance and a cruciform ground plan like the previous one, but with a different structure. It has a dromos raised above ground level that leads to a rectangular vestibule giving access to the main chamber. The chamber is rectangular, and on its three sides, oriented SSW, NNW and NNE, there are three parietal niches raised above the floor that originally had a central pilaster.

c49ef908759eb5f1.text: Nuraghe of which only a few courses remain

c4a4e73012ec3d0b.text:
It is a Neolithic burial cut into a schist ridge near a watercourse.

The burial consists of a single cell with a sub-circular plan. Traces of the entrance hatchway can be seen.

To the right on entering there is a small niche/cupboard. There is no chronological evidence, either because no finds were recovered or because the structure was used several times, even in recent times, and has been completely disturbed; indeed it lacks a floor.

c4a818853d20ca5e.text: It is one of the three nuraghi that stand around the perimeter of the artificial lake of the former Madau estate. The basal circle consists of cyclopean boulders that give it an imposing presence, almost as a guardian of the surrounding valley, which is itself heavily settled and rich in other fine remains. Nuraghe della collina dei cervi.mu

c4f3a327a835d6a3.text: Probable three-lobed nuraghe, if not actually four-lobed; the plan is almost impossible to read because of the very poor state of preservation.

c501599a31316fd9.text: The necropolis comprises seven very distinctive and strikingly beautiful domus de janas because they are cut into erratic boulders, and one in particular has natural cup-marks around the doorway.

c513a230cb4525a1.text: Single-tower nuraghe in very poor condition.

c51bfdcb7a8cab48.text: At present an old stone enclosure can be seen on the site, beneath which several boulders belonging to the nuraghe are visible.

c5297c1f4611e70a.text: The nuraghe is a complex type, consisting of a central tower enclosed by a three-lobed bastion. It still dominates the Birori plain, from which there is a breathtaking view, even though its surviving height is now only 5 metres. It was excavated in 1995.

c5332c07e7b49db9.text: This nuraghe is laid out longitudinally and has several cavities (presumably towers..) of small size.. four can be seen from the aerial photo, but there are at least five if not more... it is really interesting and it would be worth clearing the parts still standing, today cluttered with the collapse of the upper parts, to understand better how it was laid out; the towers are small and it is not clear whether they were access ramps for an upper structure or something else.

c53cc9327c752dc0.text: The structures of the nuraghe, of the simple tholos type, are buried under a considerable depth of soil and covered by dense vegetation. Some courses of local basalt blocks emerge partially on the summit of the small rise formed by the structures and the earth covering them.

c54e24aac28814eb.text: The Nuragic structures that closed the two entrances to the Domusnovas cave were already described in 1840 by Angius. He says that at the first entrance, on the left, there are the remains of a cyclopean wall that closed it off. A small doorway by the cave wall is as high as the ordinary stature of a man; to the left of the doorway a staircase 1.30 m wide led up onto the rampart where there were merlons and loopholes. At the exit there is another wall 3.20 m thick.

c55a1c858969da16.text: This is a single-tower nuraghe in a clearly degraded state. Nevertheless, its bulk and the harmony of its construction make it an interesting nuraghe both for its building techniques and its architectural features. It stands on a brown trachyte outcrop, and in places the base boulders merge with the natural rock, giving the structure solidity.

c5624e8719bd9c76.text:
The village of "Cuccuru Ambudu" extended over a broad hilly area (61 m a.s.l.) on the north-eastern outskirts of Serramanna, between the roads leading west to Serrenti and east to Villagreca.

The characteristics of the village, reconstructed through careful analysis of the finds, suggest it was already occupied in the pre-Nuragic period, in a phase datable between the Late Neolithic (Ozieri Culture) and the Chalcolithic (Monte Claro Culture).

c56bd894eeafb915.text: It is a completely ruined nuraghe that survives to a maximum height of 1.90 m.

c57fb86cdd738948.text: Remains of some Nuragic huts near Monte Margherita or Monti Mannu.

c5b86672649447ad.text: Only the base of the tomb can be seen, and what remains is almost entirely covered by vegetation.

c5bdb6bfeff2b695.text:
Situated on the southern bank of the Rio Berchida a short distance from the sea, it appears as a shapeless heap of collapse from which the upper part of the central tower can be glimpsed, and it can be inferred that additional structures were present.

On one side of the structure several courses of blocks roughly hewn from the local granite are visible, and damage caused by clandestine excavation is clearly evident.

c5f1bc81617587a0.text: Nuraghe overlooking the landings and the coast below. The masonry is in good condition. The tholos is open and has probably collapsed.

c600889faaa1001e.text: A burial of the Nuragic period of dolmenic type, built with stone orthostats set vertically and covered with horizontal slabs. The corridor of the tomb is visible, while the elements of the exedra should be incorporated in the dry-stone wall built on the façade. Also on the façade lies the beautiful arched stele, overturned and, unfortunately, fragmented.

c60ca45b26c1de04.text:
A burial of the Nuragic period.

There is hardly any need to describe it, so clearly is it visible in the satellite photograph.

The construction technique is of the coursed type, and the south-west alignment is worth noting, as it is not very common in giants' tombs.

c61c772c2d330d59.text: It is a single-tower nuraghe with a settlement that has now been completely destroyed.

c62f686572eb0cd7.text: The monument, partly hidden by dense vegetation, is of the corridor type with an elliptical plan, built of medium and large granite stones and preserved to a maximum height of 4 m on the north side.

c6470bf261419825.text: Ruined four-lobed nuraghe. The upper and lower chambers are visible through a breach in the upper floor. All around, traces of the village are visible.

c671bee4e1c533b3.text: The Nuraghe Corrulia or Currulia stands near the Flumendosa valley in the municipality of Villasalto. To reach it you cross a small bridge leading to a farmstead beside which the nuraghe stands. It is a single-tower nuraghe, now with its top missing, lying in a state of abandonment.

c6798c6a4cc69bf2.text: The two domus de janas lie in the municipality of Silanus (NU), 40 metres north of the former SS 229, a short distance from the nuraghi Ordari and s'Aspru, which stand on rocky spurs at a higher elevation.

c683581cdb74aafc.text: The site may be an animal pen used in recent centuries; however, an even earlier origin cannot be ruled out.

c686aa9b4e08e739.text: Single-tower nuraghe inside the private grounds of the Terme di Sardara hotel. It is partly buried and its entrance cannot be identified.

c6ca396973f93e2f.text: At ruin level, with disjointed circles of large boulders collapsed in great disorder. Only a very reduced part remains from which the presence of the site can be deduced. mu

c6e98bf7c576ab3b.text: This, so they say, is the area where the Castle of Burgos was initially being built at sa Pattada in Illorai, before that site was abandoned and the castle was definitively erected at Burgos... but I don't think so! ...to me it suggests something more archaic, perhaps Nuragic, ...some kind of ritual area!

c6f0d7521159e6ac.text: "Domus de gianas of Orrilì. On the slopes of Monte Sedda 'e Sos Campos, along the little valley of the Rio Orrilì; it has a single chamber cut into the limestone; elongated; on either side of the doorway there is a kind of niche hollowed in the wall, perhaps a cavity for placing offerings to the deceased. On land belonging to Pietro Farris Zumbosu."

c70bf229fc7b6b23.text:
The monument stands on the summit of a rocky granite spur and commands the whole surrounding area; it is bounded on one side by an outer wall and on the other by the natural rock.

It is not clearly legible, because only a few stones of the first course remain; it suggests a small nuraghe or a Nuragic lookout point.

c7148d484fe328f6.text: A tomb built of roughly worked limestone ashlars. Part of the exedra and the corridor survive. The lintel above the doorway is still in situ.

c7391423ee86e9c1.text: The San Nicola nuraghe is considered the oldest in the whole area, dating to the 16th century BC. The nuraghe awaits study and is still buried up to its summit.

c7464138e9685502.text: The archaeological area includes a complex nuraghe, Nuraghe Appiu, at the foot of Monte Cuccu, facing the sea, three-lobed, collapsed on the outside but with three large rooms still intact inside; a village attached to the nuraghe, of about 200 huts; another nuraghe, single-tower; a giants' tomb and two small dolmens. Nearby there are also a megalithic circle and a "megaron" temple.

c773408d75086f02.text: The temple of Antas is a Punic-Roman temple dedicated to the worship of the eponymous god of the Sardinians, Sardus Pater Babai (Sid Addir for the Carthaginians). It lies about ten kilometres south of the village of Fluminimaggiore, in an area where Carthaginians and Romans settled, attracted by the abundant lead and iron deposits in the territory.

c77742e7f1f71545.text: Single-tower nuraghe now destroyed by agricultural mechanisation

c77fd72ccc329c46.text:
The cave, about 30 metres long, has two entrances oriented north–south.

Inside, traces of wall structures and numerous potsherds are visible. The archaeological deposit shows intensive occupation from the Early Bronze Age.

c783fd315d75f389.text:
It marks the boundary between the municipal territories of Serrenti and Villagreca.

Recorded in the historical cadastral map.

c79fedb171ac777b.text: Three menhirs of decreasing height and size, representing a triad or "a family". The menhirs stand on a stone circle.

c7abce2844bec0bf.text: A few metres from Nuraghe S. Giagu the remains of a nuraghe completely covered by Mediterranean vegetation and brambles can be seen.

c7ce964af1733bc1.text:
Marked by the IGM with the nuraghe symbol, it has now disappeared.

It was probably a hut of the village or a giants' tomb.

c7ced11d6e5b7eda.text: The tomb, of dolmenic type and aligned on a west-east axis, preserves only the burial chamber, part of the exedra with the large arched stele, while the outer profile of the tomb and therefore its thickness cannot be detected. Noted by Lamarmora, who in the Atlas documents the stele already broken, as it appears today.

c7ed4924bc736f7d.text: The necropolis stands in the locality of "sa Serra", in a hilly area overlooking the stretch of the Tirso river near its confluence with the Taloro. The small necropolis consists of seven hypogea of the domus de janas type, cut into the trachyte that outcrops in individual beds or short rocky ridges.

c7f019bc11da8eb2.text: Near the nuraghe, scattered over an extensive area (about 12 hectares), the remains of numerous structures with circular plans (generally over 7 m in diameter) and rectilinear plans can be seen, attributable to the ancient settlement and probably also belonging to a sacred area. The wall profiles are double-faced, built with large and medium-sized blocks of basalt or trachyte. To the south-east, at a distance of about 90 metres from the nuraghe, a plateau stands out

c8011d3e6b758fd5.text: A ruined nuraghe of which three courses and the portal survive

c80631b062f287cd.text: 那些那些那些那些那些

c81b8ce2faad2b04.text: It lies in the municipality of Giave (SS) and comprises 4 domus de janas.

c8256ef4e3184370.text: The complex nuraghe of Santa Barbara lies about three kilometres from the village. Built of basalt, it is a four-lobed type and is surrounded by an extensive village. An excavation campaign carried out in 1986 investigated part of the village, in particular a hut. The hut was circular, built of Sinis sandstone; the floor, however, was of tufa. Near the hut a rectangular basin with two communicating hollows was found.

c855919b78a05078.text: Single-tower nuraghe, of which a few ashlars survive, not easily distinguishable. Nuraghe inhabited up to the Iron Age.

c86a38408d9a52b0.text: The evidence for this period dates no earlier than the Final Neolithic. The very simple domus de janas at Campu Estius should belong to the Ozieri culture. "and the handle of a volcanic rock, the smallest of those from Perda Longa (Lilliu, 1975 p. 3; Lilliu, 2003 pp. 98-99), like a sacred rock, witness to the artificial holes made in it and to the finds of stone rings, of green stone and of discs found whole"

c882c926a14dbbec.text: Almost completely destroyed. The presence of large boulders on the slopes of the small hill indicates the existence of the nuraghe. Dense vegetation covers what remains.

c8894c22e99f7299.text: The necropolis lies about 4 km south-west of Alghero, on the northern side of the road to Olmedo. The site consists of domus de janas cut into the foot of the trachyte plateau dominated by the nuraghe Sant'Elmo, 150 metres away.

c8965aef6536dbd8.text: A small single-tower nuraghe a short distance from the settlement of Siniscola to the north, and presumably belonging to the nearby village of Ghiramonte. The structure is badly damaged by a quarry that extends to its feet. Only a section of the wall face to the south-east is visible; fragments of Nuragic pottery can be seen on the ground nearby.

c8b2351d32b35635.text: The Nuragic site lies in the locality “Su cuccuru de i Zannas”, on the edge of the village. It is a five-lobed nuraghe with an internal courtyard, whose first phase belongs to the Final Bronze Age, overlaid by several phases of reuse ranging from the Late Punic period to the Roman Republican period. A Late Antique – Early Medieval settlement stands against the monument and was occupied at least until the 7th century AD.

c8b6c88638e3d210.text: It has a feature never described before: it is built "in the round": the water collects in an apsidal rear body. "The structure, built in isodomic masonry using basaltic and trachytic ashlars, survives for a substantial portion of its base (Fig. 1), which reveals an oblong ground plan, articulated into a straight entrance forecourt and an apsidal rear body containing the spring-water collection cell."

c8f21021f09190be.text: The tomb, of dolmenic type and now very ruined, preserves only part of the burial corridor and the outer profile, and some orthostats of the exedra, which is completely demolished. Among the stones lying overturned in the exedra area, a large slab stands out for its size: 2.50 m long, 1.25 m wide and 0.80 m thick; it may be part of the arched stele.

c91144ceab1184ec.text: Ruins of a nuraghe on which settlements from the Roman period to the medieval period have been superimposed.

c91a2300694529eb.text: A tafone which, because of its size, was probably used as a rock shelter. Various stones of different sizes, some still in their original position and others at the edges of the tafone, suggest the presence of a wall partially closing the opening. A few small potsherds of indeterminate use are present nearby. The existing vegetation prevents the detection of any further traces.

c9285c960a5723bf.text:
The Domus lies inside a private garden and is cut into a huge oval outcrop of granite, on top of which a small pit has been hollowed out with two channels running from it.

The Domus consists of an antechamber giving access to a large chamber, on the right of which opens the entrance to a further chamber.

c92bc93e64de592e.text:
A multi-lobed nuraghe, largely buried, probably still preserving intact chambers.

At present it is impossible to enter.

c9315dc691716c75.text: Unfortunately only a few boulders remain, but they still show the presence of the monument. Like most sites in our municipality it has been robbed, and it bears witness to the intense human occupation of the area. Part of the surrounding territory is known by the same name as the nuraghe. m.u

c9353d1f1201e52f.text: At certain times of the year it is inaccessible because of the high water level in the reservoir.

c94439858b330d0c.text: Near what remains of this nuraghe there is a Nuragic sacred well that has miraculously survived the surrounding quarrying activity.

c94c380ee928fb9f.text: Cyclopean giants' tomb with a corbelled corridor, of red granite. The corbel slabs are missing. A short distance away some ashlars appear to belong to the apse. The exedra has been destroyed.

c95ba23c0b59ba36.text: The site stands on a gentle hill at the edge of a plateau where sherds of pottery from various periods abound. We are at 194 metres above sea level and seven other nuraghi are visible all around. The structure is undoubtedly complex: the central part, although damaged, preserves an almost intact niche, a room filled with collapse debris, and some wall remains that suggest further rooms and structures around it. The building material is granite.

c986c4ca47cf6ae9.text: Among the many nuraghi in the area, Serrese stands out in particular for having a well-preserved tholos.

c98987e7364b4d34.text: This site, too, loudly proclaims its increasingly incipient state of ruin. Abandonment and neglect make a programme of recovery and consolidation ever more urgent. At the very least a systematic campaign of survey and assessment of the extensive archaeological heritage in the territory of Chiaramonti should be launched.

c9919d3606818410.text: The rock shelter of "Sa Conca Frabica" preserves as many as seven archaeological excavation layers that attest to uninterrupted use from the Middle Neolithic to the Iron Age. The site was used to deposit the dead, alongside whom a funerary assemblage was placed, consisting mainly of ceramic objects but also of bronze and obsidian.

c9cef61ff4fa7fed.text: It lies in the locality of Capichera (Arzachena - OT), near the winery that produces the prized Vermentino. The Nuragic complex of La Prisgiona is in the immediate vicinity.

c9d247eaa5c6d496.text: Nuraghe Senis Mannu is reached from the Church of San Giovanni after about one kilometre of road. This nuraghe, built at an altitude of 302 m above sea level, is a megalithic construction in which a tower erected thousands of years ago by stacking blocks of sedimentary rock stands out. The tholos has collapsed at the centre. From the top of the nuraghe there is a good vantage point: to the south the tabular profile of the Giara and to the north the hill of Santa Vittoria.

ca0c31a7e78adbe4.text: A hut of which only the first course of buried cyclopean ashlars survives. Near the giants' tomb of the same name and a probable village.

ca1560a785587266.text: A small nuraghe overlooking the Giants' Tomb of Coddu Vecchju. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

ca162dedcfe3b0c3.text: Domus de janas reported by a hiker.

ca207dc5c1eb4d98.text: The entrance has collapsed disastrously, blocking access to the domus de janas, which consists of several chambers arranged around a central chamber.

ca3b98bfcc8c6977.text: Four domus de janas, spaced apart

ca3fed5b34b3fd97.text: A smaller circle than the previous one, it is oval in shape and consists of 12 boulders of various sizes, almost all lying flat on the ground. The boulders, covered in moss and lichen, have irregular shapes and clear signs of working.

ca551ef3d788c283.text: Random location. Tomb cited in Annalisa Uccheddu's 1995 degree thesis, UNICA. It lies on land bordering the Villa Siotto Park. The tomb has no covering, is partly buried and free of vegetation. Length about 7 m.

ca6b1cf25de75645.text: On the map supplied by the Forestas agency it appears as such, and bears the identical toponym of the nuraghe that lies a few kilometres to the north-east.

ca7d0d5fe516873c.text: Only a few courses of the nuraghe remain, barely visible from the sanctuary area below. The nuraghe stands on a limestone spur that commands the surrounding valleys.

ca933602437fbe4f.text: The tombs of the archaeological complex lie on the south slope of the hill from its base almost to the summit, where the ruined remains of a single-tower nuraghe are found instead. Unrecorded nuraghe. A wall with a portal of apparent Nuragic date reported to the NurNet editorial team by Mauro Tavella.

ca95162e57f848c6.text: Two single-tower nuraghi a short distance apart. The second is about 70 m to the north-east.

cadc36ad6b246959.text: The Preizza necropolis consists of three small domus de janas cut into the base of modest rocky outcrops.

caf01dcf3cdd21a8.text: It is a single-tower nuraghe standing on a rocky rise. From the outside it looks in fair condition at first glance, but inside there is only a heap of rubble; the roof and part of the upper masonry are missing, so the inner chamber is filled with fallen material and cannot be examined in detail.

caf0d45bff91195d.text: It is completely covered by dense vegetation that prevents access. It is a four-lobed nuraghe built of basalt blocks.

caf9d4d320f60c45.text:
The nuraghe lies less than 100 metres north-east of Nuraghe Ordari.

The monument is not clearly legible.

The masonry survives on the west side for 3.20 m with four courses of large basalt stones, only roughly dressed and laid in irregular rows.

A better-finished stone, rectangular in shape and measuring 1.90 m long, 0.78 m wide and 0.56 m thick, appears to be the lintel of the entrance, which can no longer be identified in any way.

cb0a9c78b1cae577.text: The site includes the remains of a Carthaginian necropolis (about 120 tombs) built by the inhabitants of the Punic settlement that stood near the hill of Santu Teru, founded at the end of the 6th century BC.

cb11b560acf36ce3.text: The monument, although very well preserved, is hard to read in plan because of the dense vegetation that also makes it difficult to locate. Two towers, an internal courtyard and parts of the connecting walls between the structures can be recognised. The central body, which survives to a height of 10 courses of medium and large blocks of volcanic stone in polygonal masonry. It is characterised by steeply sloping walls and an elliptical plan.

cb23e3dce9b69f33.text: In a SSE direction from the Chentugheddas nuraghe, at a distance of more than 200 m from it, portions of the foundations of several circular-plan huts survive, forming a settlement whose occupied area cannot be estimated. On the surface, near the huts, a good quantity of Nuragic pottery is visible.

cb319781875ad46b.text: A burial of the Nuragic period of the so-called isodomic type. Of the tomb, practically destroyed, only the outer wall face and the terminal stone of the corridor are visible. A few other squared and well-finished elements on the exposed parts lie nearby.

cb40bb8fae8ab064.text: It is a small necropolis composed of 5 domus de janas, one of which is only roughly sketched out and barely visible because it is hidden by vegetation.

cb4762b0c2a954e9.text: Complex nuraghe with a central single-tower nuraghe and a quadrangular perimeter wall with four towers.

cb48819c495d886f.text: The name is the one given in: Archaeological Maps of Sardinia by Antonio Taramelli.

cb4898ad9962acc1.text: From the remains of this Nuragic structure that emerge beside the church of Madonna della Pace, I am convinced that this is the Nuraghe of Moddorocco, or else there were two nuraghi.

cb49b4f3995f1ec4.text: On the Punta Sas Baddes plateau lies the Funtana 'e Furru domus de janas, the only one with a shaft entrance, of the single-chamber type with a “forno”-shaped chamber.

cb4b6b4df67b9641.text: Single-tower nuraghe with a staircase, a corridor niche, and a chamber with three niches arranged in a cross. The tower, circular in plan, survives to a maximum height of 12.25 m over 21 courses, while on the south-east side it reaches 11 m with 19 courses. At the top the diameter is 10 metres. The masonry consists of well-worked basalt blocks laid in regular horizontal courses.

cb4ff3d14a04d51b.text: The area where the nuraghe is thought to have stood has been completely altered, I would say devastated, during the Second World War, when the probable structures belonging to the monument and to the village of the same name were dismantled and adapted for a military position.

cb7fea576cda53e1.text: Structures belonging to a simple single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The remains of the nuraghe are very scanty and lie among several contemporary structures. It must have been a small nuraghe; a few basal courses can be seen, overlain by a mass of displaced blocks, to a maximum surviving height of 1.50 m. The chamber has collapsed completely. The entrance cannot be identified.

cb81cd907801c743.text: One may suppose that the natural terrace was provided with some raised chambers that supplemented the natural cavities and were later demolished. The nuraghe stands out against the present-day village of Morgongiori, guarding the valley. For this reason it can reasonably be assigned the function of controlling the territory and maintaining visual contact with the lava bastion of Funducarongiu behind it, in which the cave of Scaba 'e Cresia, the subject of this study, opens.

cb97a2fe8f013980.text: Something cyclopean stands before something wonderful. The site is known as a nuraghe but it does not have all the features of the structure that would allow the monument to be identified with certainty. It could be a ceremonial circle. The boulders are about 5.00 m x 0.90 x 0.90. Unable to achieve the proper connecting curvature between one boulder and the next, they have been regularly chamfered. I believe I have located the quarry not far from the site. mu

cba94c985672aa86.text: About 350 m from the menhir Sa Perda de s'Omini there is a tomb circle about 150 cm in diameter, formed by boulders of various shapes and sizes arranged in a circle, and by three trachyte slabs set into the ground, one of them, the tallest, with a triangular tip. To the south of this slab the circle breaks off abruptly and resumes after about 50 cm, a gap that was very probably occupied originally by the two trachyte slabs that lie there recumbent.

cbca0a7f348a0da2.text:
On the northern outskirts of Selargius, in the locality of Su Coddu, lies an important Neolithic settlement where the remains of over 150 huts and artefacts belonging to the village have been found; it appears to have extended over 10 hectares.

These are traces of a Neolithic settlement (3000 BC), consisting of about thirty archaeological deposits belonging to the Ozieri/Monte Claro Culture.

cbe6b37de3521a3b.text: The spring lies inside the archaeological area of S'Orgioloniga, where the remains of a Nuragic settlement are also found.

cc0b8559b1520187.text: South-south-east of the nuraghe of the same name lies the village, where enclosures and walls can be seen. In some cases the surviving wall structure is rectangular; in others, barely outlined, it appears circular. It should be noted that almost all the structures are overgrown with a thicket of wild olives.

cc17ab7e1cfe09ed.text: Single-tower nuraghe of white limestone inside an olive grove; the property fence runs tangent to the structure. Three courses survive on the east and west sides. Covered in vegetation, a tree growing in the centre of the nuraghe threatens its stability.

cc2b7a5798b52465.text: Necropolis consisting of 25 tombs cut into the granite. No carved wall decorations are recorded.

cc53ca085147432c.text: Conca e Bentu (Porta del vento). Single-tower nuraghe built with cyclopean technique; it has a central chamber with three niches arranged in a cross, only the right-hand and left-hand ones being visible, the central one having collapsed.
