The chamber is reached from a lintelled corridor with a flat roof, which has a storage cell on the right and the start of the staircase that led to the upper floor or the terrace on the left.

cc6eb4a4f84ae0cc.text: Apparent, but unlikely single-tower nuraghe, with some signs of other structures in the surroundings.

ccae2a64b598b1b8.text: Nuraghe in a very poor state of preservation

ccb1b4b2896dc729.text: Nuraghe now completely vanished but studied by Silvestro Ghiani in the 1940s. S. Ghiani in “La Trexenta Antica.”

ccbd2dd4c4dd67ce.text: Complex nuraghe with a central tower and an added tower linked by a wall. The central chamber is flanked by two niches. Around the nuraghe are traces of a settlement. Archaeological excavations have been carried out. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

ccc1fa4d5f134fa0.text: Indeterminate nuraghe; only a few courses survive, immersed in lush vegetation that makes the layout of the structures hard to read. Several wall stretches, probably belonging to huts, are present in the area. Various pottery fragments are also found in the vicinity.

cccc7201b63d481b.text: Domus de janas with clear signs of its reuse in the 20th century.

cce92d35ce56fd19.text: Built of polygonal blocks of local basalt, it survives only in a few courses, to a maximum height of just under 2 m. The trapezoidal entrance, fitted with a monolithic lintel and oriented to the south, can be seen. The nuraghe stands near the crossing of the Rio Strampadorzu, where the stream forms a small waterfall.

ccfc7162a1752141.text: Complex nuraghe, probably tancato, with traces of walls around it

cd0270a68b9f2247.text: Megalithic circle composed of 16–18 large boulders standing upright on a natural rock base. Five of them lie fallen along the perimeter; three lie fallen inside it. The boulders, covered in mosses and lichens, have irregular shapes and clear signs of working.

cd09a841c84a7f27.text:
Three-lobed nuraghe.

Nearby there are also two giants' tombs and a Nuragic sacred well.

cd615b2ec06c6303.text: A complex nuraghe of which only a few courses remain, ruined and overgrown with vegetation.

cd713c8d6f352e29.text: Ruina Tassa is a single-tower nuraghe. Like Luas and Friorosu, it stands on a limestone base. The whole area shows an unusual abundance of squared stones, used in enclosures, suggesting the existence in ancient times of a village of considerable size.

cd948a0f62a2ee60.text: We are faced once again with an immense loss inflicted on the community and on history, perhaps to gain a few square metres of arable or pasture land. The monument has been reduced to a ruin and few of the building's features can be made out.

cdb0785c4ef3c26e.text: A ruined nuraghe of which a few buried courses survive, enveloped in vegetation.

cdcbb2ae5df63cce.text: It is a nuraghe with a regular lintel and a relieving window. In the corridor, 4 m long and 1.2 m wide, the stair is on the left while the guard cell is missing. The eccentric chamber, 4 m in diameter, is enhanced by two equidistant niches, narrow and deep… The nuraghe is surrounded by a double concentric wall of two faces, 3 m thick in total. On one side the wall breaks off; on the other it is 5 m high and has a small tower 6 m in diameter with a flat-lintelled entrance facing south-east.

cdf70cc9d58f9b5b.text: Single-tower nuraghe, completely ruined; the opening of an intra-mural staircase that led to the lower floor can still be seen, now filled with collapse debris. A breach in the wall towards the outside, to the east, is also visible, where a large window may have opened.

ce128ebb8d6a5c2b.text: It appears to be a single-tower nuraghe in good condition with its interior still intact. Traces of a settlement are visible around it.

ce1c2340a337e067.text: Five courses survive; their irregularity suggests a proto-nuraghe.

ce1ca98d47763810.text: It is in fair condition and can be visited, although the upper level cannot be reached because the stairs have collapsed.

ce23959fc9de4438.text: Bilobate nuraghe, with a tower added at the side.

ce271e155369e8cc.text: Megalithic tomb. This is a giants' tomb with a dolmenic covering.

ce2ade1c4d3c9efc.text: Single-tower cylindrical nuraghe; no niches or stairs are present.

ce385d8f50c7ee8a.text:
The site includes a corridor nuraghe, a circular tower nuraghe with a tholos, two giants' tombs, a sacred well, a Roman necropolis and the ruins of a country church.

The country church preserves only a wall of two square metres. The circular nuraghe and everything else listed above are practically invisible. The corridor nuraghe is entirely covered by dense vegetation, so only a few stones can be seen. Unfortunately, as of April 2013, a visit is not recommended.

ce3decf766c547ce.text:
A. Sanguinetti, who around 1970 described an elliptical-plan tower with a rather irregular outer circuit and wide gaps, especially to the south-south-west, where he hypothesised an entrance opening.

The maximum diameter of the monument has been calculated at about 11.10 m, while no observation on the construction technique employed is possible because no wall faces still in place can be distinguished.

ce4d40b2b644e07b.text: It is an archaic construction of presumably oblong shape extending on a north–south axis for a presumed length of 20 m and a width of 13.40 m. The building is erected entirely on the pre-existing bedrock with a steep slope towards the north. The south façade consists of two courses of large, rough granitic-marl blocks without any dressing, of uneven size and superimposed with an irregular archaic technique without any alignment on horizontal planes...

ce4e8b116affe49a.text: Excavations carried out in 1997 brought to light several huts of various plans bounded by orthostatic slabs and with their associated hearths. The archaeological layers yielded abundant ceramic remains, some metal objects and bone artefacts, now kept in the Teti Archaeological Museum. The site is dated from the Middle Bronze Age III to the early Iron Age.

ce7d5c41f329a08e.text: Single-tower nuraghe of large trachyte and limestone blocks; the monument retains its intact tholos. Inside are three niches arranged in a cross; the tholos is about 5 metres high. Beside the nuraghe the Nuragic well is still present and is still used today by the landowners.

ce8e4a3b6ac7ce2a.text: The ground floor should have its tholos intact.

ceb40c0295aa1c93.text: The nuraghe S'Aspru, one of the largest in the Goceano, is in poor condition and partly unstable. It is a complex nuraghe whose central tower stands in the middle of a rectangular courtyard and is enclosed within a circular bastion to which three further towers were later added; these towers are not accessible. Inside the central tower there are three niches and a corridor leading to the staircase that goes up to the upper floor, where a second chamber with a tholos roof is found.

cebf6ba456488099.text: It lies within the municipal territory of Uras; the construction technique used suggests the monument was probably built in the Nuragic period.

ceccc4cde1b4b80d.text: Today at least 12 sites with evidence of the Final Bronze Age II – Early Iron Age (S'Urbale and Genna Maria facies) are counted in the territory of Serrenti... All except one are settlements that were already active from the Recent Bronze Age. Only at Is Arruinalis, Monti Angurdu and Monti Crastu do we also find evidence of the Orientalising and Archaic phases (7th–6th centuries BC).

cee02f6cb60aa0c7.text: The nuraghe is completely ruined and overgrown with shrubs. Like the very nearby Zianeddu (B) it is classed as a “tancato” nuraghe: on the front of the main tower a wall mass encloses a smaller tower and a courtyard set between the two towers.

cf1bb874398b607a.text: A Nuragic dolmenic burial of which the tomb corridor survives, formed by well-finished basalt slabs, without a stele.

cf1c2743e056d511.text: The tomb has the usual architectural layout: an elongated apsidal body (length 14.50 m – width 4/4.30 m), a broad sickle-shaped exedra (current chord 11.70 m – depth 3.25 m) and a rectangular corridor (11.55 m long – average width 1.10 m and 0.55 m at the entrance). In the summer of 1982 the monument was excavated and partially restored.

cf4a9722a92fb246.text: Complex nuraghe with a village, very close to the better-known Nuraghe Majore. A turreted bastion (two towers) with a transverse-frontal layout and an intermediate courtyard was built against the central tower, which still has an intact tholos chamber. A third tower, set back from the two frontal ones, with an entrance corridor and an intact tholos, can also be clearly identified.

cf63e4ed23b70b5a.text: The structure in basalt blocks is ruined and collapsed. The remains are spread over a wide area covered with vegetation.

cfa5309d2c50a322.text:
It consists of a temple, an almost completely collapsed nuraghe, a large circular hut, and a series of "tafone" tombs.

The small temple of Malchittu is certainly the most interesting building in the complex, both for its excellent state of preservation and for the singularity of its construction, comparable to only a few others in Sardinia.

cfc98a6e7ec2849f.text: A sacred spring that shows features of both a spring and a Nuragic sacred well. The presence of an ashlar with a boss on the inside is noteworthy.

cfd265edc13786ff.text: Single-tower nuraghe, difficult to reach because of the vegetation.

d00c0b43df45ca62.text: The Cuili Piras site behind M. Su Crobu. The surrounding land is ploughed and reaching the place is rather difficult. Unfortunately, not long ago the area was devastated by an extensive fire. It lies inside a private property and it is best to inform the landowners of your presence.

d00de3c44f5f0aef.text:
The ground plan of the whole structure must have been rather irregular and adapted to the natural lie of the rock, which was incorporated for long stretches into the building.

The surviving structure extends along a north–south axis 7.35 m long and an east–west axis 7.80 m long, and retains an elevation reaching up to 1.90 m above ground level.

d014e7e036177489.text: In the middle of the woods, cut into the trachyte and decorated on the doorway with probable bull's-head protomes

d038a9623b75689e.text: It takes its name from an old church. It stands on a small promontory on the right bank of the Riu Mannu. The lintel is broken and the whole monument is in a state of complete decay and abandonment. There were two entrances (one has collapsed) and several sacrificial stones. The peculiarity of this nuraghe is that the tholos, perfectly intact, was built with dark boulders formed from agglomerations of fossil shells. A rarity, since no trace of this type of material is found in the area.

d06d0d919d769554.text: Spring, most likely of Nuragic origin.

d07db71fc442d1a9.text: In total ruin a few boulders forming the basal circle of white friable limestone can still be made out.

d0a51466f8a130d8.text: Nuraghe completely destroyed by quarrying activities

d0a9e6ec62a24b25.text:
The monument displays a ground plan and architecture among the most extraordinary produced by the Nuragic culture. It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997.

The complex shows various construction phases characterised by the use of local stone: the basalt of the Giara, which largely predominates, and calcareous marl.

d0b37496ca6c666c.text: Complex nuraghe with village. Ruinous and hard to read because it is covered by collapsed masonry. It occupies an area used for agriculture and pastoralism. Built of granite blocks, its central tower and two lateral towers are visible.

d0b4f39f1bfd9135.text: Bilobed frontal-addition nuraghe. Today it lies completely submerged beneath the waters of the Cuga reservoir. It belongs to the complex of nuraghi surrounding the Chessedu Cuga valley.

d0cbdc15b4bafeb7.text: The S'Ulumu spring (Dorgali) has a circular cell with a short external vestibule, built in horizontal courses and covered by a tholos. Precisely because of its simple architectural and structural appearance, it had an essentially functional character as a water supply for the nearby village.

d0d0f0dab2a01bcc.text: Single-tower nuraghe reduced to a ruin. A single stretch of circular wall survives, 4 metres high, with seven courses. The monument is almost completely destroyed and its materials have been reused to build enclosures and livestock shelters in recent times.

d0d2028b5a9f170e.text: Cut into a basalt wall, the tomb has its entrance facing west, 0.80 m below ground level; it is rectangular and well carved, set within a deep recess. The threshold has a drainage channel, and along the wall thickness, beside the jamb, there are two opposite recesses, perhaps to allow the closing slab to slide more easily. The chamber, irregularly semi-circular in plan, has a flat floor and a domed roof with curved walls.

d0d95ce95940ba14.text:
The complex consists of a nuraghe, an outer wall and a village.

The nuraghe comprises a central tower to which at least two lateral towers were added, now not fully detectable.

A large outer wall, incorporating at least four towers, with an irregular curvilinear course, surrounds the complex.

In the area in front, the remains of numerous huts and rectangular apsidal dwellings leaning against the inner profile of the outer wall.

d126d80bff729439.text: It is a single-tower nuraghe with a curtain wall, partly overgrown with vegetation around almost the entire perimeter; nevertheless, through the doorway facing south-east one can enter the tholos, which is open at the top. Inside there are two large niches and another doorway to the north-west, half buried in soil.

d15d95abbe573b2c.text:
Nuraghe with an associated village of huts.

The tholos is still intact.

d167da265c54e0bf.text: Structure covered by vegetation that is not easy to define

d16eba07d6122e10.text: Sacred area of probable Nuragic origin, reused in Punic and Roman times, where building materials and ceramics abound.

d18a0ba3c1bac185.text: They are cut into a rock formed almost entirely of white quartz pebbles. The origin of these pebbles can be traced to a fluvial-deltaic environment dating back about 166 million years.

d1ac4961f56dc8bc.text: The name of the nuraghe almost certainly comes from the place name. It is a very unusual nuraghe for its construction technique. Unfortunately it has suffered a conspicuous collapse on the west side that limits the survey. Nuraghe of the elongated height of Pantaleo or "of Pantaleo Serra", proper name. It is the first of three nuraghi that stand on the edge of an elongated height. See Sèrra Pantalèo. mu

d1bb4933fbe44235.text: Inside a private property. There are decorations in the form of probable bull's-head protomes.

d1bbab6f1d0b8fb7.text: Deruta giants' tomb. It lies in the immediate vicinity, 50 m, of another giants' tomb in better condition on which the Municipality has carried out minor cleaning and accessibility works.

d223f1efbb9e6369.text: It lies in the territory of the municipality of Urzulei at an altitude of 1030 metres. It was a complex nuraghe of which only a few ruins remain. Important giants' tombs are also found nearby.

d231605b45cbe6aa.text: The construction is unique in that it also embodies elements typical of the hypogean sphere. It is a domus de janas reused in the Nuragic period, when the stele and the corridor were built. It represents a distinctive architectural-façade tomb.

d2405514fd95f4f2.text: Domus de janas located near the provincial road. Excavated in limestone, it features distinctive bull's-head protomes in high relief.

d24912a112b0009c.text: To the north-east of the nuraghe a well is visible, its masonry built of polyhedral boulders of various shapes and sizes. The wall face of the north side is hidden by vegetation and at first glance appears to have collapsed. Around the well lie many boulders that probably belonged to the original structure.

d25a2ac77eab8454.text: Little of this nuraghe remains: the first two courses of the foundation on the north side, and the upper part of the basalt ashlars in curvilinear courses at the other cardinal points. Clearly the nuraghe is not to blame. Whatever can be documented is documented.

d2699deaf78d5358.text:
The monument, four-lobed and sub-rectangular in plan, has a central tower of trachyte with a circular plan about 10 m in diameter, and lateral towers linked by a curtain wall built in polygonal technique with roughly dressed boulders.

Near the south-east and north-west sides the remains of several structures with circular-plan rooms are visible.

d26ef3e28caad021.text: Tomb circle built of polyhedral boulders of various sizes. The structure is circular, formed by superimposing one or two rows of polyhedral boulders. The upper part consists of 13 boulders arranged in a circle (diameter about 150 cm), of which: the tallest, placed to the east in the circle, is triangular and stands out from the others; to the south and north of it are two boulders set on edge with their dressed faces visible; seven boulders of various shapes and sizes follow, completing the circle.

d27dfb8bfb7e9436.text: A giants' tomb completely immersed in the scrub, apparently never excavated and totally ruined. A few isodomic ashlars of the inner wall of the corridor...

d290ef47c5cd52f9.text: Complex nuraghe consisting of a central tower and four lateral towers enclosed within a large outer wall provided with ten towers, for a total of at least 15 towers. Seven of the outer wall's towers are visible, while the others lie buried under the mantle of earth. In the excavations of recent years the structures belonging to the complex nuraghe have been brought to light, of which two of the lateral towers are discernible.

d294397cc1203caf.text: Beyond the two monumental giants' tombs, unique and clearly visible and of exceptional workmanship, three other tombs have been identified. For anyone familiar with Nuragic buildings and settlement patterns this means the existence of a community of several hundred people that had needed to multiply its necropolises.

d2cc1e15be850e82.text: Ruined nuraghe submerged by the floral scrub

d2e0703e30c2504e.text: In a total state of ruin, the few remains are incorporated into a wall of the perimeter tancato. Only the historical memory of the owners of the adjacent properties recalls its existence. A few medium and large boulders are modestly visible.mu

d30188f3d4be921b.text: Traces of the Nuragic village are also present.

d31d575fe6b32b93.text: The nuraghe has a characteristic elongated elliptical plan corresponding to the corridor nuraghe type, and its structure is founded on the natural rock to which it partly conforms. In places the outer perimeter survives up to six courses high, so that one can see how the projection of the basal blocks decreases gradually from bottom to top.

d31e5459f60d464f.text: Dolmen near the nuraghe of the same name

d33cb2224d40573e.text:
Hidden by dense vegetation, we find the nuraghe Arigau. Completely covered in earth and vegetation, with only a few courses of the base visible.

The nuraghe lies at Santa Maria Acquas, on a hill behind the amphitheatre. Apparently a single-tower nuraghe. Never studied and completely covered in earth and vegetation.

d356e70470838dd8.text: Indeterminate nuraghe, set on the summit of a ridge between two valleys, now reduced to a heap of large ashlars.

d3588920de425e06.text: It consists of two large outcrops of rock near the SS 131 state road. The smaller of the boulders that make up Perda Longa is thought to have been used as a "sacred stone" in the Ozieri culture period, as shown by the cupmarks carved in it and the remains of obsidian tools and pottery found around it. From: Biddas e nuraxis de su sattu de Serrenti de su Brunzu de mesu a su Ferru I, by Daniele Carta

d35b8a3090d6e9bc.text: Village, giants' tomb, menhir and nuraghe remains in the middle of the farm

d3624615b25efd94.text: The ashlars making up the tomb, largely buried, are of various types: limestone, basalt and even granite can be seen. A hole lets us see several metres of the side walls and a couple of limestone roofing slabs placed to the west. The right-hand side of the exedra is visible, though not clearly because it is buried; I have tried to document it as fully as possible. To the east, beyond a few trees, stands one of the stelae that were placed at the entrance of giants' tombs, at the centre of the exedra.

d37b30cf350ee58e.text: Ruined, in poor condition, covered by vegetation and partly buried, it remains interesting for its position right against the coastal cliff. Some internal chambers are visible but cannot be entered. It is certainly a single-tower nuraghe.

d37e5d122c892cd2.text: The giants' tomb lies to the south-west of the nuraghe of the same name, of which only the tomb corridor survives.

d39c9d90e3759d9f.text: Worked rock with cupmarks on its upper surface. Probable prehistoric altar.

d3c4686ddf58c743.text: The nuraghe stands about 400 metres north-west of Nuraghe Biriola, while 350 metres to the east there is a Roman cemetery, attested by about ten cinerary urns of different shapes cut into the outcropping rock. It is a single-tower nuraghe with a niche, a corridor staircase and a central chamber flanked by two niches. The tower, circular in plan, has its top missing at a maximum height of 5.80 m with 11 courses, while a large collapse has affected the perimeter wall facing north-north-west.

d3fc9c67803464ab.text: The Santu Pedru necropolis is a pre-Nuragic archaeological site. The necropolis lies on the east slope of the trachyte hill of Santu Pedru, in a position commanding a broad view over the valley below, in the Nurra, a region of north-western Sardinia. The complex comprises about ten tombs with an entrance corridor ("dromos") and a multi-cellular ground plan.

d447ef1ba10da881.text: The complex, datable between 1600 and 900 BC, comprises a sacred well set inside an irregular courtyard, a 'megaron' temple surrounded by an elliptical enclosure, and a large circular hut with an entrance room and an inner chamber. This was a 'communal' building, the so-called 'meeting hut' typical of Nuragic villages. Pilgrims would usually stop here, perhaps for an audience with the priests.

d44c89995fb47082.text: Remains of the nuraghe and of the Nuragic and Eneolithic village.

d44e64ae9ac52f53.text: A three-lobed nuraghe that serves as the foundations for the church of San Saturnino.

d45014c26dd87254.text: The nuraghe is a single-tower type, with a curtain wall about 80 cm thick; it rises from the surrounding vegetation to a height of 4 metres. Its position is strategic, lying halfway between the Fenu nuraghe and the nearby spa area where three other nuraghi stand, one of them part of the same spa complex. It is the best-preserved nuraghe in the municipal territory of Sardara. The size of the lintel is striking

d468bac559ef6946.text: Inside a thicket of mastic, a sarcophagus (2.00 x 0.90 x 0.90 m), probably ready to be transported to the client, has been obtained from a monolith of brown trachyte of considerable size. mu

d47023be9471a3dc.text:
The necropolis comprises 11 domus de janas, generally multi-chambered, some of which are characterised by architectural decorations in relief.

The most interesting burial consists of 11 chambers arranged in an irregular layout.

d4b873756cab557f.text:
A tancato-type nuraghe, it consists of two towers linked by an internal courtyard entered through the entrance.

The oldest part of the nuraghe is the tower on the right as you enter, while the tower on the left and the connecting walls were added later.

d4bb156f199e508c.text:
A small necropolis with intercommunicating chambers and traces of red ochre still visible.

They lie on the SP 15 towards Sorradile, clearly visible at the junction leading to the lake.

The doorway is very well carved; the collapse of the antechamber is obvious, and there were certainly other chambers, since clear traces are visible in the ground in front.

d4bc681752dda768.text: It has now been largely reburied before carrying out work to safeguard it.

d4f08b93c9f1622b.text: Simple single-tower nuraghe, in very poor condition, with traces of a possible settlement around it.

d508e128e5dd10ba.text:
Hidden among the vegetation, very little of the tomb remains.

It is of the coursed type and the walls of the burial chamber were built with isodomic masonry; the monument, oriented to the south-east, has a total length, measured as far as the chord of the exedra, of 7.60 m, and a maximum width of 3.15 m. One arm of the tomb and the exedra are partially visible.

d5208b22e176bc01.text: Single-tower nuraghe in blocks of granite with, in situ, finely worked trachyte ashlars used for decorative effect.

d52295a01151f694.text: In a poor state of preservation, the corridor and various squared boulders that originally must have formed the entrance can be recognised.

d52332ff1575d804.text: Neolithic rock-cut burial, typologically perhaps attributable to the Filigosa culture (about 2500 BC). The monument is hard to read because it is covered by dense vegetation. The burial consists of an entrance corridor (dromos), an antechamber and a chamber. The narrow corridor leads into the roughly circular antechamber. The chamber proper, smaller and roughly rectangular in plan, is reached through a roughly rectangular/trapezoidal doorway.

d53a37729e4f7baa.text: Complex nuraghe, known to many elders as "Sa Reggia", was probably a three-lobed nuraghe with a village. Today it is a heap of rubble and brambles over 10 metres high.

d5531c58175dbcb0.text:
A single-tower nuraghe on the basalt plateau of Su Gollei, in the area of S'Iscampiatorju. It is a perfect tholos. The south-facing entrance, with the stair on the left and the guard cell on the right, leads to the central chamber.

To the east there are traces of a first outer wall in a crescent shape, leaning against the nuraghe itself; further east a second outer wall surrounded the Nuragic village.

d58a0616cb9f88a2.text: The site of Sant'Uanni lies on a hill a very short distance from the village of Dolianova. Besides the remains of a multi-lobed nuraghe and the basal part of a church that bear its name, some finds attributable to the Nuragic and Roman periods have been discovered, suggesting the presence of both a Nuragic and a Roman settlement.

d592317b9435e30c.text:
Uncertain location, to be defined. Single petroglyph

It overlooks the upper part of the settlement of Baunei and echoes the name of the domus de janas. It is a depiction consisting of a total of 18 shallow channels that branch from a main basin several centimetres deep, joining various terminal cupmarks arranged without any apparent order.

d59d7914654c7392.text: Very ruined, so its structure is hard to make out. A lintelled corridor is visible to the north of the chamber. To the south an ogival chamber. Around it the remains of the village huts can be recognised.

d5c3a0ed94065a6b.text: Single-tower nuraghe, of little architectural value but of considerable strategic importance, since the whole Gulf of Palmas can be controlled from it.

d5c9cb360cfe4dba.text:
The village lies a few metres south of the nuraghe of the same name, on top of Su Monte 'e Subra. Once you reach the summit you are faced with a vast expanse of stones and ashlars covering at least two hectares.

As you approach the various mounds, circular structures, rectangular structures, complex buildings, long walls and ramparts begin to emerge. The site has never been excavated.

d5d288d7881bf1f6.text: Dolmen consisting of a large horizontal slab on cyclopean dry-stone walling

d5e50e728332bbe3.text:
It is a single-tower nuraghe with a refacing and an outer wall that recalls the Nuraghe Aidu Olostru of Bortigali in some respects. To the WNW the remains of a massive outer wall (thickness 2.30 m; height 3.00 m) are visible for about thirty metres; it probably enclosed the nuragic tower but now survives only partially, with three or four courses, at a distance of 12–20 metres from the nuraghe.

An extensive village, of which the remains are visible, extended around the inside of the outer wall.

d6166759f0da947f.text: It is hard to say whether this was a village. Because the site lies on a steep slope, sediment has covered the structures. The area has never been excavated. Massive walls, tens of metres long and very thick, run downhill towards the river, while others run parallel to it. One particularly striking feature is an extensive wall made of two parallel lines of walling separated by a ditch about two metres wide.

d619bd5fce811f10.text: It may be a proto-nuraghe, and its plan is almost square.

d625226735a69329.text: The Adoni nuraghe is a complex nuraghe dating to the Bronze Age, located in the municipality of Villanovatulo in the province of Cagliari. The site stands on a rise about 800 m high in the centre of the historic Sarcidano region. The first excavations date back to the mid-nineteenth century. The whole complex consists of a central tower and a four-lobed bastion, surrounded by a village. Various finds have been recovered at the site, including pottery and a fragment of a bronze handle.

d626d094e8674722.text: It comprises two complete domus de janas and a third that has only just been started.

d6987b955baef277.text: These are two single-chambered tombs, placed side by side with a rectangular doorway.

d6ddfc4ec35fd6f1.text: complex nuraghe with a village around it

d71ce5fe8baf1ac8.text: A single-tower nuraghe in excellent condition whose tholos is intact. Traces of other towers and huts can be seen around it.

d72a420fe60bc365.text:
The nuraghe lies on the outskirts of Sassari, on the SS 127 towards Osilo, behind a sheepfold, on the edge of a precipice in a commanding position over the valley below. Besides being on the brink of the cliff, it is built on a natural bastion, standing on top of a limestone block detached from the ravine itself.

Several structures of uncertain date lean against the main tower.

d7545aaf315a461c.text: The shaped stones belonging to the Nuragic fountain still lie on the spot; the Nuragic spring was presumably destroyed during the work to build the complex of watering troughs.

d77c8dcb03ea5beb.text:
A burial of the Nuragic period. The external profile, the funerary corridor and the exedra can be observed.

The construction technique is regular coursed masonry using sub-squared polygonal blocks.

The tomb has the peculiarity of being unusually oriented towards the south-west, and is also very close to its reference nuraghe (about 25 m).

The monument lies in the municipal territory of Villagrande Strisaili (OG).

d7805428ab79f9e0.text: A singular construction set exactly on the rocky summit of Pedras Serradas, barely distinguishable. It is a kind of semicircular nuraghe. Some consider it a circular nuraghe, others the remains of a nuraghe after the collapse of the ground beneath. The view over Giorrè is priceless.

d782ee9fa6712fe6.text: The tomb is of the coursed type, built with schist slabs about 1 metre long, of which six courses of the outer wall face of the chamber and eight courses of the exedra survive in situ. The doorway at the centre of the exedra is built in dolmenic fashion, with two slabs set on edge and one above; the relieving window is missing. The exedra joins the outer wall face of the chamber with a concave line.

d78ac873d55fd7e2.text: It is an unidentifiable structure without an appropriate archaeological excavation. Limestone slabs set vertically, adjacent, tall but not very thick, are visible; a semicircular structure emerging from the ground, built of limestone blocks and with two openings. A long circular row, perhaps delimiting the structure, at the top of which cavities covered by a few slabs can be seen. Further west, a structure with two adjacent vertical limestone slabs positioned to the north, with another slab to the right while to the left there is a wall of ashlars. Traces of tomb-robbers' digging are evident.

d79b034875175522.text: The Nuragic fortification consists of a tholos tower enclosed in a courtyard which in turn is protected by an outer wall provided with five further towers. The entrance lies to the south and leads into a small courtyard where several rooms are found that were used for metal smelting, as shown by the bronze-smelting waste discovered all around. The central tower has an elliptical plan; inside, on the right, a stairway branches off leading to the upper floor.

d7c2e3441e758489.text: The nuraghe is now in a poor state of preservation, with several collapses that prevent a precise reading. Only two towers can be clearly distinguished, between which a small courtyard probably opened, as is typical of complex nuraghi. The main tower (central tower) contains niches and a stair in the corridor that led to the upper levels, which have now collapsed.

d7cf85c4ddda8b12.text: The site dates to the Bronze Age and is built entirely of finely worked basalt rock. The structure consists of a perimeter wall that is almost totally destroyed: only the base of the well is visible, as it lacks the tholos roof (which is difficult to reconstruct), even though the chamber has remained intact. Nine steps can be counted descending downwards until they reach the water about two metres underground.

d7edb05f272f2e4a.text: The nuraghe has about eight surviving wall courses. The entrance lacks the outer lintel. The stair is visible on the left side and the entrance niche on the opposite side. The tholos chamber has its top missing and is almost completely filled with vegetation, collapse debris and sediments up to a height, against the walls, that exceeds the lintels of the niches, except for the one on the left, whose far end can be glimpsed.

d802edc794fea2cd.text: Complex nuraghe of the tancato type with a central tower and a secondary tower.

d82d87f0f51fc4e0.text: A few courses of wall remain, probably belonging to the outer wall.

d84c6274704430cf.text: Nuragic village composed of about 30 huts, and a short distance away there was a sacred well.

d84ead257d019b1e.text: Archaeological trace corresponding to the area of the trigonometric point.

d8518d7d2bacb1e3.text: The Nuragic sacred well is a particular structure built against the spring vein; the structure of the sacred spring is usually composed of an area enclosed by stone slabs.

d85a45b7894d7016.text: It stands on the hill above the town of Silanus. It is a complex nuraghe, built mostly of granite. The central tower, about 12 metres high, is almost intact; it was once flanked by two or three other towers. The nuraghe has two tholoi one above the other, linked by a main staircase and by a hidden secondary staircase with a mezzanine. At the foot of the nuraghe are the ruins of other nuragic buildings, not yet properly investigated.

d8954c1a093209b4.text:
Built of limestone and sandstone blocks, it consists of a central body with two towers, an outer wall, and a village of huts.

The oldest structures, dated to the 15th–10th centuries BC, are the main tower and some huts. The tower, with its entrance to the ENE, survives to a height of 8 m. The inner chamber preserves its tholos vault intact.

In the back wall opens the ogival stairwell that led to the upper floor and the terrace.

d89f5422b023a655.text: The site contains 17 domus de janas, of which two are unfinished and one is almost completely buried. The numbering of the domus is taken from the book Itinerario Archeologico nel territorio Orgolese.

d8b65d59813a409d.text:
The complex, one of the most important and best preserved in Nuragic Sardinia, comprises a village-sanctuary with about a hundred huts, two small temples with adjoining enclosures, and two megalithic burials.

The village consists of isolated huts and clusters of huts arranged around central spaces. Six groupings can be counted, some equipped with well-cisterns and small wells connected to water channels. The huts, circular, are built of drystone masonry with irregular courses.

d8d80c2358c7c3f9.text: Three domus de janas cut into a limestone cliff, single-chambered, later decorated with a carved rock-cut stele on the façade.

d8db480b3332ff8b.text: Single-tower nuraghe enveloped in dense vegetation.

d8e81a3276dd23d4.text: The site has as many as two giants' tombs of modest size, largely stripped of the stones that made them up. The exedra and the burial chamber can still be made out.

d90fbf683aa8aba1.text: It is a Domu de Janas, a "double-oven" type burial datable to a period between the 3rd and 2nd millennium BC.

d916b729ef5179f9.text:
Single-tower nuraghe built of sandstone boulders. The main chamber has three asymmetrical niches.

From the corridor, a staircase with 15 steps starts on the right. Maximum height of the tower 9.15 m.

Nearby are the remains of the settlement and two domus de janas.

d922e4568de61dcc.text: Probably a single-tower tholos nuraghe. Almost completely hidden by dense vegetation, it appears as a heap of polygonal basalt blocks lying in disorder. A few courses can be made out inside a thicket of mastic on the west side.

d92bf8619c6bfb39.text:
The tomb was part of a funerary complex originally composed of four megalithic burials set a short distance from one another and very close to the Ilòi and Logula nuraghi.

The present road alignment has split the small necropolis of giants' tombs built to serve the villages along a network of transhumance routes. It is a dolmenic tomb, originally furnished with a bilithic arched stele with a doorway at its base, placed at the centre of the exedra.

d93ebc141a96f717.text: This is probably the Domus reported by the engineer Melis in the census of archaeological sites in Mamoiada; the locality should be Locu Lenardu, although today the whole area is called Su Dovaru. It is a single-chambered Domus cut into a granite bench.

d95d6658faedb9ef.text: In total ruin. The oldest villagers remember its existence, even if only a few basal circles remained. When the Sassari–Tempio dual carriageway was built, the earthworks for it affected more than one site, in total disregard for the enormous historical value they represented.

d96324eb985de668.text: Complex nuraghe, presumably of the front-addition type. The nuraghe shows numerous structural alterations after its initial construction. A main tower with two secondary towers added to it can nevertheless be made out.

d97db196f8676b8d.text: Single-tower nuraghe and remains of huts and giants' tomb.

d98c7ecffcf58a28.text: It is a single-tower nuraghe built of large, well-worked basalt blocks. The entrance, oriented SSW, is topped by a rectangular relieving window and leads into a corridor with an ogival roof; on the left of the corridor is a niche. The chamber, completely filled with collapse, survives to almost 5 metres (9 courses). On the right side of the chamber a niche cut into the wall thickness is visible.

d98d4d19d5673d8f.text: A tholos nuraghe whose north tower is clearly visible. The south tower has collapsed on the seaward side. An artificial entrance dug by curiosity-seekers is present.

d98f4c17cd534c03.text: It lies within the municipal territory of Seneghe (OR). Single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The vault has collapsed and the chamber is filled with the collapse debris. The surviving height of the building is about 3.50 m. The trapezoidal entrance is clearly visible, fitted with a monolithic lintel and faces east (1.70 m high x 0.80 m wide at the base).

d99720c73d5f1507.text: The monument stands on the basalt plateau that extends at the southern foot of the Marghine chain, south of the Rio Tossilo. It is a single-tower nuraghe with a niche, a corridor staircase, and a central chamber flanked by two opposing niches. The tower, circular in plan, survives to a height of 2.90 m on the north-west side, with 6 courses, and 2.20 m on the north-east side with 5 courses. The masonry consists of medium and large blocks, carefully worked and laid in regular horizontal courses.

d9a147c17cec9dc6.text: The structure still retains 12 corbels. Complex nuraghe with an outer wall and a surrounding village in basalt blocks. Noteworthy for the presence of large corbels still in situ. Entrance to the west (rare). Unfortunately covered by dense vegetation.

d9aad4bbc405b0d9.text: The tomb has a rectangular apsidal chamber, with the exedra and entrance facing south. The chamber was built of boulders of various sizes, only roughly dressed, bonded dry with packing wedges. The tomb has certainly been violated by looters; the burial chamber is covered by vegetation and filled with collapse stones and earth. On the east side of the tomb there are collapse boulders that certainly belong to the monument. The west wall is hidden by vegetation.

d9bc7e021a327f74.text: The domus de janas of Scala Coperta lies a few hundred metres from the Roccia dell'Elefante, in the locality of Pedra Sciolta. Cut into an erratic trachyte boulder, it consists of an antechamber and four small cells arranged in a cross. On the outside, on top of the boulder, there are three holes for housing small baetyls; a fourth hole is set slightly further back than the others and is now barely visible because of the vegetation.

d9c1ee4f2ba77fa9.text: Only a few basal courses of the monument survive, while the entrance has been incorporated into a hut of recent times.

d9d2fd4c6836ac7d.text: The nuraghe is completely ruined, reduced to a heap of blocks about 2 metres high. Impenetrable because of the dense vegetation. A complex structure with a Bronze Age settlement and remains of Punic-Roman houses.

da02726c5b8008cd.text:
A folk tale tells that these rocks are a married couple turned to stone by the deity for mocking the sound of the bells coming from the nearby church of Masullas during the feast of Sa Gloriosa.

It seems that in the past these statue-like rocky blocks, which geologically are nothing other than submarine lava outcrops, were worshipped by the proto-Sardinians as fertilising deities.

da084491c550f9ad.text: The condition of the tomb is unknown

da0d659e4baea129.text: The monument is a single-tower nuraghe of which no more than four courses of the outer wall face survive.

da0ff2ff4ed1b7ef.text: At present it is completely buried and covered by shrub vegetation. Because of this its ground plan cannot be read, except for a single course of blocks emerging from the hillock; judging by the extent of the remains it is likely to be a complex type. In the surrounding ground outcrops of roughly dressed limestone ashlars can be seen, suggesting the existence of a village, traces of which are also detectable through photogrammetric analysis.

da68b2309111cf6e.text: A ruined single-tower nuraghe of which half the perimeter wall survives for seven courses.

da7c28d68453325a.text: Near the nuraghe Arrubiu there are two giants' tombs, in one of which a sword was found.

da7e584051a50fa5.text: Carved stones, petroglyphs with concentric circles and cupmarks

da9020df24fd26ee.text: This nuraghe, on the boundary between the municipalities of Olmedo (SS) and Sassari, appears in Filippo Nissardi's Nuragic Map of the Nurra (published by G. Pinza in 1901) as "Nuraghe Grascioleddu" and is assigned to Olmedo.

daa6651934fe5dcb.text: These are two separate collective burials that share the same exedra. They lie a short distance from the nuraghe of the same name, which stands on top of the plateau.

dac708dae322b6ad.text: Hut with enclosure. The structure is built of small- and medium-sized polyhedral boulders, dry-stone bonded and laid in more or less regular courses. It was very probably altered and reused up to the last century.

db085f0b3e27579c.text: It lies in the municipality of Orani and consists of five hypogea.

db136495596bedbc.text:
It has a vaguely trapezoidal plan (10.50 x 10.20 x 11.10 x 4.50 m) with rounded corners and a raised entrance (0.75 m above ground level), with a rectangular opening (width 1.47 m – height 1.98 m), lintelled and facing north-east.

The interior of the monument is not visible because of the collapse.

The masonry consists of roughly dressed polygonal blocks of medium and large size laid in irregular horizontal courses.

db1e336ca2a44170.text:
The nuraghe is practically at ground level.

The poor quality of the rock must have contributed to the sad condition to which the monument is reduced.

db1f5d07fc46e977.text: South-east of Siurgus-Donigala, near the boundary with the territory of Goni. Built on a rise at 494 m above sea level, well-worked limestone blocks were used that survive today to a height of about 5 m. The inner chamber has its top missing, is filled with collapse debris, and shows an ogival entrance. Around the nuraghe the basal courses of the huts of a village can be seen, and slabs driven into the ground that may indicate burials.

db4c53f1b667d61e.text: This is the reference nuraghe, now collapsed, for the beautiful and nearby giants' tomb.

db574508c5d9245e.text: Structures belonging to a single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The inner chamber has collapsed in its upper part. Collapse material lies on the west and north sides of the nuraghe. The structure is accessible only along the entrance corridor, which is 5 m long; to its left a chamber opens, partly blocked, which must have given access to the stair leading to the upper chamber.

db5dd55d5673977a.text: Nuraghe now almost completely destroyed. Only a heap of stones remains.

db5ee561b724138f.text: The site comprises a main tower, a sub-elliptical structure that must have served as the entrance, and remains of an outer wall all round the perimeter. The various rock outcrops complete the masonry and dictate the ground plan. The sub-elliptical structure, on the south side, probably formed the entrance to the complex and linked the interior rooms by a corridor, now blocked by collapse. A terrace can be made out in the north-western area.

db64c31a6f3cd83d.text: It is a complex structure built of squared limestone blocks, in which an inner chamber is clearly visible; its archaeological deposit has been disturbed by looters. Inside, three niches with ogival vaulted roofs are clearly visible, as is the entrance, positioned to the south-east; to the right of it a short blind corridor can be seen, in front of which a small niche opens.

db6caf56e0542862.text: The place name that inspired the director Mauro Aragoni for his short film "Nuraghes S'Arena"

db88c85d98473f83.text: The nuraghe stands in an area where an Ozieri culture settlement (4th millennium BC) and a stone cist tomb of the Bell Beaker–Bonnanaro facies (late 3rd–early 2nd millennium BC) have long been known. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

dbb80234a812c936.text:
Nuragic village near Monte Maiori, in the municipality of Guspini.

A fascinating place because it is immersed in nature. It was certainly re-used by local shepherds but it keeps its history alive.

It is not the only one in this municipality.

dbb8ec5ed3f6f40a.text: The Nuragic settlement comprises about a hundred circular huts distributed without any apparent order at regular intervals from one another. It is built with regular courses of limestone blocks; the rare trachyte blocks probably come from the nearby Monte Imberi. The huts, circular (diameter 6–7 m), are for the most part currently covered by collapse debris and overgrown with dense Mediterranean maquis.

dbbbe49a2dd66bce.text: I cannot provide the location of the remains of the nuraghe Antoni Letze because the text you supplied does not contain that information. It describes a Nuragic hut and a dolmen, but does not mention this specific site.

dbf77ab3177176c5.text: The hypogeum is cut into an isolated basalt boulder. The doorway opens at some height above ground level and is surmounted by two deep grooves cut horizontally and parallel in the rock. The doorway still shows a clear rebate for the closing slab. A narrow groove cut into the thickness of the doorway outlines all four sides. The oval chamber is of the oven type. The tomb was explored in 1927 by A. Taramelli, who found it already violated and emptied long before.

dc0270bb0b757053.text: Most of the proto-nuraghi at Serrenti are small and, as far as can be seen, elliptical or irregular in plan. Those at Monti Mannu, Monti Atziaddei, Monti Crastu and Sa Corona appear larger, the last two perhaps enlarged or rebuilt between the Middle and Late Bronze Age. Around this proto-nuraghe there are traces of a small village.

dc0433b88340c4da.text: A nuraghe of which very little remains, situated in the centre of the village of Is Collus. Following a report to the Superintendency, archaeological investigations were carried out, the results of which are unknown.

dc3a231cad055670.text: The site contains, in the inner face of the wall, a room of probable domestic use and the so-called dentilled stele of a giants' tomb. The stele, finely worked, was reused in Roman times and confirms the certain presence of a Nuragic funerary structure of the coursed type in isodomic masonry, whose original position has not yet been identified.

dc42b840cbfcf454.text: Well-preserved nuraghe, part of a larger settlement. The central tower still has its roof and an underlying floor that has not yet been entered.

dc470f3442aaf81f.text: Single-tower nuraghe, enveloped in dense vegetation.

dc7b7d7cc2fd97b3.text: Settlement in considerable decay. Situated at 256 m above sea level. On the summit a crown of limestone rocks surrounded by shrubby scrub is visible, including s'arrùda (Ruta d'Aleppo). The remains of the Nuragic construction have an internal diameter of 4.05 m. It appears to be a single-tower nuraghe but the dense expanse of scrub could hide other structures. The position is strategically elevated, with a very wide visual basin.

dc91183cd164218f.text: Characterised by a large Nuragic settlement that has been excavated several times.

dca4fdd58a554597.text: Almost certainly present until the 1960s, when major land improvement and transformation works were carried out. The place name "su crastu covaccadu" suggests the presence of a trilith or covering lintels of a probable tomb. mu

dcb13d530d68941f.text:
The nuraghe was built directly on the bedrock, and its plan appears to have been adapted to the irregularities of the rock, since walling can be seen on several levels along the slopes of the outcrop.

On the summit the monument, now almost completely destroyed, seems to have an elongated plan, but its very poor state of preservation and an illicit excavation make the whole difficult to interpret.

dcc337bc3417bd67.text: Situated about a hundred metres east of the well-known giants' tomb of Imbertighe, with which it had an obvious cultural connection, the nuraghe now lies inside a farm. It is a single-tower nuraghe with a slightly elliptical plan (14.10 x 15.25 m), an entrance to the south-east, and a surviving height of 2.75 m to the north-west and 1.70 m to the south-west, with five and four courses respectively.

dcd82a569dcb1b26.text: The Orizanne nuraghe stands beside the road from Nuoro to Bitti. Like other nuraghi, a large oak tree grows inside the collapsed tholos.

dcdae954496f446f.text: Only a few traces of the nuraghe remain because the stones were taken away to build a road.

dd055adc225b2edd.text: Little of the village survives; only the ruins of huts emerge, and I believe this was the ordinary settlement, while a short distance away stands the namesake Sanctuary and Temple, with the adjacent Village of Nuragic huts partly still standing; I think these were the (Cumbissias), inhabited only on the occasion of periodic feast days or pagan rites.

dd12b30336fc1306.text: The abundant collapse of the structure and the vegetation covering the monument make it hard to interpret; it could be a corridor nuraghe.

dd217a5bdb18cf63.text: Four-lobed complex nuraghe. The central tower has a chamber flanked by three niches. Built of granite.

dd2b5c911d46148e.text: A giants' tomb completely ruined, of which only a few clear traces remain.

dd45d124c1afec08.text: Collapsed and debris-covered domus de janas

dd9b202c3eb2d06f.text: location of the remains of the nuraghe Antoni Letzesa sea

ddb55da86d576a43.text: Remains of a nuraghe or of nuragic huts

ddc9573343eef51c.text:
The hypogeal tomb opens in a rachitic outcrop, about 150 metres east of the Borore–Silanus municipal road.

The hypogeum, oriented south-west, consists of two sub-circular cells arranged along the longitudinal axis; the walls are carefully smoothed and the ceiling is slightly hemispherical.

ddd3b8510de1e7d8.text: The nuraghe has practically disappeared; only a few heaps of large boulders remain, hinting at its original position.

ddd883a269efc07b.text: Complex nuraghe with an adjacent giants' tomb and a spring, called "Roia Zrighidanu", which flows into the Riu Pizziu further downstream. It is a settlement used up to the Imperial Roman period, and the rectangular structures in the area of the nuraghe probably date from that period. Five hundred metres from the nuraghe, the researchers Dyson and Rowland report a Roman necropolis with at least 32 cist tombs.

de0007ef133122f5.text: Taramelli had already described the hut: "The remains of a circular construction were evident, which after excavation proved to be a Nuragic enclosure about 8 m in diameter … The narrowness of the wall in relation to the size of the interior space does not allow us to say it was a true nuraghe."

de04aae0be2da344.text:
The tomb, of dolmenic type and oriented south-east, has a semicircular exedra (chord 9 m – depth 3 m) bounded by orthostatic slabs, an apsidal rectangular body (length 6 m – width 4 m) and a modest burial corridor (length 3.70 m x width 0.75 m).

At present the northern flank and the right arm of the exedra are incorporated in a dry-stone wall.

de06e23a5e1f31e6.text: Part of the tomb corridor survives: six courses of stones remain on the right side and only two on the left; it has a maximum length of 7.70 m and a width of 1 m.

de09fba8a7d2ba42.text: The nuraghe has a base diameter of 12.60 m and, although demolished in its upper parts, survives to a height of 8.60 m. Through the south-facing entrance one enters the corridor, on the right of which opens a rectangular niche and, on the left, the stair, still passable, which led to the upper chamber, now destroyed. The corridor leads to the fine circular chamber, 4.15 m in diameter, off which three niches open in a cross formation.

de151e1eda156f53.text: Situated off-centre in relation to the Madau funerary complex, and despite its small size, the few visible structures suggest that it retains the characteristics (and therefore perhaps also the construction period) of its "larger sisters". Of the tomb, now half-buried by sediment, the exedra and part of the corridor are visible.

de9142f586ac3ea5.text:
Single-tower nuraghe. Four courses survive intact. In poor condition. Built of roughly dressed medium-sized blocks. Signs of human spoliation. Already shown on Filippo Nissardi's nuraghe map (in Pinza G. 1901).

The hillock occupied by the nuraghe includes a stretch of Roman cobblestone paving identified to the north-west of the monument. The dense vegetation covering the site makes it impossible to detect any remains or traces of a possible village.

dea380756fdc2f0d.text: The sacred well, or well temple, is undoubtedly the most evocative example of a sacred building among those so far discovered and studied in the Mediterranean basin. This type of building, belonging to the rich Sardinian civilisation, dates back to the long and varied Nuragic period. It was conceived as a place for performing the various rites connected with the water cult.

deabdb0e35b01cf9.text: Single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, of which only a single course of limestone blocks laid in a curvilinear line survives, 4 metres long. To the north-west a stretch of wall is visible, made of blocks set in a row for a length of about 3.20 metres.

dee57d0d9140e84b.text: Single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan and a central chamber with its top completely missing; three niches arranged in a cross can be seen. The outer wall face survives with five courses. The entrance, to the south-east, has collapsed.

df03712455c7a1e6.text: It has the characteristic of being built with both limestone and trachyte stones, like the nearby nuraghe Corvos; however, whereas the latter shows a clear separation between the part built of limestone and that of trachyte, in the nuraghe Sa Menta stones of different nature are mixed in the wall face without any criterion.

df1b5e0d1f5c9251.text: The area consists of an enclosure containing a megaron temple.

df1c504ad4f324e4.text: The menhir standing beside the ramp that leads to the upper part of the altar was erected before the altar itself was built. It was the centre of a Neolithic village.

df38461a4d5704ff.text: Up to five courses of enormous, irregularly shaped cyclopean basalt blocks survive, reaching a height of up to two and a half metres. The central tower is incomplete, forming an angle of 270 degrees. From it a wall runs east and another runs north. What structure these walls enclosed is not at all clear because of brambles and various later alterations.

df40806c99b02f41.text: Nuraghe on a ridge overlooking the Coros. Single-tower, built of ashlars of local limestone, its tholos has collapsed inwards.

df44991f001dccce.text: Nuraghe partly incorporated into the walls of the little church dedicated to San Lorenzo; on the north-east side of the structure (the one facing the village) the remains of the San Lorenzo nuraghe are still visible.

df5274cfa9d5faff.text: It appears as the most imposing monument preserved in the area. That it was a complex structure is almost certain, given the massiveness of the masonry which stands out compared to other monuments; inside the chamber a niche is still visible, positioned to the north-west, and slightly offset to the west a small access space can be seen that seems to belong to a staircase.

df77bda119c82aab.text: Practically hidden by the dense shrub vegetation.

df8510710e05e5eb.text: On the site, especially on the steeper side facing Via Aldo Moro, the remains of numerous huts are visible, together with worked stone and ceramic material of various types. The ceramic material is also present in large quantities on the opposite, flat side, to the south of the nuraghe. Some glazed fragments with fewer inclusions appear to indicate occupation later than the Nuragic period.

dfb985af6fde3dcd.text: Situated on top of a hill. It appears to be a single-tower nuraghe with evidence of huts in the surrounding areas.

dfc5cd399d2e67cf.text: It stands on a rocky spur along the Pardu River. This is a nuraghe of at least four towers surrounded by a defensive curtain wall. Of the four towers, three are still in good condition, while only the base of the fourth can be made out. The site today appears split in two. The east side, which does not face the river and stands on the rock, is still intact. The west side, which faces the river, has almost completely collapsed, with an enormous quantity of boulders scattered down the slope.

e03b2ea54d5ad52e.text:
The single-tower nuraghe stands right next to the SS131, beside a sheepfold. It is used as a shelter for sheep. The tholos is almost intact except for the top courses.

Little or nothing remains of the huts that presumably stood beside the tower.

e057e717d58b1719.text: This nuraghe, already recorded in the EEM of 1922, is placed on Taramelli's Archaeological Map a short distance to the west of Nuraghe Pischedda. The monument, which already in the 1930s appeared almost completely destroyed – "Only the base remains, to a height of one metre" – now leaves no trace at all. It was also known as S. Giuseppe.

e05cbe265415027d.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. The interpretation is based on the circular plan of the monument, although its poor state of preservation and the vegetation cover make it impossible to observe other characteristic details. The entrance cannot be identified. Much of the material from the collapse of the nuraghe has been reused to build contemporary enclosures leaning against the ancient structures.

e0879b0f376f9ea4.text: A necropolis with nine hypogeal tombs, in an area with rock outcrops on the surrounding ground. The tombs were found by chance during recent excavation work. The site is thought to have been used from the Late Neolithic (3500 BC).

e08affdc853ff2c3.text: A site that is difficult to interpret. The nuraghe is certain, but the presence of a giants' tomb also seems certain; it disappeared after land-reclamation works. The term cantòne refers to squared stone blocks, often of limestone or trachyte tuff (pèdra contonina). This surname, no longer in use, probably originated from the quarryman's trade that the unknown brothers from whom the place-name derives must have practised.

e0a6415338094b96.text:
The site underwent two main building phases: the first in the Middle Bronze Age and the second in the transition period between the Bronze Age and the Early Iron Age.

The complex consists of a megaron temple, about 17 metres long, surrounded by an enclosure known as a temenos and by other cult and residential buildings, including actual workshops for metal smelting; a complex nuraghe with a trilobate plan lies nearby.

e0c091b90000b3f9.text:
The temple of Sant'Anastasia stands near the church of the same name, in the upper part of Sardara, at the foot of the ridge that rises towards the hill of Pran'e Cuaddus, in the central Campidano.

The sanctuary, one of the most important in Nuragic Sardinia, centres on the sacred well temple.

The temple, dated to the Late Bronze Age (13th–12th century BC), is set within an articulated settlement of both civil and religious character that is still being excavated.

e0fcb310520fa884.text: Nuraghe and village of which only a few traces remain

e109717799470542.text:
Complex nuraghe.

Of the nuraghe, set on a modest hill (563 m a.s.l.), only a few courses of the central tower survive.

e1365fade1488bb2.text: Through a gap between the large ashlars of the upper part of the outer wall face, one enters the corridor that housed the helical staircase giving access to the upper part of the tower. In fact, the corridor ends against two large lintels that are completely buried. The nuraghe is in very poor condition. It is partly enveloped by mastic shrubs and prickly pears, the cause of the collapses and the burial, up to about two metres from the floor level.

e142f17b4af19adc.text: It is a bilobed nuraghe of which only a part remains, although several collapses affect most of the structure. The trilithic and lintelled junction remains evident, and is very interesting. mu

e174567bbc85569f.text: The archaeological area consists of the ruins of a Punic fortress and a Nuragic complex.

e1771376682ec7ca.text: Besides the Iscalas nuraghe, the site contains Roman-period wall structures and prehistoric menhirs. The nuraghe, of which only a few stretches of masonry now survive, had a circular tower built of medium and large polygonal boulders laid without mortar.

e1b1fc5c102e5875.text: It lies a short distance from the beautiful eponymous nuraghe of s'Enalonga, now covered in brush and thorny bushes. A small spring of water still emerges here, which in ancient times must have fed the fountain. No particular masonry is visible.

e1d7682c044398be.text: Single-tower nuraghe, not easily reached, ruined, with its tholos collapsed.

e1f13b373b8418eb.text: The nuraghe Sa Murallia takes its name from a massive wall leaning against the original structures on the downhill side; it is largely hidden by deposits, layers and structures that have been built up against or over it over the centuries. In the same period and in later phases, the first settlements sprang up beside these nuraghi, sometimes enclosed by imposing oval or circular walls that are still partly visible today (Tradori, Araganzola, Maganzosa). (from the Narbolia municipal website)

e1f28192a4e4e5d6.text: To the north-north-west, beside the rocky ridge on which the northern tower of the nuraghe stands, there are two semi-circular natural cavities, about 200 cm deep, closed off by an ellipsoidal enclosure built of polyhedral boulders of various sizes.

e1ff589e67868e7b.text: Remains of a nuragic tower built of basalt blocks.

e20574353074e43c.text: A complex structure, almost entirely buried. The nuraghe is enveloped in dense vegetation and, moreover, a fence has been installed on its summit that prevents the eastern part from being seen.

e208b5c922170cf4.text: The complex contains a sacred well with a paved area, a temple on a rectangular plan, a corridor building, and some stretches of cyclopean walls. The nuraghe Cherchizza stands at the western end, along the edge of the plateau. The site would have served as a landmark for the population of a wide surrounding area. Excavations have yielded bronze artefacts, including a figurine of the mother goddess, as well as amber objects.

e21c41a3d2e1118d.text: A few white limestone blocks of the basal perimeter. The entrance and little else can be seen, all within a dense thicket of fetid anagyris (sa giolva). The name should derive from the place-name of the land. Shepherds believe the leaves of this plant give a bitter taste to goats' milk. See Nuraghe sas giòlvas.

e227d7e1463c6f85.text: A short distance from the town of Sassari, the domus of Oredda reveals its decorative beauties only to those who go in search of the mystery that characterises the domus de janas. We went in pursuit of this jana in a field, from which you would expect anything except to find a ditch, and then to go inside and hold your breath at the art concentrated within it.

e230179f994f30a1.text: The central tower survives on the outside to a height of 6.40 m; on the left of the corridor the stairwell opens, with a trapezoidal opening, completely filled with collapse; the entrance to the chamber also has a trapezoidal opening; the inner chamber, essentially circular in plan, has a maximum diameter of 4.76 m and a maximum height of 5.60 m; the tholos survives almost entirely, except for the last two courses.

e23af137c2272a7a.text: Unfortunately not much remains, but those few surviving ashlars are enough to let us understand this temple. It has circular ritual huts, where benches run all round the inside circumference. Countless parallelepiped ashlars of basalt and trachyte tuff, shaped like a T, cover the whole site; they are perfectly worked and finished. In a sudden flashback this brings me back to other Sardinian sanctuaries.

e240a3ead73c556b.text: Genetically attributable to the Ozieri culture, 3500–2700 BC, it is a simple tomb structure of rectangular shape with the entrance facing east. It has a trapezoidal chamber 2.65 m long and 2.20 m wide. The side walls consist of a stone slab topped by packing material, while the back wall is formed by a single flat quadrangular orthostat that projects beyond the side walls by almost half a metre.

e27981b72a0b9adc.text:
Today, unfortunately, it is quite destroyed.

It also had a bilobed bastion added at a later stage.

e27da1ba503c9740.text: It is in a very poor state of preservation. Enough remains, however, to allow a basic assessment. From the hill at about 600 m above sea level it overlooks the basalt plateau below, serving well as a lookout. A short distance away, almost next to the nuraghe, some stones are visible that could be baetyls or belong to a giants' tomb.

e281fa1c16b55192.text: A natural cave used in prehistoric times as a mass burial site. It has a shaft entrance and some artificial steps. Outside, a wall remnant is still visible, badly damaged by quarrying. The area is fenced off; visiting is not recommended and is dangerous.

e28a93b2125f994e.text: A ruined single-tower nuraghe overgrown with vegetation. About five courses of the masonry survive.

e2a03facd95e7241.text: The Fund'e Monti necropolis (also known as Tracucu) consists of 15 hypogean tombs, locally known as Domus de Janas (fairy houses). The tombs, both single-chambered and multi-chambered, have entrances marked by an access corridor (dromos) up to 5 m long, or by an antechamber. The doorways are the most carefully finished elements, finely carved with frames (to hold the stone doors) and rebates (for draining liquids).

e2aa4ebfa6972353.text: Ruined nuraghe, of which very little is left

e2aa4ffb0ab4d355.text: Complex nuraghe of the tancato type, built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The building is hard to read because vegetation — shrubs and climbers — covers the structural parts. The main tower, presumably the older one, can be made out; it survives to a height of almost 6 m. This joins a secondary tower positioned to the south of the first. The secondary tower survives to a height of about 4 m.

e2bebb54c8568b9a.text: In the countryside around Osilo a very large domus de janas, much altered, lies beneath the foundations of a church now reduced to a ruin.

e2d4aa1528d3645a.text:
The monument is in very poor condition and only the terminal part of the corridor can be seen on the ground.

The construction technique was isodomic, with squared ashlars worked on the exposed faces.

e2d4c5c2dd6ab872.text: It is a building with a rectangular four-lobed plan very similar to Santa Barbara at Macomer. It has a ground area of about 400 sq m.

e2dd158c0c43b7a0.text:
Traces of a nuraghe built of basalt. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

PUC Arbus Relazione Storico Culturale p. 13 Tav 12C No. 3360

e2e72baf43c0eded.text:
From the structure a large part of the Irgoli plain is clearly visible; to the north-east Monte Oddie can be seen.

In the surrounding area there are several collapses, and many ashlars from the structure have been used to build the dry-stone walls.

This is a tholos nuraghe partly leaning against the natural rock to the west; it has an inner and an outer wall face, and between them the spiral staircase can be made out; a guard chamber to the east is plausible, and a possible access ramp starting from the west.

e2ed7f0ad70b79d3.text: The Crabia nuraghe is a single-tower type, built on two superimposed storeys that are still intact, each with a circular central chamber roofed with a tholos. Its distinctive feature is the presence of two staircases: one to the left of the entrance corridor, leading to the first floor and perfectly preserved, while the other, running in the opposite direction to the first, is concealed in a niche inside the tower on the right and leads to a hidden niche on the first floor.

e2fa0ab2edc57889.text: When the Rio Murrone joins the Rio Oloitti, several hundred metres further downstream, it drops about twenty metres, forming a waterfall of foaming, roaring water in a wild and captivating setting of unspoilt, primordial nature. The river has a winter torrent character, ceasing altogether in the driest summers.

e337a3b56430e204.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. The structures are covered by a large fig tree and bramble bushes. Despite this, the building is in fair condition, partly because it has been used as a livestock shelter, an activity that has led to some internal alterations. The lintelled entrance faces south-east. On the left side of the entrance passage opens the stairwell, now blocked by collapse debris.

e33d4c78d9a981f9.text:
1. Of the monument, unusually close to the reference nuraghe, only a stretch of the burial corridor just emerges from the ground of the site.

2. Of the monument, currently destroyed, only a few worked ashlars are visible, indicating that the tomb was of the coursed type in isodomic masonry.

e347afa507594403.text: Less than 50 metres from the right bank of the Riu Vacchetta, 250 metres from the railway and about 800 metres SW of the Protonuraghe Gazza, two small artificial caves lie a few metres apart.

e358fb6c8e9408e8.text: A vegetation-covered hill concealing a nuraghe, one of the largest in the area. It extends over at least two hectares of land at i lacaras

e35e5d9dee989695.text: It has architectural features similar to those of sacred wells with a pointed-arch entrance. The inner basin is spacious and still collects the sacred water. As of July 2022 its state of preservation is very poor, and the well is not widely known.

e381335d3c45d8c2.text:
The peculiarity of this nuraghe lies in the fact that the chamber wall opposite the entrance has a short passage leading to a large lintelled window, topped by a relieving window.

The nuraghe is a single-tower nuraghe and shows no trace of any kind of staircase. The entrance, set to the north-west, has a lintel surmounted by a carefully worked relieving window.

e3a5375d82b134ea.text:
A complex consisting of five towers linked by curtain walls often resting on the natural rock.

The site is internationally known because, for the first time in Sardinia, Mycenaean pottery was found here.

e3a8f826b418c408.text: Of the monument, largely destroyed, the burial corridor can be seen, built of well-finished polygonal blocks on the exposed faces.

e3af73782b279ef1.text: Some courses of large stones and part of the summit with a blocked access can be seen. Forty metres to the east are the remains of a "sacred" well.

e3b3700c000e9145.text: Located about 300 metres from the nuraghi Sas Casas and Columbos, respectively to the west and south-east, the monument is a single-tower nuraghe with a niche and a corridor staircase, and a central chamber bordered by three niches arranged in a cross. The tower, circular in plan, survives to a maximum height of 4.70 m with seven courses to the south-east, while the minimum height is recorded to the south-west at 0.40 m with only a single course: the wall thickness ranges from 4.25 m to 4.75 m.

e3c97795f1539f29.text: The hypogeum is cut into a limestone ridge. "The whole appears organised with care and balance of proportions, achieving a result of compositional harmony of great effect" (Giuseppa Tanda)

e3cb93959eb908eb.text:
Domus 1 has a multi-chambered layout, with a semicircular antechamber giving access to a first trapezoidal cell that features a central pillar. An opening cut into the top of the pillar leads to an upper level with two small chambers superimposed on the one below.

Domus 2 has a multi-chambered layout, with a corridor, an elliptical cell, a roughly rectangular central chamber with a niche, and a third quadrangular cell.

e3eba253bee46d79.text: The domus de janas is deeply buried and entry is practically impossible.

e3f05863d4c104f7.text: Nuragic village lying south-south-east of the eponymous nuraghe. In the area concerned one can see courses of cyclopean walls and the remains of at least one probable hut. The lush vegetation growing there, mostly mastic shrubs, makes it impossible to trace the outline of other probable wall structures. Ceramic fragments are visible on the ground near these structures.

e401af9db0d1199c.text: It stands 7.50 metres high over 21 courses, with a diameter of 11 metres, and is characterised by a very tall tholos with thick walls. A Nuragic–Roman–medieval village, later abandoned because of plagues, adjoins it; on the north-west side there is a wall face running for perhaps a hundred metres along a natural cliff.

e42f1cf47ed47211.text: This dolmenic tomb, of the Early Bronze Age, is in an excellent state of preservation; indeed it retains the funerary corridor almost intact, with a flat-lintel roof formed by stone slabs laid horizontally along the corridor walls. The large stele consists of a centinated monolith in which the small doorway giving access to the burial chamber is cut. The exedra still preserves several stones set in the ground exactly as they were originally.

e438527d273aa4bc.text: Complex nuraghe; its architecture cannot be deduced because of the very poor state of the structure.

e43cf063bcf5bbad.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. The nuraghe is built of polygonal blocks of local basalt and survives for 2–3 courses laid in a circle to a maximum standing height of about 2 m. The entrance, fitted with a well-worked monolithic lintel, like the blocks of the jambs, faces east. The passage between the inner chamber and the entrance can still be traced, although the whole upper covering is missing.

e447280a42c15953.text: Proto-nuraghe of circular or roughly circular shape

e452a11a260029a4.text: Complex nuraghe with a central tower and two added towers with a courtyard, built of limestone. Traces of a settlement.

e471eb46f34ce9d3.text: The nuraghe takes its name from “pibiri”/pepper. The monument and the surrounding area were investigated scientifically in the early 2000s. The main body, built of limestone, consists of a central tower and at least two additional towers linked by straight curtain walls. The spiral staircase is visible. The main body is enclosed within an outer wall made up of several towers connected by both straight and curved walls.

e4a2b6960c7e460a.text:
In a dominant position, a few metres from the northern bank of the Rio Merchis – which marks the boundary between the municipal territories of Borore and Norbello – less than 400 metres SE of the Nuraghe s'Istrampu and about 250 metres SW of the domus de janas of Ortigosu.

The monument appears as a hill strewn with rubble and covered by dense shrub vegetation. The collapse and the vegetation make a correct planimetric definition of the monument very difficult.

e4d25fa8c60b622d.text: The pre-Nuragic necropolis of S'Elighe Entosu consists of eight very distinctive domus de janas: for example, one preserves in its cell a circular stone hearth carved into the floor, a ceiling carved with a double pitch replicating the timbering of a wooden roof, and on the sides a reproduction of the walls of prehistoric huts. Another, called "delle Sette Stanze", has medieval graffiti along the entrance corridor and seven small cells arranged around the main chamber.

e4e0b3eb895b3578.text: It was built right at the foot of the rocky outcrop on which the nuraghe Is Berritta stands. The only visible part is perhaps the apsidal section, while the exedra has not been identified.

e4f402929f4da866.text: Built of granite as a collective burial and, at the same time, a place of worship, it is a classic example of the megalithic culture that characterised Europe, and the island in particular, during the Copper Age (3rd millennium BC). The dolmen is constructed using the trilithic system (from Greek tri, three, and lithos, stone) – the oldest known architectural scheme – characterised by vertical load-bearing elements that support others laid horizontally.

e51fc852c17a0b9a.text: Little or almost nothing remains standing; a portion of the outer facing of the south side can be distinguished, and all around a very large number of scattered blocks from the collapse. It is classified as a single-tower nuraghe with a circular base and an external diameter of about 11 metres.

e52010df6f9870d1.text: The Flumenlongu nuraghe is a single-tower structure with at least two superimposed floors, to which are attached, besides an open courtyard space, a secondary tower and several accessory rooms. A village of circular huts extends around its margins; its extent has not been defined. An important hoard came from one of them, yielding ingots, axes, an adze and several bracelets.

e56558db38bb742a.text:
The entrance, about 110 cm x 60 cm, is at floor level. There is a single oval chamber about 150 cm high, 250 cm deep and 130 cm wide, apparently undecorated.
