At the back of the chamber a pit occupies about two-thirds of the short side and is about 3 m deep; it has not been explored and contains a large niche within the same cavity.

Around the domus de janas cut into the limestone there are rectangular basins that look like quarrying for building material, almost as if the site had been used as a quarry.

e59185c4296f2fe7.text: On a small rise on the eastern side of the Monte Ozzatru stream, which joins the Caddare stream a few dozen metres away, numerous heaps of stones can be seen, presumably the result of field clearance, and in the immediate vicinity fragments of Nuragic pottery and a fragmentary granite quern emerge from the ground.

e5948832db76536c.text: A jewel among the jewels in the archaeological treasure chest of our municipality of Chiaramonti. It is a Domus that the womb of Mother Earth still preserves intact. Only the antechamber is visible, rich in petroglyphs of rare beauty. mu

e599110a9d1ce116.text:
The nuraghe stands on the summit of a hill, a short distance from the domus de janas of the same name and from Nuraghe s'Aspru.

Of the monument, perhaps an enclosure rather than a nuraghe, two or three courses survive on the west and north sides, to an average height of 2 metres, together with other stones scattered on the ground. The masonry incorporates the natural rock into its circuit and must have enclosed a diameter of about 11 metres. The stones are large and only roughly dressed.

e59ff01f3a215a4a.text: Settlement belonging to the single-tower nuraghe with outer wall

Report: name check:

On the IGM maps it is wrongly called Muggiaglio. The name is Egra e Mele.

e5e04c6cfffd75ff.text: It lies in the municipality of Mandas (CA). What remains of the nuraghe is visible on the north and north-west sides, where three courses of limestone ashlars emerge; the rest of the boulders are scattered around the nuraghe.

e5eb7022508fc1e3.text:
A few kilometres from the village of Uri, a tall stone stele stands in the middle of a field, giving the site its name: Sa Pedra Longa (The Long Stone). In the past it formed the front of a Nuragic giants' tomb, dating to the Middle Bronze Age (about 1700–1350 BC).

Of the original monument only the monolithic arched stele (cut from a single block of rock) survives; its type and relatively modest dimensions suggest an early date.

e5f8feeef7dbdb7f.text: Rock-cut chambers used and modified from the Neolithic. Nearby are the remains of a Nuragic village. Sacred well dismantled with mechanical equipment. Some sandstone blocks and T-shaped ashlars remain. Where the well or temple once stood there is now a crater.

e6044e27c8ce1c66.text: Situated on the boundary between Sindia and Macomer, this nuraghe lies about 1000 m from the important and well-known archaeological area of Tamuli (Macomer). It is a complex nuraghe with a central tower and two partially preserved secondary towers. The main chamber is circular and has three niches arranged in a cross; the tholos survives intact. At present it appears to the visitor 'protected' by dense vegetation that almost completely covers it.

e6178a33025afcf8.text: The monument was demolished by a bulldozer. All that remains is a scatter of ashlars from the walls.

e622355f5a5a212c.text: An important natural cavity called Grotta de su Mrajani, which has yielded evidence (pottery) of Early Neolithic man, even before cultures such as Bonu Ighinu or San Michele di Ozieri.

e6493e7edb0ffae0.text: The Nuragic sacred well of Is Molineddus lies in a valley rich in springs. From the little information Spano was able to gather, it consisted of a rectangular building with an entrance on the west side, built of large blocks laid dry. Behind the building a spring rose from the rock and collected in a round well, also made of large stones.

e6581cd8923bdd0e.text: Collapsed nuraghe of which about four courses remain above ground

e65d6dde69d62099.text:
Single-tower nuraghe.

It stands on private land and is partly in good condition.

e65ef0cb26400f06.text: Totally collapsed complex nuraghe. It looks towards the "Sette Fratelli" and towards the sea of Geremeas.

e66f7644cc46bf84.text: This dolmenic giants' tomb is easily visited because it lies beside the road and close to the larger Aidu complex.

e67d05c71f5b65c9.text: In the territory of Serrenti, the nuraghi with a transverse frontal addition are those of Cannedu and Monti Crabu,

e6a25045d452bcea.text: It is near the nuraghe of the same name.

e6a533c1b138e6bc.text: A burial of the Nuragic period built of polygonal trachyte blocks. Little of the tomb is visible because of the vegetation; the corridor and part of the exedra survive. From what the remains and the vegetation allow one to see, the mound has walls of roughly dressed blocks and a final cut stone. It is of interest as the only one of its type known so far: the ashlar with three holes in which three small baetyls were placed during religious ceremonies. mu.

e6d02cf11083c214.text: Given the characteristics of the little-worked stones, their small size, and the type of collapse that gives it an elongated shape, it may be a proto-nuraghe.

e6d25f13972a3b22.text: Single-tower nuraghe forming part of the complex of nuraghi at the locality Su Padru.

e6e68c047ce7767b.text: A burial of the Nuragic period, barely legible in its ground plan. Only a fragment of the arched stele survives.

e714da2c5d27cfc6.text: A single tower remains, its interior collapsed and inaccessible. A staircase can be inferred. It is surrounded by an elliptical wall with a surviving height of about 3 m and seven courses.

e724462b846d6945.text: More precisely it is a proto-nuraghe, or corridor nuraghe; an internal collapse makes it impossible to enter from the doorway.

e7368ec9842e6584.text: The settlement consisted of a complex nuraghe with the village around it, whose clear ruins are preserved by a thriving thicket of mastic and wild olive. The most important nucleus of the ancient settlement developed around a circular depression in the ground that served as a small catchment basin for rainwater in the winter and spring months.

e754a3d50d9a27f4.text: Nuraghe built of limestone blocks, it retains much of its grandeur. It consists of a central tower and a bastion formed by three lateral towers added concentrically. They are oriented to the north, south-west and south-east. The main tower survives almost intact. The tower facing south-west stands to a maximum height of 1.80 m and its interior is choked with collapse. A further tower to the south-east probably existed; only short stretches of its circuit remain and the possible chamber is covered with earth and rubble.

e75f5a8032333d29.text: Of modest extent (about 51 metres with a drop of 10 metres), easily accessible.

e761583e16a25734.text: No trace of this nuraghe now remains, as it was completely destroyed during the planting of a vineyard.

e782512835a1319d.text: Leaning against some granite rocks are the remains of a Nuragic village near an abandoned old farmstead.

e790ce817cac5b77.text: In one tomb a large bull's-head protome and traces of paint can still be seen. Six single-chamber domus de janas in poor condition can be identified. Two other tombs lie about 500 metres away to the south-east.

e7a8624bc49d5cee.text: To the south-east of the nuraghe, leaning against a rocky spur, is the structure of a well cut into the rock. It appears as a long cavity built in a semi-circular shape with boulders of various shapes and sizes. All around are fallen boulders, probably belonging to the well's original structure.

e7bd2f114bc0841c.text: The area of potsherds at Serra Ona can be delimited to the east of the nuraghe in the surrounding fields used for agriculture. They are small and medium-sized fragments of Nuragic and Roman date with a medium degree of abrasion. They are distributed unevenly and, because the fields are ploughed, they concentrate especially in the headlands where the plough turns.

e7cc064b4b6499c6.text: These are various menhirs and fragments found during land reclamation.

e7cdaa373539710a.text: It is a circle of polygonal cyclopean boulders improperly known as a nuraghe. Lacking a specific title for its definition, I therefore continue to consider it as such, but on the evidence I lean towards a ceremonial circle. Nuraghe del guado della moglie. See Badu muzère. mu

e7d8d1955311382a.text: A two-lobed nuraghe with its top missing, partly buried; the lintel is visible, striking for its remarkable size.

e7dd3fd76b8e356b.text: Only the foundation of the nuraghe remains.

e7ea8541b3e6a533.text: The structure has a constant internal diameter of 4.30 m; the walls currently measure 2.80 m in height from the present floor, which is choked with rubble, up to the highest course of boulders, located opposite the entrance, from where the height decreases towards the entrance itself. Externally, walking around the building only the topmost row of boulders is visible; the rest is completely buried in sand deliberately piled there to form a truncated cone.

e81055392f004c68.text: The megalithic settlement, now completely destroyed, was located near Casa Manis. Only a menhir remains in the area later occupied by a Roman settlement.

e81c1105b62b1a5a.text: Very badly destroyed and hard to interpret. Probably dolmenic. It is likely that the stele bore the three-dentilled stone typical of the giants' tomb on top of the entrance.

e82c215025fc9afe.text: It is one of several domus de janas located in the municipality of Alghero. Inside there is a hearth carved into the stone of the base.

e87dbd6d2a44b098.text:
The Accas nuraghe is in a fair state of preservation. The monument has not been excavated, and both the entrance and the interior are partly buried, probably to a depth of about 2 m relative to the nuraghe's original floor level.

The chamber is nevertheless accessible. Inside, on the left, the stairwell is completely buried and inaccessible.

Inside the chamber, along the walls, the three niches are only just distinguishable because they too are filled with earth.

e88d2b321797bd79.text: The nuraghe stands isolated on top of a rocky outcrop inside a large quarry.

e88f8e0313e545a4.text: It looks like one of those nuraghi classified as unfinished

e89b246bb6d05d59.text: Few remains of a nuraghe built of limestone

e8b63744f6565bf9.text:
The rock face of this hypogeum has the peculiarity of bearing, above the doorway, a bull sign consisting of a line (1.14 m) incised with its ends turned upwards (height 0.18 m).

It is a representation of the bull deity drawn in an extremely elementary and rough manner, which is nevertheless of considerable interest because it is the only known example in the area. Chamber measurements: depth 1.24 m; width 1/1.18 m; height 0.70/0.94 m.

e8cb7a68c732eb3a.text: Among the nuraghi in the territory of Mores, this is the best preserved and most articulated, thanks to its three towers linked by a bastion. Traces of the ancient village are visible around it.

e8ce87d5f260d38b.text: This spring lies a few steps from the Nuraghe Sa dom'e S'Orcu, in an area rich in springs and wells of different periods. Architecturally, the sacred area seems to recall, at least in its general lines, structural models of an earlier period. As early as 1990 G. Lilliu noted that "the plan of a round well-shaft preceded by a long rectangular atrium, widening in the middle, resembles the well-known scheme of the proto-Sardinian well temple".

e8df68cacce8d818.text: Uncertain location. Clandestine excavation. Length of the excavation about 5 m. The apse is visible at ground level.

e8f43ad02c73e666.text: It is not clear exactly what it is, perhaps a unique monument that combines a giants' tomb, a trilithic dolmen, and a Nuragic fortress. It was certainly a very important place for the defence of the territory and the clan. It is a sacred site in every sense, and it is no exaggeration to think of the crag there as the place where the rite of the Accabadora was performed. mu.

e911d0fcb0cb0aa4.text: The whole structure makes use of the natural rock. The nuraghe is in poor condition. Part of it has collapsed; a magnificent lintel and some walls remain. There is also a corridor leading to a chamber of which only a slight raised area survives.

e92c38380d646af1.text:
A ruined, buried nuraghe of unidentifiable structure.

Traditionally the locals place it near the river. Visually only a circle of stones at ground level can be seen.

e949604f361da295.text: A small domus de janas about a hundred metres from the Nuraghe Orgurù. Nine have been recorded in the area. This small domus is cut into a natural boulder and is not immediately visible because the view is initially blocked by other rocks.

e9499004541bec1f.text: Remains of the Nuragic village of Siseri Alto incorporated into the vegetation

e95b4d9bbb420247.text: "Massive and of irregular plan, in which the dimensions of the walls prevail over the internal spaces, marking an imperfect mastery of the building techniques proper to later tholos nuraghi." Following the traditional classification, the megalithic construction of Is Bangius can be ascribed to the type of monuments of the archaic phase, such as corridor nuraghi.

e964183260c9dbb7.text: Around the area there are numerous traces of very ancient presences, such as votive menhirs and ashlars of various shapes. Other constructions enrich the territory, such as the namesake spring Nuraghe. Polilobato, situated on the summit of the mountain of the same name, and, a little further on, one of the most important Nuragic sacred wells: Su Tempiesu.

e96782aa1a15d193.text: These are four tombs at Chighizzu, above the tunnels along the SS 131, Sardinia's main highway. The steep slopes and the void beneath are truly dizzying, and those who excavated these domus de janas were undoubtedly very brave.

e98f9c5fe7680656.text: Small complex nuraghe to which a transverse lateral section was subsequently added

e994cdf049bc8b9e.text:
The nuraghe lies near the village of Birori and consists of a low hill that has formed over time on the ruins of the monument.

From what can be seen it is a four-lobed nuraghe with a central tower enclosed by a bastion with four corner towers. Around the fortress the traces of an outer wall and the circular outlines of numerous huts are clearly visible.

e9998c8a4c4b922a.text: The dentilled ashlar and a monolithic arch belonging to the apsidal part remain of the tomb.

e9b52f1381aa3653.text: Bocca d'Irghiriai is a narrow, rugged rocky saddle that separates the cliff face of Monte Bàrdia from the massive stronghold of Monte Irveri. It must have been a pass used in antiquity as well: near the rocky spur that overlooks the saddle to the east lie the scant remains of a single-tower nuraghe built of limestone.

e9c587db946df73a.text: Complex nuraghe whose central tower survives in good condition and for almost all of the first level. The tholos is accessible through the entrance corridor, which is clear of collapse.

e9ef8564860afa25.text: Single-chambered domus de janas with a carved stele above the doorway.

ea0825c3fb1c4d88.text: The sacred well is the most important part of the whole sanctuary, so much so that it was the first feature to be recognised and immediately excavated. Dated to the 9th century BC by the archaeologist Anati in 1985[2], the site was built using the cyclopean technique, the same as that used for nuraghi, but unlike them with carefully dressed stones rather than roughly hewn ones. In antiquity the temple was roofed.

ea1a8d8170b09ad6.text: Nuraghe completely destroyed. On the small hillock small stones are visible which, together with the earth, cover the nuraghe that is no longer there.

ea61cfd03ed64f50.text:
Reduced to a level of ruin, only some circles of roughly shaped and disordered stones remain scattered in the courses. The remains poorly show the original construction features, despite some courses still being arranged in order.

Info: www.archeologosardos.it

Nuraghe of the site of Ginestroni, in Logudorese Tiria. See Tiriàles.

ea636b4ce9d159af.text: Nuragic hut. It is circular, built of flat stones of various sizes laid one on another in courses that corbel inwards towards the centre. The wall is conical: about 150 cm wide at the base and about 70 cm wide at the top, with a surviving height of about 130 cm. To the south-east the wall breaks off for about 100 cm (perhaps the entrance) where the structure has collapsed, probably because of wild olive and mastic trees.

ea742dff680f1835.text: Probable Nuragic village, never studied. The giants' tomb's pertinence contained 80 skeletons.

ea767326572c3c30.text: In the outer wall there is a domus de janas, and another has been cut inside the cave about 3 m from the entrance on the left-hand side.

ea77e2983ef18204.text:
A short distance before Muravera, at km 51, next to the SS 125, the monument is well signposted and easy to reach. The building consists of a central tower to which a three-lobed bastion with a concave-convex outline was added later, enclosing a small courtyard. The whole complex measures 24 m on the N-S axis and 16 m on the E-W axis.

The central tower, circular in plan (9 m external diameter), survives to a maximum height of about 10 m.

eaa98d9fb87dd18d.text:
The monument is in a fair state of preservation despite the roots of the holm oak that overshadows it undermining its stability.

The burial corridor, built of polygonal blocks in courses, still retains almost all of its roofing, while the tomb body is defined by the mound that covers it. The exedra of dolmenic type is more clearly legible, although it lacks the stele; it consists of orthostats set vertically into the ground.

enclosed by a dry-stone wall.

eac42d2f42e9c0ea.text: It is a complex nuraghe consisting of two towers. The original second floor has collapsed, blocking part of the first level.

eacecb52f734f1cc.text: The complex includes a nuraghe, consisting of a central tower on the summit of a basalt hillock and various added structures positioned along the slopes of the same rise, investigated archaeologically in 2003, and an important village of huts, located on the south-eastern slopes of the hill.

ead6516b33fa7a5e.text: From the information I have, it should be a single-tower nuraghe of which only a few traces remain.

eb10fee7cfe45b0c.text: The tomb body shows its wall faces with difficulty because of collapses and the vegetation covering the front and rear sections. From the visible parts it can be seen that it is built of large, dressed limestone blocks. The apse wall, though covered by vegetation, retains two or three courses of polyhedral blocks. The front part of the tomb is incorporated into a dry-stone wall where a parallelepiped-shaped block can be made out, perhaps the tomb's lintel.

eb12000b57040ff5.text: Single-tower nuraghe and settlement (Santu Sadurru). The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

eb55a9f14ab2c5eb.text: Unrecorded Nuragic archaeological area, reported by Davide Arzu, extending throughout the scrub wherever there are no trees. It consists of various nuraghi and huts.

eb635341ae980a87.text:
The tomb is in a poor state of preservation, hidden by vegetation, and only "recently" has a fire partly revealed the structure.

The most visible part is the exedra, in particular the lower section of the bilithic stele, while the corridor is marked by a few stones emerging from the ground and a covering slab.

eb664e0297eb9a2e.text: A ruined nuraghe, not easily reached, stands on a hill at as much as 982 m above sea level. The Serra Pirisi cave is an area that is not particularly extensive, measuring about 1.5 km in length, located in the Su Canale area, in the Supramonte of Baunei. Despite its small size, compared with other areas, it contains a considerable number of cave entrances, among them Lovettecannas, the deepest in Sardinia with a vertical drop of -520 m.

eb668cc99c148590.text: It is a single-tower nuraghe; currently two courses of the base remain standing; the stones that made it up lie both inside and outside. The entrance is perfectly clear, but the lintel cannot be identified with certainty. Built of basalt, it dominates the whole Gulf of Gonone to the south. From the top the nuraghe Buca d'Irghiriai can also be seen, on the pass of the same name.

ebad9398e80efb1a.text: The giants' tombs of Mont'Ollastu (Villamassargia) have been investigated in the past by archaeological excavations and have yielded ceramic finds on display at the Archaeological Museum of Cagliari.

ebc9640a79e82402.text: The Nuraghe Gorroppu, or 'Presethu Tortu', stands on a rocky spur south-west of the gorge of the same name. The settlement is naturally fortified on the south side, while on the opposite side it is protected by a substantial megalithic wall, very well preserved, reaching a height of over 3 metres. Inside the settlement there are numerous quadrangular buildings, some in a fair state of preservation.

ebce50bbe66c6e6b.text: The nuraghe consists of a single circular tower and is not in a good state of preservation. The building was constructed using medium-sized, roughly dressed blocks of metarenite (schist). The tholos survives with a maximum diameter of almost five metres and a height of less than two. The nuraghe is reached by an uphill path, steeply sloping, set in Mediterranean scrub.

ebf304d29e9431c8.text: It could belong to the category of unfinished nuraghi, of which there are many examples between Macomer and Sindia.

ec0bb33626253e66.text: “Human presence on the island of Sant’Antioco is attested from the 5th millennium BC13 in rock shelters, caves, lithic scatters and tombs.” A tafone that, because of its size, was used as a rock shelter. Human use is clear, also shown by stones of various sizes, some still in their original position and others in large numbers nearby, which probably formed a wall partly closing the opening.

ec125e5b63d068fd.text: The dolmen is located at Berchiddeddu. The dolmenic chamber has an almost square plan; the covering slab, which is the largest element, measures about 1.60 x 1.20 m. Near the dolmen there is also a menhir, as well as traces of other destroyed structures and fragments of Ozieri Culture pottery.

ec149eed50c4f9be.text: Probable nuragic spring on a perennial vein of water

ec3b6cae75462412.text: In cell c the rock-cut rendering of the rectangular hut appears very faithful. The central beam, the side rafters resting on it and on two horizontal beams parallel to it, and the two symmetrically placed pillars are all reproduced.

ec40451667a905bd.text: The Pranu Muttedu park is one of the most evocative archaeological sites in inland Sardinia. The park area is divided into two parts, for a total extension of about 200,000 sq m. Excavations have brought to light numerous artefacts attributable to settled communities of the "Ozieri" culture dating to the Late Neolithic (3200–2800 BC). The archaeological complex has the highest concentration of menhirs known in Sardinia.

ec95bacdb18e7421.text: It is a single-tower nuraghe with its roof collapsed.

eca7c24bc7dc9932.text:
In the 1990s it was discovered that the Zapata palace had been built over the well-preserved remains of a Nuragic settlement that the archaeologist Giovanni Lilliu named Nuraxi 'e Cresia.

Thanks to an architectural restoration project of great scenic impact designed by the architect Pietro Reali, both the baronial palace and the underlying nuraghe, duly brought to light, have become the seat of a museum complex, inaugurated on 29 July 2006.

ecb39d6e2f53b4bd.text: The arched stele of this giants' tomb lacks an entrance doorway, so it must have rested directly on the jambs that frame the entrance. Or on a lintel that gave the monument greater grandeur.

ecd19520f8f9d6a2.text:
The Nuragic people decided to wall up the tafoni and erect a single, distinctive tower that probably had an additional room above the surface of the rocky outcrop.

Inside these walls fitted into the granites there are very steep stairways.

Not much remains of the large central communal building, perhaps also because of the choices made by La Marmora and Spano who, in their search for the "floor level", had part of the original superstructure moved and pushed down below.

ecd4a550946a6f95.text: Ugas mentions this site as a probable village and workshop of the pre-Nuragic period. Along the furrows of the regular ploughing, potsherds, obsidian and stone mace heads are still found today.

ecd7b8c4f882b053.text: The tower, circular in plan (13.20 x 13.50 m at the top where the roof is missing) with its entrance facing south-east, survives to a maximum height of 9.30 m, while the average height is about 8.50 m. The masonry consists of carefully worked trachyte blocks laid in regular horizontal courses with occasional chock stones.

ece780c4be8735af.text: The Nuragic construction lies in a striking area above Lake Flumendosa. It is hard to reach for two reasons: you must find the path that links the Sa Scala e Trinched'assu waterfall to the Sa Ucca 'e is Canis giants' tomb and, above all, locate the tomb's exedra, which is literally submerged by extremely dense vegetation. Almost the entire corridor of the Nuragic construction survives in good condition, except for the final apsidal stretch, which is missing its covering slab.

ecfe5aff0855d35b.text: It lies within the municipal territory of Nuoro. The region takes the name Intranuraches because three massive nuraghi stand on three rocky "mammelloni". Unfortunately the nuraghe is in poor condition and looks more like a fortification, built by making full use of the granite outcrop.

ed0ce61f99c0902c.text:
Remains of a building divided into several rooms (vaguely rectangular in plan) bounded by walls built of medium-sized stones and clay mortar. In particular, seven steps of a staircase that linked floors at different levels survive.

Among the surface finds, Phoenician pottery fragments and Nuragic vessel forms of the Early Iron Age have been identified.

ed145012cfd8c54c.text: Nuraghe enveloped in vegetation. On the edge of the village, a single-tower nuraghe with an elliptical ground plan still in a fair state of preservation.

ed1aefce089e2b34.text: Near the settlement, which has never been excavated or studied. Particularly ruined, it shows traces of huts in the vicinity.

ed582a2608738bd9.text: Probable single-tower nuraghe, built of limestone.

ed68f865264df7f4.text:
The domus de janas consists of three sub-rectangular chambers opening onto five smaller elliptical or semi-circular cells.

The tomb is entered through a rectangular vestibule whose ceiling reproduces a double-pitched roof with a central beam (20 x 5 cm deep) from which the side rafters (eight on each side) spring, alternating with broad flat bands (20–30 cm).

ed6eafa4ed4bfb91.text: Eight domus de janas scattered along the area delimited on the map, plus a few tafoni.

ed9afdccf656112d.text: A probably multi-lobed nuraghe whose exact structure cannot be determined; the massive collapse and the dense vegetation on the hill where the monument stands prevent its understanding. To the south, although filled with earth and collapse boulders, an oval chamber is visible, exposed by the action of looters. From NW to NE a curvilinear wall, about 9 m high, set against the rocky ridge, could be part of the central tower's wall face.

edaae2bfa6fc2dd7.text: Ruins of a nuraghe located near the thousand-year-old wild olive tree of "Sa Tanca Manna"

edcf3d8e8e72c51e.text: It is a single-tower nuraghe with a large circular chamber whose walls corbel particularly steeply. A distinctive feature of the nuraghe is the absence of the corridor niche and the staircase. Outside, in the area around the tower, several worked blocks of varying size are visible.

edee51e16e2981a7.text: The nuraghe is probably a complex type and provided with an outer wall, although the extensive collapse and the vegetation covering it do not allow a more precise assessment.

ee0225e9ff279b57.text:
It is a complex nuraghe, built of basalt, on a small rise composed of at least three towers and surrounded by a village.

The foundations of the towers and of what must have been the huts are clearly distinguishable. The central tower still stands partially. Climbing to the top of the tower one can indeed see the interior chamber. Debris accumulated inside and outside, however, prevents access from the base.

ee28ba180258603a.text: The nuraghe, built of blocks laid in courses of differing shapes and sizes, is a complex type with the particularity of the fusion of the central tower, originally single, with six later buildings, joined to one another by curtain walls, which surround it.

ee3e26c4c48ba81e.text: The imposing hypogeum of Sas Puntas, cut into a low limestone bench a short distance from the settlement, reproduces a giants' tomb in full, both in its exedra façade and inside, with an elliptical burial chamber. The tomb belongs to the category of tombs with an architectural façade, also known as "Nuragic domus", that is, hypogeal burials cut into the rock, often by reusing pre-existing Neolithic domus de janas.

ee54e9f73db79d2a.text:
The main monument stands on a plateau in a commanding position. It is a single-tower nuraghe built in regular courses of well-worked trachyte blocks. The entrance, oriented S-SE, has been horribly altered into a pointed-arch opening, because the nuraghe was long used as a pigsty.

Above it the relieving window survives. A corridor 4 m long and 1.00–2.00 m wide, corbel-vaulted in the first part and flat-lintelled in the second, leads into the chamber.

ee6de48669b12b81.text: We are faced with only a few elementary basal circles of the construction, which appear with stones arranged in courses, some of which are disordered and affected by collapse. Interesting are certain constructional details that highlight even more the genius loci of those who commissioned its building.

ee85d08721943851.text: The single-tower nuraghe currently preserves a standing height of five or six courses, and the ground plan of the lower chambers is quite easy to make out. On the west side of the corridor the stairwell opens, still retaining eight steps in place, which originally curved following the circular line of the perimeter wall.

ee8fa2caf156014a.text: Complex nuraghe consisting of a tower with an added structure, built of trachyte.

eea87621066960dd.text:
The nuraghe forms the central nucleus of an articulated system of enclosures, the first of which is a massive wall that in several places incorporates the natural rock. Inside this perimeter a second courtyard develops in two semicircular arms that lean against the tower.

The tower itself has a slightly elliptical plan and its perimeter wall also incorporates stretches of natural rock.

eeb272ad30c5a586.text: It stands on the summit of the mountain of the same name. Hard to reach by climbing the slopes from the village of Bottidda below, it is more easily reached from the nearby road to Foresta Burgos. From its ruins one can admire the view over the valley below, known as "Su Campu".

eec12bf89d783ced.text: The complex comprises a corridor nuraghe with an attached settlement and a giants' tomb. The proto-nuraghe was entered through an opening at the north-western corner. A short distance from the nuraghe the remains of several huts from the ancient village can be identified.

eec69d7c9d8350ad.text: The building, of complex type, incorporates an earlier structure within its bastion at the western end of the rocky spur: probably a pseudo-nuraghe, whose ground plan cannot be determined because of its poor state of preservation. The outer wall face is legible only on the north-east side and consists of basalt blocks laid in irregular courses that incorporate outcrops of natural rock.

ef07978c2436f22c.text: Single-tower nuraghe in good condition; the lintel and the access to the staircase leading to the upper floor are missing. Maximum height five metres.

ef1139cb5a5130df.text: Nuraghe Muromoi overlooks a village of huts. It is a complex nuraghe that is hard to read because it is hidden by a conspicuous collapse. A central tower and the traces of lateral towers built with roughly dressed andesite blocks can nevertheless be made out. A small village of huts extends to the south-east.

ef13c293be82f9a0.text: Complex nuraghe, a main tower with a second tower added to the front. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

ef1c4173d4b34551.text: It has an irregular pyramidal shape with the face oriented to the south-south-east. The boulder retains the natural roughness of the rock from which it was hewn in places, but shows traces of working. The slightly rounded upper part bears signs of working and smoothing.

ef38ee2d96915e25.text: The temple, built of irregular blocks of granite, porphyry and more rarely limestone, consists of two quadrangular rooms leading into a circular chamber that preserved an altar inside reproducing two nuraghe towers. Outside, a structure with an irregular rectangular plan yielded an extraordinary deposit of votive bronzes, dedicated to the deity during the cults.

ef3e425b7c7441c6.text: Among the evidence of funerary hypogeism in the Usini area, the Iscala de Sa Figu necropolis, although mentioned in the literature for its five domus de janas, has not yet been the subject of specific analysis. Following detailed reports, research and surveys using different methodologies, both traditional and innovative, were carried out at the site. These operations made it possible to identify two further hypogea and to verify previously undocumented symbols.

ef467964a1bb0e3e.text: Nestled in the Lanaitto valley, the village of Sa Sedda e Sos Carros (literally “the crossing point of the carts”) dates from a period between the Recent Bronze Age and the Early Iron Age (12th–9th centuries BC). It is particularly important for the presence of traces of metal smelting and working in the Nuragic period. It consists of numerous huts, with circular and oval plans, among which one is of particular interest for its ritual religious function.

ef74bb418164333f.text: The nuraghe Tinteriè appears to be a single-tower nuraghe with very irregular masonry. It has a circular plan 12 m in diameter and preserves its entrance intact; this leads into a curvilinear corridor 4.50 m long roofed with flat slabs. On the left inside the passage is the stairwell, while the interior is blocked by collapse.

ef761d7c1cc2d0a8.text:
The site is distinguished by the presence of a Nuragic-period settlement documented by the discovery, during private building work, of wall structures attributable to the Iron Age.

It consists of a stretch of a structure in isodomic ashlars of tufaceous marl datable to Early Iron Age, whose function has not yet been clarified.

ef78ec3a3ad5aa08.text: Proto-nuraghe with an elliptical or sub-elliptical profile

efa6a320cb0a18ca.text: The hypogean necropolis of "Sa Perda Puntunta", better known as "Roccia dell'Elefante", consists of two domus de janas: the first is in the upper part of a large trachyte boulder and only traces of three chambers remain; the second tomb opens a little lower down on the same boulder, consists of four small cells, and is interesting and very well known for the presence of bull's-head protomes carved on the walls of the first chamber.

efbe457f32e012ba.text: Situated about 300 metres north-east of the Nuraghe Su Figu and less than 600 metres south-east of the Nuraghe Columbos, the monument is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, a maximum surviving height of 3.65 m and five courses. The entrance, facing south-east and with a rectangular opening, is raised 0.40 m above ground level by a threshold slab and is topped by a well-finished lintel resting on jambs that stand out from the rest of the masonry for the better dressing of the stones.

efcaf3adf27d03d0.text: The spring consists of a main horseshoe-shaped body and a front enclosure of which a semicircular sector survives. The spring was already frequented in the pre-Nuragic period, as shown by some stemmed obsidian arrowheads and especially a ceramic fragment decorated in the Ozieri style.

effabf17344f11ca.text:
It is an architectural-façade tomb, that is, a hypogeal tomb that reproduces in rock the external façade of a Nuragic giants' tomb, with an arched stele and an exedra.

In the early medieval period it was reused as a rock-cut chapel (its dedication is unknown).

f003b6a8bf755291.text: The arcosolium-type hypogeum with a rectangular basin, cut into the limestone ridge like the domus de janas, showed two distinct deposition levels; the upper one with the remains of 8 inhumations; the lower one with 5 inhumations. The nuraghe has not been located.

f01326ffe7eb1180.text: Situated on the slopes of the Còrongiu Sènes hill. It has a longitudinal layout. Chambers built in progressive heightening from the entrance inwards, consisting of an antechamber and two cells with entrances almost perfectly aligned. The domus is entered through an elliptical opening. The first cell has a sub-rectangular plan, where traces of working consisting of slight vertical grooves are evident. The second cell is sub-elliptical in shape with traces of working.

f01796c728e9944f.text: The nuraghe has been destroyed; only a few traces of wall face remain, observed in various sectors of the hill.

f03beccf16c9609c.text: Only a few remains of the nuraghe survive.

f04151eb611926ed.text: The nuraghe of Santa Lucia di Assolo stands in the countryside, within the archaeological area that includes the rural church dedicated to the same saint. It has a single-tower structure of truncated-conical shape; at present the base is visible, consisting of four superimposed dry-stone courses made of large stone blocks.

f0483ed2ddaeab78.text: Reused in the Roman period and as a position during the Second World War.

f082fef7375b0b2a.text: It is a sacred area composed of seven menhirs, six of which are heaped nearby about ninety metres to the west, piled up during land-clearing work. This one, however, simply lies on the ground, unique in the area, finely shaped, 6.20 m long.

f0856e4ab16ea083.text: The monument, legible in its various component parts, is notable in particular for the large trapezoidal stele. It stands in the locality of the same name in the municipality of Aidomaggiore.

f0ac2204107febff.text: Poor visibility and the vegetation cover prevent a proper reading of the monument. Part of the east and north sides can be seen, with a wall face built of large polygonal basalt blocks laid in four to five courses to a height of 3–3.50 m. The whole building is buried to a considerable depth, especially on the western side. The inner chamber has collapsed and the surviving part is filled with collapse debris, as can be seen from the top of the nuraghe.

f0cec45c461ebfbe.text: The Nuragic structure of Donna Ciccia is of interest; its name comes from the place-name of one of the plots of land on which it stands; locally it is better known as "sa traversa" because the roads to Sassari and Ozieri cross there. The colour of the stones used in its construction immediately catches the eye. It is still partly visitable despite being in an advanced state of decay. I would invite any reporters to do so with good reason "and not by hearsay".

f0dd300ecfbccfc6.text: It is very ruinous and covered by dense vegetation.

f0df513b06bf5474.text: Of the monument, now destroyed, only two alignments of roughly squared sandstone blocks that define the corridor are just visible above ground. The front part and the apse are not currently visible.

f0fa400be632b8dd.text: It is a fine example of a nuraghe built with a subsidiary staircase and a sub-floor chamber. It can be entered to reveal its structure, which rises with blocks of friable white limestone inside a grove of oaks, ashes and yews that make the setting pleasant and evocative. It is almost entirely covered by fill earth that has fallen from the slope, so that it is nearly completely buried. Nuraghe of the valley of the judge, of the king of Torres.

f0fa9827787a431c.text: The well-known necropolis of Noeddale lies on the western edge of a saddle that drops steeply to the west towards the Sae valley. It consists of six hypogea, three cut into a gently sloping limestone outcrop, one into a low rock face below, and two more into a higher rock face. Two hypogea are preceded by short dromoi.

f10bca532c578709.text: Single-tower nuraghe built of trachyte and andesite blocks. It survives to a height of about 3 metres above the present ground level.

f13fa83328c540a1.text: They lie within the municipal territory of Sassari. They are two Abealzu culture hypogea cut into the limestone, a short distance from each other, on the left side of the SS131 heading towards Porto Torres. The entrances of the domus are barely perceptible to anyone walking along the track that runs alongside them and leads into a built-up area, because they are completely overgrown with spontaneous vegetation.

f1474a6b0ddc0560.text: In very poor condition, completely ruined, only a couple of courses are visible.

f163fa4505e2d2e9.text: Unfortunately no significant structure remains, as it was completely destroyed together with the village of the same period. On the surface it yields evidence of a hilltop settlement attributable to the early phases of the Middle Bronze Age (17th–16th century BC); indeed, fragments of obsidian, sherds of Nuragic pottery and stone tools have been recovered, indicating the existence of domestic shelters.

f16d707c0938a632.text: It stands on the banks of Lake Cuga and spends a good part of the year under its waters. It too belongs to the nuraghi of the Cuga valley.

f180c4a9a91d5803.text: The nuraghe is in very poor condition, certainly reused over time for various purposes.

f18263b9f271a827.text: It consists of a rectangular doorway leading into a small antechamber originally roofed. This is followed by a doorway with four rebates arranged like steps to receive the closing slab. The tomb is single-chambered and the walls are carefully worked. In the small antechamber, on the right-hand wall and in the ceiling of the left-hand side, there are traces of red ochre that must originally have coloured the whole chamber. Copper Age material (Monte Claro culture) comes from this domus de janas.

f1aca344b24af90b.text: Ruined nuraghe, of which 5 or 6 courses survive.

f1b34acd672aac8a.text: Three single-chambered domus de janas with a rectangular doorway

f1d2685dd311cf87.text:

I. Giants' tomb with stele, attributed to the Middle Bronze Age I (16th–15th century BC).

II. Neolithic tomb.

III. Punic burial.

f1d287418cec35e7.text:
Giants' tomb dating to the Middle Bronze Age. It lies in the immediate vicinity of the equipped area of Sa Sinèpida.

f1d4cd26ffccc9e9.text:
They are two hypogea.

They lie just outside the settlement, about 800 m away. They are reached via the farm track that leads towards Murruzzone and Su Lu'e. Only one of the two is in good condition, but its interior is small; it stands on an isolated rock outcrop with its entrance facing east, the first in the photo. The other appears heavily damaged and overgrown with brambles, as shown in the image below. The two 'oncheddas are about 100 m apart.

f1d9cdd139126f02.text: The giants' tomb Su Pranu est is not in an optimal state of preservation, but its fundamental components can still be made out. In the facade only a few blocks of the exedra remain in their original positions; at the centre stands the monumental monolithic arched stele, which has the peculiarity of lacking a doorway. The stele is now broken in two, uprooted and lying overturned on the remains of the chamber. The tomb can be dated to the beginning of the Bronze Age, about 1800 BC.

f1f4a81476255798.text: Ruined and buried complex nuraghe whose structure cannot be defined

f217c76777fe6f46.text: The probable staircase can be seen. The tholos has collapsed.

f21d9fce71306b4c.text: The nuraghe, located in a grazing area on a granite outcrop, is irreparably destroyed. Its lintelled entrance can still be seen, filled with collapse debris. As for the chamber, again because of the collapsed state of the nuraghe, only a short stretch on the northern side can be made out.

f2270071e8640dea.text: The nuraghe is now reduced to a heap of enormous ashlars, though the base circumference can still be made out.

f242d4c2cfaeca2c.text: This singular monument, composed of two superimposed towers, stands alone on a very high and impressive cliff overlooking the great valley of the Rio S'Acqua Callenti, right near its junction with the Flumendosa valley.

f269cdddefdd5b25.text: It consists of a central nucleus attributable to the type of the so-called “corridor nuraghi”, which are older and structurally different from the “tholos nuraghi” (because the roof is not a false dome but flat-arched), in which two chambers can be identified: one is circular, with a diameter of about 7 metres, the other oval, with a diameter of about 8 metres, connected to each other by a “flat-arched covered corridor”.

f27bf499dfc42fb3.text:
The Domus de Janas of Sant'Andrìa are in the municipality of Mara (Sassari), in the rural locality of "Sant'Andrìa", from which they take their name.

They consist of a single "niche", set in dense vegetation.

They are easy to find; they can be seen from the road to Bonu Ighinu, high up on the left.

f2a1469247b67cb6.text: Nuraghe reported on Wikimapia, unnamed, in the locality of Punta Sa Cresia

f2a8f2b27ec35b29.text: Nuragic village of the Recent and Final Bronze Age I

f2a9d1c23abc3a0e.text: The nuraghe stands on a low hill in an area now used for pasture and arable land. Its very poor state of preservation makes it impossible to determine its type or analyse its architectural development. A stretch of the outer perimeter survives, forming a semicircle. The blocks that make up the masonry are of granite, only roughly dressed and of medium–large size; in the short visible stretch they are laid in irregular courses.

f2af8abee2b63789.text: It includes several tafoni that are thought to have been used for both funerary and habitation purposes.

f2b438aef4d1115e.text: A nuraghe that was demolished to build a radar base on the Is Ebbas headland in 1965, called Nuraghe Is Ebbas or Nuraghe Su Brecconi. Information from local elders.

f2bf2c426f63ff4e.text:
Trilobate nuraghe (?) on the summit of the Ghilotta hill, built with polygonal blocks of the local volcanic rock.

The towered monument is surrounded by a village of circular huts whose perimeter walls survive to a fair height. Collapses and vegetation make the complex hard to read.

At the south-east edge of the complex the Case Lenzu, an agro-pastoral farm of the medau type, have been extensively altered in recent times.

f2c3c9b2a59d69a8.text: The concentration of menhirs in this area is remarkable; they are in close continuity with those of Ovau, S'Aspiddarju and Teularju. The menhir FIRULI nearby is 6.60 metres long.

f2c4c0916b4388fb.text: Subtrapezoidal in plan, it stands on a granite outcrop. It is built of large granite blocks laid in polygonal masonry. The only well-worked block is the lintel, with a sub-triangular section shaped to divert the thrust of the overlying structures onto the jambs. On the more accessible sides, to the west and east, the nuraghe is enclosed by a curtain wall, of which the west stretch survives for about 17 m.

f2c82eb40ec06195.text: A. Moravetti describes it as a nuragic enclosure

f2c99517e7dc5fa3.text: Corridor nuraghe in a good state of preservation

f302a1b77171a55e.text: A single-tower nuraghe of which very little remains

Unfortunately the latest restoration work has not had the desired effect, since the workforce and the site directors have not always been up to the task. The area that was meant to be equipped for groups leaves much to be desired. The interior spaces, on the other hand, are interesting (when they are not full of water), as are the engravings/drawings on the walls.

f376d0b367dce40e.text: It is impossible to enter because of the conspicuous collapse that has affected the entrance area.

f39a942d57b139de.text: Nuraxi Fenu, inside which, during the excavations, remains of a hearth and animal bones, fragments of Roman pottery and a coin datable to the 3rd century AD were found, allowing a sporadic occupation of the site between the 2nd and 3rd centuries AD to be hypothesised. A violent fire marked the end of the Nuragic occupation, although it was sporadically frequented in the Punic and Roman periods.

f3a3d3a892ffa9ed.text: The nuraghe is a single-tower structure on two levels, elliptical in shape, which makes use of natural rock outcrops into which it is fitted. Because of its poor state of preservation it is not clearly legible.

f3a46a07ce3a0a73.text: From the upper floor of the nuraghe, to the north-east, there is a view over the village with huts that can still be made out amid dense vegetation and among the various collapses.

f3b2acdc7a0d8204.text: The nuraghe is in very poor condition amid the dense woods of Scala Argiolas, the ancient entrance to the Giara plateau.

f3b3c1af43ef1439.text: One of the very many nuraghi in this area, situated near three giants' tombs

f3d10a55b2c66ede.text: A collective burial of the Nuragic period. Of the monument, hidden by the Mediterranean scrub bushes that cover it, the corridor, the exedra, and inside it the dentilled stele that adorned the facade can be made out.

f423dcd210ef0792.text: Single-chambered domus de janas cut into the trachyte

f45da258f064349b.text: Multi-tower proto-nuraghe, almost completely destroyed. With its height it dominates the whole "Su Padru" area. The name comes from the fact that the nuraghe stands on a very pointed hill, hence Punzu Rudu.

f47cb66549d8acd4.text: A small, isolated domus de janas, very unusual for the presence of a rock-cut wine press (ancient vats for treading grapes to obtain must) on the rock into which it was cut

f47d19cfceeefad7.text: In very poor condition, the outer megalithic circle destroyed to make room for pasture; in this nuraghe a bronze model boat was found and stolen, the largest ever discovered in Sardinia, as much as 38 cm long, called the Sun King's boat, now kept in the Sanna Archaeological Museum in Sassari.

f49006a28db8618c.text: The nuraghe stands near the coast of Trinità d'Agultu, south of Isola Rossa. It has an almost elliptical plan and can be reached from the hamlet of Paduledda by taking the road to “La Scalitta”.

f4919576d2c121cc.text: A kind of ceremonial altar of uncertain date. Situated in the immediate vicinity of the nuraghe and Nuragic village of the same name.
