f4bb53af72c53186.text: It stands on the summit of the hill of the same name. At first sight it looks like a single-tower nuraghe partly buried, but it is probably a multi-lobed one. The lintel above the entrance is very unusual, being slightly curved. The main entrance has a pointed vault. It too is semi-buried, for its lintel is only a few centimetres above the ground.

f550c4ac582b7b54.text: This nuraghe is unique in the Pattada area, because it is built of boulders that are distinctly smaller than average, except for the beams and lintels. Its structure suggests that it is a proto-nuraghe (1800–1600 BC).

f55cdea5f0cd56c4.text: The oval perimeter outline survives intact. The outer wall face reaches its greatest height on the west-facing side, where eight courses of polyhedral blocks can be counted. Unfortunately the interior is covered with vegetation and collapse, which prevents the contents from being seen.

f55d0efab5cb5dfa.text:
The structure consists of a large horizontal basalt slab resting on seven smaller stones that form a polygonal chamber. Around it is a circle of stones that must have retained the earth forming the covering mound.

The construction of this funerary monument is dated to the third millennium BC.

f55daf4229a67ee3.text: Complex nuraghe consisting of three interconnected towers. The structure shows heavy disturbance by tomb robbers.

f582ac75132cb3a5.text: It comprises at least seven hypogea, largely compromised by collapses and extensive reuse.

f587316a48eb3340.text: The monument, built in polygonal masonry with granite stones, is of the corridor type and has a sub-circular plan; the entrance leads, through a small lintelled corridor, to a central circular chamber without a roof, which gave access to two further chambers, now inaccessible because of collapses.

f58748b4e7edfb53.text: During the earthworks for the road that leads from Santu Miali down to the church of Santa Maria de Aidos, a burial was destroyed that was probably a giants' tomb or perhaps a medieval tomb. A dark trachyte lintel can still be seen in its original position.

f58789204a38c8f3.text: A small alignment of menhirs appears on the slope leading to Mamucada inside the plot of sa Figu on the border with the land of Padedda. On closer inspection they seem little worked and of a shape vaguely comparable to a pyramid prism with a polygonal base that is never the same. According to the old people most of them come from the steep part of Badde Saltara, which looks over the plain of S.M de Orria Pitzinna. mu

f58e05194543ceb9.text:
It consists of a hundred Nuragic huts reused in the Roman period.

Near the village there is also a Nuragic well and what appear to be some menhirs.

f58f1902cab54c35.text:
Other towers, perhaps five in number, lean against the central tower. The whole complex is hard to survey because of the trees and tangled thorny bushes that block access (just as well!). Inside, almost the entire structure can be visited and the harmonious development of the whole massive and majestic construction can be appreciated.

The word ùi, which is probably Paleo-Sardinian.

f5b2d63e141f7165.text: They are three isolated tombss in the municipality of Mamoiada

f5b50a933890f662.text: In the broad and complex picture of the island's hypogean architecture, the majestic necropolises of Mesu 'e Montes, S'Adde 'e Asile, S'Isterridolzu, Noeddale, Su Littu, and the Tomb of Littos Longos have provided extremely significant data for understanding the phenomenon of hypogeism. The entrance is characterised by a long dromos cut into the limestone. Inside, bull's-head protomes and other carved decorations.

f5f5545418180708.text: The well consists of a rectangular, paved atrium that leads to the stairwell through a strongly tapering trapezoidal passage; the stairwell, about 6 metres long, leads down to the underground chamber, which is sub-circular and covered by a tholos, where the water table is intercepted. The structure is built of local marl blocks, regularly squared, bush-hammered and laid in staggered courses with earth inserted between the bedding planes.

f60dcaa3fa7bab60.text:
In a dominant and strategically privileged position.

It is a single-tower nuraghe with an added structure, a circular chamber with three niches arranged in a cross.

Because of the collapse, the entrance to the south-east is not currently detectable, nor are the corridor and any subsidiary spaces (niche and/or staircase), although their presence can be considered certain given the evolved type of the chamber.

f613b83ada713f78.text:
These are two single-chamber hypogea cut into a trachyte outcrop at an elevation of 190 metres.

Wrapped in dense, impenetrable vegetation, they are very difficult to find.

f6327688ca2f5c4f.text: The tomb is cut into a bank of granitic rock; it consists of a dromos and a chamber in which a small niche has been carved. The hypogeum opens on a gentle slope a few centimetres above ground level.

f639262e3349aa36.text: Dolmen consisting of a large covering slab supported by three upright orthostats

f63b1f8e424adb01.text: A collective burial of the Nuragic period. The monument is built in isodomic masonry with well-squared and finished basalt elements, found both in their original position and incorporated into the surrounding dry-stone enclosure walls. The corridor with the terminal head slab, the exedra with the central slab in which the entrance doorway is cut, and the dentilled stele are visible.

f63d89bd50809220.text:
The monument has a fairly complex plan characterised by successive additions to the main body; the latter has an elliptical plan with a maximum diameter of 13.5 m and is provided with two entrances, to the north and south-west, which give access to two corridors that join at right angles at the centre of the central tower.

Two structures abut the central tower: one is on the north side, the other must have encircled at least two-thirds of the whole.

f644622b6b8c9b0d.text: Single-tower nuraghe, partially collapsed, situated on a trachyte rise near the Cuga valley.

f674d3f5d3b021e8.text: Single-tower nuraghe of large roughly dressed limestone blocks with the entrance facing south-east. The superstructure survives to a maximum height of 2.50 m. The stair is to the left of the entrance. The nuraghe is very hard to see because it is covered in vegetation.

f67971527f6c581f.text: Simple nuraghe, completely ruined, reduced to a heap of rough blocks about 2 metres high.

f67b4bed0b90390d.text: Datable to the 13th century BC. Belonging to the Albucciu nuraghe. In this tomb the rectangular body, of flat slabs, is surrounded by a mound of rubble. The exedra is reduced to a series of blocks and small slabs that deprive the monument of the sense of grandeur that characterises the other megalithic burials. The wall thickness of the tomb is remarkable, at about 6 metres. The structure has undergone alterations in different periods and has been reused several times.

f6abda7cd426bf59.text: Complex nuraghe with settlement. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

f6c3a122942a31e6.text: The exceptional nature of the Pranu Siara site lies in particular in the fact that the tomb is not isolated but forms part of an extensive necropolis perfectly aligned for several hundred metres and overlooked, at the change in level, by a kind of fortified enclosure that appears to protect the plateau, following settlement models of a similar type documented in the north-western area of the island, in the Olmedo and Castelsardo zones.

f6d1af4d6ca11320.text:
It is a single-tower nuraghe with a niche, a corridor staircase, and a chamber flanked by two niches.

The tower, circular in plan (diam. 11.60 m), survives to a maximum height of 6.00 m with 14 courses to the north-west, while at the entrance the elevation reaches 5.20 m over 11 courses: the south-west wall, by contrast, has largely collapsed.

f6d76858a0c60287.text: Single-tower nuraghe, half-destroyed, at Su Billianu in Uri

f6eedb7cbdfc8ddf.text: Probable complex nuraghe, now ruined and difficult to interpret

f7085f2892398844.text: Two huts with sacred functions are present. One, Structure A, is semicircular and much larger than Structure B.

f73daf49bfff75c8.text: Nuraghe of undetermined type; only a few remains survive on the site among the vegetation. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

f73f6be823ce93d0.text:
Remains of a megalithic tomb which, from what can be seen, appears to be decidedly a dolmen.

Only one orthostat remains in situ (width 1.52 – thickness 0.40 – visible height 1.10), while numerous other slabs lie overturned in the area in front of the exedra. The capstone lies broken in several fragments; the existence of the peristalith can be inferred.

f74c016b9d786654.text: Single-tower nuraghe. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

f74f1f085cefbd57.text: The dolmenic tomb stands on a modest rocky rise, about 200 metres north-west of the giants' tomb of the same name and less than 500 metres south-east of the Nuraghe Cherbos. The burial chamber, of a vaguely quadrangular shape, is bounded by five stones set on edge that appear to rest directly on the outcropping rock. The cover consists of a polygonal slab, now slightly tilted by the fall of an orthostat and with widespread chipping, thinner than the supports.

f767fbc5d1c7449c.text: Complex nuraghe visible seasonally depending on the water level of the Cuga reservoir. A substantial village stood around the nuraghe.

f771b3b38e61fc3a.text: Situated a short distance from the Durane stream, the tomb has a burial chamber about 9 metres long and a broad exedra on the front, 14 metres long. It is built entirely of granite with ashlars laid in regular courses. The central part has the entrance doorway surmounted by the so-called “dentilled ashlar”. The large exedra, provided with bench-seats for pilgrims to rest on, contains a small baetyl to the east, which must have been an object of worship.

f782502dedad9526.text: (From Mitz'arramini, the locality where it stands), it is a complex multi-tower nuraghe near which a village is also present. The vaulted building, with a toponym recalling copper, where the central tower and a secondary tower are clearly identifiable but unfortunately still sealed by aeolian and agricultural deposits for lack of thorough investigations.

f79e1f9d0c05b770.text: Su Stampu de su Turrunu o de su Turnu is a remarkable swallow hole and resurgence, formed by the rio e Spinedda, whose waters pour out in a cascade from a hole in the rock, falling into the centre of a delightful pool.

f7a1960119590c79.text: Only small portions of the wall of the nuraghe remain. The collapse makes it impossible to read the plan.

f7a59fefd43d79f0.text:
Only a few boulders of the basal circle survive. They are of hard white tuff that is still friable. It stands right above the curvilinear alignment of the mountain ridge where several domus de janas are visible on the ridge of the same mountain and on the slope.

Nuraghe del monte forato. See Mònte pertùsu.

f7d0ffbe10e3373e.text: Archaic corridor nuraghe with an ellipsoidal–sub-quadrangular plan, built of polygonal basalt blocks. A few basal courses remain visible for less than 2 m in height. The nuraghe stands on a solid foundation of outcropping bedrock that forms an integral part of the structure.

f7e2745200540474.text: The Tolinu nuraghe, set in a fine position on a plateau overlooking the Tirso valley, is an imposing complex Nuragic monument composed of a large central tower of truncated-conical shape surrounded by a bastion that incorporates several smaller towers.

f7ed994da8c83104.text: On the site a few large slabs can be seen, partly embedded in the ground, partly broken and not in situ, which may belong to a dolmen-type structure. Although no archaeological material is found on the ground, the shape and size of the blocks suggest that the site should be included among areas at risk. The name recalls other dolmen toponyms.

f7f4c8b7dd4dfc5f.text: Externally two small windows are visible, 1.6 m above the floor level, about 35 cm square. The entrance opening, 1.60 m high and 1.30 m wide, has a step down of 35 cm leading into the chamber. About 4 m wide, 3 m deep and 2.5 m high, it has at its centre a circular pit 60 cm across and 10 cm deep, set slightly to the right of the entrance.

f804e5469d184ec2.text: Against an enclosure of probable Nuragic origin stands a block of red trachyte that at first glance looks like a hatch or an entrance slab. Irregularly parallelepiped in shape, its visible face shows a surface on two offset levels. In the upper level, at the ends, there are two holes, one round and the other rectangular.

f82e6fa968831119.text: It appears as a heap of stones and a few large blocks of red sandstone, situated on ground excluded from cultivation and grazing, near the Anghelu Ruiu necropolis. State of preservation: poor.

f83b987b336768aa.text: A single-tower nuraghe of limestone, about half covered by vegetation, stands on the edge of a cultivated area inside a bend of the Riu Filibertu. State of preservation: good. The existence of a surrounding village is hypothesised.

f845fe40cb8ec562.text:
Angius with the name “Macariu 1849. Taramelli. and 1883 land register. Also Girillis.

It is a single-tower nuraghe built of trachyte, its structure hard to read because of the dense vegetation. Inside, the outline of the tower is partly distinguishable. Next to the nuraghe are structures probably belonging to the village. The area also contains several pottery fragments.

f84be14d210d8c80.text: Like many others, in total ruin. Enough evidence of the ancient construction can still be distinguished, with some boulders of the basal circle visible. Unfortunately, in the 1960s several sites in the area disappeared because of land-reclamation works, but above all because of the construction of the reservoir dam, which never fully served its intended purpose. Nuraghe of the hill of the deer. See Montìju de chèlvos I.mu

f86b3c41e6b8c2de.text: Archaic corridor nuraghe. The building stands on a valley floor just 4 m from the watercourse called Riu e'Sa Tanca, on its eastern bank. It is completely covered by vegetation, in particular dense bramble thickets growing abundantly along the stream banks make observation difficult. Some large polygonal basalt blocks laid one on another can be seen on the north and east sides.

f86f82064355b713.text: A structure whose ground plan is not easily interpreted

f87196502bd98591.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe, built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The structures are almost completely covered by vegetation. The superimposed blocks of the southern side can be seen, surviving to a height of just over 2.50 m. The rest of the building cannot be observed because of poor visibility. Piles of collapsed blocks are visible on the small slope to the south of the nuraghe.

f89844ce83439de1.text: Single-tower nuraghe, in poor condition; traces of an intra-mural staircase and lateral niches are visible. At the best-preserved point the nuraghe rises for about 3 m with six courses of roughly dressed boulders.

f89dd727c4f245f5.text: In this area there are 11 menhirs and a cup-marked stele, most of them in granite. None of them has kept its original position; almost all are broken, probably knocked over by machinery during land improvements.

f8a7a7f7a4a5066e.text: The whole area between the domus de janas necropolis and the church of Santo Stefano is rich in tafoni rocks adapted into niches and large niches, where it is often difficult to distinguish the action of nature from that of man. In particular, around the church five sites with carved rocks can be identified:

f8b84bc99e1b017b.text: Single-tower nuraghe, built of limestone blocks, of which 1–2 courses of the outer wall face survive.

f8c85955ead52a60.text: Single-tower nuraghe with its tholos still intact

f8e9b0f387b41e54.text: About 200 m from the rise in the ground that marks the nuraghe, to the north-north-east, a settlement is visible covering an area of 600–700 sq m and showing a series of rooms with a quadrilateral plan bounded by large trachyte boulders.

f909c7ac01cea8dd.text: The necropolis is cut into a granite outcrop on the Buddusò plateau. It consists of 6 hypogea and is dated to 3200–2800 BC. Some domus de janas have single-chambered rooms while others have a multi-chambered plan. One of the domus de janas shows traces of red wall painting in parallel bands on raised bands.

f948b1e845f77d37.text:
The nuraghe, set on the summit of the rise, is very badly damaged.

It consists of a circular tower and an eccentric elliptical curtain wall elongated towards the south-east, where the entrance presumably lay.

f96370418bbe8e11.text:
Nuraghe. It stands on top of a hill, with a view over the locality of sa Gruttixedda (Nuragic Well/Village).

Covered with large stones and vegetation.

f98302bd9075f52f.text: In its present condition no scatter of lithic or ceramic material is visible on the ground; however, the presence of structures belonging to a possible village cannot be ruled out, their remains may have been obliterated at the surface by changes in land use.

f9a5e072dac89868.text: Tholos nuraghe. There were two towers; one has been completely dismantled to build the drystone wall that runs along the mountain. On the south-east side the tower stands over 4 m high, while the interior is blocked by a layer of earth and debris that makes it inaccessible. Beside it is a cave recently explored by the Uras caving group.

f9afde37a6e644d4.text: It overlooks the Monte Ozzastru valley, a short distance from the Porchiles nuraghe, and only the base of the monument is visible.

f9bfb89fb91ce480.text: Nuraghe Carcina stands in the countryside of Orroli, about 1.5 km south-east of the village. It is abandoned but in fair condition. It appears as a complex nuraghe with two towers clearly visible. The main tower has a surviving height of over 3 metres and is entered through a doorway topped by a fine sloping lintel. This doorway is largely buried and gives access to a chamber with a tholos that is missing its top courses.

f9c315ab016e26fe.text: Of the nuraghe, which is in very poor condition, only a few large trachyte boulders remain; they formed the basal course and today barely convey the idea of the circular ground plan.

f9e26b52a065f70a.text: The tomb, situated beside a lane and built of courses of large blocks, has its exedra facing south and a partially damaged gallery. Scattered blocks and large heaps of clearance stones can be seen nearby.

fa03111ac3187ba2.text: Ruins of the base drum of a classic single-tower nuraghe in polygonal masonry, with a maximum surviving height of about 4 m, an internal chamber roofed with a tholos and provided with a small subsidiary niche, and an entrance stair – unfortunately completely destroyed – defended by an opposing guard chamber. The building, already dismantled in Roman times, was reused, incorporating five fragments of figured statue-menhirs that already existed in the area.

fa1ff845685f491c.text: The domus de janas necropolis is cut into a basalt outcrop overlooking the Riu Mannu valley, along the provincial road from Suni to Pozzomaggiore, in the Planargia region of north-western Sardinia. The hypogean complex comprises 12 single-chamber and multi-chamber burials, almost all accessed through a vestibule.

fa243a4645808007.text: Sacred area, probably pre-Nuragic. It consists of a rock ledge with niches, cupmarks and artificial basins. The hilltop is covered with collapse stones from a nuraghe.

fa2a800d2061a5b5.text: the rock visible at the site) and a landslide of small to medium-sized stones

fa7947fcf31658e4.text: It is an almost inaccessible site with a clear view of much of the nuraghi of the Ogliastra plain. I think it is a multi-lobed nuraghe, but between the vegetation and the collapse it is illegible. The photo I sent is the only part facing south from which anything can be understood; the rest is embedded among natural rocks and, I repeat, with the collapse nothing can be made out. The area is scattered with small terracotta ashlars. (Report by Daniele Murgia, Triei)

fa7e5213f7cfa712.text:
Nuragic sacred well with a circular chamber, originally covered by a tholos vault, now lost, preceded by a staircase of which seven steps remain.

The hypogean structure is built of andesite blocks laid in concentric courses, eight of which survive.

Groundwater still collects at the bottom of the chamber. The monument now stands inside a small fenced area.

faa2c4fa0c577fe4.text: A completely ruined giants' tomb of which only a few ashlars remain, and which is difficult to locate.

faa3a4b8c0f08c01.text: Site located in the Su Pranu area on a truncated-pyramidal hill. Here are found the remains of a nuraghe or, more probably, a small temple, attested by votive material found at the base of the site and along the ridges of the hillock; on its south-facing flank there are hypogeal tombs that are difficult to reach.

faa792395ac7ad13.text: The Sa Linnarta complex, a three-lobed nuraghe with numerous attached huts and a beautiful sacred well, is considered by experts to be one of the most important Nuragic finds in the Baronia.

faad4995253ac71c.text: Towards the road that leads from Samatzai onto the SS 128. On the right you reach the locality of Bidda Mendula. On a low sandstone promontory (altitude 150 m) the ruins of a nuraghe built of large sandstone marl blocks can be seen, belonging to a Nuragic settlement. On the surface a circular building is visible, probably a single-tower nuraghe, 14 m in diameter, which on the west side shows the remains of a facing wall 2.30 m thick, visible for several metres.

faf45d335e2c3b6e.text: Complex nuraghe consisting of a central tower and probably two other towers. Unfortunately the original structure is hidden by a conspicuous collapse and dense vegetation. Leaning against the central tower, on the front side, the structures of two probable towers can be glimpsed. To the north-east a rectangular room built in cyclopean masonry is visible, with a flat-lintelled roof.

fb0d2457164c04ea.text: The site comprises the nuraghe and the remains of an extensive village. The presence of two burials is also reported: a giants' tomb and a burial known as "dei gigli" because lilies appear to grow there in abundance.

fb182f0caf95328d.text: Su Scusorgiu: "Il Tesoro". In this hoard 40 complete Nuragic hilted swords were found. Now on display at the Cagliari Archaeological Museum.

fb18a5b9d3b2f7a7.text: It is the 'father of all nuraghi', the proto-nuraghe Madugui (its local name) or Maduli (its archaeological name), which towers over the south-eastern edge of the plateau, where it juts out furthest. Its walls now stand four and a half metres high, once higher. It is one of the most significant examples of the proto-nuragic (or pseudo-nuragic) type of building, the prototype of the 'corridor nuraghi', which later evolved into towers, or clusters of towers, closed by a corbelled dome (tholos).

fb301922607a2eac.text: In the centre of the village, research has shown "the existence of important portions of the Nuragic building still preserved around the water reservoir built on the site in the 1920s. Although the ancient building was used as a foundation for the modern one, the excavations have brought to light extensive portions of a tower displaying a massive fabric of polygonal basalt blocks".

fb6644344bea5b86.text: A single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. Almost completely destroyed, it appears as a heap of basalt stones. The first two courses of the base can be made out on the south side.

fb8985aded7908ce.text: Situated in the valley of the Rio Siniscola, a short distance from the river mouth, it has a rectangular plan with an internal elliptical chamber, survives to a height of about 2 metres, and is built of white limestone with schist inserts.

fb9499c609bafb9e.text: Baetyls placed near the Corbos nuraghe, used as gateposts for a metal gate

fb9e63b8625cf8c7.text: The tomb extends along a north-east/south-west major axis 5.50 m long and has its entrance opening to the south-west at the centre of a semicircular exedra that has almost entirely disappeared. The rear apse was probably straight-sided, but the closing masonry has not survived. It should be noted that the tomb is still largely buried, giving the impression that what is currently visible is actually the uppermost courses, lacking their covering.

fbb2eed84bd46dac.text: The spring has no steps and is in an almost perfect state of preservation[1]. The wall structure, entirely of granite, is completely preserved and the entrance to the inner chamber consists of a large vaulted opening. The spring is covered with two granite slabs. It encloses a spring vein, still active, and has a large threshold stone at the front with a channel cut into it for the water to drain away.

fbb3e610f2dae881.text: The Nuraghe Nuracale is a four-lobed type, consisting of a central tower, or central tower, surrounded by four smaller towers held together by massive straight walls. The main entrance, located in the east bastion, gives access to the internal courtyard, shaped like a half-moon, onto which open the entrance of the central tower and of the south-east and north-east lateral towers, while the other two towers were linked to the courtyard by two long corridors cut into the bastions.

fbb5a74985bbfa45.text: the two menhirs stand about fifty metres apart

fbba8f913b13c586.text: It is a hilltop surrounded by a wall probably of the Nuragic period, partly buried, never investigated, near which the baetyl (the Bulzi warrior's head) was found. From it one commands all the not few nuraghi that existed in the surrounding area.

fbbc493b97e8f1d7.text:
The monument stands on the edge of a rise looking towards Montagna di Sant'Antonio; the Nuragic tower is bounded on the west-south-west by the steep profile of the rock, while a quadrangular enclosure opens on the front.

The building is circular, but the western profile tends to be straight for a length of about 5 metres: the sector facing west-south-west cannot be surveyed because of the collapse and the dense shrub vegetation.

fbc25345bf108503.text: Collapsed nuraghe of which about six courses remain above ground

fbca86f75858ba19.text: It belongs to the group of nuraghi with a basement level, I say this with the benefit of inventory because survey is prevented by sturdy thorny plants that have colonised the structure. The basal circle is composed of vaguely squared boulders that interlock well, creating a regular wall face together with some natural rock outcrops. It has a raised entrance above ground level that highlights the sacred character of the construction.

fbef0f274d3b10c7.text: Nuraghe situated a few metres from the cliff created by the Carrabusu stream. Its state of preservation is precarious and the structure is partially buried.

fbfd681976746b46.text: The nuraghe was almost completely destroyed in the 1960s to obtain building stone for houses. Near the nuraghe there is a well of the same period, which presumably belonged to the building.

fc094f50a6b7c095.text: USAI (2014, p. 42) places it in the type of the "small nuraghi, presumably unfinished".

fc154a54a2ac1867.text: Buried nuraghe whose plan is not easy to understand. It was certainly complex and multi-lobed. The name indicates its probable function as a garrison for the landing place in the Nuragic period.

fc20f83eb4b7e08f.text: The place name certainly dates from the medieval period and is due to the fact that the nuraghe rises on the very outermost hilltop, directly overlooking the valley below. Several stone circles, variously collapsed, are still visible. The interior can be visited, and the entrance, rigidly oriented towards the south-south-east, can also be seen.

fc5030e9a5d685c4.text: Multi-lobed nuraghe. A nuraghe with the addition of two lateral towers linked to the original tower by a semi-circular corridor.

fc6b39cc50a65fdf.text: The Sos Muros complex covers an area of over twenty hectares with clear surface traces of circular huts and this sacred well.

fc6ecf5a0dbdcea3.text: Two small domus de janas visible from the road

fc707613e2068e85.text: A very unusual building, unique in shape. Known as the rectangular nuraghe. It stands on a stratified limestone outcrop shaped like a reproductive organ, around which the stream makes a loop. It may be a temple with buildings serving communal gatherings.

fc86be8b0caff09b.text: The surviving buried structure, for at least two metres below the present ground level, because the core has spilled out from inside the wall face, making it impossible to enter the internal chambers of the nuraghe, which is classified as a corridor nuraghe.

fcab5573bd524538.text: The condition of the domus de janas is unknown

fcb5ab8be88326d0.text:
Only a few of the basal stones remain. They are hard white tuff, still friable. They are located directly above the curved alignment along the mountain ridge, where several domus de janas are visible, extending along the crest of the named mountain and down its slope. www.archeologosardos.it

Nuraghe of the forated mountain. See Mònte pertùsu.

fccc75b5fbc13e1d.text: A collective burial of the Nuragic period. The monument is completely covered by a thicket of mastic, but the terminal part of the corridor is still visible.

fcd57e39e9c6e1a8.text: Domus de janas for which no description is available

fd0964e804d0836b.text:
The Nuraghe Tunis is in a precarious state of preservation, particularly the central tower and the southern parts of the four-lobed bastion; of the latter the two northern towers can be seen, with stretches of the three adjacent curtain walls, and the eastern boundary wall of the courtyard with the large window connected to the staircase leading to the wall-walks.

Around the ruins of the bastion, stretches of straight walls and parts of circular buildings emerge.

fd155c02bd32a2da.text: Near the Massidda or Ghisu medau two small dry-stone buildings with circular plans can still be seen, occupying two eminences overlooking the valley that slopes down to Porto Paglia: they are probably a single-tower nuraghe or a tower-hut and a smaller hut.

fd2177e6984fa4c7.text: It is undoubtedly the most imposing and best-preserved nuraghe in the Solarussa area. The layout is that of a tancato nuraghe, with a main tower and a secondary tower separated by a courtyard. The main tower is in good condition, with its tholos vault substantially intact. The secondary tower has partially collapsed, while the internal courtyard is blocked by the collapse debris.

fd23d4c303ffeef3.text: The megalithic structure is currently inside a sheepfold.

fd3383f2b505e42c.text: It lies in the area of the great Nurra land-reclamation scheme and is one of the nuraghi in the zone that has a mezzanine floor. A complex nuraghe of roughly dressed sandstone blocks, well preserved, it stands inside a private farm used for fruit and vegetable growing. It was reused during the Second World War by the construction of bunkers. In 1940–43 Nuraghe Cubalciada was incorporated into the defensive system of the 204th Coastal Division.

fd3f82b84c03b85c.text: Probable archaic nuraghe, with a semi-circular plan leaning against a rocky outcrop. Two menhirs present.

fd58b5336eaf9fdc.text: Dolmen II at Arbu, on the other hand, consists of a rectangular corridor (1.84 x 0.78/0.72 m) bounded on the long sides by carefully levelled natural rock and by an orthostat at the end; above it lies the covering slab (1.70 x 1.22 x 0.45 m thick).

fd83a28f99273c82.text: The tomb now consists only of a corridor, oriented along a SE–NW axis, bounded by orthostats and open at the short ends, which are now destroyed. Even in the absence of certain evidence, which could only come from an excavation that would clarify on which of the two sides the entrance opened, it can be assumed that, in keeping with what generally occurs in these tombs, it faced SE.

fd85671eecc1347f.text: The Nuraghe Agnu is built of granite, with a horseshoe plan because it is partly set against the rock face. It has a monumental entrance, oriented to the east and fitted with a lintel, leading into a corridor that was once fitted with a wooden sliding door descending from above. On the sides two corridors open; one leads to a domed cell, the other passes through the wall and out through the natural rock.

fd94a6f1c8ce55fb.text: Very ruinous: the masonry of vertical orthostats (cut), the closure of the mound and part of the exedra can still be made out.

fd987d6a233dc248.text:
The tower, truncated-conical in shape, shows a marked structural subsidence on the south side running from the entrance up to the top where the masonry is missing, also affecting part of the tholos.

From the entrance, oriented south/south-east and lacking its lintel, you enter a corridor that splays inwards with a partially surviving ogival roof. On the left side of the corridor the stairwell opens, roofed with flat slabs, of which three blocks remain.

fdc43627ba1d11b0.text: Reduced to a ruin like most of the other sites in the municipality of Chiaramonti. It does, however, show a few basal circles of cyclopean boulders, among which the main entrance stands out with its massive lintel facing south-south-east.

fe0340317c28f0c7.text: A ruined single-tower nuraghe; its position is uncertain, as it does not appear on the IGM map.

fe0bc79b77e531ad.text: The monument is a single-tower nuraghe with a staircase, a corridor niche, and a central chamber flanked by three niches in the classic cruciform layout. The masonry consists of large boulders in the lower courses and progressively smaller stones towards the top. Around the nuraghe are remains of the village to the east and a stretch of outer wall to the north.

fe1df8b11052f037.text: The giants' tomb lies in the municipality of Romana; the remains of the burial are visible, now set into a dry-stone wall.

fe21abc9cd50b160.text: Small atypical single-tower nuraghe, belonging to the Appiu village context. It stands at the end of a path that leads from the village to the Giants' Tomb, two small dolmens, and finally this small nuraghe.

fe3973eb52d17df1.text: The necropolis, dated to the second half of the 4th millennium BC and attributable to the Arzachena culture, consists of five stone cists, four of which are surrounded by circles of stones driven into the ground that originally marked the edge of the mound of earth and rubble raised over the burial.

fe3bfdbec79fdad3.text: Inside an olive grove, ploughing has brought to light numerous ceramic finds of various periods; among the prehistoric coarseware, fragments of typically Nuragic vessels such as cooking pots and baking trays can be identified without any doubt. No obvious structures are visible, as the site has undergone constant agricultural changes.

fe452ca654dee2e2.text: Unfortunately it has been almost entirely destroyed by stone-robbing. Only a very few blocks remain in their original position.

fe63d02db97953c6.text: The nuraghe is a complex structure consisting of a main tower to which two further towers, linked by a straight curtain wall, were added at later stages. The main tower, built of well-worked basalt blocks (especially in the upper parts) laid in regular courses, has its entrance to the north-east, topped by a lintel with a relieving window and raised above ground level.

fe76130759960867.text: Because of the collapse, which affects the entrance itself, it is not possible to enter the chamber. The polygonal masonry consists of well-shaped granite blocks with frequent use of wedges of the same stone. The base, by contrast, has a much more compact structure than the upper part of the monument, with large, roughly worked blocks.

fe7821f6883fa64a.text: The nuraghe consists of a main tower, two additional structures joined to it, remains of the outer wall along much of the perimeter, and the remains of several huts. It is not well preserved except for the main lintelled entrance with its relieving window and the remains of a staircase. A few dozen metres to the north-west there is a cave used as a necropolis. The skeletal remains have been studied and date to the Nuragic period.

feafbb6e16c99040.text: A temple dedicated to Astarte, the Punic goddess of love, fertility and war. What made her places of worship famous was their association with a particular practice, that of sacred prostitution.

fec2af2adc342f0b.text: At 'Perdas de Fogu', on the ridge of a small hill, are the remains of a giants' tomb built of large limestone boulders. The burial chamber is polygonal with an entrance to the south where part of the exedra is visible, having a chord of 12.10 metres. The chamber survives for a length of 6 metres, a width of 1.20 metres and a height of 0.50 metres.

fedb614b06203502.text: It is a large village, presenting a spread of ruins with Nuragic walls covering about eight thousand square metres.

ff0129571dd7d385.text: A ruined single-tower nuraghe of which very few remains can be seen

ff0a204cd398bbbd.text: Single-chamber domus de janas cut inside a "trovante"

ff161b8db71ec684.text: It consists of a Nuragic village, a circular temple and a megaron temple, and, upstream, a series of springs, wells and channels for capturing, collecting and channelling water towards the sacred area situated downstream.

ff280b1622433f81.text: The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

ff3b22b43a6cd206.text: Domus de janas submerged by the Omodeo reservoir. It preserves a bull's-head protome in high relief, unique of its kind.

ff42f029c5a65adc.text: Ruined nuraghe enveloped in vegetation, of which three or four courses survive.

ff572b34e36bfaa0.text:
The name is linked to a legend: after a human skull was found inside the cave, it was thought to belong to one of the unmarried mothers who, it is said, were shut inside as punishment until they died of suffocation.

More recently, human remains accompanied by coarseware pottery fragments have been found there. It is clear that Su Secretu is a small natural cave that must have served for funerary depositions.

ff70b1020d9ee8aa.text: A single-tower nuraghe overlooking the Rio Santu Milanu valley in an area reused in the medieval period.

ff848ec6f1270da6.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. In very poor condition, a few boulders of the entrance jamb and part of a basal course are visible. The entrance faces west. The nuraghe has suffered repeated robbing, as shown by several heaps of basalt boulders a short distance away. Even so, it cannot be ruled out that the nuraghe was never finished, as is documented elsewhere in the area.

ffbbac4cae4ffe49.text:
There are not enough elements to define it as a nuraghe. It appears to be a simple wall of roughly squared megaliths, like a rudimentary fortification for a guard post (?).

Nuraghe delle macerie. The rubble implied by the name is that of the nuraghe from which the locality takes its name. See Carràlzu. Ardu Pinzone = cardo. mu
